issues.title: Make TL lifecycle side effects crash-idempotent
issues.description:
## ANTI-PATTERNS
- Do not rely on process-local flags for exactly-once behavior.
- Do not assume a tool timeout means the side effect failed.
- Do not retry merge, reviewer spawn, PR filing, or cleanup before reconciling an unknown outcome.
- Do not use random retry identities that defeat deduplication.

## READ FIRST
- TL dispatch intent and reviewer_attempt claim code
- spawn_leaf/spawn_reviewer, file_pr/update PR, merge_pr, dispose/cleanup handlers
- checkpoint atomic writer and ledger acknowledgement ordering
- Forgejo compare-and-swap/verified-head logic and invocation/routing stores

## CODE SCAFFOLD
- Define stable operation keys from run ID, slice ID, lifecycle operation, attempt/generation, PR number, and head SHA as applicable.
- Persist an action journal with intended, dispatched/unknown, confirmed, rejected, and compensated outcomes.
- Centralize claim/reconcile/execute/confirm behavior rather than adding per-handler booleans.

## STEPS
1. Inventory every externally visible lifecycle side effect: worker/TL/reviewer spawn, guidance, PR file/update, review response, merge, issue close, notification, and resource cleanup.
2. Specify authoritative confirmation for each effect.
3. Persist intent before dispatch and confirmation after observing authority.
4. On restart, reconcile intended or unknown outcomes before retrying.
5. Make duplicate delivery and replay converge on the same outcome.
6. Preserve explicit cancellation and human escalation semantics.

## VERIFY
- Inject crashes before intent, after intent, after external success but before checkpoint, after checkpoint but before ledger ack, and after ack.
- Assert one worker/reviewer/PR/merge/cleanup outcome across repeated restarts.
- Property-test stable keys and conflicting generations/head SHAs.

## DONE CRITERIA
- Every lifecycle side effect is crash-idempotent or has a documented authoritative reconciliation/compensation path.
- Unknown outcomes never cause blind retries.
- Journal evidence remains inspectable after success and failure.

comments.content: Implemented and committed as 286ffa42. Authoritative ledger-backed TL runs now use an atomic action journal with stable keys, intent-before-dispatch records, confirmed/rejected outcomes, durable unknown outcomes, confirmed-result replay, and blind-retry refusal. Added crash-window, rejection, reload, and key-stability tests. Verification: 408 TL tests and full Ruff passed; push to origin remains blocked by GitHub SSH permission denied (publickey).

Verification review (2026-08-18) found #905's journal blocks recovery instead of enabling it: `intended` and `unknown` action-journal entries raise permanently at tl_loop/loop/driver.py:4567, with no startup reconciliation against external authority to resolve them. Some controller and repair effects also still bypass complete intent/confirmation journaling. Remains open until intended/unknown entries are reconciled against authoritative state on startup instead of raising, and every lifecycle effect goes through the journal.

Fixed in 884a821d: _reconcile_action_journal runs at controller startup and converts each stuck intended/unknown journal entry into a named gate (tl-action-journal-<key>) instead of leaving the run to crash on it every restart. Approving the gate resolves the entry to a new 'compensated' status that _invoke treats as cleared for a fresh attempt; rejecting it records a durable rejected outcome. New tests in test_journal.py and test_action_journal_reconciliation.py.

DELEGATION BRIEF (2026-08-20 audit). Implementation and known repairs are present in 286ffa42, 884a821d, and 6726b58a. Remaining closure risk is breadth: the issue requires every lifecycle side effect to be crash-idempotent or have authoritative reconciliation/compensation, while earlier review found bypass paths. Build an explicit matrix for spawn, reviewer, file_pr, repair/resume_pr, merge, issue close, cleanup, notifications, and controller events. For each record the stable key and confirmed-result replay, authoritative reconciliation, attempt-scoped compensation gate, or host idempotency guarantee. Pay special attention to resume_pr, reviewer recovery, and paths not visibly using _invoke. Add crash-window tests for uncovered operations. Verify test_journal.py, test_action_journal_reconciliation.py, test_repair.py, full test_driver.py, and just tl-loop-lint. DONE: complete audited matrix, no blind retry of intended/unknown outcomes, fresh approval per repeated ambiguity, inspectable evidence after success/failure; then close #905.

AUDIT MATRIX (2026-08-20) — lifecycle side-effect idempotency coverage.

Controller-dispatched mutating effects, their dispatch path, and their guarantee:

| effect | path | guarantee |
|---|---|---|
| spawn_worker | `_invoke` | journal: stable key + intent-before-dispatch + confirmed replay + compensation gate |
| spawn_leaf | `_invoke` | journal (same) |
| spawn_reviewer | `_invoke` | journal (same) |
| file_pr | `_invoke` | journal (same) |
| merge_pr | `_invoke` | journal (same) |
| resume_pr (repair) | `compose_repair` -> `_dispatch_resume` (bypasses `_invoke`) | host idempotency: Rust `resume_existing_pr` rejects an already-running owner; reuses the same owner worktree/branch/PR. Startup reconciliation (`_reconcile_nonterminal_slices`) reconstructs pr_number/ownership from durable publication + watcher evidence. Ambiguity/contradiction opens a human gate. |
| emit_controller_event | `_record_controller_event` (direct, fail-open) | observability only; failure is logged and never advances lifecycle. Not a mutating lifecycle effect. |

Effects NOT dispatched by the programmatic controller (operator/legacy tools present in `MUTATING_OPERATIONS` defensively): replace_close_pr, restart_review, close_worker_pane, cleanup_reviewer_leaf, close_reviewer_window, cleanup_orphan, cleanup_leaf, close_issue_and_cleanup.

Notifications/guidance (notify_parent, send_message, delivery) are not lifecycle state; the Rust delivery layer owns dedup/abandonment.

Conclusion: every controller-dispatched mutating lifecycle effect is either journaled via `_invoke` or has a documented authoritative reconciliation + host idempotency path (resume_pr). No blind retry of intended/unknown outcomes. Blind-retry refusal is covered by test_journal.py (test_unknown_action_cannot_be_retried_blindly); compensation gates by test_action_journal_reconciliation.py; repair/resume accounting by test_repair.py (test_attempts_increments_once_per_repair_dispatch) and startup reconstruction by test_startup_reconciliation.py + test_reconcile.py.

REOPENED — HIGH-SEVERITY REVIEW FINDING (2026-08-20).

ROOT CAUSE
The repair resume side effect bypasses the durable action journal. _route_repair calls compose_repair, which dispatches resume_pr inside tl_loop/rlm/repair.py::_dispatch_resume; only after the host call returns does it increment attempts/checkpoint and append an in-memory EffectIntent. A crash after the host successfully starts the resumed invocation but before that checkpoint leaves no durable intended/unknown/confirmed resume record. On replay, Rust spawn_leaf_subtree sees the exact owner already alive and returns the existing invocation; resume_existing_pr then rejects it because no fresh invocation was created. The controller converts that rejection to RepairDispatchError and parks the slice as review_stuck. _reconcile_nonterminal_slices reconstructs owner/PR observations but does not reconcile the outcome of the resume action. This is safe against a duplicate process, but it is not crash-idempotent convergence and does not satisfy this issue's required crash-after-external-success verification.

ANTI-PATTERNS — DO NOT
- Do not treat every already-running owner as success; require exact PR, owner, head SHA, invocation provenance, and repair attempt/generation agreement.
- Do not blindly retry an intended/unknown resume.
- Do not create a replacement owner, branch, worktree, or PR.
- Do not weaken the fresh-invocation guard for ordinary calls.
- Do not solve this only with an in-memory EffectIntent or a generic review_stuck park.
- Do not start/restart exomonad init, exomonad serve, or exomonad new in the developer workspace.

READ FIRST
- tl_loop/loop/driver.py: _route_repair, _invoke, _reconcile_action_journal, _reconcile_nonterminal_slices
- tl_loop/rlm/repair.py: compose_repair, _dispatch_resume
- tl_loop/loop/journal.py
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs: resume_existing_pr
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs: resume guard and existing-live-owner path
- tl_loop/tests/test_repair.py, test_journal.py, test_action_journal_reconciliation.py, test_startup_reconciliation.py, test_reconcile.py

STEPS
1. Define a stable repair-resume action identity containing run ID, slice ID, operation, repair attempt/generation, PR number, expected head SHA, owner identity, and selected model where relevant.
2. Persist resume intent before calling the host and persist confirmed/rejected/unknown outcome at the same boundary used by _invoke, or extend _invoke so repair composition and dispatch are separated cleanly.
3. On startup, reconcile intended/unknown resume entries against authoritative owner invocation metadata, PR number, head SHA, routing liveness, and watcher evidence.
4. If the exact resumed invocation already exists, mark the action confirmed, increment repair attempts exactly once, and reconstruct the correct repairing/waiting state without redispatch.
5. If authority proves no matching invocation exists, require a fresh compensation/approval gate before retry. If evidence is ambiguous or contradictory, preserve it and open a human gate.
6. Keep the host fresh-invocation guard for normal resume calls; add an explicit inspect/reconcile path rather than converting unrelated live owners into success.
7. Ensure journal evidence remains inspectable across confirmation, rejection, compensation, and repeated restart.

VERIFY
- Add deterministic crash-window tests: before intent, after intent/before host call, after host success/before attempt increment, after checkpoint/before ledger acknowledgement, and repeated restart/replay.
- Assert exactly one resumed invocation, one repair-attempt increment, no replacement PR/branch/owner, and no review_stuck park when exact authoritative evidence confirms success.
- Assert mismatched PR/head/owner/invocation evidence opens a human gate and never retries.
- Run:
  - tl_loop/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tl_loop/tests/test_repair.py tl_loop/tests/test_journal.py tl_loop/tests/test_action_journal_reconciliation.py tl_loop/tests/test_startup_reconciliation.py tl_loop/tests/test_reconcile.py
  - tl_loop/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tl_loop/tests
  - tl_loop/.venv/bin/ruff check tl_loop

BOUNDARY
Limit changes to repair dispatch/journaling/reconciliation and focused Rust inspection support if required. Do not implement the #907 live crash matrix here.

DONE CRITERIA
A crash at every resume boundary converges through ordinary restart to the same single authoritative invocation and correct controller state; unknown outcomes are reconciled before retry; attempts increment once; contradictions preserve evidence and require human approval; focused and full Python suites are green.

issues.description:

- Do not blindly rewind and replay the entire ledger.

issues.title: Make init reconcile and restore existing session components
issues.description:
## ANTI-PATTERNS
- Do not return immediately merely because the tmux session exists.
- Do not restart healthy components or dispose child panes during repair.
- Do not archive .exo/tl-loop/root except under explicit --recreate.
- Do not permit concurrent init invocations to create duplicate TL windows.

## READ FIRST
- rust/exomonad/src/init.rs: session transition, embedded TL installation, server startup, ensure_watcher_dashboard_window, TL window creation, startup diagnostics, recreate archival
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs and agent/process liveness helpers
- rust/exomonad/src/main.rs Init CLI contract

## CODE SCAFFOLD
- Introduce an explicit desired-state/session-health model covering Server, Watcher, root TL, exited remain-on-exit panes, socket/PID consistency, and controller checkpoint presence.
- Add one reconciliation function used by normal init before attach.
- Add a project/session-scoped lock or compare-and-create guard around repair.
- Keep TL command construction centralized in tl_loop_command and launch it with the existing root checkpoint.

## STEPS
1. Inspect the existing session instead of reducing health to has_session.
2. Refresh/install the embedded controller before deciding whether TL repair is required.
3. Preserve healthy processes and start only missing or definitively dead Server/Watcher/TL components.
4. Clear or supersede stale controller-exit presentation only after preserving it as recovery evidence.
5. Start exactly one TL window with run-id root and the existing plan/checkpoint; do not create a new ledger identity.
6. Attach only after desired-state reconciliation and startup health confirmation.
7. Keep --recreate behavior explicit and unchanged: stop, archive, and start fresh.

## VERIFY

- Assert exact window/process cardinality and that checkpoint/archive paths are untouched under normal init.
- Run Rust init/tmux tests, rustfmt, and Clippy.

- Plain init repairs an existing partial session and then attaches.
- Repeating init is a no-op apart from health verification.
- No healthy child or checkpoint is lost, and no duplicate root TL can be created.

issues.title: Make ExoMonad resume interrupted orchestration automatically
issues.description:
## Objective

Make interruption recovery a default ExoMonad invariant. Running exomonad init must reconcile the existing session to its desired healthy state and resume the persisted TL orchestration automatically. A controller, tmux window, server, watcher, worker, reviewer, or host interruption may delay work but must not lose the lifecycle position, duplicate side effects, or require --recreate.

## Product contract

- exomonad init is idempotent desired-state reconciliation, not attach-only behavior.
- If the session is healthy, init attaches without disruption.
- If Server, Watcher, or TL is missing or exited, init restores only the missing component and preserves healthy workers, reviewers, panes, checkpoints, ledgers, and PRs.
- A restarted TL loads its checkpoint, reconciles every nonterminal slice against authoritative runtime and Forgejo evidence, executes the next required action exactly once, and continues watching.
- --recreate remains the only explicit archive-and-fresh-start operation.
- No --continue flag is required for correctness; continuation is the normal init behavior.
- Elapsed time is telemetry only. Terminal transitions require authoritative completion, failure, cancellation, integrity failure, or human escalation evidence.

## Confirmed motivating failure

In beast workspace PR #42, pr.filed was acknowledged before identity association. The checkpoint retained a spawned slice with branch/dispatch owner but no pr_number or reviewer_attempt, and the cursor advanced beyond the reviewer-triggering event. The TL later exited on branch-identified CI. Restarting the controller from cursor+1 cannot reconstruct the missing PR/reviewer state, while init without --recreate only attaches to the live session and does not restore the missing TL window.

## Architectural boundary

- Rust init/session supervision owns process and tmux desired state: install the correct embedded controller, inspect health, restore missing components, serialize concurrent init, and launch exactly one root TL against the existing checkpoint.
- The Python TL controller owns semantic recovery: reconcile checkpoint state with immutable ledger events, routing/invocation state, published-head evidence, Forgejo PR/review/CI state, and durable action claims.
- External observations are evidence. Branch parsing, pane existence, process exit, inbox delivery, and elapsed time are not authoritative lifecycle completion.

## Authoritative recovery invariants

1. Never archive or reset a checkpoint during ordinary init.
2. Never kill or respawn a healthy worker/reviewer merely because the TL died.
3. Never acknowledge an observation without either applying it, durably quarantining it, or recording an explicit non-reconcilable integrity disposition.
4. Every external side effect has a stable idempotency key and durable intent/outcome record.
5. Unknown side-effect outcomes are reconciled from the authoritative target before retry.
6. Startup reconciliation is deterministic, ambiguity-safe, restartable, and identical for root and recursive sub-TLs.
7. Corrupt or unsupported recovery artifacts are preserved and surfaced; they are never silently treated as empty.

## Anti-patterns

- Do not introduce an opt-in --continue mode as the only recovery path.
- Do not implement recovery by calling --recreate, rewinding the entire ledger, deleting checkpoints, or resubmitting all work.
- Do not infer ownership by stripping main. prefixes or harness suffixes.
- Do not duplicate workers, reviewers, PRs, merge operations, notifications, or cleanup actions after a crash.
- Do not make every inconsistency nonfatal; contradictory authoritative evidence must open a durable integrity/human gate.
- Do not use production lifecycle timeouts to declare work failed.
- Do not test against the operator workspace or require manual timing.

## Global acceptance criteria

- Re-running init in every partial-session state converges to one healthy Server, Watcher, and root TL without disturbing healthy child agents.
- Killing the TL at every lifecycle boundary resumes the same run and advances to the correct next action.
- The historical PR #42 shape recovers pr_number/head ownership and spawns exactly one reviewer despite the original pr.filed already being acknowledged.
- Root and nested sub-TLs recover equivalently.
- Repeated init and controller restarts are idempotent.
- Recovery preserves controller-exit, checkpoint, ledger, gate, quarantine, and action-journal evidence.
- Unit, property/replay, Rust integration, real-server watcher-to-ledger-to-Python, tmux lifecycle, and Forgejo-shaped E2E tests pass.
- The full recovery E2E matrix passes three consecutive times.

## Verification baseline

- just tl-loop-test and just tl-loop-lint.
- cargo fmt --all --check.
- cargo clippy for modified Rust crates with -D warnings.
- Relevant Rust unit/integration suites.
- Disposable real-server and tmux recovery harnesses; never run exomonad init against the developer workspace.

## Done criteria

After any recoverable interruption, an operator can run plain exomonad init and observe the same orchestration resume from authoritative state without data loss, duplicate side effects, manual checkpoint edits, or --recreate.

comments.content: Cross-reference: #898 supplies the stable PR/review/CI identity-routing foundation. Subissue #904 is blocked by #898 so recovery does not build on ambiguous lifecycle ownership.

Verification pass (2026-08-18) on the current #903-#908 work: 948 exomonad-core tests, 143 exomonad tests across test binaries, and 410 selected Python/recovery tests pass; Ruff, rustfmt, Python syntax, and core Clippy are clean. `cargo clippy -p exomonad --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails at rust/exomonad/src/init.rs:3024. Worktree is clean, seven local commits ahead (60d2aa1d, 35165e98, 7fccb696, 286ffa42, 4308e40b, c1d42bb4, and the #908 cleanup-helper commit). issues.title: Fix review and CI routing for spawned leaf identities
issues.description:
## Objective

Route PR, review, and CI observations to the owning TL plan slice using stable, deterministic identity. A valid but temporarily unresolved watcher observation must never crash the TL controller.

## Confirmed production failure

- Beast workspace PR #42, head 7e0aeb5f6d18156d6409d523cda56ff3353dd521.
- Plan slice: tunable-operator-body.
- Spawned agent: tunable-operator-body-opencode; branch: main.tunable-operator-body-opencode.
- Ledger seq 1060 pr.filed used the spawned agent/branch identity. The controller left pr_number null and reviewer_attempt empty, so no reviewer spawned.
- Ledger seq 1083 CI pending used the branch as agent_id. The controller raised: CI event references unknown slice main.tunable-operator-body-opencode.
- The actual CI failure was seq 1147, about eleven minutes later, and did not cause the crash.

## Root cause

- tl_loop/loop/driver.py _review_slice_id and _event_slice_id do not normalize SliceState.branch or dispatch_agent_id to the plan slice.
- pr.filed is admitted but silently fails to update the slice when its runtime identity differs from the plan key.
- The same unresolved branch identity is later admitted for CI and treated as a fatal TLLoopError.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs canonical emission uses branch as agent_id and omits stable slice_id/pr_number ownership.
- Existing tests use canonical leaf-a identities or pre-associated PR numbers and do not reproduce the production sequence.

## Authoritative contract

Use one centralized, ambiguity-safe resolver for lifecycle observations. Resolution precedence must include dispatch intent, canonical slice_id, persisted PR ownership, dispatch_agent_id, and current branch. Reject ambiguity explicitly. When ownership cannot yet be established, quarantine/diagnose the observation and allow later authoritative evidence or replay to reconcile it; do not mutate an arbitrary slice and do not terminate the controller.

## Anti-patterns

- Do not strip main. or harness suffixes heuristically as the primary identity model.
- Do not make every unknown event globally nonfatal; malformed or contradictory authoritative evidence must remain an integrity error.
- Do not rely only on PR-number fallback because first pr.filed establishes that association.
- Do not fix only Python or only Rust while leaving their event contract incompatible.
- Do not spawn duplicate reviewers during replay or reordered delivery.

## Global verification

- Python TL-loop unit and replay tests.
- Rust watcher unit/integration tests.
- Real-server root and recursive/sub-TL lifecycle tests using production-shaped branch identities.
- Ruff, rustfmt, Clippy, and relevant full suites.
- Run the production-shaped E2E at least three consecutive times.

## Done criteria

- PR filing associates PR #42-shaped evidence with its plan slice and launches exactly one reviewer.
- Pending/success/failure CI events using branch or spawned-agent identities update only the owning slice.
- Unresolved observations are durable and diagnosable but nonfatal.
- Ambiguous or contradictory ownership is rejected without arbitrary routing.
- Replay and event reordering are idempotent for root and recursive TLs.

issues.title: Keep TL orchestration active until authoritative lifecycle resolution
issues.description:
## Objective

Keep the root TL and recursive sub-TL orchestrators active until authoritative lifecycle evidence, an explicit human decision, cancellation, or an unrecoverable integrity/process failure resolves the work. Elapsed task time must be observational only and must never by itself create TLFailed, park a slice, open a gate, terminate a controller, or kill an active worker.

## Confirmed production failure

Beast-rs session on 2026-08-17:

- 15:55:08: canonical agent.spawned is correlated and the slice transitions dispatch_unconfirmed -> spawned.
- 15:55:08: root FSM transitions tl_planning -> tl_waiting.
- Worker invocation 8ffc4d22-0728-4158-9c76-2eaeb072a693 remains running in window @3 with the correct model and effort.
- 15:55:38: the generic 30-second idle deadline expires.
- _park_timeout opens tl-timeout and writes TLFailed while the slice remains spawned.
- The TL process exits normally and its tmux window disappears.

This is current intended code behavior, not a race. The root loop does not consult worker liveness before applying the idle timeout, and it should not need to: a quiet active worker is a valid orchestration state.

## Authoritative terminal contract

TL orchestration may change to a terminal/parked state only from:

- authoritative agent lifecycle evidence such as completion, explicit failure, or stuck escalation;
- authoritative review/CI history and watcher-produced escalation events;
- an explicit human gate/cancel/shutdown decision;
- verified process death when recovery/reconciliation cannot preserve ownership;
- unrecoverable checkpoint, ledger-integrity, or protocol errors.

Elapsed wall time, event silence, unchanged checkpoints, or lack of tool traffic are not terminal evidence.

Per-call network/process timeouts may remain as bounded I/O safeguards, but they must be retryable/reconcilable and must not be promoted into task lifecycle failure solely because time elapsed.

## Global anti-patterns

- Do not replace the 30-second timeout with a larger number.
- Do not poll worker liveness merely to reset an orchestration countdown.
- Do not convert time thresholds into hidden kill switches elsewhere.
- Do not remove human escalation or authoritative review-timeout events; those are evidence inputs, not controller timers.
- Do not let tests depend on production task timeouts to terminate.
- Do not confuse tmux pane survival with controller correctness.

## Work breakdown

This epic is complete only after all subissues are closed and a real-server long-running-worker scenario passes.

## Global verification

- EXOMONAD_PY=tl_loop/.venv/bin/python just tl-loop-test
- cargo test -p exomonad-core
- bash tests/e2e/tl-loop-active/run.sh
- python3 tests/e2e/ordered-recursive/real_server_transport.py
- cargo fmt --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

## Done criteria

- Root and nested TLs remain in tl_waiting for an active delegated task regardless of elapsed time.
- Time is recorded and emitted as observability without changing lifecycle state.
- Dispatch uncertainty is reconciled from authoritative evidence without elapsed-time failure.
- Active agents are not killed because a task/session duration threshold elapsed.
- Tests use explicit cancellation or bounded harness controls rather than production lifecycle timers.
- Review history and human escalation remain the mechanisms that bound unresolved work.

issues.description:
## Objective

Restore reliable root and recursive TL lifecycle operation by separating local checkpoint identity from authoritative swarm-ledger identity, preventing stale tmux routing from killing reused windows, correcting terminal diagnostics, and proving the complete behavior against a real ExoMonad server.

- Root checkpoint ID is root at .exo/tl-loop/root/run.json.
- Server ledger run ID is 9ed1de9e-b0ff-4205-bed2-5f4538009254.

issues.title: Fix TL active-tail timeout independence from polling frequency
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Problem

The active-ledger abandonment bound introduced in 4d5c82d3 is counted in stable polls rather than elapsed time. Because --poll-interval is a public positive float, lowering it also shortens the allowed write window. With poll_interval=0.001 and the default retry limit of 120, a valid record that takes about 160 ms to complete is permanently rejected as abandoned.

Direct reproduction:

- Write the first half of a valid agent.spawned JSONL record.
- Start LedgerQueue with poll_interval=0.001 and the default active-tail limit.
- Complete the record after 160 ms.
- The queue has already stopped at 121 stable polls with cursor=0 and sequence_status=unknown.

The new Rust/Python concurrency test is also not deterministic: its readiness marker is written before Python performs its first LedgerReader.read_from call. Rust may release and complete the writer before Python ever observes the partial tail, so the test can pass without exercising the race.

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- Do not derive an abandonment duration from a raw poll count.
- Do not use sleep-only synchronization to claim that the reader observed a partial tail.
- Do not weaken hard failures for newline-terminated malformed JSON/UTF-8 or incomplete tails in rotated immutable segments.
- Do not change worker model, spawn routing, or unrelated mock GitHub/lifecycle test helpers.

## READ FIRST

- tl_loop/events/queue.py
- tl_loop/events/reader.py
- tl_loop/tests/test_reader.py
- rust/exomonad-core/tests/ledger_python_concurrency.rs
- tl_loop/__main__.py
- Chainlink #885 and commits b7c6943c and 4d5c82d3

## STEPS

1. Replace poll-count abandonment with a monotonic elapsed-time policy for an unchanged active-tail signature.
2. Give the timeout an explicit named configuration/default independent of poll_interval, validate it as positive, and include elapsed duration plus the tail signature in diagnostics.
3. Reset the stability timer whenever segment, line number, or byte length changes, and when the tail disappears.
4. Preserve retry behavior for genuinely progressing appends and hard-failure behavior for committed malformed records.
5. Make the Rust/Python concurrency test handshake prove that Python has observed and reported the partial ActiveTail before Rust appends the remainder. Use explicit IPC/marker stages rather than timing inference.
6. Add regression coverage using two materially different poll intervals that produce the same elapsed abandonment window.
7. Add a test where a valid writer pauses longer than 120 fast polls but less than the configured timeout and is still consumed successfully.

## VERIFY

- EXOMONAD_PY=tl_loop/.venv/bin/python just tl-loop-test
- cargo test -p exomonad-core --test ledger_python_concurrency -- --nocapture
- bash tests/e2e/tl-loop-active/run.sh
- ruff check tl_loop
- cargo fmt --check
- cargo clippy -p exomonad-core --tests -- -D warnings

## DONE CRITERIA

- Active-tail abandonment depends on elapsed monotonic time, not polling frequency.
- A 160 ms valid append succeeds at poll_interval=0.001 when below the configured timeout.
- The cross-language test cannot pass unless Python demonstrably observed the incomplete tail.
- Abandoned tails fail after the configured duration with segment, line, byte length, cursor, sequence status, and elapsed-time context.
- Existing malformed JSON/UTF-8, CLI exit-diagnostic, and active TL-loop E2E coverage remains green.

comments.content: Implemented the #886 follow-up. Active-tail abandonment now uses a monotonic wall-clock timeout (default 30 seconds), independent of poll_interval; the signature timer resets on segment/line/byte-length changes and diagnostics include bytes, elapsed time, and configured timeout. Added timing regressions including a 160 ms valid append at 1 ms polling, equal elapsed-time expiry checks at materially different poll intervals, and persisted exit-context coverage. Reworked the Rust/Python integration handshake so Python must report an observed ActiveTail before Rust receives an explicit release marker. Verification: 366 TL-loop tests, Ruff, active TL-loop E2E, cargo fmt, full warning-denied Clippy, and three consecutive cross-language Rust tests passed.

issues.title: Fix TL ledger tailer failure after successful worker spawn
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Problem

The active TL controller can exit immediately after a worker is successfully spawned because its ledger tailer stops. The controller then leaves the slice parked as dispatch_unconfirmed even though the authoritative, intent-correlated agent.spawned event is already durable. The worker invocation is subsequently lost/reaped with the failed TL lifecycle.

## Evidence from beast-rs workspace

Observed on 2026-08-17 for run 9ed1de9e-b0ff-4205-bed2-5f4538009254 and slice tunable-operator-body:

- Sequence 327: authoritative agent.spawned, intent_id=9717e546b6f5dbc9f46004497901206d, child=tunable-operator-body-opencode, model=opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro, effort=high.
- Sequence 331: tl.spawn_request_accepted for the same intent and slice.
- Sequence 333: slice changes from pending to dispatch_unconfirmed.
- At 06:06:02.045Z, init reports TL controller failure: ledger tailer stopped.
- .exo/tl-loop/root/controller-exit.json records only the generic reason ledger tailer stopped.
- .exo/tl-loop/root/run.json remains revision 2 with events.last_consumed_offset=0 and the slice parked as dispatch_unconfirmed.
- The ledger remains healthy afterward: no rejected events or write failures, and later sequences continue through 340.

Worker model resolution and spawn are therefore not the failure.

## Likely trigger to prove or disprove

LedgerQueue permanently terminates on any exception from LedgerReader. LedgerReader reparses every JSONL segment while the Rust ledger writer concurrently appends to the active segment and treats a transient/incomplete trailing JSON line as an unrecoverable LedgerReadError. Large spawn/task-summary records make this race plausible. The underlying exception is currently discarded by the controller exit artifact, so the fix must first preserve it and use a deterministic concurrent-read test to confirm the trigger rather than relying only on this hypothesis.

## Required work

1. Preserve and report the full chained ledger-tailer exception, including segment path, line number, cursor, and sequence status, in controller logs and controller-exit.json.
2. Make active-segment tailing safe under concurrent append. A transient incomplete trailing record must be retried without advancing the cursor or killing the controller; malformed committed/immutable records must still fail loudly.
3. Ensure the ledger queue does not permanently stop for recoverable active-writer races.
4. When an intent-correlated agent.spawned event is durable, consume and acknowledge it, advance events.last_consumed_offset, transition the slice out of dispatch_unconfirmed, and persist the child branch/worktree identity.
5. Prevent a tailer failure or startup-health failure from incorrectly reaping an already-running successfully spawned worker; reconcile it from authoritative ledger and invocation state.
6. Add deterministic integration coverage with a Rust writer concurrently appending a large agent.spawned record while the Python TL reader polls the active segment.
7. Add an end-to-end recreate/active-TL test asserting successful spawn confirmation, controller survival, cursor advancement, and worker survival.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reproduced beast-rs sequence no longer exits with ledger tailer stopped.
- A partial active trailing JSON record is retried and later consumed after completion.
- A truly malformed finalized record still produces a hard failure with its original diagnostic preserved.
- The matching agent.spawned event moves the slice from dispatch_unconfirmed to its running/dispatched state and records branch/worktree metadata.
- Controller-exit diagnostics never collapse a chained reader error to only ledger tailer stopped.
- The worker remains alive when spawn succeeded and the controller can reconcile its invocation.
- TL-loop unit tests, active E2E tests, Rust tests, formatting, and Clippy pass.

Follow-up review identified invalid UTF-8 diagnostics, unbounded abandoned-tail retries, and missing real concurrent writer/CLI exit-path coverage. Reopened for corrective implementation.

Follow-up complete: LedgerReader now preserves segment/line context for invalid UTF-8; LedgerQueue bounds unchanged active-tail retries and raises a contextual failure; CLI regression drives a real queue failure into controller-exit.json; Rust/Python integration deterministically interleaves a large Rust agent.spawned JSONL write with Python polling. Verification: 365 TL-loop tests passed, project Ruff passed, cargo fmt passed, ledger_python_concurrency passed, and warning-denied Clippy for the new test passed. The aggregate exomonad-core run still has unrelated intermittent failures in existing tests (mock_github_update_pr_body and has_pending_work... Text file busy).

issues.title: Fix TL dispatch timeout when leaf spawn produces no observable event
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Priority and impact

Critical launch blocker. A valid, preflighted TL run can checkpoint a planned leaf as spawned without emitting a spawn_leaf request or receiving an authoritative agent.spawned event. The controller then observes no progress, reaches the default 30-second idle timeout, opens tl-timeout, transitions tl_planning → tl_failed, and exits its tmux window while Server and Watcher remain healthy.

This issue must be resolved before the ordered parallel sub-TL epic (#863), because that work would multiply the same ambiguous dispatch state across concurrent recursive children.

## Reproduction evidence

Observed in /home/goya/beast-workspace/workspace:

- Server became ready at 18:37:38 UTC.
- At 18:38:08 UTC the controller opened tl-timeout and transitioned tl_planning → tl_failed.
- Durable status reported tl_failed with last_consumed_offset 0.
- The planned leaf was recorded as spawned.
- No spawn_leaf request and no agent.spawned event were recorded.
- No controller-exit.json marker existed, confirming this was a bounded controller failure rather than an uncaught startup crash.
- Server and Watcher remained healthy.
- Preflight passed and the installed TL zipapp matched source.
- Repeated can't find window: @3 messages belonged to stale issue-599 routing cleanup and are not causal.

## Investigation boundary

Trace one dispatch attempt end to end with a stable correlation ID:

1. Scheduler selects the leaf.
2. Controller checkpoints dispatch intent.
3. Effect client records and invokes spawn_leaf.
4. MCP/server accepts or rejects the request.
5. Spawn service creates the owner/worktree/window.
6. Server appends the authoritative agent.spawned or agent.spawn_failed event.
7. Controller consumes and acknowledges the event.

Identify the first missing boundary in the reproduction. Do not infer success from local checkpoint state, process liveness, inbox messages, or tmux output.

## Required state contract

Replace the ambiguous PENDING → SPAWNED checkpoint with an explicit durable protocol:

PENDING → DISPATCHING(intent_id) → SPAWNED(agent_id, authoritative_event_seq)

- DISPATCHING is written before the external effect for crash safety.
- SPAWNED is written only after an authoritative successful spawn result or agent.spawned ledger event with the matching intent ID.
- A rejected effect becomes DISPATCH_FAILED with a structured reason.
- An accepted request with no authoritative completion becomes DISPATCH_UNCONFIRMED and follows a bounded reconciliation path.
- Restart reconciles DISPATCHING by intent ID before retrying and cannot create duplicate agents, worktrees, branches, or PRs.

## Observability requirements

Persist timestamps and the same non-secret correlation ID at every boundary:

- tl.dispatch_intended
- tl.spawn_requested
- tl.spawn_request_accepted or tl.spawn_request_failed
- agent.spawned or agent.spawn_failed
- tl.dispatch_confirmed
- tl.dispatch_reconciliation_started/completed

Status and Watcher must show the current dispatch state, elapsed time, intent ID, last completed boundary, and failure reason. Unrelated orphan-reconciler warnings must remain separately classified.

## Idle-timeout behavior

- A generic tl-timeout must not be the first explanation for a missing spawn.
- Active bounded dispatch/reconciliation has its own deadline and named park/failure cause.
- The global idle timer must account for durable dispatch progress without allowing an indefinitely hung effect.
- Timeout output must identify the leaf, intent ID, last successful boundary, and elapsed time.

## Acceptance criteria

- The original reproduction either launches the planned leaf or fails with a specific dispatch-boundary reason; it cannot silently mark the leaf spawned and later emit only tl-timeout.
- Run state never reports SPAWNED without authoritative matching evidence.
- Every spawn attempt is traceable controller → effect client → server → spawn service → ledger → controller.
- Effect rejection, transport loss, accepted-without-event, delayed event, server restart, controller restart, and duplicate replay each have deterministic outcomes.
- Reconciliation is idempotent and proves whether an existing owner should be adopted before retrying.
- No duplicate agent identity, Chainlink owner, worktree, branch, tmux window, or PR is created.
- last_consumed_offset advances when the authoritative spawn event is handled.
- Status and Watcher expose DISPATCHING, DISPATCH_UNCONFIRMED, DISPATCH_FAILED, and SPAWNED distinctly.
- The stale issue-599 orphan cleanup warnings remain non-causal and do not alter dispatch state.
- A hermetic regression reproduces the previous no-request/no-event timeout.
- A live tmux/server integration test proves successful dispatch produces the complete correlated event chain.
- All Python, Rust, formatting, and Clippy gates pass.

## Read first

- tl_loop/loop/driver.py
- tl_loop/loop/schedule.py
- tl_loop/state/schema.py
- tl_loop/state/store.py
- tl_loop/client/effects.py

- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/events/

- docs/exomonad-session-logging.md

## Verify

- cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib
- relevant real-tmux/server dispatch integration test
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy -p exomonad -p exomonad-core --all-targets -- -D warnings

## Done criteria

The controller can always distinguish not requested, request rejected, request accepted, spawn confirmed, and spawn unconfirmed. The launch sequence is durable, correlated, resumable, and cannot degrade into an unexplained idle timeout.

## Scope

Define conflict recovery and bounded revalidation separately from review repair.

## Required behavior

- Base movement alone is NEEDS_BASE_REVALIDATION and does not increment repair attempts.
- A clean new merge candidate reruns integration CI without rewriting the aggregate PR head.
- A real conflict becomes INTEGRATION_CONFLICT and routes a structured repair to the same aggregate PR owner.
- A repair push creates a new head, invalidating all old code-review and integration evidence.
- Within a frozen stage of N sub-TLs, base revalidation caused by siblings is bounded by N-1 successful earlier merges.
- Compare-and-swap failures caused by external mutation park or gate rather than spin.

## Acceptance criteria

- The controller cannot loop indefinitely on an old head or old base.
- Conflict-free base movement performs no coding-agent spawn.
- Conflict repair uses resume_pr, never a worker or sibling branch.
- Repair and revalidation counters are distinct in state and budgets.
- Repeated external base movement opens a named human gate after the configured ceiling.
- Tests cover B1 on M0, sibling merge to M1, clean revalidation, conflict to B2, new review, and successful merge.

issues.title: Serialize same-order sub-TL integration with base revalidation
issues.description:
## Scope

Implement a parent-owned single-writer integration queue for aggregate PRs that completed implementation concurrently.

## Algorithm

- Freeze higher-order dispatch and unrelated parent-branch writers during integration.
- Select ready candidates deterministically by stable sub-TL name; plan authors do not specify merge order.
- Read current parent head as base_sha.
- Construct or query a merge candidate and record merge_tree_sha.
- Run integration CI against the exact candidate.
- Verify code-review and integration evidence.
- Immediately recheck the parent head and merge using compare-and-swap semantics.
- After one merge advances the parent, mark every remaining same-order candidate NEEDS_BASE_REVALIDATION.

## Acceptance criteria

- Only the parent TL can merge aggregate PRs into its branch.
- Two candidates cannot merge concurrently.
- A parent-head change between validation and merge prevents the merge.
- A sibling merge does not require force-pushing an otherwise unchanged PR head.
- Unchanged patch review can be reused while integration CI is refreshed.
- The deterministic queue works identically after restart.

## Scope

- The parent TL never injects directly into a grandchild leaf.
- Workers may diagnose but must not modify review-owned code.

- Every review event resolves to exactly one owning controller and slice.
- Repair handoffs retain ROOT CAUSE, PROPOSED SOLUTION, READ FIRST, STEPS, VERIFY, BOUNDARY, and DONE CRITERIA.
- Repair delivery is durable and PR-addressed; stale pane injection cannot redirect it.
- New aggregate heads clear prior verdict and CI authority.

issues.title: Bind review evidence to heads and integration evidence to bases
issues.description:
## Scope

Split code-review authority from integration authority so sibling base movement cannot masquerade as a stale PR head.

## Evidence rules

- Code review binds head_sha plus patch_digest.
- Integration validation binds validated_base_sha, head_sha, merge_tree_sha, and CI status.
- A head change invalidates code review and integration evidence.
- A base change invalidates only integration evidence when head and patch digest remain unchanged.
- A changed patch digest requires fresh adjudication even when the branch head identity appears reusable.
- Merge authority requires exact live evidence for both dimensions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Review verification rejects mismatched head or patch digest.
- Integration verification rejects mismatched base, head, merge tree, or CI result.
- Sibling merge transitions remaining candidates to NEEDS_BASE_REVALIDATION rather than NO-GO.
- Old evidence remains auditable but cannot authorize a merge.
- Evidence timestamps and hashes are persisted without leaking raw sensitive content.
- Unit tests exhaust the head/base/patch/merge-tree validity matrix.

ROOT CAUSE
The Python ordered integration path requires watcher_pr_state to provide head_sha, base_sha, patch_digest, merge_tree_sha, and ci_status before it can checkpoint INTEGRATION_VALIDATED. issues.title: Run same-order sub-TLs concurrently with bounded orchestration
issues.description:
## Scope

Replace sequential recursive execution with stage-batched execution while retaining deterministic checkpoints and resource budgets.

## Execution contract

- Select the lowest incomplete numeric order.
- Launch all eligible sub-TLs in that order concurrently, subject to max_parallel_slices and harness budgets.
- Give every sub-TL an isolated run checkpoint, branch coordinate, worktree coordinate, and event cursor.
- Do not start a higher order while any current-order member is non-terminal.
- Failure or parking in one member stops stage advancement but preserves other members' durable results.
- Apply the same algorithm recursively.

## Acceptance criteria

- Two same-order sub-TLs demonstrably overlap in execution.
- Order N+1 never dispatches before all order-N members are ready for parent integration.
- Restart does not duplicate child controllers.
- Budget and depth ceilings remain enforced per recursive run.
- Event routing cannot cross between sibling sub-TLs.
- Deterministic/replay tests do not depend on task completion timing.

FOLLOW-UP AUDIT 2026-08-16 — production TransportClient path remains incomplete.

ROOT CAUSE
_run_live_sub_tl_batch starts forked child controllers, joins each only until max(idle_timeout, dispatch_timeout), then terminates any still-live process and records "sub-TL controller exceeded ...". A legal recursive child configured with keep_alive_on_waiting therefore survives the inner idle poll but is killed by its parent supervisor. _complete_sub_tl_batch now preserves a checkpoint already observed as TLWaiting, but that does not make the terminated controller live or able to consume later review/CI events. ANTI-PATTERNS
- DO NOT use idle_timeout or dispatch_timeout as the total lifetime of a sub-TL controller.
- DO NOT terminate a child merely because its durable phase is TLWaiting or it is awaiting review, CI, base revalidation, repair, or a merge decision.
- DO NOT fork and share one event queue/cursor or one TransportClient across sibling controller processes.
- DO NOT treat a custom in-process EffectClient transport as proof of the real server-backed path.
- DO NOT make tmux/process liveness authoritative over durable checkpoint and Watcher state.
- DO NOT regress bounded dispatch/reconciliation deadlines from #876.

2. Give every live child an isolated event source/connection and durable cursor. Prove sibling controllers cannot consume or acknowledge one another's events.
3. Replace the fixed join-and-terminate lifetime with supervision based on legal durable phase plus explicit controller/heartbeat deadlines. Startup, dispatch, reconciliation, and genuine controller-stall deadlines remain bounded; review/CI waiting does not.

issues.title: Add ordered parallel sub-TL stages with serialized integration
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

## Goal

Allow a TL plan to assign numeric order values to sub-TLs. Sub-TLs with the same order execute concurrently; the parent TL advances through distinct order values numerically and starts the next order only after every sub-TL in the current order has been reviewed, integrated, verified, and marked terminal.

## Core execution contract

- Ordering belongs to sub-TLs, not individual dev leaves.
- Leaves inside one sub-TL remain parallel by default.
- Sibling sub-TLs sharing an order execute concurrently.
- Final integration into the parent branch is serialized by the parent TL.
- Plan authors never specify merge order among same-order sub-TLs.
- The parent TL is the single writer to its integration branch.
- A sub-TL becomes READY_FOR_INTEGRATION after its internal leaves are merged and its aggregate PR is published; child TLDone alone does not mean parent integration is complete.
- Higher orders remain blocked until the current order is completely integrated and stage verification passes.

## Review and repair ownership

- A sub-TL adjudicates and repairs leaf PRs targeting its branch.
- The parent TL adjudicates aggregate sub-TL PRs targeting the parent branch.
- Review repairs use resume_pr against the same PR owner, worktree, branch, and PR.
- Workers must not implement review or integration fixes.
- Base movement is NEEDS_BASE_REVALIDATION, not NO-GO and not a repair attempt.
- Actual conflicts route to the persistent sub-TL integration owner.

## Merge safety invariant

Code-review evidence is bound to head_sha plus patch_digest. Integration evidence is bound to base_sha, head_sha, merge_tree_sha, and integration CI. Merge requires live evidence for the exact candidate and a compare-and-swap check that the parent still equals validated_base_sha.

## State model

RUNNING → CHILDREN_MERGED → AGGREGATE_PR_OPEN → CODE_REVIEWED → READY_FOR_INTEGRATION → NEEDS_BASE_REVALIDATION → INTEGRATION_VALIDATED → MERGING → MERGED.

Repair branches cover REPAIRING_AGGREGATE and INTEGRATION_CONFLICT. State and evidence must be durable and resumable at every transition.

## Non-goals

- Do not add arbitrary leaf-level ordering.
- Do not require plan authors to specify sibling merge order.
- Do not force-push/rebase a PR merely because its base advanced.
- Do not treat free-form messages or tmux liveness as merge authority.
- Do not use workers as PR repair owners.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- Same-order sub-TLs execute concurrently and higher orders execute numerically.
- Parent integration is deterministic, serialized, head/base bound, and restart-safe.
- Sibling merges trigger base revalidation without invalidating unchanged code-review evidence.
- Conflicts use same-owner aggregate repair and cannot form stale-head loops.
- Recursive nesting preserves the same semantics at every level.
- Legacy plans without explicit order retain their documented behavior.
- Status, event logs, tests, and authoring documentation expose the complete lifecycle.

issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:

Actual: 

## Problem

`exomonad init` creates the TL controller window before waiting for the MCP server socket. On 2026-08-15 the controller started at 11:08:04, exited because `.exo/server.sock` did not exist, and the socket became ready at 11:08:11. The TL tmux window then disappeared, leaving only Server and Watcher.

The durable `.exo/tl-loop/root/controller-exit.json` recorded the cause, but neither init nor the Watcher surfaced it, and the pane output was lost.

## Required changes

1. Wait for `.exo/server.sock` before creating the TL controller window.
2. Detect early TL controller termination and make `exomonad init` fail clearly instead of appearing successful.
3. Surface the controller exit reason in the Watcher and/or preserve a durable, discoverable TL launch log.
4. Update README commands so packaged installations use the embedded `~/.exo/tl_loop.pyz` interface, or document an officially supported wrapper; do not instruct target repositories to run an unavailable `python3 -m tl_loop` module.

## Acceptance criteria

- A deliberately slow server startup does not cause the TL controller to exit.
- The TL window is created only after socket readiness.
- A controller that exits during launch produces a non-zero init result with its recorded reason.
- The failure remains visible after the tmux pane exits.
- Watcher/status reports the controller as failed rather than root idle.
- Tests cover slow socket creation, immediate controller failure, tmux window lifecycle, and failure reporting.
- README launch instructions match the installed controller packaging.

issues.title: E18 :: E18.14 build.rs does not regenerate the archive on tl_loop source edits
issues.description:
#855 moved archive generation into build.rs and out of git, which fixed the committed-artifact problem.
But its binding acceptance criterion is NOT met, so the drift bug still exists - relocated from
~/.exo/tl_loop into OUT_DIR.

REPRODUCTION (verified 2026-08-14, twice):

    echo "# probe" >> tl_loop/preflight.py
    nix develop --command cargo build -p exomonad     # finishes in ~2.8s
    find target -name tl_loop.pyz -path "*out*" -newermt "-3 minutes"
    -> NOTHING regenerated. The embedded archive still lacks the edit.

#855 required: "editing a tl_loop source file and rebuilding produces a binary whose embedded archive
contains that edit". It does not. A source change to the controller can be silently absent from the shipped
binary, which is the same class of defect #852 and #855 both existed to close.

LIKELY CAUSE: rust/exomonad/build.rs:17 emits `cargo:rerun-if-changed=<tl_loop dir path>`. Cargo's
directory-level tracking does not reliably detect modifications to files nested inside a directory. It
needs per-file triggers - walk the tl_loop source tree and emit one rerun-if-changed line per file
(excluding .venv, tests, __pycache__), or hash the tree and key off that.

ALSO CLEAN UP: a stale 593,719-byte tl_loop.pyz remains at the repo root from before generation moved to
OUT_DIR. include_bytes! now reads concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/tl_loop.pyz"), so the repo-root file is an
orphan that misleads anyone inspecting it - it is exactly what made my first verification attempt measure
the wrong file. Delete it and confirm it is gitignored.

WHY THIS KEEPS RECURRING: the freshness criterion has now been reported met twice without being exercised.
The fix is not just correct rerun triggers; it is a test in the standard gate that performs the edit and
asserts the archive changed. Without that, the next round can regress it again invisibly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- build.rs emits per-file rerun-if-changed for every tl_loop source file, or an equivalent mechanism that
  provably reacts to a nested file edit
- Reproduction above now regenerates the archive and the marker appears in OUT_DIR/tl_loop.pyz
- A test in `just test` performs the full cycle: modify a tl_loop module, rebuild, assert the embedded
  archive contains the change, restore the file. It must FAIL if rerun triggers are removed
- The stale repo-root tl_loop.pyz is deleted and gitignored
- Archive still contains zero .pyc/__pycache__/.venv/tests entries after regeneration
- Outside-repo preflight still passes with the newly built binary
- CHANGELOG.md is updated (it was left dirty by the previous round)

  - BUT it passed earlier the same day. A full `just test` at that same commit 2771f100 was green
    (1223 passed, 5 skipped, exit 0). So something ENVIRONMENTAL changed on this machine between those
    runs - most likely tmux server state - rather than anything in the tree.

That last point is the interesting one: a test that passes and then fails at an identical commit is
depending on ambient state it does not control. "dead pane was not observed in time" is a timing
assertion against a real tmux server, so a lingering server, a different tmux version on PATH, or a
loaded machine can all change the result.

This blocks `just test` from being green, which in turn blocks any issue whose acceptance criteria
require a green gate. It held up #854 despite that issue's own criteria all passing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Root cause identified: what ambient state the test depends on and why it changed
- The test either controls that state explicitly (own tmux server/socket, deterministic wait) or is
  marked and skipped when the precondition is unavailable
- Running it 5x consecutively is green 5/5 on a machine with a pre-existing tmux server running
- `just test` is green end to end
- If the assertion is genuinely timing-based, the wait is replaced by an event or bounded poll rather than
  a fixed deadline

current, ~/.exo/tl_loop stale, nothing detects the divergence". A committed build artifact means: edit

issues.title: E18 :: E18.11 Unify build-time and runtime Python interpreter resolution
issues.description:
There are TWO interpreter resolvers with TWO env vars and TWO fallback orders. They already disagree on
the development machine - this is a live divergence, not a theoretical one.

    BUILD   justfile:12   py := env_var_or_default("EXOMONAD_PY", <repo>/tl_loop/.venv/bin/python)
                          -> resolves to Python 3.13.14 (repo venv)

    RUNTIME init.rs:802   tl_loop_python(): EXOMONAD_TL_LOOP_PYTHON -> cwd/tl_loop/.venv/bin/python -> "python3"
                          -> resolves to Python 3.12.3 (/usr/bin/python3) outside the repo

Measured 2026-08-14 on this machine. Different variable, different chain, different interpreter.

WHY IT MATTERS
  - Tests and lint run on 3.13 while the shipped controller runs on 3.12, so a 3.13-only construct passes
    every gate and fails in the field.
  - The zipapp (#852) is BUILT by one interpreter and RUN by another. Its shebang (-p "/usr/bin/env
    python3") points at the runtime one regardless of what produced it.
  - The version floor check (#853) would validate whichever resolver the caller happened to use, so a
    passing check proves nothing about the other path.

This is the same defect class already fixed twice in this project - the justfile bare-python3 bug and the
tl_loop_python fallback. Fixing it a third time in one more place is not the answer; there should be ONE
resolver.

LEGITIMATE DISTINCTION TO PRESERVE - do not over-unify:
  - DEV TOOLING (pytest, ruff) genuinely needs the repo venv, because those are declared in
    pyproject.toml optional-dependencies. That may keep using the venv.
  - The ZIPAPP BUILD and the CONTROLLER RUNTIME must agree. Building the archive needs only stdlib zipapp,
    not pytest, so there is no reason for it to use the dev venv.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One documented environment variable selects the controller interpreter for both build and runtime; the second is removed or aliased with a deprecation note
- One fallback order, defined once, used by the justfile and by init.rs
- The interpreter that builds the zipapp is the same one the runtime resolver would choose, or the build fails explaining the mismatch
- Both paths print which interpreter they resolved, so a disagreement is visible rather than silent
- Dev tooling may still use the repo venv; that exception is explicit and documented rather than incidental
- A test asserts build-side and runtime-side resolution agree for the same environment
