issues.title: E18 :: E18.10 Verify and document the python3 interpreter floor
issues.description:
SEPARATE FROM PACKAGING - #852 does not solve this. Bundling fixes WHICH MODULES exist; it does not fix
WHICH INTERPRETER runs them.

Operator context: "even my system is all sorts of configurations for python". A zipapp still needs a system
python3, and tl_loop/pyproject.toml declares requires-python = ">=3.11". Nothing verifies that today.

Current resolution (init.rs:802 tl_loop_python) is:
    EXOMONAD_TL_LOOP_PYTHON -> cwd/tl_loop/.venv/bin/python -> "python3"

The middle branch exists only inside the exomonad repo, so consuming projects always land on bare python3 -
whatever that happens to be on PATH. On a machine where python3 is 3.9, the failure is a syntax error deep
in an import, not a clear message.

`just install-all` already requires system Nix, Rust, and Haskell toolchains, so requiring python3 >= 3.11
is consistent with how this project already treats toolchains - it just has to be STATED and CHECKED rather
than assumed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Install fails loudly and by name when the resolved python3 is older than the requires-python floor, naming the version found and the version needed
- Preflight performs the same check at runtime, so a machine that changes python3 after install is caught
- The floor is read from tl_loop/pyproject.toml rather than hardcoded in two places
- EXOMONAD_TL_LOOP_PYTHON remains the explicit override and is documented for multi-interpreter systems
- README/install docs list python3 >= 3.11 alongside Nix, tmux, and just
- A test covers the too-old-interpreter path and asserts the message names both versions

comments.content:
OPERATOR QUESTION: can `just install-all` install a viable python3 for the system?

PUSHBACK - it should VERIFY, not INSTALL. A build tool that installs system packages needs sudo, differs
per platform (apt/brew/dnf/pacman), and can break an OS-managed interpreter. That is a large, invasive, and
platform-specific surface for a check that can be a one-line comparison.

Two distinct interpreters are involved and only one is install-all's business:

  BUILD-TIME - making the zipapp needs python3 during `just install-all`. GAP FOUND: flake.nix does NOT
  currently provide python3, so the build already depends on an ambient system interpreter. Adding python3
  to the nix devShell is the right fix here and IS in scope - it makes the build hermetic, matching how Nix
  already supplies Rust and Haskell.

  RUN-TIME - the consuming machine still needs its own python3 >= 3.11 to execute the archive. Nix cannot
  install that system-wide, and install-all should not try. This one is verified and reported, never
  installed.

So: add python3 to the nix devShell for the build, and fail loudly with a named version at runtime. If a
fallback is ever wanted for a machine with no viable python3, resolving one from the nix store is a better
avenue than a package manager - but that is a separate decision, not part of this task.

Additional acceptance criterion:
- flake.nix devShell provides python3 >= the requires-python floor, so `just install-all` no longer depends on an ambient system interpreter

ESCAPE HATCH, documented not built: python-build-standalone ships a complete relocatable CPython (~25MB). It is the right answer ONLY if the >=3.11 floor turns out to be a real field problem on machines where no viable python3 can be installed. Do not build it pre-emptively - the floor check has to demonstrate an actual failure first. Recorded from the packaging alternatives reviewed on #852.

Verified #853 in commit 60646aa0eba1594aa09f8daeeb61b0f2a0cc7055: tl_loop/pyproject.toml is the sole source for the requires-python floor; build and runtime checks report found/needed versions and reject Python 3.10.9 with both names; EXOMONAD_TL_LOOP_PYTHON remains supported; flake.nix devShell includes python3; README prerequisites document Python 3.11+ alongside Nix, tmux, and just plus the dev-only EXOMONAD_PY venv exception. Checks passed: cargo fmt --all; cargo test -p exomonad --no-default-features (80 tests passed); cargo test -p exomonad init::tests::old_tl_loop_interpreter_error_names_found_and_required_versions --no-default-features; just tl-loop-python-check; nix flake check --no-build; git diff --check. Working tree clean.

issues.title: E18 :: E18.9 Ship tl_loop as a zipapp - installed package is incomplete, init broken in consuming projects
issues.description:
BREAKS EVERY CONSUMING PROJECT. `exomonad init` currently fails at preflight in any repo that is not
the exomonad source tree, because the installed Python package is incomplete.

REPRODUCTION (the exact path the binary takes in a consuming project):
    cd /home/goya/beast-workspace/workspace
    PYTHONPATH=$HOME/.exo python3 -m tl_loop preflight --project-root .
    -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tl_loop.plan_validation'

ROOT CAUSE - justfile:268-269 copies an ENUMERATED allowlist:
    cp tl_loop/__init__.py tl_loop/__main__.py ~/.exo/tl_loop/
    cp -R tl_loop/{client,events,fsm,harness,loop,rlm,select,shadow,state} ~/.exo/tl_loop/

Two named files and nine named directories. Any NEW top-level module is silently dropped.
    source:    __init__.py __main__.py plan_validation.py preflight.py
    installed: __init__.py __main__.py

Blast radius is wider than preflight: rlm/intent_contract.py imports tl_loop.plan_validation, so M12's
interpret_operator_intent is also broken in the installed package.

Why it was not caught: every test and manual check ran against the source tree with the repo-local
tl_loop/.venv. init.rs tl_loop_python() prefers cwd/tl_loop/.venv/bin/python, which exists ONLY in the
exomonad repo; a consuming project falls back to bare python3 with PYTHONPATH=~/.exo, which is the broken
path nothing exercises.

DO NOT CREATE A VENV FOR CONSUMING PROJECTS. tl_loop/pyproject.toml declares requires-python = ">=3.11"
and dependencies = [] - the controller is genuinely stdlib-only at runtime (verified: the source package
imports cleanly on system Python 3.12.3). A per-project venv would contradict that design, add an artifact
that goes stale, and reintroduce the interpreter-mismatch bug class already fixed twice in the justfile and
in tl_loop_python(). What is missing is not a venv but a VERSION FLOOR CHECK: bare python3 is correct only
when it is >=3.11, and nothing verifies that today.

Note `exomonad new` does NOT copy the package - new.rs:177 write_tl_loop_defaults writes CONFIG defaults
only. Package installation is `just install-all` alone. Keep that split; new should not become an installer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The install recipe copies every top-level tl_loop *.py rather than naming files, and copies subpackages without an enumerated list
- Removals propagate: a module deleted from source is pruned from ~/.exo/tl_loop rather than lingering
- Installing then running `PYTHONPATH=~/.exo python3 -m tl_loop preflight` from a directory OUTSIDE the exomonad repo succeeds
- Preflight (or install) fails loudly and by name when the resolved interpreter is older than the requires-python floor
- No venv is created for consuming projects; the controller stays stdlib-only at runtime
- A smoke test exercises the INSTALLED artifact the way a consuming project does - outside the repo, bare python3, PYTHONPATH=~/.exo - and fails if a module is missing
- `just install-all` followed by that smoke test is green

comments.content:
DIRECTION CHANGE (operator, 2026-08-14): bundle the Python package INTO the binary rather than
glob-copying it to ~/.exo. This is the stronger fix - it makes install drift IMPOSSIBLE rather than merely
less likely, because the binary and the controller package stop being two artifacts that can disagree.
The bug being fixed is precisely that the binary was current while the Python beside it was three commits
stale.

Prefer: embed the tl_loop tree in the Rust binary (rust-embed or include_dir) and materialize it to a
VERSION-KEYED cache directory on first use, then point PYTHONPATH at that. Precedent in this workspace:
zuihitsu embeds its web console the same way (rust-embed 8, Cargo.toml:29).

Cost is negligible: the package is 804K against a 580M binary.

Alternative worth weighing: python3 -m zipapp produces a single .pyz that `python3 tl_loop.pyz preflight`
runs directly. zipapp is stdlib and works here ONLY because tl_loop has no third-party dependencies. It is
simpler than embedding but keeps a second file on disk, so it does not fully close the drift gap.

WHAT BUNDLING DOES NOT SOLVE: the interpreter itself. Embedding the SOURCE still requires a system python3
>= 3.11 (tl_loop/pyproject.toml requires-python). Only bundling an interpreter (PyOxidizer-class) removes
that, at a large size and fragility cost that is not justified for a stdlib-only package. So the version
floor check in the acceptance criteria REMAINS REQUIRED under either approach - keep it.

Materialization must be version-keyed (e.g. by binary version or content hash), or a stale cache directory
recreates the same drift bug one layer down.

APPROACH DECIDED: zipapp. VERIFIED WORKING 2026-08-14, not speculation.

Experiment run:
    mkdir stage && cp -R tl_loop stage/tl_loop        # keep tl_loop a PACKAGE inside the archive
    rm -rf stage/tl_loop/{.venv,tests,__pycache__}
    printf 'from tl_loop.__main__ import main\nimport sys\nsys.exit(main())\n' > stage/__main__.py
    python3 -m zipapp stage -o tl_loop.pyz -p "/usr/bin/env python3"

Results, all from OUTSIDE the exomonad repo on bare system python3 (3.12.3):
  - 580K single file
  - `python3 tl_loop.pyz preflight --project-root <beast>` -> "TL preflight passed: ..." (correct)
  - `python3 tl_loop.pyz status --project-root <beast>` -> correct missing-checkpoint report
  - walk_packages + import_module over every non-test module from inside the archive: ZERO import failures

Compatibility confirmed: tl_loop has NO __file__, importlib.resources, or pkgutil usage outside tests, and
every runtime file read is project-path-relative (ledger segments, run state) rather than package-relative.
Those are the two things that normally make a package zipapp-hostile; neither applies.

The staging shim matters: `python3 -m zipapp tl_loop` directly would flatten the package to the archive
root and break every `tl_loop.x` import. The archive must contain tl_loop/ as a package plus a top-level
__main__.py shim.

PUSHBACK, recorded honestly - a SIMPLER fix exists for the bug alone:
    rsync -a --delete --exclude .venv --exclude tests --exclude __pycache__ tl_loop/ ~/.exo/tl_loop/
One line, no build step, no invocation change, and --delete prunes removed modules. It fixes the reported
defect completely.

zipapp is still the better choice HERE, for one specific reason: this bug was a PARTIAL-UPDATE bug. A
directory copy can always be interrupted, half-applied, or leave a stale file; a single archive is replaced
atomically or not at all. Given the failure mode we actually hit, atomicity is worth a build step. But if
the build step proves annoying, rsync --delete is a legitimate fallback that closes the same defect.

SCOPE: this is tl_loop packaging only. Do NOT bundle a Python interpreter (PyOxidizer-class) - tl_loop is
stdlib-only and that trade is not justified.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the glob-copy wording above)
- `just install-all` produces a single ~/.exo/tl_loop.pyz built via python3 -m zipapp from a staging tree
- The staging tree excludes .venv, tests, and __pycache__
- init.rs invokes the archive (python3 <pyz> preflight ...) instead of `-m tl_loop` with PYTHONPATH
- Running preflight and status from OUTSIDE the exomonad repo on bare python3 both succeed
- A smoke test walks every non-test module inside the archive and fails if any import breaks
- Any previously installed ~/.exo/tl_loop directory is removed by install so the stale copy cannot shadow the archive
- No Python interpreter is bundled

REVISED DELIVERY (operator, 2026-08-14): EMBED the zipapp in the binary and have the binary write it out.
Do NOT have `just install-all` copy it to ~/.exo.

Operator's objection, and it is correct: the justfile is a DEVELOPER tool. A user who obtains the binary
any other way never runs it, so anything the justfile installs is missing for them.

VERIFIED - this is not hypothetical. try-exomonad/Dockerfile and bootstrap.sh contain ZERO tl_loop or
install-all handling, so Docker users get no controller package at all today. The justfile path is not
merely fragile; it already fails for one shipped install route.

DESIGN:
  1. A build step produces tl_loop.pyz from the staging tree (see the zipapp comment above).
  2. The Rust binary embeds it with include_bytes! - one 580K file, so rust-embed/include_dir is
     unnecessary; a single include_bytes! is enough.
  3. `exomonad init` materializes it into the project (or a version-keyed cache) when absent or stale,
     then points the controller at it.

PRECEDENT ALREADY IN THE CODEBASE - this is not a new pattern:
  - new.rs already carries content as a const and writes it to disk (HARNESS_CAPABILITY_CONTENT).
  - init.rs already uses include_str! (init.rs:2708).
The binary-carries-content-and-writes-it-out shape is established; this extends it to a binary blob.

WHY THIS BEATS BOTH EARLIER OPTIONS:
  - vs rsync/glob to ~/.exo: nothing to install separately, so no install route can skip it. Fixes Docker.
  - vs justfile-built pyz in ~/.exo: the binary and the controller become ONE artifact that cannot disagree,
    which is the exact defect being fixed here (binary current, Python stale).

`exomonad new` vs `exomonad init`: prefer init. `new` is one-time project bootstrap; init runs every
session and is where staleness must be re-checked. Materialization must be version-keyed (binary version or
content hash) so an upgraded binary replaces an old archive instead of silently reusing it.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the ~/.exo wording above)
- A build step produces tl_loop.pyz from a staging tree excluding .venv, tests, and __pycache__
- The binary embeds that archive via include_bytes!
- `exomonad init` writes the archive out when absent or when the embedded version differs, and never reuses a stale one
- init points the controller at the materialized archive; PYTHONPATH=~/.exo is no longer relied upon
- A pre-existing ~/.exo/tl_loop directory cannot shadow the archive
- Preflight and status both succeed from a project OUTSIDE the exomonad repo, with NO `just install-all` having been run against that project
- A smoke test walks every non-test module inside the archive and fails if any import breaks
- No Python interpreter is bundled

PACKAGING ALTERNATIVES EVALUATED (2026-08-14) - PyInstaller, PyOxidizer, python-build-standalone,
multi-executable+installer, Docker/Nix. Decision unchanged: zipapp + include_bytes!.

THE FACT THAT DECIDES IT: tl_loop/pyproject.toml declares `dependencies = []`. The controller is
stdlib-only. Nearly every tool in the general packaging playbook exists to solve DEPENDENCY BUNDLING -
shipping numpy, C extensions, wheels. We have no dependencies, so that entire class of tooling solves a
problem this project does not have.

Second decisive fact: Haskell here is NOT a native binary needing static linking. It compiles to WASM
(.exo/wasm/*.wasm) and is loaded through Extism by the Rust runtime. Generic advice about GHC RTS static
linking, musl, and gmp does not apply.

Rejected, with reasons:

  PyInstaller - inverts the architecture. It makes Python the main program, but Rust is the runtime and the
  controller is called BY Rust. It also bundles a CPython runtime (~25-50MB) to ship 580K of stdlib-only
  code, and --onefile re-extracts to a temp directory on every invocation.

  PyOxidizer - designed to embed an interpreter plus dependencies. We need neither. Before anyone revisits
  this, check its current maintenance status; do not bet the install path on it without that.

  python-build-standalone - ships a full interpreter (~25MB). Legitimate ONLY as a fallback if the runtime
  version floor (#853) proves to be a real field problem. Not now.

  Multi-executable + installer (fpm/makeself/AppImage/WiX) - this is essentially what exists today (binary
  + WASM + tl_loop), and the INSTALLER is precisely the part that broke. Adding packaging machinery for one
  580K file is a large surface for a small payload, and it would still need per-platform work.

  Docker / Nix - both already present (try-exomonad/, flake.nix). Neither fixes the native install path,
  which is what is broken.

WHY ZIPAPP WINS HERE: zipapp is stdlib, needs no new dependency, produces one 580K file, and is VERIFIED
working end to end (preflight and status from outside the repo on bare python3, every module importable
from inside the archive). include_bytes! then makes the binary and the controller a single artifact that
cannot disagree - which is the exact defect being fixed.

The one idea worth keeping from the alternatives is python-build-standalone as a documented escape hatch
for a machine with no viable interpreter. Record it in #853, do not build it.

CORRECTION (2026-08-14): disregard the Docker justification in the earlier comment. ExoMonad should not
rely on Docker, and the argument for embedding does not need it.

The Docker observation was also weaker than stated: try-exomonad's own flow begins with `git clone` +
`just install-all-dev` (README:18), so every install path currently routes through the justfile. There is
no binary-only distribution today.

THE ACTUAL ARGUMENT, which is stronger:

The bug we OBSERVED had nothing to do with Docker or any alternative install route. It happened on a normal
development machine, through the standard `just install-all` path, because justfile:268 enumerates the
files to copy. The binary was current while ~/.exo/tl_loop sat three commits stale, and nothing detected
the divergence.

The root problem is that the controller is HOST-GLOBAL STATE (~/.exo/tl_loop) kept in sync by hand with a
binary that can be rebuilt independently. Two artifacts, two lifetimes, one manual copy list between them.
Embedding collapses that to one artifact, so the two cannot disagree by construction - regardless of how
anyone obtains the binary.

That reasoning holds whether or not Docker is ever supported, and it is the justification of record.

Implemented and committed as 4be7b096e2486f79e9a29bb86cb8f31f0dc92844. Added package-preserving staged zipapp build with top-level shim and archive import smoke test; embedded tl_loop.pyz via include_bytes!, materialized it atomically in init when absent/stale, removed legacy ~/.exo/tl_loop shadow directory, and invoked the archive for preflight/TL windows. Verified cargo test -p exomonad --no-default-features, cargo fmt, git diff --check, and just tl-loop-archive-test. Issue left open pending full acceptance verification.

Verified for closure. Checks completed: just tl-loop-archive-test passed, including the archive import smoke walk over every non-test module; cargo test -p exomonad --no-default-features passed (34 + 82 + 8 + 1 tests); the Rust tests cover embedded archive materialization and stale-version handling. just install-all produced a non-empty ~/.exo/tl_loop.pyz, and the pre-existing ~/.exo/tl_loop shadow directory was absent afterward. From /tmp with PYTHONPATH=, python3 ~/.exo/tl_loop.pyz preflight --project-root /home/goya/beast-workspace/workspace passed, and status produced the expected missing-checkpoint report. The Rust implementation invokes the materialized archive for preflight/TL windows. issues.title: E18 :: E18.8 Preflight example is empty and duplicates the Rust template
issues.description:
The capability template exists TWICE and the Python copy is empty, so preflight's remediation
advice does not work.

  rust/exomonad/src/new.rs  HARNESS_CAPABILITY_CONTENT  -> [capabilities] WITH codex/gpt-luna and claude/sonnet
  tl_loop/select/capability.py  DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_CONTENT -> '# ...\n\n[capabilities]\n'  (EMPTY)

    missing required TL file(s): .../.exo/harness_capability.toml
    Example harness_capability.toml:
    # Static capability ratings. Each entry records the operator's basis.
    [capabilities]

then hands over something that does not fix it.

E18.6 (#848) required the default be defined ONCE and shared with new.rs. It is shared on the Rust side;
Python received a second, hollow copy. That is the duplication the task was meant to prevent.

BETTER FIX than syncing the two constants: preflight already parses harness_policy.toml, so it knows the
exact allowlist. Generate the example pre-populated with every allowed harness/model entry plus a
"standard" placeholder and a basis comment. That is directly usable and correct PER PROJECT, rather than a
generic default that is wrong for any project whose allowlist differs.

Real evidence: /home/goya/beast-workspace/workspace allows codex/gpt-5.6-luna, codex/gpt-5.6-sol,
opencode/deepseek-v4-flash, and opencode/deepseek-v4-pro. NEITHER template covers any of them, so both the
empty Python example and the Rust default fail that project's coverage check.

## Acceptance Criteria
- There is exactly one capability template definition; Python does not carry a second copy
- preflight's example is populated, not a bare [capabilities] header
- The example is derived from the project's own harness_policy.toml allowlist and lists every allowed entry

issues.title: E20 :: E20.5 Persist and surface the controller exit reason
issues.description:
A TL window dies with its process, so a startup failure leaves no trace and `tl_loop status` reports only a missing checkpoint. That is what made this capability bug invisible.

Persist the controller's exit reason somewhere status can read it - e.g. .exo/tl-loop/<run_id>/last-exit.json with timestamp, exit kind, and a bounded message - and have status --watch render it when no run.json exists.

This is diagnostics only: it must not become a second source of run state, and it must never influence a merge decision or an FSM transition.
EVIDENCE (reproduced 2026-08-14 against /home/goya/beast-workspace/workspace):
  PolicyMissing: .exo/harness_capability.toml: capability file is missing

tl_run calls load_capability() immediately after load_policy(), BEFORE run_tl_loop reaches create(). So the controller dies at startup and no run.json is ever written. `tl_loop status` then reports a missing checkpoint, which hides the real cause.

Root defect: .exo/harness_capability.toml is a FOURTH required file with no upgrade path.
  - new.rs:198 creates it, but only `if !capability_path.exists()` - fresh projects only
  - init.rs has ZERO references to it - no check, no backfill
  - undocumented: zero mentions in README.md, CLAUDE.md, or docs/guides/programming-the-tl.md
Any project migrated rather than `new`-ed hits this.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A controller that dies before create() leaves a durable, readable exit reason
- status --watch renders 'controller exited: <reason>' instead of a bare missing-checkpoint error
- The record is diagnostics only, never read back as run state
- A test forces a startup failure and asserts status surfaces the cause

issues.title: E17: Controller denominator rules and coverage refresh
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Four new rules in expected-events.v1.json so a missing controller event is DETECTABLE rather than indistinguishable from a quiet run, plus a refresh of the stale coverage audit.

tl-loop-event-coverage.md is dated 2026-08-11 and predates M9, M11, and M12. It cites worktree_event_watcher.rs line numbers for merge_ready semantics that E4 removed.

HARD BOUNDARIES:
- tl_loop must NOT gain a ledger writer. Python decides; Rust writes. There stays exactly ONE ledger writer.
- Do NOT reuse log.emit_event (handlers/log.rs:128). The registry dynamic_event_rule confines dynamic types to
  the custom. namespace at local_sensitive, which EXCLUDES them from L4 aggregate export - exactly where this
  signal must land. Declared types with aggregate_dimensions are required.
- Bodies stay local. Identities and bounded dimensions only: no utterances, diffs, repair prose, or plan docs.
- Emission is best-effort and never load-bearing. A failed emit is logged; the run continues. Observability
  must never stall a run or alter a merge decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Four rules added following the existing eleven in style and correlation fields
- gate_opened_requires_answer has no delay bound, making human-gate latency a measurable number
- Coverage audit re-dated and re-verified against the watcher-as-sensor boundary; no removed line numbers cited
- Coverage extended to the controller and guidance-queue surfaces
- agent.stop_check, [DEV FAILED], and [RATE LIMITED] each either gain a producer or are removed
- just validate-observability-contracts passes

issues.title: E15: Verb-first topic vocabulary as an addressing layer
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Adopt lanius's grammar {verb}/{category}/{noun}/{locators} as the naming scheme for guidance and observation.

  in/     addressed, at-least-once, durable  -> rides the M11 guidance queue (enqueue_batch)
  obs/    telemetry, droppable               -> a VIEW over the existing ledger event vocabulary
  signal/ algedonic, never coalesced         -> park causes and human gates

ANTI-PATTERNS - both are hard failures:
1. Do NOT rename or replace the ledger event registry. pr.filed, ci.status_changed, agent.stuck and the rest keep their identities. obs/ topics are a VIEW over them, not a second vocabulary.
2. Do NOT introduce a transport. in/ resolves to the M11 queue's existing operations. A topic names a destination; it is not a new way to reach one. No broker, no MQTT listener - see the scoping section of docs/decisions/operator-control-plane.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Delivery contract is decidable from segment one
- in/agent/<agent_id>/{steering,follow_up} resolves to M11 enqueue_batch with the matching queue class
- Every obs/ topic maps to an existing registry event; no new event identity is minted
- No transport, listener, or broker is added
- Topic names percent-encode MQTT wildcard characters so a future listener stays possible
- just validate-observability-contracts passes

issues.title: E14: interpret_operator_intent as a fourth RLM judgment
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Operator prose -> structured intent, alongside decompose, adjudicate_review, and compose_repair.

  interpret_operator_intent(utterance, read_model) -> Query | GateAnswer | PlanProposal | Unclear

Same contract as the existing three: closed output schema, explicit context budget, bounded attempts, token charge, replay record, tools=(), no effect client, no filesystem capability.

The model TRANSLATES; it does not DECIDE. Every intent still passes the same validation and authority checks as if typed as a CLI argument. Unclear is a first-class outcome - the model asks rather than guessing, because a misread instruction moves real work.

AUTHORITY RULE (non-negotiable): the console may ONLY read projections, answer NAMED gates, and propose plan mutations that are inert until confirmed. It may never merge a PR, approve a review, set a verdict, alter the FSM phase, widen harness_policy.toml, or raise a budget ceiling. A free-form message never carries workflow authority.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Closed output schema; invalid responses retry at most three attempts then raise JudgmentFailed
- Unclear is returned rather than a guessed intent when the utterance is ambiguous
- Every attempt records model, input hash, token counts, latency, attempt number, replay flag, redacted result
- A produced intent has no more authority than the same intent typed as a CLI argument
- Agent-authored text in the read model is never rendered as operator instruction (injection boundary)
- Hermetic replay tests avoid network access

comments.content: All E14 subissues #806-#810 are closed. Operator intent has a closed schema, tool-free RLM boundary, shared CLI validation, provenance/injection protection, and hermetic replay fixtures.

issues.title: E13: Read model and /control surface on the existing UDS
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

The console is a CLIENT of tl_loop, never a peer. tl_loop remains the single writer of run state.

Zuihitsu's rule: transport and authority are orthogonal; co-location is never an authority escalation. Clients deliver and receive; the server owns scheduling, time, and memory.

No new listener, no broker, no second event log. Reuse the ExoMonad UDS and tl_loop/client/transport.py.

AUTHORITY RULE (non-negotiable): the console may ONLY read projections, answer NAMED gates, and propose plan mutations that are inert until confirmed. It may never merge a PR, approve a review, set a verdict, alter the FSM phase, widen harness_policy.toml, or raise a budget ceiling. A free-form message never carries workflow authority.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The console cannot write run.json; every mutation goes through tl_loop
- Read model carries the ledger cursor it was built from, so staleness is visible
- /control auth is a separate concern from agent/effect routes; a control credential never authorises an agent route
- Read model answers: current phase, per-slice status, per-head review/CI evidence, budgets, gates, park causes, recent transitions
- No second event log is created
- just rust-test and tl_loop tests pass

issues.title: E12: Retire the in-memory FIFO as delivery authority
issues.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

P6. AgentInbox (agent_inbox.rs, 596 lines) is an in-memory VecDeque with a 32-message cap and a 30-second dedup window, all lost on restart. Rebuild it from durable pending/expired rows, then remove it as an AUTHORITY - it may remain only as a transport worker cache reconstructible from durable state.

GATE: remove authority ONLY after restart, lease, duplicate, retry, and abandonment gates pass for ALL supported runtimes.

- AgentInbox is rebuilt from durable pending/expired rows on restart
- Its in-memory dedup window no longer determines durable identity

- No queue or delivery acknowledgement carries merge, review, or PR authority
- just test passes

issues.title: E11: Observability contract for the guidance queue
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

P5. Extend the EXISTING event vocabulary by payload fields. Do NOT create a second message authority.

Events: inbox.state_changed (enqueue, claim, lease expiry, acknowledgement, cancellation, abandonment), message.delivery (each transport attempt), message.consumed (positive acceptance + ack_kind/confidence), agent.guidance.delivery, agent_inbox.messages_abandoned.

Bodies stay local-sensitive. Ledger carries identities and bounded dimensions only: batch_id, item_id, agent_id, queue_class, queue_seq, run_id, session_id, invocation_id, generation, runtime, harness, role, attempt, consumer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Event registry, expected-events.v1.json, and fixtures updated in the same change
- Ledger replay produces the same pending/accepted/terminal projection as SQLite state
- No message body is copied into aggregate ledger projections
- A durable enqueue expects eventual acceptance or explicit abandonment; a transport success without either stays pending/unknown

issues.title: E10: Runtime adapters with boundary and acceptance evidence
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

P4. One adapter at a time, strongest evidence first: Claude Code, then Codex, then OpenCode. Each reports a boundary phase (turn_finished / would_stop) and supplies acceptance evidence carrying batch_id, item_id, queue_class, and invocation generation where the runtime can echo them.

Keep legacy delivery in SHADOW MODE until queue and ledger projections agree.

ExoMonad does NOT take over any runtime's active model loop - that is the ADR decision, not a gap.

HONEST LIMIT: the strongest available evidence on every current runtime may still fall short of proving the model accepted the message into its next context. An adapter must NEVER upgrade transport success to runtime_accepted. An unproven batch stays pending/unknown and visible. Ambiguity made observable is the goal, not a fabricated 100% delivery rate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each adapter reports a boundary phase before any claim
- No adapter infers a turn boundary from pane liveness, empty input buffer, or a successful write
- An adapter that cannot echo batch identity records confidence as inferred or unknown and does not upgrade it
- A runtime with no safe boundary retains the batch and surfaces pending rather than streaming tmux input
- Legacy delivery runs in shadow until projections agree
- just test passes

issues.title: E9: Separate transport evidence from runtime consumption
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

P3. CORRECTNESS FIX. InboxStore::drain_unread currently marks rows read and emits message.consumed BEFORE any runtime has proved it accepted a new turn. Today's consumption metrics are therefore overstated.

Split acknowledgement: ack_kind='inbox_read' (legacy, weak) vs ack_kind='runtime_accepted' (adapter-proven), each carrying a confidence. A Teams file timestamp, UDS 2xx, tmux injection success, or hook exit-zero is TRANSPORT evidence only.

HONEST LIMIT: the strongest available evidence on every current runtime may still fall short of proving the model accepted the message into its next context. An adapter must NEVER upgrade transport success to runtime_accepted. An unproven batch stays pending/unknown and visible. Ambiguity made observable is the goal, not a fabricated 100% delivery rate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Transport success alone NEVER emits message.consumed with ack_kind=runtime_accepted
- Every message.consumed carries ack_kind and confidence
- Legacy inbox reads are recorded as ack_kind=inbox_read
- A batch with no acceptance evidence remains pending/unknown and is visible, not silently consumed
- just rust-test passes

issues.title: E8: Route guidance producers through enqueue_batch
issues.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

P2. Steering and follow-up producers commit a durable batch before transport begins. The existing messages row is retained as a compatibility pointer via source_message_id. The two stores must never independently be treated as proof of consumption.

Replaces the 30-second body-hash dedup window with identity-based idempotency. Free-form messages get a UUID and stay distinct even when bodies match; structured events supply a stable idempotency key.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every steering/follow-up producer enqueues durably before transport
- source_message_id links a guidance batch to its compatibility inbox row
- Idempotent enqueue: the same idempotency key does not create a second batch
- Two identical free-form message bodies remain two distinct batches
- queue_seq is retained across retry, cancellation, and abandonment so replay ordering stays explainable
- just rust-test passes

issues.title: E7: Durable guidance queue schema and transactional API
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

P1. Add guidance_batches and guidance_items to .exo/inbox.db plus all seven queue operations, WITHOUT changing legacy InboxStore::drain_unread behavior. Pure addition; nothing routes through it yet.

Ops: enqueue_batch, claim_next, record_transport_attempt, acknowledge_runtime, release_for_retry, cancel_batch, recover_expired_leases.

States: pending, leased, submitted, accepted, abandoned, cancelled. All transitions are compare-and-set inside SQLite transactions. At most ONE active lease per agent across both queue classes.

Existing: .exo/inbox.db has only messages + agent_inbox_meta. inbox_store.rs is 955 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Atomic enqueue with contiguous batch item ordering from zero
- Concurrent claims for one agent never lease two batches
- Independent agents progress concurrently
- Unique (agent_id, queue_seq); terminal batches are never re-claimed
- recover_expired_leases returns expired leased/submitted rows to pending with bounded backoff
- Legacy drain_unread behavior is unchanged
- just rust-test passes

issues.title: E6: Evaluate owning the agent loop for durable TL->agent steering
issues.description:
Question: 

Context: 

Findings: 

prime-agent's steering works because prime-agent OWNS the agent loop: runLoop (packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts:317-344) polls getSteeringMessages and pushes straight into currentContext.messages before the next assistant response, with a second getFollowUpMessages channel drained when the agent would otherwise stop (agent.ts:185, PendingMessageQueue, one-at-a-time).

ExoMonad does not own the loop - Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode do. Our only injection points are the Teams inbox, HTTP-over-UDS, and tmux paste-buffer. That is the root cause of the messaging flakiness, and no amount of transport hardening fixes it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Failure modes of the three current transports documented with ledger evidence, not assertion
- Recommendation states explicitly whether ExoMonad should own the agent loop, per harness
- Any proposed mechanism works across Claude, Codex, and OpenCode - no single-harness fix
- An ADR lands in docs/decisions/
- Authoritative workflow state stays on the ledger regardless of outcome; the steering channel never carries merge authority

issues.title: Watcher: skip legacy inbox/tmux delivery for ledger-owned (tl_loop) worktrees
issues.description:
ANTI-PATTERNS (FIRST)
- Do not implement anything outside the STEPS below; scope creep across milestone boundaries is a review failure.
- Do not add a second code path that duplicates an existing one; ExoMonad forbids redundant paths.
- Do not add undocumented heuristics or silent fallbacks; prefer explicit failure.
- Do not ship without the tests named in VERIFY; an untested feature is not done.
- Do not touch the ledger-write side (`event_log()` calls, #709-#712). That plumbing is correct and already what `tl_loop`'s `LedgerQueue`/`reader.py` consumes. This issue is about the separate action-execution side (`handle_event_action`) that still unconditionally tries interactive delivery.
- Do not add a new `AgentType` variant that changes spawning/CLI-selection behavior. This is a delivery-routing concern, not a new kind of spawned process.
- Do not silently no-op delivery for loop-owned worktrees without logging why; a swallowed `DeliveryResult::Failed` is exactly the silent-failure pattern CLAUDE.md § Logging forbids.

CONTEXT
`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs::handle_event_action` (~line 2703) executes every `EventActionResponse::InjectMessage` / `NotifyParent` by calling `delivery::deliver_to_agent` or `delivery::notify_parent_delivery` — both write to the durable inbox store and fall back to tmux STDIN injection. That whole path assumes the recipient is an interactive Claude Code session with a registered session UUID (`ClaudeSessionRegistry`) and a live tmux pane.

A `tl_loop`-owned worktree (M5.1 onward, and every sub-TL under M7) has neither. It reads the canonical ledger directly via `LedgerQueue`/`reader.py` — the events it needs are already landing there correctly (#709-#712 fixed that). But the watcher has no way to know this and keeps firing `handle_event_action` anyway for every review/CI/merge event on that worktree: writing dead inbox entries nothing will ever poll, and attempting `resolve_tab_name_for_agent`/tab-name resolution against a branch with no tmux window.

`AgentType` (`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/mod.rs:247`) has five variants — Claude, Shoal, OpenCode, Codex, Process — and none represent "owner reads the ledger, has no pane, do not attempt interactive delivery." This is a real gap, not yet hit in practice because #713 has only been exercised against synthetic event streams (`just tl-loop-test`); it will bite for real at M5.6 (#694), the first live run against the actual watcher, and applies with equal force to every M7 sub-TL worktree.

READ FIRST
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs (`handle_event_action`, ~line 2703; the `EventActionResponse` dispatch above it, ~line 522)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/delivery.rs (`deliver_to_agent` ~line 1347, `notify_parent_delivery` ~line 757)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/mod.rs (`AgentType` enum, line 247)
- tl_loop/CLAUDE.md § "Ledger-backed event projection"
- #700's CONTEXT section (updated 2026-08-11) — same single-hop `parent_agent_id` / ledger-is-authoritative framing this issue extends into the delivery layer

STEPS
1. Add a way to mark a worktree/branch as ledger-owned at spawn/registration time (e.g. a field on the existing worktree/agent registry record, not a new registry). This is what a `tl_run` invocation sets when it claims a worktree (M5.1/M7.1's worktree-exclusivity check is the natural place to also record this).
2. In `handle_event_action`, before calling `deliver_to_agent`/`notify_parent_delivery`, check whether `branch` is ledger-owned. If so, skip interactive delivery entirely and return early — log at info level that delivery was skipped because the owner is ledger-only, with the branch and event kind. Do not attempt tab-name resolution or inbox writes for that branch.
3. This is a pure skip, not a substitute write: the ledger already has the event via the existing `event_log()` call sites earlier in the same watcher cycle. Do not add a second ledger write here.
4. Test: for a ledger-owned branch, `handle_event_action` returns without calling `deliver_to_agent`/`notify_parent_delivery` (mock/spy the delivery functions) and logs the skip; for a normal Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Shoal/Process branch, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

VERIFY
- `just test` (rust/exomonad-core watcher unit tests)
- `just tl-loop-test` (confirms tl_loop's own consumption path is untouched)

DONE CRITERIA
- A ledger-owned worktree never receives a tmux/inbox delivery attempt from the watcher; a non-ledger-owned worktree's delivery behavior is unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- No inbox entries are written for ledger-owned branches.
- Existing watcher delivery tests (InjectMessage/NotifyParent fallback tests, e.g. `test_no_plugin_dispatch_uses_native_fallback_for_sub_tl`) still pass unchanged for non-ledger-owned branches.

issues.title: Add a bounded TL loop for workers and dev leaves
issues.description:
ANTI-PATTERNS (FIRST)

- Do not implement fork_wave, spawn_leaf_subtree, recursive sub-TLs, or a second TL owner in this deliverable.
- Do not add the M4 selector/catalog/policy/budget chain here; #682-#688 remain deferred prerequisites for the later selector-integrated loop.
- Do not scrape tmux panes, worktrees, or agent state; use the event queue and run-state checkpoint as authorities.

READ FIRST

STEPS

1. Implement one active TL loop body in tl_loop/loop/driver.py that runs a bounded single wave.
2. Have the TL invoke direct spawn_worker calls for bounded worker tasks and direct spawn_leaf calls for implementation/dev-leaf tasks. Do not invoke fork_wave or create a sub-TL.
3. Consume lifecycle events from the existing event queue, transition the shared FSM, and checkpoint run state plus event offset after every handled event.
4. Reuse the M3 shadow loop structure and deterministic judgment seams; active mode supplies a mutating effect capability, while shadow mode supplies the read-only capability.
5. Wait for all direct workers/dev-leaves, adjudicate their results, and merge successful dev-leaf PRs through the existing typed effect client. Keep the loop alive until a terminal phase.
6. Log effect calls and FSM transitions using the existing logging conventions.

VERIFY

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- The later selector-integrated M5.1 task can wrap this loop without replacing it.

issues.title: M7.1 Recursive sub-TL loops with the one-agent-one-branch invariant
issues.description:
ANTI-PATTERNS (FIRST)
- Do not implement anything outside the STEPS below; scope creep across milestone boundaries is a review failure.
- Do not add a second code path that duplicates an existing one; ExoMonad forbids redundant paths.
- Do not add undocumented heuristics or silent fallbacks; prefer explicit failure.
- Do not ship without the tests named in VERIFY; an untested feature is not done.
- A sub-TL loop owns exactly one worktree and one branch. Two loop instances sharing a worktree is a correctness failure.
- Do not let a sub-TL see its siblings' slices or run state. Compression boundaries are the point.
- Do not recurse without a depth ceiling.
- Do not call the `fork_wave` MCP tool/effect, and do not expect Claude-Code session semantics (`--fork-session` context inheritance, Teams inbox registration, a tmux window) anywhere in this recursion. A sub-TL here is another `tl_run` instance in this process or a subprocess of it, not a spawned Claude Code session. Reuse only the worktree-creation + `{parent}.{name}` branch-derivation primitive that `fork_wave`/`spawn_leaf` already call in Rust.
- Do not have the sub-TL spawn reviewers directly. Reviewers are triggered automatically by `file_pr` via the existing review-policy watcher, exactly as for a flat dev-leaf. The sub-TL only waits on ledger events for the children it directly spawned.

CONTEXT
- A "sub-TL" is not a new agent context window. It is a recursive call to `tl_run` (the M5.1 driver), whose decompose/adjudicate/repair judgment comes from the bounded `rlm()` primitive (M6.1, #695), not free-running agentic reasoning. This is a real dependency: recursion has nothing to call at each level without `decompose()` (M6.3, #697), `adjudicate_review()` (M6.4, #698), and `compose_repair()` (M6.5, #699) already existing.
- The worktree event watcher is not eliminated by this milestone and is out of scope to touch. It keeps polling PR/CI/review state in Rust and appending canonical envelopes to the immutable ledger. All this milestone changes is that a sub-TL's `LedgerQueue`/`reader.py` tails only its own run_id-scoped segment of that ledger, instead of the watcher injecting text into a tmux pane or Teams inbox for an LLM to parse.
- Message/event scoping is not new infrastructure to invent — it is the existing single-hop `parent_agent_id` pattern, applied one level deeper. Today, `notify_parent` (rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/events.rs) already resolves exactly one direct parent via structural birth-branch identity (never a tree-wide broadcast), and the canonical ledger event schema (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/analysis_import.rs) already carries `agent_id` and `parent_agent_id` per event. For this milestone: every leaf/worker a sub-TL spawns is registered with `parent_agent_id` = the sub-TL's own agent_id, not the root's — so a reviewer-comment event on a grandchild's PR is only ever visible to the sub-TL that owns it. The root observes a new event only when the sub-TL itself emits one upward (files its own PR, or reaches a terminal state).

READ FIRST
- CLAUDE.md § "Depth over Breadth" and § "Branch Naming as Coordinate System"
- tl_loop/loop/driver.py (M5.1)
- tl_loop/state/store.py (M2.3 — run-state path layout)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/events.rs (`notify_parent` — the single-hop parent-resolution pattern to extend, not replace)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/analysis_import.rs (canonical ledger event schema — `agent_id`/`parent_agent_id` columns already exist)
- tl_loop/events/reader.py, tl_loop/events/envelope.py (M2 — the ledger projection a sub-TL's queue tails)

STEPS
1. Make `tl_run` recursive: a slice classified as a sub-TL spawns a child loop instance — another `tl_run` invocation, not a Claude Code session — rather than a leaf. Reuse the worktree-creation + `{parent}.{name}` branch-derivation effect that `fork_wave`/`spawn_leaf` call in Rust; do not call the `fork_wave` MCP tool itself.
2. Give each sub-TL its own run-state document and event log under `.exo/tl-loop/<run_id>/<sub_tl_id>/`; the parent sees only the child's terminal result.
3. Enforce the invariant structurally: run state records the owning worktree and branch, and `create` refuses if another live run state claims the same worktree.
4. Derive the child's branch name from the parent's via the `{parent}.{name}` convention; the child files its PR against the parent branch.
5. Add a configurable depth ceiling; exceeding it parks with cause `schedule_deadlock` (or a new closed cause) rather than recursing.
6. Test: a two-level tree completes; two loops cannot claim one worktree; child PRs target the parent branch; the depth ceiling holds; a grandchild's review event never reaches the root's event queue.

VERIFY
- `just tl-loop-test`
- `just tl-loop-typecheck`

ADR DECISION (resolved 2026-08-10 — do not re-open)
This task's Step 1 previously asked which ingest mechanism to use. It is now answered from
source inspection; the worker writes the ADR up but does not re-decide.

CHOSEN: the Python bridge tails the server's EXISTING on-disk append-only ledger by `run_seq`.

  a canonical append-only L1 ledger via `LedgerWriter`, and a per-agent compatibility JSONL view
  at `<event_dir>/{agent_id}.jsonl`. It fsyncs (`sync_data`), serializes with a process mutex plus
  `nix` flock advisory locks, and allocates `run_seq` from a `run_seq` file written via
  temp-file + atomic rename.
- `ledger_paths()` resolves segments to `.exo/ledger/segments` when the event dir is under `.exo`.

  invocation_id, generation, provider, runtime, harness, role, source, lifecycle_state, data.
  `LedgerWriter` exposes `read_events()` and `read_resolved_events()`; segments are immutable and
  returned in lexical sequence order; `sequence_status()` reports contiguous vs partial;
  `resolve_superseded_events()` handles supersession.

  `HasEventLog` / `HasEventQueue` traits, so PR/CI/review events reach the ledger today.

calls today; adding a push stream is new I/O surface for no gain when the events are already
durably on disk with a monotonic sequence.

issues.title: M2.5 Python reader and in-process queue over the existing ledger segments
issues.description:
ANTI-PATTERNS (FIRST)
- Do not implement anything outside the STEPS below; scope creep across milestone boundaries is a review failure.
- Do not add a second code path that duplicates an existing one; ExoMonad forbids redundant paths.
- Do not add undocumented heuristics or silent fallbacks; prefer explicit failure.
- Do not ship without the tests named in VERIFY; an untested feature is not done.
- Do NOT re-implement gap detection, supersession or segment ordering. `immutable_ledger.rs`
  already defines all three; reuse its semantics or you create a second, divergent notion of a gap.
- Do NOT invent a `run_seq` for an event that has none. immutable_ledger.rs:94 is explicit:
  consumers do not invent run_seq values.
- Do not busy-wait. The queue blocks; poll intervals are explicit and configurable, never a spin.
- Do not drop unacknowledged events. Acknowledgement is the persisted `run_seq` cursor in run
  state, nothing else.
- Do NOT write to `.exo/ledger/segments/`. The reader is strictly read-only.

READ FIRST
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/immutable_ledger.rs (`read_events`, `read_resolved_events`,
  `sequence_status` — contiguous vs partial, `resolve_superseded_events`; segments are immutable
  and returned in lexical order)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/ledger_retention.rs (segment lifecycle and dropping —
  the reader must tolerate a segment being retired beneath it)
- tl_loop/events/envelope.py (M2.4 projection)
- tl_loop/state/store.py (M2.3 — where the cursor is persisted)

STEPS
1. Implement `tl_loop/events/reader.py` reading `.exo/ledger/segments/` directly: enumerate
   segments in lexical order, parse records, and project each through the M2.4 envelope.
2. Resume by GLOBAL `run_seq`, spanning segment boundaries. The cursor is a `run_seq`, never a
   per-file byte offset — a retired or rotated segment must not corrupt resumption.
3. run_seq = None policy: the ordered queue consumes ONLY events with `Some(run_seq)`. Do not
   invent one. If an event kind the loop requires arrives with `run_seq = None`, that is a
   server-side emit gap: log it and record it as a hard finding for M2.7 (#677). Never silently
   drop it, and never assign a sequence to it.
4. Reuse `sequence_status()` semantics for gap detection (contiguous vs partial) rather than
   defining a second notion of a gap. A partial sequence surfaces to the loop as a typed condition.
5. Apply `resolve_superseded_events()` semantics so a superseded event never drives a transition.
6. Implement `tl_loop/events/queue.py`: a bounded in-process queue fed by a reader thread tailing
   the segments, exposing blocking `get(timeout)`.
7. Persist the consumed `run_seq` cursor into run state through the M2.2 single write path; restart
   resumes from `cursor + 1`. Handling is idempotent by `run_seq` (at-least-once); document that
   requirement in tl_loop/CLAUDE.md.

VERIFY
- `just tl-loop-test` covering: replay from an arbitrary run_seq yields the exact suffix; resume
  across a segment boundary; a retired segment mid-tail does not corrupt the cursor; a partial
  sequence surfaces via sequence_status semantics; a `run_seq = None` event is recorded as a
  finding rather than consumed or dropped; kill-and-restart re-delivers only unacknowledged events.
- `just tl-loop-typecheck`

DONE CRITERIA
- The loop consumes the existing ledger by global run_seq, checkpoints its cursor, restarts and
  continues without loss beyond documented at-least-once semantics.
- Zero new storage was introduced.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The reader opens nothing under `.exo/ledger/` for writing.
- Gap and supersession semantics match `immutable_ledger.rs`; a divergent second definition fails
  review.
- The queue never spins; CPU is idle while waiting.

issues.title: M2.4 Define the TL event envelope as a projection over the existing immutable ledger
issues.description:
ANTI-PATTERNS (FIRST)
- Do not implement anything outside the STEPS below; scope creep across milestone boundaries is a review failure.
- Do not add a second code path that duplicates an existing one; ExoMonad forbids redundant paths.
- Do not add undocumented heuristics or silent fallbacks; prefer explicit failure.
- Do not ship without the tests named in VERIFY; an untested feature is not done.
- Do NOT create `.exo/tl-loop/<run_id>/events.log` or any other new durable event log. One already
  exists at `.exo/ledger/segments/`; building a second is exactly the redundant path
  CLAUDE.md § Single Code Path forbids. This task was rescoped for that reason.
- Do NOT write to `.exo/ledger/segments/`. See the WRITE-BOUNDARY RULE below.
- Do NOT invent new ledger `event_type` values. Map onto the values already in
  `SAFE_CATEGORICAL_VALUES`.
- Do not introduce a message broker. Single-host, file-backed; MQTT/NATS remain out of scope.

WRITE-BOUNDARY RULE (epic-wide, non-negotiable)
The TL loop treats `.exo/ledger/segments/` as READ-ONLY.
- The loop's own control state — decompose plans, verdicts (GO / GO-WITH-NITS / NO-GO), budget
  charges, harness and model selections, checkpoints, gate approvals — goes to the TL run-state
  under `.exo/tl-loop/<run_id>/` (M2.1-M2.3). It never enters the ledger.
- Reason: those event_type values are not in `SAFE_CATEGORICAL_VALUES`
  (scripts/compile_failure_atlas.py:37), so writing them would land as `custom` or distort the
  Failure Atlas aggregates. The ledger's `data` payloads are also meant to stay local and coarse.
- Reading is safe and cannot confound the atlas: every event_type the loop consumes
  (pr.filed, pr.merged, pr.updated, copilot.review, ci.status_changed, agent.completed,
  agent.notify_parent, agent.sibling_merged) is already allowlisted, and reading writes nothing.
- EXCEPTION: a TL control event may be emitted through `LedgerWriter` only after its event_type is
  added to `SAFE_CATEGORICAL_VALUES` deliberately, in its own reviewed change. Never as an ad-hoc
  `custom` leak.

READ FIRST
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/immutable_ledger.rs (`LedgerEvent` at :25, its 19 fields;
  `run_seq: Option<u64>` at :32; the "not invent run_seq values" note at :94; `LedgerWriter`,
  `read_events`, `read_resolved_events`, `sequence_status`, `resolve_superseded_events`)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/event_log.rs (`EventLog::append` — the dual write: canonical L1
  ledger plus the per-agent compatibility JSONL view)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/ledger_retention.rs:33 (`.exo/ledger/segments` path resolution)
- scripts/compile_failure_atlas.py (`ALLOWLIST_COLUMNS` at :24, `SAFE_CATEGORICAL_VALUES` at :37)
- docs/observability/event-registry.json and docs/observability/expected-events.v1.json

STEPS
1. Implement `tl_loop/events/envelope.py` as a typed PROJECTION of `LedgerEvent`, not a new record
   type. Carry: `run_seq`, `event_type`, `run_id`, `agent_id`, `session_id`, `invocation_id`,
   `generation`, `harness`, `role`, `lifecycle_state`, `observed_at`, plus the review fields the
   loop needs (PR number, head SHA, review state, CI status) extracted from `data`.
2. Define the loop's closed `kind` set as a mapping ONTO existing allowlisted `event_type` values.
   At minimum: pr.filed, pr.updated, pr.published, pr.merged, pr.merge_failed, copilot.review,
   ci.status_changed, agent.completed, agent.stuck, agent.notify_parent, agent.sibling_merged.

3. Preserve `reviewed_head` on every review-related projection; it is load-bearing for M5.4.

4. Validate the projection: an envelope whose `event_type` is outside the mapped set is rejected at

5. Document in tl_loop/CLAUDE.md that the ledger is the storage layer and the envelope is a read

  projects with no field loss; an unmapped event_type is rejected.
- `just tl-loop-typecheck`
- `just validate-observability-contracts` still passes (no registry change should be needed).

- The TL envelope exists as a projection over `LedgerEvent` with a closed kind set mapped onto

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

issues.description:

- Do not implement anything outside the STEPS below; scope creep across milestone boundaries is a review failure.
- Do not add a second code path that duplicates an existing one; ExoMonad forbids redundant paths.
- Do not add undocumented heuristics or silent fallbacks; prefer explicit failure.
- Do not ship without the tests named in VERIFY; an untested feature is not done.
- There must be exactly ONE function in the codebase that writes run state. Any second write path is a review failure.
- Do not write in place. Every write is: temp file -> fsync -> atomic rename.
- Do not skip the post-apply validation; writing an invalid document is worse than failing.

READ FIRST
- /home/goya/agent-workspace/opencode-feature-factory/packages/feature-factory/core/atomic-write.js
- /home/goya/agent-workspace/opencode-feature-factory/packages/feature-factory/core/write-core.js
- /home/goya/agent-workspace/opencode-feature-factory/packages/feature-factory/core/run-lock.js
- /home/goya/agent-workspace/opencode-feature-factory/packages/feature-factory/state/session-lock.js

STEPS
1. Implement `tl_loop/state/lock.py`: an advisory file lock over `.exo/tl-loop/run.lock` with an explicit acquisition timeout and stale-lock detection (pid liveness).
2. Implement `tl_loop/state/write.py::apply(mutator)` following the full discipline in order: acquire lock -> read current -> validate -> apply mutator -> validate result -> compare-and-swap against the observed version/mtime -> re-observe from disk -> confirm CAS -> fsync temp -> atomic rename -> release lock.
3. Bump a monotonic `revision` field on every successful write; CAS is on `revision`.
4. Raise `ConcurrentWrite` if the revision changed under us; the caller retries the mutator, never the write.
5. Make `apply` the only public write entry point; the module exports no raw file-writing helper.
6. Test: concurrent writers from two processes never interleave or lose an update; a crash between temp write and rename leaves the previous document intact; an invalid mutator result aborts without touching the file on disk.

issues.title: EPIC: Replace the interactive TL with a programmatic orchestration loop
issues.description:
EPIC — TL-as-loop

GOAL
Invert control at the tech-lead layer. Today the TL is an interactive LLM chat session whose
"loop" is emergent: a narrative prompt (.exo/roles/devswarm/context/tl.md), a phase FSM whose
transitions fire as side effects of tool calls (.exo/roles/devswarm/TLPhase.hs, TLRole.hs), and
stop hooks that coax the model into not ending its turn (.exo/roles/devswarm/TLStopCheck.hs).
That coordination logic cannot be unit-tested, replayed, rate-limited or composed, and it burns
Opus tokens on control flow.

After this epic the loop is code — a Python controller that owns the FSM explicitly — and the
LLM is a set of three bounded, structured function calls used only where judgment is required:
decompose(), adjudicate_review(), compose_repair().

WHAT STAYS
All Rust effects (git, Forgejo/GitHub PRs, tmux, worktrees, watchers), the review loop, Chainlink
issues, file_pr / merge_pr / resume_pr / dispose_leaf semantics, worker and reviewer roles, and
worktree isolation. Nothing about ExoMonad's I/O layer changes.

WHAT CHANGES
The TL RoleConfig stops being the coordinator. Boundary option A is chosen: the Haskell TL tools
remain as an RPC surface that the Python controller calls over the existing UDS socket. The
Haskell side keeps schemas and effect dispatch and loses its coordination role.

SOURCES BORROWED FROM (all under /home/goya/agent-workspace/)
- prime-agent      — loop-as-code driver (packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts); LM-as-bounded-call;
                     model resolution ladder (packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts);
                     continual harness with snapshot/rollback; goals and heartbeats.
- opencode-feature-factory — durable control plane as a validated state file with ONE atomic write
                     path (packages/feature-factory/core/atomic-write.js, write-core.js,
                     run-lock.js; state/schema.js, transition.js); closed-key schema; slices that
                     own paths + depends_on + base_ref + test_plan; max_parallel_slices /
                     max_retries ceilings; reviewed_head SHA binding; host-neutral core with
                     per-harness adapters.
- lanius           — worker-to-worker dispatch, shared observability, explicit human gates.
- zuihitsu         — event-log-as-source-of-truth; deterministic context budget floor(ctx * 0.8).

KEY DECISIONS RECORDED HERE
1. NO MESSAGE BROKER. The inbox stays. The loop consumes a durable append-only event log plus an
   in-process queue — reusing the ledger that already exists (see decision 3), not building one. The topology is single-host: all agents are local processes sharing a
   filesystem and a UDS socket. opencode-feature-factory runs a full parallel multi-agent pipeline
   with no bus at all. What is actually needed — durability, ordering, replay — a log provides,
   and it is what makes the replayable loop tests possible. REVISIT ONLY IF agents move to
   multiple hosts or containers that cannot share the socket or the state file.
2. TWO-LAYER HARNESS SELECTION. Layer 1 is a human-authored .exo/harness_policy.toml declaring,
   per role, an ordered allowlist with cost ranks and token ceilings. Layer 2 is an automatic
   selector that picks the cheapest allowed harness whose capability meets the task's classified
   difficulty and which still has budget. The selector can never widen an allowlist or raise a
   ceiling. Default worker is codex/gpt-luna; costlier harnesses are reachable only on a `hard`
   classification or after a recorded NO-GO, and only while their per-harness budget holds.
   Budget is charged in the SAME atomic run-state write as the spawn, or ceilings drift.
3. LEDGER IS READ-ONLY FOR THE TL LOOP. The append-only event log already exists at
   `.exo/ledger/segments/` (LedgerWriter / immutable_ledger.rs). The loop reuses it and builds no
   second log. The loop's own control state — verdicts, budget charges, harness and model
   selections, decompose plans, checkpoints, gate approvals — goes to the TL run-state under
   `.exo/tl-loop/<run_id>/`, never the ledger. Writing it to the ledger would land outside
   `SAFE_CATEGORICAL_VALUES` (scripts/compile_failure_atlas.py) and confound the Failure Atlas.
   Reading is safe: every event_type the loop consumes is already allowlisted. A TL control event
   may join the ledger only by deliberately adding its event_type to the allowlist in its own
   reviewed change.
4. GEMINI IS RETIRED (M0). Too expensive relative to alternatives. Old configs fail closed with a
   deprecation message; a CI grep gate prevents reintroduction.
5. VERDICT VOCABULARY is GO / GO-WITH-NITS / NO-GO, each bound to the head SHA it judged.
   Merging a head the verdict did not judge is structurally impossible (M5.4).
6. BOUNDED LOOPS EVERYWHERE. max_parallel_slices gates spawn width; max_retries gates repair
   attempts; exhaustion parks a visible needs-human chainlink issue rather than looping.

ASSUMPTION REQUIRING OPERATOR CONFIRMATION
The Python controller is scoped to `tl_loop/` at the repository root, standard-library-only at
runtime, with its checks wired into `just test` and `just pre-commit`. If it belongs elsewhere
(a subdirectory of scripts/, or its own repo), say so before M1.1 starts — every later task
references this path.

STRUCTURE
9 milestones (M0-M8), 48 subissues in a strict serial blocker chain. A worker pulling
`chainlink issue ready` gets exactly one task at a time. Every subissue carries ANTI-PATTERNS
(first), READ FIRST, STEPS, VERIFY, DONE CRITERIA and ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.

HUMAN GATES
- M3.4 shadow parity sign-off — no milestone writes to the world before this passes.
- M5.6 first live active run — outcome and interventions recorded as an ADR.
- Any harness switch outside the declared allowlist — EXOMONAD_ALLOW_HARNESS_SWITCH=1, audited.

RISKS TRACKED IN-TREE
- Event completeness (M2.7 audit produces the coverage table; gaps block M5.1).
- Budget accounting accuracy (M4.6 same-write charging plus estimate-vs-actual reconciliation).
- Determinism vs judgment (rlm calls are narrow, structured, and never branch control flow).
- Recursion identity (M7.1 enforces one worktree and one branch per loop instance).
- Harness capability map (M4.3 seeded static, M7.3 evidence-gated refinement).
- Resume correctness across restarts (M2.3 checkpoint plus M2.5 offset replay).

issues.title: Fix reviewer model and effort propagation across harnesses

comments.content:
Root-cause context:
- exomonad init resolved reviewer=codex, reviewer_model=gpt-5.6-luna, reviewer_effort=high, but the generated exomonad serve command propagated only EXOMONAD_REVIEWER_AGENT_TYPE. The long-lived server therefore loaded reviewer model=None and effort=medium.
- Commit eb82bf0a broadened the generic tmux model fallback from OpenCode-only to OpenCode plus Codex. A reviewer with no resolved model consequently inherited EXOMONAD_WORKER_MODEL=opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro, producing an invalid Codex command and a 400.
- The reviewer harness was correct; the model was cross-role leakage from the worker configuration.

Scope:
1. Propagate reviewer model and reviewer effort from exomonad init CLI overrides into the server process/config, while preserving project/global config behavior and precedence.
2. Make model/effort resolution role-aware. A reviewer must never inherit a worker or TL model merely because its own model is absent.
3. Define sensible harness-specific defaults. If the reviewer harness defaults to Codex, its fallback must be a Codex-supported default or no explicit model flag so Codex selects its own default. Do not pass OpenCode model IDs to Codex.
4. Make init reject incompatible reviewer harness/model/effort combinations with actionable errors before starting tmux. Cover defaults and explicit overrides, including reviewer, worker, and TL settings where relevant.
5. Add regression tests for the init-to-serve handoff, generated reviewer command/config, Codex and OpenCode defaults, effort propagation, and cross-harness model rejection.

Definition of done:
- Happy path: init with reviewer codex, gpt-5.6-luna, high starts a reviewer with exactly that model and effort.
- Default path: reviewer harness/model/effort defaults produce a valid command for the selected harness.
- Error path: incompatible reviewer model or effort fails during init with a clear message and no reviewer spawn.
- Isolation path: missing reviewer model never falls back to the worker model.
- Environment/restart path: a recreated or freshly started server receives the same resolved reviewer settings.
- Existing file-config and reviewer harness behavior remains covered.
- No secrets or tokens are added to logs, tests, or committed config.

Implemented in commit b0c8bf8d. exomonad init now propagates reviewer model and effort through EXOMONAD_REVIEWER_MODEL and EXOMONAD_REVIEWER_EFFORT_LEVEL; reviewer launches resolve role-aware settings and never inherit worker/TL model or effort. Added propagation, isolation, parser, and cross-harness validation regression tests. cargo test -p exomonad passed; exomonad-core role-isolation test passed. Clippy remains blocked by pre-existing warnings outside this change.
Final commit after including the generated changelog entry: 1ad2a468.

# DEFERRED (Phase 3): automatic memory capture hooks

NOT part of the current wave plan. Do not spawn this until Waves 1-3 are merged
and the ledger schema has been exercised by hand through the explicit
`memory_append` tool.

## WHY DEFERRED

Wiring eleven handlers before the record shape is settled invites a rewrite. The
explicit `memory_append` path from Wave 2 is the proving ground: once the useful
`kind` values, importance ranges, and summary conventions are known from real
use, automatic capture becomes mechanical.

## SCOPE WHEN UNBLOCKED

Automatically append `session_memory` records at these points:

| Trigger | kind |
|---|---|
| `chainlink_issue_create` | `wave_plan` / `next_action` |
| `chainlink_issue_comment` | `decision` |
| `chainlink_session_end` | `child_handoff` |
| `notify_parent` | `child_handoff` or `blocker` by status |
| `spawn_leaf` / `spawn_worker` | `spawned_child` |
| `resume_pr` | `fix_direction` |
| `file_pr` | `spawned_child` follow-up / PR link |
| watcher review events | `review_feedback` |
| watcher CI events | `ci_result` |
| `merge_pr` | `merge_result` |
| `shutdown_server` | `session_summary` |

The high-value captures are child handoffs and blockers — exactly the
between-runs context that is lost today.

## CONSTRAINTS (carry forward)

- Store concise semantic facts with capped detail and references to
  files/PRs/issues. Never dump raw tool output into the ledger.
- Capture must be fail-open: a ledger write failure logs and continues; it never
  fails the originating tool call.
- Append-only. No overwrite of earlier records; supersession is expressed via
  `supersedes_id`.

## DECOMPOSITION HINT

Split by handler group, not by kind — roughly: chainlink triggers, spawn/resume
triggers, PR/watcher triggers, lifecycle triggers. Four narrow leaves, minimal
file overlap.

issues.description:
# W2: ContinuationBriefRenderer (deterministic markdown)

Wave 2. BLOCKED until both Wave 1 subissues are merged — this consumes
`BriefInputs` and `SessionMemoryService`.

## ANTI-PATTERNS (read first)

- No LLM summarization, no calls to any model, no network. The renderer is a
  pure function.
- No I/O of any kind in this file. It takes `BriefInputs` and returns `String`.
  If you need data that `BriefInputs` lacks, extend `BriefInputs` — do not fetch.
- Output must be deterministic: no `HashMap` iteration order, no timestamps
  computed at render time, no random ordering. Sort every collection explicitly.
- Do NOT silently drop an unavailable section. Render it with its stated reason.
- ZERO new external dependencies. No templating crate.
- Do NOT wire this into SessionStart, spawn, or resume — that is Wave 3.

## READ FIRST

- `CLAUDE.md` (project root) — § Rules
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/mod.rs` and `adapters.rs` —
  the merged `BriefInputs` and `SectionData` types
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/session_memory.rs` — `MemoryKind`,
  `MemoryRecordRow`
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md` — the vocabulary the brief must speak
  (`[MERGE READY]`, `resume_pr`, `review-stuck`, etc.)

## STEPS

1. Create `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/renderer.rs`.

2. Public surface:
   - `pub fn render_tl(inputs: &BriefInputs, ledger: &[MemoryRecordRow]) -> String`
   - `pub fn render_child(inputs: &BriefInputs, ledger: &[MemoryRecordRow], slice: &ChildSlice) -> String`
   where `ChildSlice` carries the child's `agent_id`, assigned `issue_id`, and
   optional `pr_number`.

3. `render_tl` emits exactly this block, sections in this order:

   ```
   <exomonad-continuation-brief>
   ## Original plan
   ## Current objective
   ## Active issues
   ## Child workstreams
   ## New since last run
   ## Decisions made
   ## Blockers / risks
   ## Recommended next action
   </exomonad-continuation-brief>
   ```

   Section sources:
   - Original plan / Current objective — latest `original_plan` and `wave_plan`
     ledger records for the run
   - Active issues — chainlink open issues, `- #<id> <title> (<status>)`
   - Child workstreams — join agent summaries, PR summaries, and
     `child_handoff` ledger records, one line per live child
   - New since last run — ledger records newer than the previous
     `session_summary` record, plus chainlink issues created after it
   - Decisions made — `decision` records
   - Blockers / risks — `blocker` records plus any PR in a stuck/failing state
   - Recommended next action — a numbered, deterministically derived list, e.g.
     merge-ready PRs first, then `resume_pr` for PRs with review feedback, then
     unassigned open issues. Derivation rules must be stated in a doc comment.

   An `Unavailable` section renders as
   `_(unavailable: <reason>)_` under its heading.

4. `render_child` emits `## Parent plan context` (original plan, current
   objective, sibling workstreams at one line each) followed by
   `## Your specific slice` (the child's issue, PR, and any `fix_direction` or
   `review_feedback` records scoped to it). It must NOT include the full active
   issue list or unrelated blockers.

5. Size cap: hard limit of 4096 bytes on the rendered block. When over cap, drop
   ledger records lowest-`importance`-first (ties broken by oldest-first) and
   append a final line stating exactly how many records were dropped. Never
   truncate mid-line and never exceed the cap.

6. Empty-input case renders a structurally valid brief with each section
   explicitly marked empty. It must never render as a bare empty string.

## VERIFY

```
just build
just rust-test
just test
```

Tests in `renderer.rs`:
- golden-file tests under `rust/exomonad-core/tests/fixtures/brief/` for: a
  full-population TL brief, an empty-input TL brief, a child brief, and a brief
  with one `Unavailable` section
- determinism: render the same `BriefInputs` twice, assert byte equality; and
  build the inputs from shuffled collections, assert identical output
- size cap: construct inputs exceeding 4096 bytes, assert output is under cap,
  the dropped-count line is present, and the highest-importance records survived
- `render_child` does not contain unrelated sibling blockers

## BOUNDARY

Files you may create or modify — exhaustive:
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/renderer.rs` (new)
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/mod.rs` (add `pub mod renderer;`
  and `ChildSlice`; extend `BriefInputs` only if genuinely required)
- `rust/exomonad-core/tests/fixtures/brief/*` (new)
- `rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md`

Do not touch handlers, Haskell, `.exo/roles/`, `spawn.rs`, or `agent.rs`.

## DONE CRITERIA

`just test` green, golden files committed, determinism and cap tests passing,
`rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md` updated, PR filed.
