# W1: chainlink + forgejo state adapters for the continuation brief

Wave 1. Independent of the other W1 subissue — no shared files.

## ANTI-PATTERNS (read first)

- Do NOT open `.chainlink/issues.db` with rusqlite. Chainlink is read ONLY by
  shelling out to `chainlink ... --json`. A direct read couples exomonad to
  chainlink's private schema and breaks silently on their migrations.
- Do NOT drain the inbox. Read metadata (unread counts, last-checked) only.
  `InboxStore::peek_unnotified` mutates `notified_at` — do not call it here.
- Do NOT emit markdown. Adapters return typed data. Rendering is a separate
  subissue.
- Do NOT silently return an empty section when a source fails. Return an
  explicit typed "unavailable" with the reason.
- ZERO new external dependencies.
- No `unwrap()` outside tests.

## READ FIRST

- `CLAUDE.md` (project root) — § Rules, § Logging
- `rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md`
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/process.rs` lines 60-175 — how chainlink is
  invoked today, including `chainlink_db_env` (line 68) and the tracing pattern
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/command.rs` — the command execution service
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs` — available metadata queries
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resolver.rs` — `AgentIdentityRecord`,
  `all()`
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/pr_registry.rs` and
  `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/forgejo.rs`
- Run `chainlink issue list --help`, `chainlink issue show --help`,
  `chainlink session status --help` to confirm the exact `--json` shapes.

## STEPS

1. Create `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/mod.rs` and
   `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/adapters.rs`. Register
   `pub mod continuation;` in `services/mod.rs`.

2. Define the shared result type so every adapter degrades explicitly:

   ```rust
   pub enum SectionData<T> {
       Available(T),
       Unavailable { reason: String },
   }
   ```

   There is no `Empty` variant and no `Default` impl — an available-but-empty
   source is `Available(vec![])`.

3. Chainlink adapter. One struct with methods that shell out through the
   existing command path, passing `CHAINLINK_DB` explicitly (resolve it the way
   `ProcessHandler::chainlink_db_env` does — `project_dir/.chainlink/issues.db`):
   - `issues(&self) -> SectionData<Vec<ChainlinkIssue>>` from
     `chainlink issue list --json`
   - `issue_detail(&self, id: i64) -> SectionData<ChainlinkIssueDetail>` from
     `chainlink issue show <id> --json`
   - `sessions(&self) -> SectionData<Vec<ChainlinkSession>>` from
     `chainlink session status --json`
   `ChainlinkSession` must carry at least `agent_id`, `active_issue_id`,
   `handoff_notes`, `last_action`.
   Per CLAUDE.md § Logging: `tracing::info!` the full command line before, exit
   code after, `tracing::error!` stderr on non-zero exit. A non-zero exit or a
   JSON parse failure yields `Unavailable { reason }` — never a panic, never an
   empty `Available`.

4. Inbox adapter: `unread_summary(&self) -> SectionData<Vec<AgentInboxSummary>>`
   with `agent_id`, `unread_count`, `last_checked_at`. Metadata only.

5. Agent adapter: `agents(&self) -> SectionData<Vec<AgentSummary>>` from
   `AgentResolver` — `agent_id`, `birth_branch`, `role`, `alive`. Use the
   composite liveness predicate that `AgentHandler::list` uses (tmux liveness +
   not retired + has a delivery target), not `AgentResolver::all()` raw. See
   chainlink issue 619 for why the raw registry over-reports liveness.

6. PR adapter: `open_prs(&self) -> SectionData<Vec<PrSummary>>` with
   `number`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, `owner_agent`, `review_state`,
   `ci_state`, sourced from `ForgejoClient` / `pr_registry`. When Forgejo is not
   configured, return `Unavailable { reason: "Forgejo is not configured" }`.

7. Define `pub struct BriefInputs` in `continuation/mod.rs` holding one field per
   adapter output plus `run_id`, `agent_id`, `role`. This is the type the
   renderer subissue will consume — get the shape right, it is the contract.
   Do NOT write the renderer.

## VERIFY

```
just build
just rust-test
just test
```

Tests in `adapters.rs`:
- fixture JSON strings for each of the three chainlink subcommands, asserting
  the typed parse (put fixtures inline as `const` strs or under
  `rust/exomonad-core/tests/fixtures/chainlink/`)
- a non-zero exit yields `Unavailable` carrying the stderr text
- malformed JSON yields `Unavailable`, not a panic
- inbox adapter does not mutate `notified_at` (append two messages to an
  in-memory `InboxStore`, run the adapter, assert both are still unnotified)
- Forgejo-unconfigured yields `Unavailable` with a stated reason

## BOUNDARY

Files you may create or modify — exhaustive:
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/mod.rs` (new)
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/adapters.rs` (new)
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/mod.rs` (add `pub mod continuation;` only)
- `rust/exomonad-core/tests/fixtures/chainlink/*` (new, optional)
- `rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md`

Do not touch `session_memory.rs`, proto files, handlers, Haskell, or
`.exo/roles/`.

## DONE CRITERIA

documented, `rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md` updated, PR filed.

## STEPS

   `rust/exomonad-proto/proto/effects/memory.proto` (identical content; both
   files are required — the second is not generated from the first). Define:
   - `enum MemoryKind` with values: `MEMORY_KIND_UNSPECIFIED`,

   - `message MemoryListRequest` (filters: run_id, agent_id, issue_id, kind,

   Follow the field-numbering and naming conventions already used in

   `pub struct SessionMemoryService { db_path: PathBuf, conn: Mutex<Connection> }`
   and the exact schema:

   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS session_memory (
     id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
     run_id        TEXT    NOT NULL,
     agent_id      TEXT    NOT NULL,
     birth_branch  TEXT    NOT NULL,
     issue_id      INTEGER,
     kind          TEXT    NOT NULL,
     importance    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 50,

   CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_session_memory_agent ON session_memory(agent_id);
   ```

   `FromStr` / `Display` round-tripping the snake_case strings stored in the

5. Implement, all `-> Result<...>`:
   - `append(&self, record: NewMemoryRecord) -> Result<i64>`
   - `list(&self, filter: MemoryFilter) -> Result<Vec<MemoryRecordRow>>`

```
just test
```

- unknown `kind` string fails to parse
- empty summary, 201-char summary, 4097-byte detail, importance 101 each error
- `supersedes_id` pointing at a missing row errors
- `list` filters by run_id, agent_id, issue_id, kind, min_importance, limit
- `latest_by_kind` returns the newest matching row and `None` when absent

issues.title: feat: session memory ledger + TL continuation brief
issues.description:
# EPIC: Session memory ledger + TL continuation brief

## PROBLEM

Continuity policy (original plan, active issues, child handoffs, blockers, next
action) lives only as prompt text the TL is expected to remember. It does not
survive a context reset, `--recreate`, or a resumed session. Between runs the
world changes — children file PRs, reviewers comment, CI fails, issues get
created — and none of it is re-presented to the continuing TL.

Every input already exists but nothing composes them:

- Chainlink sessions (`active_issue_id`, `handoff_notes`, `last_action`) live in
  `.chainlink/issues.db`, reached only by shelling out. `ProcessHandler`
  special-cases `command == "chainlink"` and injects `CHAINLINK_DB`
  (rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/process.rs:68). Never read back into a brief.
- `InboxStore` (.exo/inbox.db, rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs:26)
  is drain-on-read notification state, not history.
- `EventLog` (.exo/events/*.jsonl,
  rust/exomonad-core/src/services/event_log.rs:14) is raw tool-call granularity
  with no semantic layer.
- `AgentResolver` liveness is never surfaced at startup.
- Forgejo PR/review/CI state is delivered as one-shot events only.
- `defaultSessionStartHook` (haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Types.hs:187)
  injects exactly one line: "Create a team using TeamCreate before proceeding."
  It is the obvious injection point and is currently unused for continuity.

## GOAL

An append-only semantic ledger plus a deterministically rendered continuation
brief, injected automatically at root/TL SessionStart and prefixed onto
`spawn_leaf` / `resume_pr` task text. Continuity becomes a system property, not
a prompt-compliance property.

## ARCHITECTURE

Three layers:

1. Ledger — append-only structured records in `.exo/memory.db`.
2. Adapters — chainlink (via CLI `--json`), Forgejo/PR, inbox metadata, event
   log, agent resolver.
3. Renderer — deterministic markdown `<exomonad-continuation-brief>` block.

```
chainlink CLI (--json) -+
InboxStore metadata ----+
EventLog ---------------+--> SessionMemoryService --> ContinuationBriefRenderer
AgentResolver ----------+       (.exo/memory.db)              |
ForgejoClient/watcher --+                                     v
                              SessionStart additionalContext (root/TL)
                              spawn_leaf task prefix
                              resume_pr handoff prefix
```

## DECISIONS

- Chainlink is read by shelling out to `chainlink ... --json`. Do NOT add a
  second SQLite reader against chainlink's private schema — a chainlink
  migration would silently break the brief.
- Scope is Phases 1+2 (ledger, adapters, renderer, injection, explicit
  `memory_*` tools). Phase 3 (automatic capture inside every tool handler) is
  the deferred subissue and is NOT built in this epic.
- No LLM summarization anywhere in the brief path. The renderer is a pure
  function of structured inputs and is unit-testable as such.
- Per CLAUDE.md: no direct Rust MCP tools. Rust adds effect handlers only; every
  tool schema and dispatch lives in Haskell WASM.

## WAVES

- Wave 1 (scaffold, parallel): proto+SessionMemoryService; state adapters.
- Wave 2 (after W1 merges, parallel): ContinuationBriefRenderer; memory effect
  handler + Haskell `memory_*` tools.
- Wave 3 (after W2 merges, parallel): SessionStart injection; spawn_leaf and
  resume_pr task prefixes.
- Deferred: automatic memory capture hooks.

W1 must merge before W2 is spawned — W2 depends on the proto and service types
landing.

## SCAFFOLD COMMIT (TL, before Wave 1)

Commit `proto/effects/memory.proto` stub and
`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/continuation/mod.rs` stub so W1 leaves share a
foundation.

## DOCUMENTATION (required, distributed across the child PRs)

- `CLAUDE.md` — MCP tools table rows for `memory_append`, `memory_list`,
  `continuation_brief`; Built Infrastructure row for the ledger.
- `rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md` — `session_memory.rs`, `continuation/`.
- `haskell/wasm-guest/CLAUDE.md` — memory effect + tools.
- `docs/decisions/session-memory-ledger.md` — new ADR: why append-only, why
  deterministic rendering, why not the inbox, why chainlink stays behind its CLI.
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md` and `tl.md` — the brief arrives
  automatically; TLs need not call `continuation_brief` manually.

## DONE CRITERIA

All non-deferred subissues merged, `just test` and `cabal test all` green, the
E2E test under `tests/e2e/continuation-brief/` passing, and docs updated.

comments.content: Starting the required scaffold commit: shared memory.proto type stub and continuation/mod.rs interface stub. W1 #621 and #622 will dispatch only after this foundation is committed.

Completed the remaining epic documentation gap by adding docs/decisions/session-memory-ledger.md, covering the append-only ledger, CLI-backed Chainlink adapter boundary, inbox distinction, deterministic renderer, fail-open SessionStart/task injection, and deferred Phase 3 capture. Verification passed: just check-e2e-continuation-brief; just e2e-continuation-brief; just test (1204 Rust tests passed, 5 skipped; 69 role-hook tests passed); cabal test all (all suites passed); git diff --check. All non-deferred subissues are closed and no ExoMonad session was started.

issues.title: fix: has_pending_work reports dead agents as alive, blocking shutdown convergence
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

# fix: has_pending_work reports dead agents as alive (blocks shutdown convergence)

## PROBLEM

`has_pending_work` and `shutdown_server` report agents as alive that are actually
dead. `list_agents` reports the same agents correctly as dead. Two code paths
compute "which agents are alive" and they disagree — the CLAUDE.md "Single Code
Path" rule violation.

### Root cause

`rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/lifecycle.rs:160-171`

```rust
async fn live_non_root_agents<C: HasAgentResolver>(ctx: &C) -> Vec<AgentIdentityRecord> {
    ctx.agent_resolver().all().await
        .into_iter().filter(is_non_root_agent).collect()
}
fn is_non_root_agent(record: &AgentIdentityRecord) -> bool {
    record.agent_name.as_str() != "root"
}
```

The `live_` prefix is a lie. There is no liveness check of any kind — no tmux
probe, no routing snapshot, no retirement check. `AgentResolver::all()`
(`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resolver.rs:215`) returns the whole
in-memory registration map; entries leave only via an explicit `deregister()`
call. Any agent that dies without clean deregistration (crash, pane kill,
session teardown, a dispose path that skips deregister) is reported alive
forever.

By contrast `AgentControlService::list_agents()`
(`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/cleanup.rs:365-376`) scans
`.exo/worktrees/` and `.exo/agents/` and verifies liveness against
`get_tmux_windows()`. `AgentHandler::list()` (`handlers/agent.rs:1554-1614`)
then refines it further:

```rust
let is_alive = agent_is_alive(info)
    && !routing_snapshot.retired
    && routing_snapshot.routing.as_ref().is_some_and(RoutingInfo::has_delivery_target);
```

That composite predicate is the correct definition of alive. `has_pending_work`
uses none of it.

### Second defect: fabricated proto fields

`agent_record_to_proto` (`lifecycle.rs:182-203`) hardcodes fields it has no data
for, because `AgentIdentityRecord` carries no liveness or inbox state:

```rust
alive: true,
is_alive: true,
has_unread: false,
last_check_inbox_at: 0,
```

This is the source of the "zeroed timestamps" the operator observed. They are
not stale reads — they are literal constants. This is an undocumented fallback,
which CLAUDE.md forbids ("Always prefer failure to an undocumented heuristic or
fallback").

### Impact (why this matters, not cosmetic)

`shutdown_server` (`lifecycle.rs:89-102`) calls the same
`live_non_root_agents` and refuses to shut down while it returns non-empty:

```rust
return Ok(ServerShutdownResult { success: false, error: live_agent_error(&alive_agents), .. });
```

So a single stale registry entry makes `shutdown_server` fail permanently with
`"N agent(s) still alive: [...]"`. The idle/shutdown convergence protocol
documented in `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md` ("call `has_pending_work` …
if no open issues and no live agents, call `shutdown_server`") can never
complete on any session where an agent died uncleanly. That is every long
session.

## ANTI-PATTERNS (read first — DO NOT)

- DO NOT add a second liveness helper. The whole bug is that two paths compute
  liveness differently. Exactly one predicate must survive this change.
- DO NOT "fix" it by making `agent_record_to_proto` set `alive: false` or guess
  a timestamp. Do not fabricate proto field values at all.
- DO NOT change the semantics of `list_agents` / `AgentHandler::list()`. It is
  the correct path. Reuse it; do not rewrite it.
- DO NOT add a config flag, env var, "strict mode", or `legacy_liveness` toggle.
- DO NOT delete `AgentResolver::all()` or `deregister()` — other callers use
  them. This is about `lifecycle.rs`, not the resolver.
- DO NOT add external crates.
- DO NOT widen scope into fixing *why* agents fail to deregister. That is a
  separate concern; this issue is about liveness being observed, not recorded.
- DO NOT leave `live_non_root_agents` in place "for compatibility". Delete it.
- No `todo!()`, no stream-of-consciousness comments.

## READ FIRST (exact files)

1. `CLAUDE.md` — § Rules (Single Code Path; prefer failure to undocumented
   fallback), § Logging
2. `.claude/rules/rust.md` (if present)
3. `rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md`
4. `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/lifecycle.rs` — whole file (~440 lines)
5. `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs` — `list()` at 1554-1614,
   `read_agent_routing_snapshot` at 3405, `agent_matches_filter` at 3498,
   `agent_is_alive` at 3509, `service_info_to_proto` + `AgentListMetadata`
6. `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/cleanup.rs:365-450` —
   `list_agents`
7. `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resolver.rs:150-220`
8. `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/groups.rs:55-77` — handler wiring

## STEPS

1. **Extract the canonical liveness predicate.** In `handlers/agent.rs`, lift
   the composite check currently inlined in `list()` into one reusable async
   function, e.g.:

   ```rust
   pub(crate) async fn resolve_agent_liveness(info: &AgentInfo) -> (bool, AgentRoutingSnapshot) {
       let snapshot = read_agent_routing_snapshot(info.agent_dir.as_deref()).await;
       let is_alive = agent_is_alive(info)
           && !snapshot.retired
           && snapshot.routing.as_ref().is_some_and(RoutingInfo::has_delivery_target);
       (is_alive, snapshot)
   }
   ```

   Rewrite `list()` to call it so there is exactly one definition. `list()`
   behavior must be unchanged.

2. **Give `LifecycleHandler` access to `AgentControlService`.** At
   `handlers/groups.rs:66-71`, `agent_control: Arc<AgentControlService<Services>>`
   is already in scope at the exact site where `LifecycleHandler` is
   constructed. Add it as a field:

   ```rust
   pub struct LifecycleHandler<C> {
       ctx: Arc<C>,
       agent_control: Arc<AgentControlService<C>>,
       shutdown_signal: Option<Arc<Notify>>,
       chainlink_bin: PathBuf,
   }
   ```

   Thread it through `new` and `with_shutdown_signal`, and update the two call
   sites in `groups.rs`. Widen the `C` bound as required by
   `AgentControlService<C>`. If the trait-bound explosion makes this untenable,
   the acceptable alternative is a narrow `HasAgentControl` accessor trait in
   `services/mod.rs` alongside the existing `Has*` traits — but prefer the
   direct field, and do not do both.

3. **Rewrite `live_non_root_agents`** to go through the real path:

   ```rust
   async fn live_non_root_agents(&self) -> EffectResult<Vec<AgentInfo>> {
       let infos = self.agent_control.list_agents().await.effect_err("lifecycle")?;
       let mut alive = Vec::new();
       for info in infos {
           if info.internal_name.as_str() == "root" { continue; }
           let (is_alive, _) = resolve_agent_liveness(&info).await;
           if is_alive { alive.push(info); }
       }
       Ok(alive)
   }
   ```

   Keep the `!= "root"` filter — that part was correct.

4. **Delete `agent_record_to_proto`** (`lifecycle.rs:182-203`) and
   `service_agent_type_to_proto` if it becomes unused. Populate
   `HasPendingWorkResult.alive_agents` using the same
   `service_info_to_proto` + `AgentListMetadata` path `AgentHandler::list()`
   uses, with real values for `is_alive`, `has_unread`, and
   `last_check_inbox_at` read from `ctx.inbox_store()`. No hardcoded field
   values.

5. **`shutdown_server`** picks up the fix automatically via the shared helper —
   confirm it does, and that its error string still names the agents.

6. **Logging** (CLAUDE.md § Logging). Add `tracing::info!` in
   `has_pending_work` recording `open_issue_count`, total agents scanned, and
   alive count; add `tracing::warn!` in `shutdown_server` when shutdown is
   refused, naming the agents that blocked it. Silent refusal is what made this
   bug invisible.

7. **Tests** — required, in `lifecycle.rs`'s `mod tests` (existing harness at
   lines 217-438) plus `agent.rs` if the extraction warrants it:
   - registered agent whose tmux window is gone ⇒ NOT counted; `has_pending_work`
     is `false` when there are also no open issues (this is the regression test —
     it fails on `main`)
   - registered agent with a live tmux window ⇒ counted
   - agent with `routing.retired = true` ⇒ NOT counted
   - `shutdown_server` succeeds when the only registry entries are dead agents
   - `shutdown_server` still refuses with a live agent, error naming it
   - existing open-issue-count tests still pass unchanged

## VERIFY

```bash
just build
just test
just pre-commit
```

All must pass. Do not use raw `cargo build` or `cargo test` — see
`.claude/rules` / CLAUDE.md build workflow.

## BOUNDARY

Files you may modify — this list is exhaustive:
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/lifecycle.rs`
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs`
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/groups.rs`
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/mod.rs` (only if step 2's fallback is taken)
- `rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md` (only if the liveness contract is documented there)

No proto changes. No Haskell changes. No changes to `agent_resolver.rs`,
`agent_control/cleanup.rs`, or any role prompt.

## DONE CRITERIA

- Exactly one liveness predicate exists in the codebase; `live_non_root_agents`
  as written on `main` is gone.
- `has_pending_work` and `list_agents` agree on the alive set for the same
  session state.
- No proto field in the `has_pending_work` response is a hardcoded constant.
- `shutdown_server` succeeds when all registered agents are dead.
- New regression test fails on `main`, passes on the branch.
- `just build`, `just test`, `just pre-commit` all green.
- PR filed.

Lifecycle now uses AgentControlService discovery plus the shared AgentHandler liveness predicate, reports real inbox/routing metadata, logs convergence decisions, and tests dead, live, and retired agents. Verification: just build passed; just test attempted but cannot create /run/user/1000/just temp dir (read-only); just pre-commit unavailable because no recipe; just test-fast passed 920/920 (3 skipped) outside sandbox; just check-fmt passed; repository integrity passed. issues.title: Fix ExoMonad worktree identity clobbering across agents
issues.description:
EXOMONAD BINARY SCOPE
This issue concerns the Rust ExoMonad binary's linked worktree creation, not beast-rs or an external repository.

ROOT CAUSE
rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs used git config --local for per-agent user.name/user.email. In a linked worktree, --local writes the shared repository config, so each new dev or reviewer spawn overwrites every existing agent and the main repository identity.

REQUIRED FIX
1. Before creating the first linked worktree, validate safe core.bare/core.worktree values and enable extensions.worktreeConfig idempotently.
2. Write only user.name and user.email with git config --worktree at both create_workspace and create_workspace_detached sites.
3. Keep exomonad.remote on git config --local because the ExoMonad multi-remote selection must remain shared.
4. Migrate existing linked worktrees by deriving the agent identity from each worktree branch's final dot-separated segment, and remove legacy shared user.name/user.email entries from the main repository config.
5. Add Rust regressions for dev/dev isolation, detached reviewer identity, main-repo non-clobbering, migration, safe-config rejection, and shared exomonad.remote visibility.

VERIFY
just rust-test

STATUS
This has already landed in the ExoMonad binary as the #609 implementation (3827b9c6), with changelog commit 8ca46cd5.

BOUNDARY
rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs and its tests/migration only. Do not alter PR-body Authoring-Agent provenance.

comments.content: Resolved by the already-landed #609 implementation (commits 3827b9c6 and 8ca46cd5): extensions.worktreeConfig validation, --worktree identity writes, existing-worktree migration, shared exomonad.remote preservation, and five regressions. Closing this duplicate tracker record without another changelog entry.

TRIPWIRE
Add a cheap, deterministic ExoMonad repository-integrity check and wire it into the fast test/CI path.

The check must run from the ExoMonad repository root and fail if:
- git rev-parse --show-toplevel does not resolve to the expected workspace;
- known ExoMonad sentinels such as Cargo.toml and rust/exomonad-core/src/lib.rs are not tracked;
- the repository's local config contains the fixture identity CI Test or ci@test.local;
- the working tree/index has the characteristic fixture-collapse shape that replaces the real ExoMonad tree with a tiny synthetic tree.

Prefer stable sentinel and suspicious-identity checks over a hardcoded tracked-file count, since the binary may be consumed from repositories with different sizes. Make the command explicit, fast, and safe to run from CI without mutating Git state.

VERIFY
just test-repo-integrity
just rust-test

DONE CRITERIA
The tripwire runs in the ExoMonad fast verification path, catches the known root-repository corruption signals, and has a focused passing test for both healthy and synthetic/corrupt states.

issues.title: fix: per-agent git identity is written to shared config and clobbered by every spawn
issues.description:
DEFECT
Every spawned agent commits under the git identity of whichever worktree was created most recently. Agent identity is not stable after worktree creation, despite being set exactly once at creation.

ROOT CAUSE
git config --local inside a linked worktree does NOT write per-worktree config. It writes to the shared $GIT_DIR/config, i.e. the main repo .git/config. Git supports per-worktree config only when extensions.worktreeConfig=true and the caller uses git config --worktree.

Both identity sites use --local:
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs:244-262 (create_workspace, dev leaves)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs:303-317 (create_workspace_detached, reviewers)

So each new spawn overwrites user.name/user.email for every existing worktree AND the main repo. Last writer wins.

EVIDENCE (/home/goya/storage/RustDebuggerRepo)
extensions.worktreeConfig unset, no .git/worktrees/*/config.worktree files, and all 12 worktrees resolve user.name to exomonad-review-pr-123-codex, a reviewer identity, including every dev leaf. The main repo local user.name is clobbered to the same value, displacing the human operator identity.

IMPACT
Silently voids the reviewer identity discipline in CLAUDE.md (an agent never reviews under the identity that authored the PR) and the authorship invariant from issues #298-#301. The Authoring-Agent line in the PR body is currently the only real provenance; the git author field is noise.

READ FIRST
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs (create_workspace, create_workspace_detached)
- CLAUDE.md, Review Policy section, Reviewer identity discipline
- CLAUDE.md, Multiple git remotes section (explains why exomonad.remote must STAY shared)

STEPS
1. Before the first worktree is created, set extensions.worktreeConfig=true on the main repo, idempotently. Assert core.bare/core.worktree are safe in shared config first rather than assuming; core.bare=false is present on the observed repos and is correct for the main worktree.
2. Change both identity sites from git config --local to git config --worktree for user.name and user.email only.
3. Leave exomonad.remote on --local deliberately. CLAUDE.md documents that it SHOULD be shared across worktrees. Only identity moves.
4. Add a migration for existing repos: stamp each live worktree identity from the last dot-segment of its branch, and unset the clobbered user.name/user.email from the main repo shared config so it falls back to the operator global identity. Without this, existing worktrees keep committing under the wrong identity because --worktree on new spawns is not retroactive.

VERIFY: just rust-test

DONE CRITERIA / TESTS (all required)
- Creating a second worktree does not mutate the first worktree resolved user.name.
- Each worktree resolves user.name to exomonad-{its own agent name}.
- A detached reviewer worktree gets its own identity, distinct from the dev leaf it reviews.
- The main repo user.name is not modified by any spawn.
- exomonad.remote remains readable from every worktree after the change.

ANTI-PATTERNS
- Do not move exomonad.remote to --worktree; that breaks documented multi-remote behavior.
- Do not set identity via env vars (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME etc.) as a substitute; the config must be durable in the worktree.
- Do not enable extensions.worktreeConfig without handling core.bare/core.worktree.

BOUNDARY: git_worktree.rs plus the migration and tests. Do not change PR body Authoring-Agent handling.

The TL only sees NotifyParentRepair -> [REPAIR HANDOFF].

TARGET CONTRACT (operator decision)
Reviewer comment and changes-requested events dispatch to the parent role in addition to the PR owner, producing the TL-facing messages from tlPrReviewHandler. [REPAIR HANDOFF] remains only for approved and merge_ready.

STEPS
1. In the PendingAction::WasmEvent arm, dispatch review-comment kinds (review_received, review_commented) to the parent role in addition to the PR owner, reusing the parent resolution in deliver_parent_repair_handoff (:2151-2162). Keep the rule that no event is ever injected into an exited reviewer pane.
2. Stop emitting PendingAction::NotifyParentRepair for the commented and changes_requested outcomes. Leave approved and merge_ready unchanged.
3. Reconcile the redundant text paths: review_parent_message (:564) and Tpl.reviewCommentedForParent. Exactly one message-construction path survives per event kind. Delete whichever is unreachable after step 1.
4. Update rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md (Reviewer completion routing) and root CLAUDE.md notification vocabulary to state the new contract.

issues.description:
Test-first. Establish ground truth for how the watcher observes a reviewer that leaves inline comments without submitting a verdict. This informs the disposal fix and may itself be a second cause of both reported symptoms.

READ FIRST
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs: obs_to_review_parts (~:3366), aggregate_review_state (~:3345), the commented branch (~:3135-3175)

STEPS
1. Add a watcher unit test feeding an Observation with non-empty comments and empty reviews.
2. Assert the resulting review_state, the emitted PendingAction set, and whether disposal is reached.
3. If the observed state is PendingReview, fix the upstream derivation so bare inline comments aggregate to Commented. If it is already Commented, keep the test as a regression guard and change nothing else.

VERIFY: just rust-test

DONE CRITERIA: test exists and passes; behavior for comment-only reviews is documented in the test name and assertions.

BOUNDARY: no changes to disposal or notification routing.

issues.title: fix: reviewer disposal, TL review notification, and CI panel columns
issues.description:
Umbrella for two operator-reported defects and one dashboard change.

DEFECT A - reviewers do not close themselves when done.
review_state_disposes_reviewer (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:167) treats only Approved | ChangesRequested as terminal, so a COMMENT-state review never reaches the disposal block at :1840-1867 and dispose_reviewers_for_pr never runs. Contradicts restart reconstruction at :1778-1788, which already counts ReviewerAttemptPhase::Commented as reviewer_disposed = true. Live and restored state disagree about one verdict.

DEFECT B - TL is not notified when reviewer comments are posted.
call_handle_event_for_role (:1942) dispatches each review event to exactly one target, the PR owner dev leaf. tlPrReviewHandler (.exo/lib/PRReviewHandler.hs:128-179) has complete ReviewCommented / ReviewReceived / ReviewerRequestedChanges cases that are unreachable. The TL only ever sees NotifyParentRepair -> [REPAIR HANDOFF].

OPERATOR DECISIONS
- The TL receives reviewer comment events directly via tlPrReviewHandler.
- [REPAIR HANDOFF] is retained only for approved and merge_ready. ci_blocked and stuck are not reviewer verdicts and are out of scope.
- Subissues 4 and 5 are an ordered pair.

issues.title: Add Rust integration tests to the aggregate test gate
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

`just test` runs no Rust integration test target, so every guard written as an integration test is unenforced. This has now happened three times in a row.

## SYMPTOM

`just test` step 2/7 is `just rust-test`, which runs
`cargo nextest run --workspace --lib --no-fail-fast`. `--lib` excludes every
`tests/*.rs` target. Six exist and none of them run:

    rust/claude-teams-bridge/tests/integration.rs
    rust/exomonad-core/tests/mock_github_integration.rs
    rust/exomonad-core/tests/tmux_liveness.rs
    rust/exomonad-core/tests/wasm_integration.rs
    rust/exomonad-proto/tests/wire_compat.rs
    rust/exomonad/tests/cli.rs

Consequences observed this week, each landing in a target nothing automated runs:

- #593/#594: `tests/tmux_liveness.rs` — the regression tests for the liveness
  probes that wedged `resume_pr` for hours.
- #595: `wasm-guest-tests` was in no target at all until a `just wasm-guest-test`
  recipe was added and wired in. That fix was correct and is the precedent here.
- #598: `runtime_protocols_list_every_wasm_granted_mcp_tool` — the guard that is
  supposed to stop MCP tool grants drifting out of the runtime protocols. Its own
  documentation (`rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md` § Runtime protocol tool coverage)
  tells the reader to run `just test-cargo-all` manually, conceding it is outside
  the gate.

A guard that only runs when a human remembers a second command is not a guard.
The pattern is systemic, not three coincidences: `just test` is understood to be
"the checks", and anything not reachable from it decays.

## ROOT CAUSE

`just rust-test` was scoped to `--lib` for speed. `just rust-test-all`
(`cargo nextest run --workspace`, alias `just test-cargo-all`) covers every
target but is referenced by no aggregate recipe. Nothing states which tests are
expected to gate a change, so new tests land wherever is convenient and the
author assumes coverage.

`wasm_integration` additionally requires built WASM, which is why it was
originally excluded; `just test` already builds WASM at step 4/7, so ordering can
satisfy that.

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- DO NOT fix this by moving integration tests into `src/` unit test modules to
  get them into `--lib`. The test belongs where it belongs.
- DO NOT add a fourth ad-hoc recipe per test file. `just wasm-guest-test` was
  right for a WASM-only suite with no cargo target; native cargo targets need
  the general fix, not more special cases.
- DO NOT make the slow targets opt-in via an env var that defaults to off.
- DO NOT silence a target that turns out to be slow or flaky by dropping it back
  out of the gate — fix or quarantine it explicitly, with the quarantine visible.
- No new dependencies.

## READ FIRST

- justfile:28-46 (`rust-test`), :39-43 (`rust-test-all`, `test-cargo-all`), :56-72 (`test`)
- rust/CLAUDE.md § Testing, § Diagnosing Rust test failures
- rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md § Runtime protocol tool coverage
- .config/nextest.toml (per-target slow-timeout and retry overrides)

## STEPS

1. Make `just test` run every Rust test target. Replace the `--lib` step with the
   full-workspace run, ordered after the WASM build (step 4/7) so
   `wasm_integration` has its plugin. Keep `--no-fail-fast` and the JUnit
   preservation added in #599.

2. Keep a fast inner loop. `just rust-test` (or `just test-fast`) stays `--lib`
   for iteration; `just test` is the gate. Document the distinction in
   rust/CLAUDE.md § Testing so the next author knows which one gates a change.

3. Measure the cost. Report the wall-clock delta for `just test` before and after
   in the PR body. If a specific target is unacceptably slow, give it a
   `.config/nextest.toml` override rather than removing it from the gate.

4. Audit what the change turns on. Running these six targets together for the
   first time may surface pre-existing failures (`tmux_liveness` drives a real
   tmux server; `wasm_integration` needs current WASM). Every failure surfaced is
   either fixed in this PR or filed as its own issue and explicitly quarantined —
   not left red and not silently dropped.

5. State the rule where it will be read: a new test must be reachable from
   `just test`, in rust/CLAUDE.md and the root CLAUDE.md testing section.

## VERIFY

    just test
    just rust-test
    git status --porcelain     # must be empty afterwards

## DONE CRITERIA

- `just test` executes all six Rust integration targets plus the lib tests.
- The runtime-protocol guard from #598 and the liveness tests from #593/#594 run
  without any manual second command.
- The fast/gate distinction is documented in rust/CLAUDE.md.
- Wall-clock delta for `just test` reported in the PR body.
- Any pre-existing failure surfaced is fixed here or filed and quarantined
  visibly; nothing is left red.
- PR filed.

comments.content: Wired the aggregate gate to run all Rust targets after WASM build while retaining just rust-test as the fast --lib loop. The shared runner now preserves JUnit and uses --no-fail-fast for both modes. Fixed the pre-existing wasm_integration nextest failure by assigning binary_id(exomonad-core::wasm_integration) to an explicit one-permit test group; the previous test(wasm_integration) override did not match the binary. Verification: just test passed 1,101 tests across 12 binaries with 5 skipped, plus 60 WASM guest tests and proto freshness; just rust-test passed 910/910 with 3 skipped; cargo fmt --check and git diff --check clean. Baseline just test 55.24s; final 64.74s (+9.50s).

issues.title: Fix lost inbox writes under concurrent delivery
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

The lock-file publication race that was losing Teams inbox writes was fixed without a regression test, and the fix leaks temporary files.

## SYMPTOM

`rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/file_lock.rs::try_create_lock` previously created
the canonical lock path with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` and *then* wrote its metadata. A
contender arriving inside that window read an empty, unparseable lock file,
classified it as corrupt-therefore-stale, and broke it while its owner was still
writing. Two holders then believed they owned the lock and an inbox write was
lost.

Fixed in commit 10b93103: metadata is written to
`.{lock_name}.{pid}.{nanos}.tmp` first, and the canonical path is claimed with
`fs::hard_link`, which still fails `EEXIST` and so preserves mutual exclusion.

The fix is sound. The problems are what surrounds it.

## ROOT CAUSE (of this issue, not of the race)

1. **No regression test.** `git show 10b93103 -- rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/file_lock.rs`
   adds zero `#[test]`. The module already has eight tests, including
   `test_corrupt_lock_file_treated_as_stale` — the exact behavior the race
   exploited — so a home for the test obviously existed. Nothing in the repo now
   fails if `try_create_lock` reverts to writing the canonical path first.

2. **The verification is not reproducible.** The fix was reported as validated by
   "50/50 focused iterations", but no stress harness was committed. Nobody can
   re-run that evidence.

3. **Temporary files leak.** If the process dies between creating
   `.{lock_name}.{pid}.{nanos}.tmp` and `fs::remove_file`, the temp file is
   orphaned. Nothing reaps it. Stale detection only inspects the canonical lock
   name, so these accumulate silently in every inbox directory.

4. **Filed under the wrong heading.** A production data-loss fix in
   `claude-teams-bridge` shipped inside a commit titled "Make Rust test failures
   diagnosable" (#599, test infrastructure). The change has no issue of its own,
   no CHANGELOG entry describing the data loss, and is invisible to anyone
   reading the history for messaging bugs.

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- DO NOT revert or rewrite `try_create_lock`. The hard-link publication is
  correct; this issue adds coverage and cleanup around it.
- DO NOT test the race with `sleep`-based timing. Drive the interleaving
  deterministically, or exercise it with enough concurrent threads that the
  pre-fix code fails reliably and the post-fix code never does.
- DO NOT weaken `test_corrupt_lock_file_treated_as_stale`. A genuinely corrupt
  lock must still be breakable; only the mid-publication window changes.
- DO NOT reap temp files by globbing and deleting on a timer. Tie cleanup to a
  defined owner or a defined lifetime.
- DO NOT mark the new test `#[ignore]` or give it retries.
- No new dependencies.

## READ FIRST

- CLAUDE.md § Logging (silent failures are unacceptable)
- rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md § Delivery Pipeline
- rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/file_lock.rs (all of it; note `try_break_stale`, `is_pid_alive`)
- rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/file_lock.rs:240-360 (existing tests)
- commit 10b93103

## STEPS

1. Add a regression test that fails against the pre-fix implementation. The
   property to assert: while a holder is publishing its lock, a contender never
   observes a breakable lock at the canonical path. Spawn N threads contending for
   one lock path and assert exactly one holder at a time and no lost acquisition
   over many rounds. Verify it actually catches the bug by temporarily reverting
   `try_create_lock` locally before committing.

2. Add a test for the leaked temp file: after a successful acquire/release cycle
   no `.{lock_name}.*.tmp` remains in the directory.

3. Handle orphaned temp files. Either make cleanup crash-safe (claim and unlink
   in an order that leaves nothing behind), or have lock acquisition remove
   temp files whose pid is dead, reusing `is_pid_alive`. Log at `debug` when one
   is reclaimed; never delete a temp file belonging to a live pid.

4. Log the publication path per CLAUDE.md § Logging: `debug` on successful claim,
   `warn` when a stale lock is broken and by which pid. A silently broken lock is
   how this went unnoticed.

5. Add a CHANGELOG entry that names the user-visible symptom (lost inbox writes
   under concurrent delivery), not just the mechanism.

## VERIFY

    nix develop --command cargo nextest run -p claude-teams-bridge
    just rust-test
    just test

## DONE CRITERIA

- A committed test fails against the pre-fix `try_create_lock` and passes now,
  with that verification stated in the PR body.
- No `.tmp` lock artifact survives a normal acquire/release, and orphaned temp
  files from dead pids are reclaimed rather than accumulating.
- Lock claim and stale-break are logged.
- CHANGELOG names the data-loss symptom.
- PR filed.

comments.content: Implemented deterministic publication regression coverage (fails with the pre-fix canonical-create-then-write implementation), dead-PID temp reclamation that preserves live owners, normal-cycle temp cleanup assertions, and debug/warn lock lifecycle logging. Verified: focused tests pass; pre-fix negative run fails with observed_breakable=true; Nix-shell claude-teams-bridge suite passes 65/65 with 2 skipped; cargo fmt --check and git diff --check clean.

issues.title: fix: intermittent rust-test failure is unidentifiable because fail-fast discards the test name
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

`just rust-test` failed intermittently and fail-fast discarded the failing test's identity, leaving no way to diagnose it.

## SYMPTOM

Observed once on branch gh-573/watcher-review-message-test at 52ca66a6:

    $ just rust-test
    warning: 349/909 tests were not run due to test failure
    error: test run failed
    error: Recipe `rust-test` failed on line 29 with exit code 100

The name of the failing test never appeared in the output. Three immediately
subsequent runs — including `cargo nextest run --workspace --lib --no-fail-fast` —
reported `909 tests run: 909 passed, 3 skipped`. Not reproducible on demand.

Two distinct problems:

1. An intermittent failure exists somewhere in the workspace lib tests.
2. When it fires, the operator cannot tell which test failed, so it cannot be
   investigated after the fact.

Problem 2 is the one that must be fixed first — without it, problem 1 is
undiagnosable.

## ROOT CAUSE

`just rust-test` (justfile:28-29) runs `cargo nextest run --workspace --lib` with
nextest's default fail-fast behavior. On first failure the run aborts; the summary
reports a count of un-run tests and the recipe exits non-zero, but the failing
test's name is not surfaced in the tail of the output that an operator or agent
actually reads.

`.config/nextest.toml` sets `failure-output = "immediate"` and writes JUnit to
`target/nextest/default/junit.xml`, so the identity is recoverable in principle —
but the next run overwrites that file, and nothing points an operator at it.

Likely flake surface, unverified: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs`
carries several `#[serial_test::serial]` tests that touch tmux and process
environment. Those are the tests whose isolation depends on runtime state rather
than on inputs. Confirm before assuming.

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- DO NOT add a blanket `retries = N` to the default profile to make it green.
  Retrying an unidentified flake hides it permanently.
- DO NOT mark a test `#[ignore]` to silence it.
- DO NOT "fix" a flake you have not reproduced and whose mechanism you cannot
  state. If the cause is not identified, the deliverable is the diagnosis, not a
  code change.
- DO NOT add sleeps to stabilize timing.
- DO NOT change the semantics of any test to make it pass.
- No new dependencies.

## READ FIRST

- justfile:28-29 (`rust-test`), :56-72 (`test`)
- .config/nextest.toml
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs (the `#[serial_test::serial]` tests)
- rust/CLAUDE.md § Testing (note the TMPDIR / outside-repository tempdir precondition)

## STEPS

1. Make the failure identifiable. Run the workspace lib tests with
   `--no-fail-fast` in `just rust-test` so a failing run names every failure
   instead of aborting at the first. Keep `failure-output = "immediate"`.

2. Preserve the evidence. Either stop overwriting `junit.xml` per run (timestamped
   or `--retain` behavior), or have the recipe echo the JUnit path on failure so
   the next operator knows where to look. One mechanism, documented in
   rust/CLAUDE.md § Testing.

3. Hunt the flake with the improved output: run the workspace lib tests in a loop
   (at least 50 iterations) at default concurrency and record any failure with its
   name and output. Do this before changing any test.

4. If a flake is identified: state the mechanism (shared tmux server, shared env
   var, TMPDIR, filesystem path collision, port, clock) in the issue, then fix the
   isolation at its source. If it turns out to be a test that depends on the host
   tmux server, that is the same class of coupling as #593/#594 and should be cut,
   not serialized harder.

5. If 50+ iterations do not reproduce, say so explicitly and close with steps 1-2
   delivered. A documented non-reproduction plus permanent failure visibility is a
   valid outcome; a silent green is not.

## VERIFY

    just rust-test
    for i in $(seq 1 50); do just rust-test || break; done
    just test

## DONE CRITERIA

- A failing `just rust-test` names every failing test in its output.
- The JUnit record of a failing run survives long enough to be read, and
  rust/CLAUDE.md says where it is.
- Either the flake is identified with a stated mechanism and fixed at its source,
  or a 50+ iteration non-reproduction is recorded in the issue.
- No test was retried, ignored, or weakened to reach green.
- PR filed.

comments.content: Implemented and verified #599. just rust-test now uses --no-fail-fast. On failure it preserves target/nextest/default/junit.xml as a unique target/nextest/failures/junit-*.xml and prints the path; nextest config corrected to path = "junit.xml" because the configured path was profile-relative and previously produced no report. rust/CLAUDE.md documents the workflow. Diagnosis: FileLock published an empty canonical lock file before serializing metadata; a competing writer could treat that transient file as corrupt/stale, delete the active lock, and lose one read-modify-write update in claude-teams-bridge::inbox::tests::test_concurrent_writes_no_lost_messages. The source fix writes and syncs metadata in a temporary inode, atomically claims the canonical path with hard_link, and only the owner cleans its temp file. The failure reproduced in the improved full workspace hunt as the named concurrent-writes test; after the fix, 50/50 focused iterations passed, just rust-test passed (908/908, 3 skipped), cargo fmt --all --check passed, and just test passed all 7 stages including 60 WASM tests and proto freshness.

issues.title: fix: derive runtime-protocol tool manifest from Haskell role configs instead of mirroring it
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

The runtime-protocol drift guard added in #596 mirrors the Haskell role tool grants in a hand-maintained Rust list, so the drift it was meant to close can still happen silently.

## SYMPTOM

`test_runtime_protocols_list_every_granted_mcp_tool`
(rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:2498) asserts each
embedded runtime protocol string names every tool in `DEV_PROTOCOL_TOOLS` /
`WORKER_PROTOCOL_TOOLS` / `REVIEWER_PROTOCOL_TOOLS` (spawn.rs:2458-2494). Those
constants carry their own comment:

    // These manifests mirror the Tools records in the Haskell role configs.

Nothing checks that the mirror is accurate. Grant a new tool in
`.exo/roles/devswarm/DevRole.hs` and the test still passes, because
`DEV_PROTOCOL_TOOLS` was not updated either. The guard only fires when someone
updates the Rust manifest and forgets the protocol prose — the narrower half of
the failure.

This is the same class of defect as #596 itself (`check_inbox` was granted in
`DevRole.hs:137` and named in no runtime protocol), relocated one level up. It is
now two hand-maintained lists instead of one.

## ROOT CAUSE

Role tool grants are declared in Haskell (`.exo/roles/devswarm/*Role.hs`, the
`Tools` records) and are the single source of truth per CLAUDE.md § All Tools and
Hooks in Haskell WASM. The Rust host has no machine-readable view of them, so the
test transcribes them by hand.

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- DO NOT widen the hand-maintained manifest or add more roles to it. That deepens
  the defect.
- DO NOT parse `*Role.hs` with a regex from Rust. A brittle text scrape of Haskell
  source is a new failure mode, not a fix.
- DO NOT move tool definitions out of Haskell. Haskell WASM stays the single
  source of truth for tool definitions.
- DO NOT make the check a warning. It must fail the build.
- DO NOT delete the existing test until its replacement covers strictly more.
- No new dependencies.

## READ FIRST

- CLAUDE.md § All Tools and Hooks in Haskell WASM, § Single Code Path
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:2454-2534 (manifests + test)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:261-490 (protocol constants)
- .exo/roles/devswarm/DevRole.hs, WorkerRole.hs, ReviewerRole.hs (the `Tools` records)
- haskell/wasm-guest/CLAUDE.md (role/tool registration)

## STEPS

1. Decide where the derived manifest comes from. Preferred: the WASM guest already
   answers `handle_list_tools` per role — have the check ask the built WASM for each
   role's tool list rather than transcribing it. That reuses the existing dispatch
   path and cannot drift by construction.

   If a build-time WASM call is not workable in a unit test, emit a generated
   manifest from the Haskell role configs as part of the WASM build and read that
   file from the test. Generated, committed, and covered by a freshness check
   (`just proto-check` is the existing precedent for that pattern).

2. Rewrite `test_runtime_protocols_list_every_granted_mcp_tool` against the derived
   list. Keep the assertion shape (`- {tool}:` present in the protocol string) and
   the per-runtime coverage.

3. Delete `DEV_PROTOCOL_TOOLS`, `WORKER_PROTOCOL_TOOLS`, `REVIEWER_PROTOCOL_TOOLS`
   once the derived source is in place. Two lists is the bug.

4. Add the negative test: a role granting a tool absent from its runtime protocol
   must fail. Prove the guard actually fires — the current one has never been shown
   to fail.

5. If a tool is intentionally omitted from a runtime protocol, make that explicit
   and named in one place, not implicit by absence from a manifest.

## VERIFY

    nix develop --command cargo nextest run -p exomonad-core --lib
    just wasm-guest-test
    just test

## DONE CRITERIA

- The runtime-protocol check derives its tool list from the Haskell role configs
  (via WASM or a generated, freshness-checked manifest) — no transcribed list.
- Adding a tool to a role's `Tools` record without updating that role's runtime
  protocol text fails the build, demonstrated by a test that fails when the guard
  is bypassed.
- The three hand-maintained constants are gone.
- Intentional omissions are explicit and documented in one place.
- `just test` green.
- PR filed.

## CONTEXT

Follow-up to #596 (commit 606be077). #596 is correct and should stay closed — the
protocols now name `check_inbox` and role context reaches OpenCode and Codex. This
issue only hardens the guard that is supposed to keep it that way.

comments.content: Implemented the guard against protocol/tool drift using the compiled Haskell WASM as the source of truth: the integration test calls handle_list_tools for dev, worker, and reviewer and checks all five OpenCode/Codex protocol strings. Deleted the three mirrored Rust manifests. Added a test proving the guard reports a missing tool. Documented the contract in rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md. Verification: cargo fmt --all --check passed; just wasm-all passed; targeted guard and derived WASM integration tests passed. Full just test-cargo-all reached the separate #599 tmux liveness flake routing_target_process_alive_rejects_dead_command_in_retained_window.

issues.title: fix: check-fmt and proto-check are mutually exclusive on generated Haskell proto
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

`just check-fmt` and `just proto-check` cannot both pass: the Haskell proto generator emits code ormolu rejects, so each gate is only green while the other is red.

## SYMPTOM

On branch gh-573/watcher-review-message-test at abb0bcf8:

    just check-fmt    PASSES
    just proto-check  FAILS
      ERROR: Generated proto files are out of date.
      haskell/proto/src/Effects/Agent.hs | 372 +++++++-------
      1 file changed, 216 insertions(+), 156 deletions(-)

`just test` therefore fails at step 6/6. Before abb0bcf8 the polarity was
reversed: `check-fmt` failed on that same file and `proto-check` passed.

Confirmed the drift predates abb0bcf8 — the regenerated output differs from the
1fe42d67 blob too (248 insertions / 181 deletions), so `haskell/proto/src/Effects/Agent.hs`
first diverged from generator output at 8d702fbd.

## ROOT CAUSE

`proto-codegen/generate.sh` (invoked by `just proto-gen-haskell`) does not run
ormolu on its output. `just check-fmt` runs
`ormolu --mode check` over every non-vendored `haskell/**/*.hs`, which includes
`haskell/proto/src/`. So generator output is permanently unformatted, and the
only way to satisfy `check-fmt` is to hand-format generated code — which
`proto-check` then reports as drift, and which the next `just proto-gen` silently
reverts.

Two gates, one file, mutually exclusive. Whichever was fixed most recently is the
one that is green.

Secondary: `proto-check` regenerates **into the working tree** and leaves the
regenerated file modified on failure (justfile `proto-check` recipe). Running it
dirties the repo, which matters because spawn and issue-close paths refuse to act
on a dirty worktree.

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- DO NOT hand-format generated code again. It is reverted by the next proto-gen.
- DO NOT exclude `haskell/proto/src/` from check-fmt as the fix without deciding
  the policy — silently unformatted generated code is a choice, make it explicitly.
- DO NOT add a third gate that reconciles the other two.
- DO NOT commit a regenerated Agent.hs without confirming it is byte-identical to
  generator output on a clean tree.
- No new dependencies; ormolu is already in the dev shell.

## READ FIRST

- justfile: `check-fmt` (:19), `proto-gen-haskell` (:194), `proto-check` (:72), `test` (:56)
- proto-codegen/generate.sh
- haskell/proto/src/Effects/Agent.hs (the diverged file)
- haskell/CLAUDE.md

## STEPS

1. Pick one policy and implement it:
   - **Preferred:** run ormolu as the last step of `proto-codegen/generate.sh`, so
     generated output is formatted at birth. Both gates then agree.
   - Alternative: exclude `haskell/proto/src/` from `check-fmt` and document in
     haskell/CLAUDE.md that generated proto is not ormolu-managed.
   Whichever is chosen, record it in haskell/CLAUDE.md.

2. Regenerate `haskell/proto/src/` on a clean tree under the new policy and commit
   the result, so `proto-check` and `check-fmt` are both green from the same bytes.

3. Make `proto-check` non-destructive: regenerate into a temp directory and diff,
   or restore the tree on failure. A check must not dirty the worktree.

4. Add `just check-fmt` to the `just test` sequence. It is currently absent, which
   is why the branch carried a red fmt gate through several commits.

## VERIFY

    git status --porcelain            # must be empty before and after
    just proto-check
    just check-fmt
    just test

## DONE CRITERIA

- `just check-fmt`, `just proto-check`, and `just test` all pass on a clean tree.
- `git status` is clean after running `just proto-check`.

issues.title: fix: OpenCode/Codex agents never learn check_inbox and get role context at an unread path
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

OpenCode and Codex agents are granted check_inbox but are never told it exists, and their role context is written to a path their runtime does not read. Durable inbox guidance is delivered and never consumed.

## SYMPTOM

Observed on /home/goya/beast-workspace/workspace, agent issue-715-fmt-emitter-opencode
(OpenCode dev leaf, PR #27), across 4 invocations over ~1.5 hours:

    .exo/inbox.db messages:  11 of 11 to the dev leaf have read_at = NULL
                             every one has notified_at set (delivery worked)
    agent_inbox_meta:        last_check_inbox_at = NULL   -- never called, ever
                             poke_backoff_secs escalated 30 -> 240
    root (Claude) in the same db: last_check_inbox_at set, its mail read

Delivery is not the problem. Routing is not the problem. The agent never calls
`check_inbox`, so TL corrections and CI-status events sit unread while the TL waits.

## ROOT CAUSE

Two independent defects, both in per-runtime context delivery.

**A. `check_inbox` is absent from every embedded runtime protocol.**

rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs defines five protocol
constants injected into non-Claude agents:

    :253  CODEX_TL_RUNTIME_NOTES
    :261  OPENCODE_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS
    :298  OPENCODE_WORKER_INSTRUCTIONS
    :332  CODEX_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS
    :366  CODEX_WORKER_INSTRUCTIONS
    :429  CODEX_REVIEWER_INSTRUCTIONS

`grep -n check_inbox` over that file returns nothing. None of them mention it.
`OPENCODE_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS` lists exactly four MCP tools — file_pr,
notify_parent, send_tmux_message, send_mailbox_message — and separately says
"continue consuming durable inbox guidance" without ever naming the tool that
does it. The tool IS granted: .exo/roles/devswarm/DevRole.hs:137 binds
`checkInbox :: mode :- CheckInbox`. The agent simply does not know it exists.

**B. The role context markdown lands where the runtime cannot read it.**

spawn.rs:1415-1423 writes the OpenCode role context to
`<worktree>/.claude/rules/exomonad_role.md`. That is a Claude Code path.
OpenCode reads `AGENTS.md` and `opencode.json.instructions`; neither references
it. spawn.rs:1424+ does the same for Codex with `.codex/exomonad_role.md`.

In the observed worktree the file is additionally a **dangling symlink**:

    .claude/rules/exomonad_role.md -> ../../../../.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md

which escapes the worktree, has no target, and names the *root* role for a *dev*
agent. Nothing failed loudly — the copy is `warn!`-on-error and non-fatal.

So `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/dev.md:8` ("Call `check_inbox` at the start of
each task and after completing each major step") reaches Claude and Gemini and
reaches neither OpenCode nor Codex.

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- DO NOT fix this by adding a line about check_inbox to one constant. The defect
  is that tool grants and runtime protocol text are maintained independently and
  drift. Fix the drift, then the text.
- DO NOT write role context to a runtime path without evidence that runtime loads
  it. Cite the runtime's documented context mechanism in the code comment.
- DO NOT leave the context copy silently non-fatal. A role agent spawned without
  its role context is a broken agent; failing to place it must be loud.
- DO NOT special-case Claude. Every runtime gets the same guarantee.
- DO NOT add a symlink fallback or a path-guessing heuristic. Prefer failure.
- No new dependencies.

## READ FIRST

- CLAUDE.md — "All Tools and Hooks in Haskell WASM", Logging rules
- .claude/rules/orientation.md — harness agnosticism is a design priority
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:253-470 (protocol constants)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1390-1440 (per-runtime context copy)
- .exo/roles/devswarm/DevRole.hs, WorkerRole.hs, ReviewerRole.hs (tool grants)
- .exo/roles/devswarm/context/dev.md (the guidance that never arrives)

## STEPS

1. Add `check_inbox` to every embedded protocol constant that belongs to a role
   granted the tool, with the same instruction dev.md gives: call it at the start
   of the assignment and after each major step, and treat unread guidance as
   authoritative TL direction. Also state that unread mail piggybacks on MCP tool
   results.

2. Fix the context destination per runtime so it is actually loaded:
   - OpenCode: append the role context to `opencode.json.instructions`, or write
     it to a path listed there. Do not write to `.claude/rules/`.
   - Codex: place it where `.codex/config.toml` declares developer instructions.
   Remove the `.claude/rules/exomonad_role.md` write for non-Claude runtimes.

3. Make placement failure loud. If the resolved role context cannot be written to
   a location the target runtime loads, fail the spawn with a clear error instead
   of `warn!` and continue.

4. Close the drift: add a check that every MCP tool name a role grants appears in
   that role's runtime protocol text (or is explicitly listed as intentionally
   omitted). A unit test over the constants plus the role tool lists is enough;
   this is the regression that lets the next tool go unmentioned.

5. Clean up the stale artifact: nothing should create a symlink from a worktree
   into `.exo/roles/`. Verify the copy is a real file write.

## VERIFY

    nix develop --command cargo nextest run -p exomonad-core --lib
    just wasm-guest-test
    nix develop --command cargo fmt --all --check
    just e2e-cross-harness-inbox

## DONE CRITERIA

- Every runtime protocol constant names `check_inbox` where the role grants it.
- Role context for OpenCode and Codex is placed where that runtime documents it
  loads context, and the `.claude/rules/` write for non-Claude runtimes is gone.
- Missing/unplaceable role context fails the spawn loudly.
- A test fails if a role grants a tool its runtime protocol never mentions.
- No symlinked role context in spawned worktrees.
- PR filed.

## OUT OF SCOPE

Whether OpenCode/Codex should get a push-style inbox rather than polling
`check_inbox` is a separate design question. This issue only makes the existing
pull mechanism reachable.

comments.content: Implemented runtime messaging/context delivery. All five OpenCode/Codex protocols now enumerate check_inbox and their granted MCP tools with a drift regression test; OpenCode instructions and Codex developer_instructions include resolved role context; missing context fails config generation; non-Claude .claude/rules and standalone Codex context writes are gone. Verification: focused agent-control suite 90/90, just wasm-guest-test 60/60, cargo fmt/check clean, harness syntax check passes. Cross-harness E2E reached startup but was blocked by unrelated port 7433 already in use; cleanup removed its temp environment.

issues.title: fix: agent routing has two stores with opposite lifetimes (blank pane + stale window id)
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Agent routing is stored in two places with opposite lifetimes, so an exited agent shows a blank pane and a stale window id at the same time.

## SYMPTOM

`poll_workers` renders a row with `PANE = "-"` and `ALIVE = yes` simultaneously, and the
TL narrates a stale window id ("still live in tmux window @17") for a window that no
longer exists. Observed in /home/goya/beast-workspace/workspace against
issue-715-fmt-emitter-opencode:

    .exo/agents/issue-715-fmt-emitter-opencode/
      routing.json      MISSING
      exited_at         1785731541
      exit_code         0
      invocation.json   { "routing": { "window_id": "@17" }, "status": "exited", ... }

    tmux list-windows -a  =>  @0 Server, @1 TL, @2 Watcher     (no @17)

The blank pane column next to a live-looking row is what makes a TL distrust its own
snapshot and hand-wait instead of acting.

## ROOT CAUSE

Routing is persisted twice, with opposite lifetimes and no shared vocabulary for
"retired":

1. `.exo/agents/<agent>/routing.json` — written at spawn finalization
   (services/agent_control/mod.rs:1027, guarded by `has_delivery_target()`), then
   **deleted** by the orphan reconciler when `exited_at` appears
   (services/orphan_reconciler.rs:275-280, "Cleaned routing for exited agent").
2. `.exo/agents/<agent>/invocation.json` `.routing` — written by `start_invocation`,
   and **never invalidated**. It retains the window id of the last invocation forever
   as historical metadata.

Three consequences:

- **poll_workers / list_agents** read routing.json for the pane column, so every
  cleanly-exited agent renders `-`. There is no rendering for "routing retired after
  clean exit" distinct from "no routing was ever recorded", which are very different
  conditions for a TL deciding whether to resume.
- **orphan_reconciler.rs:266-272** skips session timeout entirely once routing.json is
  gone ("Skipping session timeout because routing.json is missing"). After the
  reconciler deletes the file itself, that agent is permanently exempt from timeout
  reconciliation. The cleanup path disables the very path that would have caught it.
- **routing_liveness** (services/agent_control/cleanup.rs:32-50) falls back to
  `invocation.routing` and emits `warn!("Using routing captured by current invocation
  metadata")` when routing.json is unreadable. For a cleanly-exited agent this is the
  expected steady state, so the normal case is logged as an anomaly, burying real ones.

The liveness *decision* is correct today — `routing_liveness` short-circuits on
`exited_at` before consulting tmux (#593, #594 landed). This issue is about the
*reported* routing being unusable and self-contradictory, and about the reconciler
exemption the deletion creates.

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- DO NOT "fix" this by keeping routing.json around forever. Stale delivery targets are
  what #593 was about; the answer is an explicit retired state, not immortal routing.
- DO NOT add a third routing store. Two is already the bug.
- DO NOT make poll_workers infer routing by scanning tmux. Persisted state is the
  source of truth; tmux is the probe.
- DO NOT change liveness semantics. `exited_at` / `invocation.status` precedence stays
  exactly as #594 left it.
- DO NOT silence the routing_liveness warn by deleting the log line. Distinguish the
  expected post-exit case from a genuine unreadable-routing case and log accordingly.
- No new dependencies. Rust-only.

## READ FIRST

- rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md — "Agent Resume and Liveness Contract", "Ownership versus invocation"
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/mod.rs:1005-1040 (spawn finalization, routing write)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/cleanup.rs:12-72 (routing_liveness)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs:255-300 (routing deletion + timeout skip)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/domain.rs:837-880 (RoutingInfo, write_to_dir, read_from_dir)
- rust/exomonad-core/tests/tmux_liveness.rs (existing liveness test harness)

## STEPS

1. Decide and document the retired-routing representation. Preferred: stop deleting
   routing.json in orphan_reconciler.rs and instead let `exited_at` + invocation
   status be the retirement signal, so routing.json remains readable history while
   liveness continues to short-circuit on `exited_at`. Whatever is chosen, record it in
   rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md under the liveness contract.

2. Remove the reconciler self-exemption at orphan_reconciler.rs:266-272. A missing
   routing.json must not silently exempt an agent from timeout reconciliation — handle
   it explicitly (reconcile using invocation routing, or skip with a reason that
   distinguishes never-had-routing from retired).

3. Make the agent-status surface report routing honestly. `poll_workers` and
   `list_agents` must distinguish, in their output:
     - live routing target (window/pane id, alive)
     - retired routing (last known window/pane id, agent exited, exit code)
     - no routing ever recorded (genuine anomaly)
   `-` for all three is the defect. Include the last-known id for the retired case so a
   TL can correlate against tmux history instead of guessing.

4. Narrow the routing_liveness warn at cleanup.rs:35-48: expected post-exit fallback is
   `debug!`, genuinely unreadable/corrupt routing stays `warn!`.

5. Tests. Add to rust/exomonad-core/tests/ (extend tmux_liveness.rs or a sibling):
     - agent dir with exited_at + invocation routing and no routing.json reports
       retired-with-last-known-id, not blank, and reports not-alive
     - agent dir with neither routing.json nor invocation routing reports the
       no-routing-recorded case distinctly
     - reconciler does not permanently exempt an agent whose routing.json is absent
   Pure/fixture-driven where possible; use the existing tmux harness only where a real
   probe is required.

## VERIFY

    nix develop --command cargo nextest run -p exomonad-core
    nix develop --command cargo fmt --all --check
    nix develop --command cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

## DONE CRITERIA

- One documented lifetime for agent routing, recorded in rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md.
- poll_workers/list_agents never render a bare `-` for an agent that had routing; the
  three states above are distinguishable in the output.
- The reconciler no longer exempts agents whose routing.json it deleted.
- New tests pass; full exomonad-core suite green; fmt and clippy clean.
- PR filed.

## CONTEXT — related churn observed, not in scope here

The same agent was resumed twice in 16 minutes, each invocation exiting cleanly without
reaching merge-ready:

    23:14:35 -> 23:24:14  window @5,  exit 0, head 71f7b68
    23:30:50 -> 23:32:21  window @17, exit 0, head 03927d9  (91 seconds)

Clean short exits that advance the head SHA without converging are a separate review-loop
question. File separately if it recurs.
