issues.title: fix: window existence is not process liveness (dead runtime keeps window alive)
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Follow-up to #593. Fixing the tmux probe makes window existence *accurate*, but window existence still is not agent liveness.

A runtime that exits leaving a shell in the window — or a window with remain-on-exit — keeps the window addressable, so routing_target_alive() reports the owner live forever. resume_pr (rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs:2350) then refuses to start a fresh invocation, and cleanup/orphan reconciliation never disposes the worktree.

routing_liveness (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/cleanup.rs:16) already has two stronger signals it consults *before* the tmux probe: the .exo/agents/<agent>/exited_at marker, and invocation.status via read_invocation(). The tmux probe is the last word and overrides neither — the ordering and precedence need to be reconsidered, and a process-level signal added.

DO NOT start this before #593 lands; it builds on the corrected probe.

Scope to decide during design:
- Whether #{pane_dead} / #{pane_current_command} is a sufficient process signal per runtime (claude, opencode, codex, gemini, shoal all differ in what they leave behind).
- Whether the spawned window should use remain-on-exit at all, and what writes exited_at on a clean runtime exit.
- Precedence between exited_at, invocation.status, and the tmux probe when they disagree.

Must include tests. Extend rust/exomonad-core/tests/tmux_liveness.rs with a case where the window survives but its command has exited.

comments.content: Dependency #593 is complete and committed on main as 80dda861. The exact session-scoped window/pane probes now make routing_target_alive accurate for stale IDs. This issue remains open as the separate process-level liveness follow-up; no #594 code was changed in the #593 implementation.

Implemented and verified process-level liveness. routing_liveness now treats an exit_code marker as dead before tmux probing, preserves exited_at and terminal invocation-status precedence, verifies exact target existence, then requires the exact routed pane to report pane_dead=0. Added session-scoped pane process parsing and a real-tmux regression where remain-on-exit retains a window after its shell exits. Verification: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test -p exomonad-core services::tmux_ipc::tests (25 passed); cargo test -p exomonad-core --test tmux_liveness -- --nocapture (8 passed); cargo test -p exomonad-core --tests --quiet (820 unit, 8 mock-GitHub, 8 tmux, 39 WASM; 3 ignored); no leftover tmux sessions. cargo clippy -p exomonad-core --all-targets -- -D warnings remains blocked by the same 17 pre-existing repository warnings and reports no new warning from this change.

issues.title: fix: tmux liveness probes always report alive (wedges resume_pr and spawn)
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

tmux liveness probes always return true, so an exited agent is permanently "live".

## SYMPTOM

A root TL cannot spawn or resume anything. `resume_pr` rejects with "owner is still
live in tmux window @3" and `list_agents` reports `is_alive: true` for an agent whose
window does not exist. Verified on the live `workspace` session (windows @0/@1/@2 only):

    tmux display-message -t @3     -p "" ; echo $?   # 0
    tmux display-message -t @99999 -p "" ; echo $?   # 0
    tmux display-message -t %77    -p "" ; echo $?   # 0
    tmux display-message -t bogus  -p "" ; echo $?   # 0

`tmux display-message` does not fail on an unresolvable target, so the probe is a
constant-true function.

## ROOT CAUSE

rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs:764 `TmuxIpc::window_exists` and :792
`TmuxIpc::pane_exists` both shell out to `tmux display-message -t <id> -p ""` and
return `status.success()`. Two defects:

1. `display-message` exits 0 for any target, existing or not.
2. Neither probe is session-scoped, unlike `TmuxIpc::list_windows` (:285) which
   passes `-t <session>`. tmux ids are server-global, so once (1) is fixed a
   window belonging to a different session would still read as alive.

Blast radius — every caller of `routing_target_alive` (tmux_ipc.rs:806) inherits
"always alive":

  - handlers/agent.rs:2350          resume_pr readiness guard (wedges the tree)
  - handlers/agent.rs:3109          agent liveness reporting
  - handlers/session.rs:595         session liveness
  - services/agent_control/cleanup.rs:65   routing_liveness -> list_agents, dispose/cleanup safety
  - services/agent_control/mod.rs:1105     invocation liveness
  - services/orphan_reconciler.rs:462      orphan reconciliation
  - services/delivery.rs:1104              delivery target liveness
  - services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1088/1090/1159/1775  spawn idempotency

No test covers either probe. The `tmux_ipc` unit tests only exercise id parsing
and `qualify_tmux_target`.

## SCAFFOLDING ALREADY LANDED

rust/exomonad-core/tests/tmux_liveness.rs — 7 integration tests driving a real
tmux server, each in its own uniquely named session, torn down on Drop, skipped
when `tmux` is absent. Current state:

    nix develop --command cargo nextest run -p exomonad-core --test tmux_liveness
    => 7 tests run: 2 passed, 5 failed

Passing (positive cases, already correct):
  - window_exists_reports_true_for_a_live_window
  - routing_target_alive_reports_true_for_current_routing

Failing (the bug):
  - window_exists_reports_false_for_an_id_that_was_never_created
  - window_exists_reports_false_after_the_window_is_killed
  - window_exists_is_scoped_to_the_probing_session
  - pane_exists_reports_false_for_an_id_that_was_never_created
  - routing_target_alive_reports_false_for_stale_routing

## ANTI-PATTERNS

- DO NOT keep `display-message` as the probe with an added `-p '#{window_id}'`
  string comparison as the only check. Enumerate and match instead — it is one
  call, session-scoped, and has no target-resolution fallback semantics.
- DO NOT add a new probe alongside the old one. `window_exists`/`pane_exists`
  are the single code path; rewrite them in place.
- DO NOT weaken or delete any test in tests/tmux_liveness.rs to make it pass.
- DO NOT add dependencies. No new crates.
- DO NOT add a `todo!()`, a fallback branch, or an "assume alive on error"
  heuristic. On probe failure, log and return the error; callers already decide.
- DO NOT change `qualify_tmux_target`, the injection path, or any caller's
  logic. This issue is the probe only.
- DO NOT touch Haskell or proto. Rust-only change.

## READ FIRST

- CLAUDE.md (root) — Logging rules, Single Code Path rule
- .claude/rules/rust.md
- rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md — "Agent Resume and Liveness Contract"
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs:285-320 (list_windows, the correct pattern)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs:760-814 (window_exists, pane_exists, routing_target_alive)
- rust/exomonad-core/tests/tmux_liveness.rs

## STEPS

1. In rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs, rewrite `window_exists` to
   enumerate the probing session's windows and match on id:

       pub async fn window_exists(&self, window_id: &WindowId) -> Result<bool> {
           let output = Command::new("tmux")
               .args(["list-windows", "-t", &self.session_name, "-F", "#{window_id}"])
               .output()
               .await
               .context("Failed to run tmux list-windows")?;
           if !output.status.success() {
               let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
               if session_missing(&stderr) {
                   return Ok(false);
               }
               anyhow::bail!("tmux list-windows failed: {}", stderr);
           }
           Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout)
               .lines()
               .any(|line| line.trim() == window_id.as_str()))
       }

   A missing session means no live target, not an error — that is the only
   tolerated non-success. Add a small private helper for that stderr check
   rather than inlining a bare string match twice.

2. Rewrite `pane_exists` the same way with
   `["list-panes", "-a", "-F", "#{session_name}\t#{pane_id}"]`, keeping only
   rows whose session equals `self.session_name`. `list-panes -t <session>`
   lists panes of the session's *current window* only, so `-a` plus an explicit
   session filter is required — do not use `-t <session>`.

3. Add tracing per the root CLAUDE.md logging rules: `debug!` the probe target
   and outcome, `warn!` on a non-success exit that is not a missing session.

4. Leave `routing_target_alive` as is — it becomes correct once the two probes are.

5. Add a unit test in the `tmux_ipc` `mod tests` block for the pure parsing
   introduced in steps 1-2 (id matching against a captured listing, and the
   session filter for panes). Keep it pure — no tmux process in unit tests.

## VERIFY

    nix develop --command cargo nextest run -p exomonad-core --test tmux_liveness
    nix develop --command cargo nextest run -p exomonad-core
    nix develop --command cargo fmt --all --check
    nix develop --command cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

## DONE CRITERIA

- All 7 tests in tests/tmux_liveness.rs pass, unmodified.
- `cargo nextest run -p exomonad-core` is green; no other test regressed.
- fmt and clippy clean.
- Only rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs is modified (plus its inline
  unit tests). No caller changed, no new dependency, no placeholder.
- PR filed.

## OUT OF SCOPE (file follow-up, do not fix here)

Window existence still is not process liveness: a runtime that exits leaving a
shell (or `remain-on-exit`) keeps the window, so the owner reads as live. That
needs a `#{pane_dead}` / process signal reconciled against `exited_at` and the
invocation status, and is a separate issue.

## OPERATOR WORKAROUND WHILE THIS IS OPEN

`routing_liveness` (services/agent_control/cleanup.rs:16) short-circuits to
`Some(false)` when `.exo/agents/<agent>/exited_at` exists. Touching that file
for a known-dead owner unwedges `resume_pr` without a rebuild.

Missing sessions/no tmux server return false, other tmux failures error, and probes emit debug/warn telemetry. Added pure parser unit coverage and retained the 7-test real-tmux scaffold in tests/tmux_liveness.rs. issues.title: list_agents reports stale is_alive/last_check_inbox_at for resumed agents (reporting only)
issues.description:
list_agents (rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs:1548-1597) surfaces two potentially misleading fields for a dev-worker resumed via resume_pr:

1. last_check_inbox_at stays 0/stale because it is a pull-based heartbeat written only by InboxStore::drain_unread on check_inbox (inbox_store.rs:129-159) -- resume_existing_pr (agent.rs:2181-2313) never refreshes it, nor does notify_parent, commits, or pushes.
2. is_alive (agent.rs:3311-3317) is recomputed live from tmux window-name match + exited_at tombstone, so a false reading after resume may indicate a window-name mismatch introduced by owner-slug reuse in resume_pr, separate from the heartbeat issue.

Unlike #574's sibling subissue, this path is NOT destructive -- cleanup_leaf/dispose_verified_orphan already re-verify liveness live at disposal time (agent.rs:2003-2020) -- but it misleads the TL reading list_agents into thinking a resumed, actively-working dev-worker is dead or unresponsive.

Fix direction: either (a) have resume_pr write a heartbeat refresh so last_check_inbox_at reflects resume time, or (b) have list_agents reconcile against the same live tmux/Chainlink signal that session_status/poll_workers already use (routing_alive, session.rs:372-420) instead of surfacing the raw pull-based heartbeat as if it were current. Needs a test asserting list_agents does not report is_alive:false / last_check_inbox_at:0 for a freshly-resumed, live agent.

comments.content: Implemented in e919ae66. list_agents now reports routing-aware liveness and separate resume activity metadata without changing inbox heartbeat semantics. Focused agent-handler tests pass.

issues.title: orphan_reconciler kills resumed dev-workers on age alone, no activity check
issues.description:
reconcile_session_timeouts (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs:220-316) computes age_secs = now - spawned_at and unconditionally calls kill_agent_window once age_secs exceeds the limit, with no check of recent activity (no last_check_inbox_at, no tool-call/commit recency), beyond an exited_at tombstone short-circuit (lines 266-273).

This is the destructive half of #574: a dev-worker resumed via resume_pr past the session-time limit, without an intervening check_inbox call, can be killed mid-task even though it is actively committing/pushing.

Fix direction: before killing, re-verify liveness the same way cleanup_leaf/dispose_verified_orphan already do (live tmux check via orphan_agent_window_alive, agent.rs:2003-2020) instead of relying solely on the spawned_at age checkpoint. Also confirm whether finalize_spawn (agent_control/mod.rs:963-994) is invoked on the resume_pr path (spawn.rs:1642+) to refresh spawned_at, or is skipped when tab_alive is already true -- if skipped, that alone may explain premature timeouts for resumed agents.

Needs a test per project convention (no feature ships without one): a resumed agent that is actively producing tmux/commit activity past the nominal session-time limit must NOT be killed by reconcile_session_timeouts.

Actual: 

Root cause: last_check_inbox_at (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs:129-159, agent_inbox_meta table) is a PULL-based heartbeat, written only when the agent calls check_inbox (sole write site: InboxHandler::check, rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/inbox.rs:41-65). issues.title: Add reviewer round limit override to exomonad init

comments.content:
## Objective
Expose the reviewer convergence cap through `exomonad init` as an explicit session override. An explicit `--reviewer-max-rounds N` value must take precedence over `.exo/review-policy.toml`; when omitted, preserve the existing policy-file/default behavior.

## ANTI-PATTERNS
- Do not silently rewrite `.exo/review-policy.toml` when the init flag is supplied.
- Do not bypass the watcher policy loader or mutate persisted watcher state as part of ordinary init.
- Do not allow zero/invalid round limits that disable reviewer creation without a clear validation error.
- Do not change precedence for direct `exomonad serve` or existing config-file workflows unless required to carry the explicit init override safely.

## READ FIRST
- `rust/exomonad/src/main.rs` — `Init` CLI definition and dispatch
- `rust/exomonad/src/init.rs` — init argument threading and server tmux command/environment
- `rust/exomonad/src/config.rs` — config discovery and environment precedence
- `rust/exomonad/src/serve.rs` — review policy loading and watcher construction
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/review_policy.rs` — policy defaults/loading
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs` — reviewer-spawn cap semantics
- `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` — CLI/configuration documentation

## STEPS
1. Add `--reviewer-max-rounds <N>` to `exomonad init`, thread it through `main.rs` into `init::run`, and validate that N is at least 1.
2. Carry the explicit init value to the server process using the existing non-secret init override mechanism, without embedding it in shell-sensitive command text.
3. Add a clearly documented highest-precedence override path to policy resolution (CLI/init override > `.exo/review-policy.toml` > built-in default). Keep omitted-flag behavior backward compatible.
4. Ensure the resolved value reaches the worktree watcher and all cap checks, including reviewer creation and terminal `Stuck` handling.
5. Add focused unit tests for parsing/validation, precedence against a conflicting policy file, default fallback, and server/init propagation. Add or update CLI/configuration documentation with an example.
6. Run formatting, clippy, and the relevant Rust test targets.

## VERIFY
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p exomonad -p exomonad-core`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `exomonad init --help` lists `--reviewer-max-rounds`

issues.title: Add typed existing-PR resume enforcement to prevent orphan branches
issues.description:
## ANTI-PATTERNS — READ FIRST

- Do not block spawn_leaf merely because any open PR exists; legitimate new leaves must remain possible.
- Do not parse freeform task text for PR numbers or infer intent from a proposed leaf name.
- Do not ask the caller to supply the owning leaf name or runtime for an existing PR. The host must resolve ownership.
- Do not document the last branch segment as a bare spawn slug; internal names include runtime suffixes and can be double-suffixed.
- Do not silently retry identity or branch collisions with a -2 name.
- Do not auto-close, replace, or mutate the source PR. replace_close_pr remains a separate human-approved recovery path.
- Do not duplicate spawn or replacement logic. Reuse the existing agent.spawn_leaf_subtree effect and AgentControlService path.
- Keep MCP tool/schema policy in Haskell WASM; Rust executes typed effects and validates host state.
- Fail before creating a worktree, branch, tmux window, or PR whenever ownership is unresolved or inconsistent.

## READ FIRST

- CLAUDE.md sections All Tools and Hooks in Haskell WASM, Single Code Path, branch naming, and failure over undocumented fallback.
- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/Spawn.hs.
- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/WatcherPrState.hs.
- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/ReplaceClosedPr.hs.
- proto/effects/agent.proto SpawnLeafSubtreeRequest and replacement messages.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs: ensure_tl_spawn_preflight, watcher_pr_state, spawn_leaf_subtree, replacement helpers, and tests.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs: spawn_leaf_subtree resume-by-slug path and worktree.branch_exists handling.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs: exact existing-branch worktree creation.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resolver.rs: AgentIdentityRecord and lookup rules.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/pr_registry.rs: PrEntry ownership, branch, SHA, and Chainlink metadata.

## CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE

Current spawn_leaf carries no PR identity from Haskell through protobuf to Rust, so it cannot know a new name is intended to repair an existing PR. The documented exact last branch segment is an internal agent name, while spawn_leaf expects a bare slug and appends the runtime suffix. A separate worktree.branch_exists fallback silently retries with name-2, which can manufacture another orphan sibling.

## STEPS

1. Add a Haskell-defined resume_pr MCP tool for root/TL roles. Require pr_number and a complete task/spec; do not accept leaf name or agent type.
2. Reuse watcher state primitives to require an existing open, unmerged PR with non-empty head branch and head SHA.
3. Extend the typed spawn effect with an explicit resume target, using new protobuf fields after existing tags, including resume_pr_number and expected_head_sha. Make new-WASM/old-host combinations fail closed rather than fall through to ordinary spawning.
4. In Rust, re-fetch the PR to close races and require the expected SHA to match.
5. Resolve exactly one AgentIdentityRecord whose birth_branch equals the PR head branch. Cross-check Authoring-Agent and Birth-Branch metadata when present.
6. Use the resolver's stored bare slug and agent type; never derive identity by blindly passing the branch tail back through AgentIdentity::internal_name.
7. Resume the exact existing worktree/branch. If the worktree is missing but ownership is valid, reconstruct or reattach the exact PR branch from its head SHA and original base without creating a sibling name.
8. Reuse AgentControlService::spawn_leaf_subtree and existing branch/worktree helpers; keep replacement behavior in replace_close_pr.
9. Remove the automatic name-2 retry for worktree.branch_exists. Return a clear collision error with zero branch/worktree side effects.
10. Define fail-closed responses for unknown, closed, merged, changed-SHA, unresolved-owner, duplicate-owner, or metadata-mismatch cases. Direct genuinely unrecoverable cases to human-approved replace_close_pr without invoking it automatically.
11. Keep ordinary new spawn_leaf calls backward-compatible and allowed.
12. Update the canonical root protocol to use resume_pr for existing PR work instead of instructing callers to round-trip an internal name through spawn_leaf.

## REQUIRED TESTS

- Haskell schema and JSON-to-effect roundtrip for resume_pr.
- WASM tool visibility and protobuf roundtrip.
- PR #104 regression fixture resolving main.m7-3a-fixture-oracle-opencode to bare slug m7-3a-fixture-oracle plus OpenCode runtime.
- Assert no m7-3a-fixture-oracle-opencode-opencode identity is produced.
- Exact live-owner idempotence, dead-owner worktree reuse, and missing-worktree exact-branch reattachment.
- Unknown/closed/merged/stale-SHA/duplicate-owner/metadata-mismatch rejection before side effects.
- worktree.branch_exists returns one explicit error and never retries with -2.
- Ordinary new spawn_leaf remains allowed.

## VERIFY

- just check-fmt
- just proto-check
- just wasm-all
- just build
- just test-cargo-all
- just test-wasm-integration
- just role-hook-tests
- nix develop --command cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

## DONE CRITERIA

- Existing PR recovery has a typed, PR-number-based tool with host-resolved ownership.
- The PR #104 scenario cannot create pr104-oracle-review-fix-opencode or any other sibling branch through the recovery path.
- Runtime suffixes are normalized from stored identity, not appended twice.
- Branch collisions fail closed; no -2 fallback remains.
- All rejection cases leave no worktree, branch, tmux, or PR side effects.
- New leaf creation remains available and is not blocked by unrelated open PRs.
- Unrecoverable cases point to the existing human-approved replacement workflow.

comments.content: Coordination boundary: this issue owns Haskell tool/schema, protobuf, Rust validation/resume behavior, collision removal, and their unit/WASM/service tests. Do not edit canonical root protocol delivery adapters; provide the final resume_pr wording and contract to #563.

Implemented typed existing-PR resume enforcement: resume_pr accepts only pr_number and task; the host re-fetches the exact PR/head SHA, resolves one persisted worktree owner by birth branch, verifies identity metadata and branch topology, and resumes the same agent/worktree with typed expected_agent_name and expected_head_sha. Ordinary spawns clear typed resume fields, automatic -2 branch retry was removed, and closed/merged/unresolved/stale/duplicate/mismatched PRs fail closed.

issues.description:
## ANTI-PATTERNS — READ FIRST

## READ FIRST

- .exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md
- .exo/roles/devswarm/context/chainlink-tl.md
- .claude/rules/exomonad.md

## CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE

Commit 58a49ec2 added the exact existing-PR owner/resume rule to root.md and .claude/rules/exomonad.md. Claude loads those surfaces. OpenCode, Codex, Gemini, and custom root commands use different generated/native context paths, so the rule was not reliably delivered. Four protocol sources have drifted.

## STEPS

1. Make .exo/roles/{wasm_name}/context/root.md the canonical root TL protocol and add one reusable resolver/loader based on resolve_role_context_path.
2. Preserve Claude's working rule loading while ensuring it resolves the same canonical file.
3. Configure OpenCode with the canonical root protocol path on its documented instructions surface. Keep initial_prompt task-only and ensure both Some and None branches retain the protocol.
4. Render the canonical protocol into Codex developer_instructions, appending only Codex-specific runtime notes.
5. Configure Gemini root context to load the canonical protocol path, matching the existing worker context pattern. Add deterministic config tests only; do not launch Gemini.
6. Define explicit behavior for custom root_command, preferably an environment variable containing the resolved canonical context path plus a warning that the custom command must consume it.
7. Remove or reduce duplicated TL protocol prose in generated Rust constants so future edits have one source of truth.
8. Add temporary-project sentinel tests proving each adapter receives the same canonical protocol with and without initial_prompt.
9. Add a contractual assertion for the existing-PR recovery concepts: watcher_pr_state, head_branch, host-resolved owner/resume flow, no unrelated leaf name, and human-approved replace_close_pr fallback.

## VERIFY

- just check-fmt
- just build
- just test-cargo-all
- Run the focused init/config/instruction parity tests added by this task.
- nix develop --command cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
- Do not run live harness E2E or any Gemini-backed command.

## DONE CRITERIA

- All supported root harness adapters derive protocol context from the canonical root.md source.
- OpenCode and Codex receive the existing-PR recovery rule through their actual supported instruction mechanisms.
- Gemini configuration points at the canonical protocol and is covered deterministically without a live model call.
- initial_prompt cannot suppress root protocol delivery.
- Custom root commands have an explicit, observable context contract.
- Deterministic parity tests fail if a supported adapter drops the canonical protocol.
- No paid LLM matrix is part of the merge gate.

comments.content: Dependency note: implement after #564 establishes the typed resume_pr contract. This issue owns canonical root protocol content and harness adapter delivery; it must replace the flawed internal-name-through-spawn_leaf recipe with the host-resolved resume_pr workflow.

Handoff contract from #564: resume_pr sends typed SpawnLeafSubtree fields resume_pr_number and expected_head_sha. Host must resolve the exact persisted owner by PR head branch and runtime; callers never supply a leaf name, branch name, or agent type. Closed or unrecoverable PRs remain human-approved replace_close_pr cases.

Implemented canonical root TL protocol delivery. The shared loader resolves .exo/roles/{wasm_name}/context/root.md (project-local, then global) and strips frontmatter. Claude receives the canonical file through exomonad_role.md; OpenCode instructions point to its resolved path; Gemini root settings add it to context.fileName; Codex developer_instructions render it plus Codex runtime notes. initial_prompt remains task-only, and custom root_command receives EXOMONAD_ROOT_TL_PROTOCOL_PATH with an explicit warning. issues.title: Watcher dashboard Event Log panel never showed live poll-cycle activity
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Problem

The `exomonad watch` TUI's "Event Log" panel (rust/exomonad/src/dashboard.rs
draw_events/read_events) only scans `.exo/logs/*.jsonl` files written via
`EventLog::append()` (agent lifecycle events: tool.called, pr.filed,
agent.completed, agent.notify_parent, etc.).

`WorktreeEventWatcher::poll_cycle` (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs)
never wrote to that structured log — its poll-cycle and PR-observation
activity only went through `tracing::info!` (stderr/server log) and a
plaintext `append_watcher_log()` write to `.exo/logs/watcher.log`, which is
excluded from the dashboard's `is_jsonl` filter. Net effect: the panel could
sit showing hours-old entries even while the watcher was polling and
observing PR state correctly every cycle underneath it — surfaced live in
RustDebuggerRepo where the panel looked frozen at yesterday's timestamps
despite the watcher being healthy.

## Fix

Added `WorktreeEventWatcher::log_watcher_event()`, which appends
`watcher.poll_cycle` (pr_count) and `watcher.pr_observation`
(pr_number, review_state, ci_status, head_sha, changes_requested_rounds)
events to the shared `EventLog` (writes to `.exo/logs/watcher.jsonl`) using
the same `HasEventLog` capability the file already had in scope. This reuses
the existing structured-event pattern (see the `event.dispatched` /
`agent.sibling_merged` call sites in the same file) instead of adding a
second logging path — no dashboard changes needed, since it already scans
all `*.jsonl` files in `.exo/logs/`.

## Verification

`cargo build -p exomonad-core --lib` compiles clean. Full effect requires
rebuilding/reinstalling the `exomonad` binary (`just build` /
`just install-all-dev`) and restarting the server in any live project
(e.g. RustDebuggerRepo) to pick it up — not done as part of this fix since
that project has active leaves/PRs in flight; deploy on next natural
restart or explicit request.

comments.content: Fixed in 5d78b976 — WorktreeEventWatcher::log_watcher_event() mirrors poll_cycle/pr_observation into .exo/logs/watcher.jsonl, which the dashboard's Event Log panel already scans.

issues.title: spawn_leaf orphan-PR bug recurred despite #549-552 fixes — investigate root cause
issues.description:
Question: 

Context: 

Findings: 

## Observed recurrence

Live in the RustDebuggerRepo project (2026-07-28, ~11:09 local), the root TL
called `spawn_leaf` with a brand-new name `pr104-oracle-review-fix-opencode`
to address PR #104's reviewer-requested changes, instead of resuming the
owning agent by its exact branch-derived name (`m7-3a-fixture-oracle-opencode`,
the last dot-segment of PR #104's head_branch `main.m7-3a-fixture-oracle-opencode`).

This is exactly the failure mode #549 described and #550/#551/#552 were
closed against yesterday (2026-07-27). The installed `exomonad` binary was
freshly built from HEAD (1f43be4b, 2026-07-28 11:09:56) at the time of the
incident, so this is not a stale-binary problem — the resume-by-name code
path and the root.md protocol guardrail (added in #550) are both present and
in effect.

## Why this needs fresh investigation, not a reopen

- #550's fix was docs-only: it added the "Fixing an Existing PR's CI/Review
  Problem" section to `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md` /
  `.claude/rules/exomonad.md`. That prose guardrail exists verbatim in the
  live session's root.md and was violated anyway.
- The TL agent that violated it identifies itself as a non-Claude harness
  (transcript shows "gpt-5.6-luna xhigh" as the model, consistent with an
  OpenCode-driven root TL, not Claude Opus). Investigate whether role context
  (root.md) is reliably loaded/weighted by non-Claude root harnesses, or
  whether the guardrail is Claude-context-window-specific and needs a
  structural (WASM-level) enforcement instead of relying on prose the model
  may deprioritize.
- Consider whether `spawn_leaf` itself should refuse (or warn loudly) when
  called with a new name while an existing open PR's head_branch resolves to
  a different, still-live agent slug for the same PR number/target branch —
  i.e. move part of #550's guidance from prose into a structural check in
  the `spawn_leaf` effect handler, per CLAUDE.md's "Always prefer failure to
  an undocumented heuristic or fallback."

## Anti-patterns (read first)

- Do NOT just reopen #549-552 and re-close them once docs are proofread again
  — the docs already say the right thing and were still bypassed. The gap is
  either non-Claude-harness context loading or missing structural enforcement.
- Do NOT silently auto-block spawn_leaf in a way that could deadlock a
  legitimately new leaf; any structural guard must be precise (match on
  PR-owning branch slug, not just "any open PR exists").
- Do NOT touch RustDebuggerRepo (the live incident project) directly — that
  session has active leaves/PRs in flight. Reproduce or validate the fix in
  a disposable project instead.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a root TL with `root_agent_type = "opencode"` (or another
   non-Claude harness).
2. Get a PR into `ChangesRequested` state.
3. Ask the TL to "address the review comments" without naming the leaf.
4. Observe whether it resumes the owning agent by name (correct) or invents
   a new `spawn_leaf` name (bug).

## Related

Parent investigation: #549 (closed). Docs guardrail: #550 (closed). Resume
mechanics: #551, #552 (closed). This issue captures the live recurrence and
should stay open until the guardrail is verified to hold across harnesses,
or a structural check is added.

comments.content: Diagnosis confirmed: #550 fixed Claude-facing protocol files, but OpenCode, Codex, Gemini, and custom root commands use different instruction paths and do not reliably receive the existing-PR recovery rule. Current spawn_leaf has no structured PR identity, so it cannot precisely detect that a new name is intended to fix an existing PR. Two additional orphan risks were found: the docs prescribe an internal name whose runtime suffix can be appended again, and the Haskell worktree.branch_exists fallback silently retries with a -2 name. Decision: implement deterministic host/tool enforcement and tests; do not use a paid live-LLM matrix. Gemini remains code-supported but live Gemini testing is explicitly excluded while the subscription is inactive.

Implementation scaffold created: #564 adds typed PR-number-based resume enforcement and removes double-suffix/-2 orphan paths; #563 then makes canonical root protocol delivery consistent across harnesses; #565 adds one deterministic no-LLM E2E. Order: #564 -> #563 -> #565. Live harness matrix is intentionally excluded; Gemini remains code-supported but not live-tested.

Operator testing decision: #565 is narrowed to one opt-in Codex-as-TL E2E. It is implemented and statically validated but excluded from default/required CI; any live run is Codex-only and performed at most once with explicit operator opt-in. No Claude, OpenCode, or Gemini live matrix will be run.

Investigation started. The existing #564 typed resume path and #563/#565 canonical-protocol/Codex regression artifacts are present on current HEAD; focused resume identity tests and the deterministic orphan-PR syntax harness pass. The remaining recurrence gap is tool selection: ordinary spawn_leaf has no PR identity, so the host cannot distinguish a review repair from new work. The uncommitted #567 review handoff scaffolding now routes review feedback to TL root-cause analysis plus resume_pr; I am validating whether an additional precise host guard is warranted without blocking legitimate new spawns.

Added a precise host-side guard in rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs: ordinary spawn_leaf requests are inspected only when the task explicitly contains PR #N / PR#N / pull request #N; if that PR is open, unmerged, and has a persisted worktree owner, spawn_leaf is rejected with a direct resume_pr instruction. Closed PRs, tasks without an explicit PR marker, projects without Forgejo, and PRs without a persisted owner remain allowed. Added malformed-token/parser regression coverage. Passed cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check, the new parser test, and the existing typed-resume test. Changes remain uncommitted alongside the prior #567 scaffolding.

  can't be torn down while the caller's worktree is dirty — this tool must
  respect that invariant the same way `dispose_leaf`/`cleanup_orphan` do, or
  explicitly and loudly refuse with a clear error naming the dirty files.
- Do NOT silently fire from the worktree event watcher or the automatic
  orphan reconciler (see sibling issue in #554 for the automatic-sweep fix —
  that is a separate, independent track). This tool is the *manual*,
  on-demand path a TL or human explicitly invokes; it does not change
  reconciler behavior.
- Do NOT require the caller to already know whether a worktree's PR merged,
  closed-unmerged, or is still open — a leaf commonly can't tell why its
  sibling worktree is stale. The tool should determine PR/issue state
  itself (reusing the same Forgejo/Chainlink lookups `watcher_pr_state` and
  `orphan_reconciler`'s `chainlink_issue_is_closed` already perform) and
  refuse loudly rather than guess if state is ambiguous (CLAUDE.md: "Always
  prefer failure to an undocumented heuristic or fallback").
- ZERO new external dependencies.

## READ FIRST

- `/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad/CLAUDE.md` — "All Tools and Hooks in
  Haskell WASM", "Single Code Path", "Logging" sections.
- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/DisposeLeaf.hs` in full — the
  closest existing tool: infers a Chainlink issue id from a leaf name and
  closes it, relying on the `IssueClosed` event handler
  (`.exo/lib/PRReviewHandler.hs:183-189`, `orphan_reconciler.rs` in the live
  server, not the event handler — teardown here specifically happens via
  the background reconciler noticing the issue is now closed, NOT
  synchronously inside `dispose_leaf` itself; confirm this by reading
  `chainlinkIssueCloseCore` in `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/Chainlink.hs:662-702`
  and noting it does not itself call any teardown effect).
- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/CleanupOrphan.hs` in full —
  the other existing tool: disposes a *named*, tab-dead agent immediately
  (synchronously), via the `agent.dispose_orphan` effect. This is likely
  the better base to extend or call into for an immediate (non-reconciler-tick)
  disposal, since it already does the "is this agent's window actually
  dead" check this new tool also needs.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/cleanup.rs` — read
  `cleanup_agent` (~17-193), `cleanup_agents` (~197-218), and
  `cleanup_merged_agents` (~225-267) in full. Note `cleanup_merged_agents`'s
  doc comment ("Without worktrees, there are no per-agent branches to check
  for merge status") appears stale/inaccurate given per-agent worktrees
  demonstrably exist today — do not trust that comment; verify current
  behavior by reading the code, and correct or remove the comment if this
  issue's changes touch that function.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs` — read in full for
  how PR/issue-closed state is currently determined (`chainlink_issue_is_closed`,
  ~85-104) so this tool's state-detection logic is consistent with, not
  divergent from, the automatic reconciler (see sibling issue for the
  reconciler-side fix; this issue does not modify that file, only reuses its
  approach).
- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/PollWorkers.hs` — has an
  existing `watcher_pr_state`-style PR lookup pattern; check whether it
  exposes anything this tool can call to determine merged/closed-unmerged
  state per PR, to avoid re-implementing that lookup.
- `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` — the dirty-worktree
  precondition this tool must not violate.
- Parent issue #554 for full symptom/root-cause context — this subissue is
  specifically the "manual, on-demand + covers ad-hoc-named leaves" track,
  not the automatic-reconciler fix (that's the sibling subissue).

## CONTEXT

Roughly half of the leaked worktrees found in the live investigation behind
#554 have no `issue-<N>` prefix in their slug at all (`ci-gdb-install-review-fix-opencode`,
`pr52-golden-alignment-ci-followup-opencode`, `rdb-step-count-fix-opencode`,
etc.) — these are structurally invisible to the automatic reconciler, which
can only key off a Chainlink issue id parsed from the slug or read from an
`active_issue` file. There needs to be a manual path where a TL (having
noticed a stale sibling worktree, e.g. via `poll_workers` or
`watcher_pr_state`) can say "clean up this specific leaf" and have the tool
itself determine whether that's actually safe (PR merged, or PR
closed-unmerged with a dead tmux window and a clean worktree) rather than
the TL having to reason about `dispose_leaf` vs `cleanup_orphan` vs
`force=true` semantics, none of which currently do this state check.

This is the tool the human explicitly asked for in #554
(candidate name `cleanup_leaf`) — but the exact name and whether it's a new
tool vs an extension of `cleanup_orphan` is this issue's first decision, not
a given.

## STEPS

1. Decide (and state the decision + why in the PR description): does this
   extend `cleanup_orphan`'s existing schema with an optional stricter mode
   (e.g. `require_pr_resolved: true`, which additionally checks Forgejo/GitHub
   PR state before allowing disposal of a dead-window agent), or is it a
   distinct tool `cleanup_leaf` that internally calls the same
   `agent.dispose_orphan` effect after doing its own PR-state check? Given
   CLAUDE.md's "Single Code Path" rule, prefer extending `cleanup_orphan`
   unless the semantics genuinely diverge enough to justify a second tool
   (e.g. does this new capability need to run without a specific agent name,
   as a full sweep, whereas `cleanup_orphan` is always single-target? If a
   sweep mode is wanted, that's a concrete reason for a distinct tool or a
   distinct mode flag — write out which and why).
2. In whichever module hosts the new/extended tool, add the PR-state check:
   for the target agent's worktree branch, determine merged / closed-unmerged
   / open via the same Forgejo lookup `orphan_reconciler.rs`'s
   `chainlink_issue_is_closed` or `watcher_pr_state`'s handler
   (`rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs:1235`) already perform. Refuse
   with a clear error if the PR is still open (that is not a safe disposal —
   direct the caller to `replace_close_pr` or manual investigation instead).
3. Preserve the existing dirty-worktree refusal from `cleanup_orphan`
   (window-alive check) and add a check for uncommitted changes in the
   worktree before disposal, matching `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md`.
   Loudly report which files are dirty if refusing.
4. Support both single-name (`name` arg, like `cleanup_orphan`) and an
   optional sweep mode that iterates `.exo/worktrees/` similarly to
   `orphan_reconciler`'s scan, reusing the same per-worktree check from step
   2-3 for each. Keep `dry_run` (already present on `cleanup_orphan`) so a TL
   can preview what a sweep would remove before committing to it.
5. Log aggressively per CLAUDE.md's "Logging" rule: before checking each
   candidate (name, current PR state), and on disposal/refusal (reason).
6. Update `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md` to document when to reach
   for this tool: after noticing a stale sibling worktree with no clear
   Chainlink issue association, as an alternative to `dispose_leaf` (which
   requires an inferable issue id) and to `cleanup_orphan --force` (which
   does not check PR state before disposing).

## VERIFY

- `just wasm-all` (WASM build for the Haskell schema/tool change) — never
  raw `wasm32-wasi-cabal`.
- `just build` (Rust) — never raw `cargo build`, only if step 2's PR-state
  check requires a new or extended effect.
- `cabal test all` / `cargo test --workspace` via their `just` targets.
- New tests: (a) Haskell-side schema/arg parsing; (b) refuses to dispose an
  agent whose PR is still open; (c) refuses to dispose a dirty worktree with
  a clear error naming the dirty files; (d) disposes a dead-window agent
  whose PR is merged or closed-unmerged and whose worktree is clean; (e) if
  a sweep mode is implemented, a test with multiple candidate worktrees in
  mixed states confirming only the safe ones are disposed.
- `just pre-commit`.

## DONE CRITERIA

- A TL (or human) can trigger disposal of a specific stale leaf worktree —
  including ones with no `issue-<N>` naming — via one tool call, and the
  tool itself verifies it's safe (PR resolved, worktree clean) rather than
  trusting the caller's judgment.
- `root.md` documents when to reach for this tool versus `dispose_leaf`,
  `cleanup_orphan`, and the automatic reconciler.
- Tests pass; no duplicate teardown code path introduced.

issues.title: Fix orphan reconciler: per-worktree idempotency instead of per-issue-id
issues.description:
## ANTI-PATTERNS (read first)

- Do NOT remove the persisted idempotency ledger (`.exo/events/issue_closed.jsonl`)
  entirely to fix this — it exists to avoid re-shelling `chainlink show` every
  tick for issues already known closed. Rescope its key, don't delete it.
- Do NOT special-case the two known slug patterns (`issue-33...` vs
  `issue-33...-replacement...`) as a string-match hack. The real fix is
  structural: track disposal per-worktree-slug, not per-issue-id, since any
  number of worktrees can legitimately share one issue id (respin/replacement
  pattern is intentional, documented product behavior, not an edge case).
- Do NOT change `dispose_agent_resources` or `cleanup_agent` — they are
  correct and shared by multiple callers. This issue is scoped to the
  reconciliation *decision* (which worktrees to check, how to dedupe), not
  the teardown mechanism.
- Do NOT add a new external dependency for JSON-lines handling; the existing
  `serde_json` line-by-line parsing in `orphan_reconciler.rs` is sufficient.
- Preserve the existing behavior of skipping worktrees whose Chainlink issue
  is still open — only the "already reconciled, skip forever" shortcut is
  wrong, not the closed/open check itself.

## READ FIRST

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs` in full — this is
  the only file this issue touches. Read `reconcile_issue_worktrees` (lines
  ~54-83), `issue_id_from_slug` (~112-120), `issue_closed_event_already_recorded`
  / `append_issue_closed_event` (~122-165), and the existing test module at
  the bottom (confirm current line numbers with
  `rg -n "fn reconcile_issue_worktrees|fn issue_id_from_slug|fn issue_closed_event_already_recorded" rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs`
  since this issue may land after other reconciler changes).
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resources.rs` — `dispose_agent_resources`
  (~lines 51-80), the shared teardown function this reconciler calls. Do not
  modify it.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs` lines ~167-263
  (`reconcile_session_timeouts`) — note it already reads
  `.exo/agents/{slug}/active_issue` per-agent as a reliable issue-id source
  independent of slug naming. This issue should reuse that same file, not
  reinvent issue-id resolution.
- Parent issue #554 for full symptom/root-cause context — do not
  re-investigate the symptom, it is already diagnosed there.

## CONTEXT

`reconcile_issue_worktrees` scans `.exo/worktrees/`, and for each dir whose
slug parses as `issue-<N>...`, checks whether Chainlink issue `<N>` is
closed and if so tears down that one worktree via `dispose_agent_resources`.
It then permanently records `issue_id -> closed` in
`.exo/events/issue_closed.jsonl` and skips any future check for that issue
id, on any worktree.

Two independent worktrees for the *same* issue id (the "original attempt,
replaced by a respin under the same issue" pattern —
`issue-33-performance-debugging-opencode` and
`issue-33-performance-debugging-replacement-opencode` are both issue 33)
means only the first one the directory scan reaches gets disposed; the
second is permanently skipped, because the ledger check happens before
disposal and is keyed only on issue id, not on which worktree was actually
disposed.

Separately, `issue_id_from_slug` requires an `issue-<N>` prefix and returns
`None` for anything else, so worktrees named without that convention are
invisible to this reconciler no matter what. (This second gap is out of
scope here if it requires anything beyond swapping to
`active_issue`-file-based resolution — leaves with literally no Chainlink
issue association are the manual-tool issue's problem, not this one's. If
`active_issue` resolves it as a side effect, that is a welcome bonus, not a
required outcome of this issue.)

## STEPS

1. In `reconcile_issue_worktrees`, for each worktree dir, resolve the issue
   id by reading `.exo/agents/{slug}/active_issue` first (same file
   `reconcile_session_timeouts` already reads), falling back to
   `issue_id_from_slug(slug)` only if that file doesn't exist or doesn't
   parse. Keep `issue_id_from_slug` as-is for the fallback case.
2. Change the idempotency key from bare `issue_id` to `(issue_id, slug)`:
   - Update `issue_closed_event_already_recorded` to accept the slug and
     match on both `issue_id` and a new `slug` field in the recorded JSON
     line (or equivalently, check "does this specific worktree path still
     exist" as part of the guard — a worktree that's already gone needs no
     further action regardless of what's in the ledger).
   - Update `append_issue_closed_event` to record `slug` alongside
     `issue_id` in the JSON payload.
   - Update `issue_closed_line_matches` (and its call sites/tests) to match
     on both fields.
3. Keep the rest of the control flow identical: still skip worktrees whose
   Chainlink issue is open; still call `dispose_agent_resources` and still
   append to the ledger on disposal.
4. Log aggressively per CLAUDE.md's "Logging" rule: when a worktree is
   skipped because a *different* worktree already reconciled the same issue
   id, log at INFO with both slugs and the issue id, so this exact failure
   mode is diagnosable from logs alone next time.
5. Update the existing unit tests in `orphan_reconciler.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)]`
   module for the new ledger line shape (`issue_id` + `slug`), and add a new
   test: two worktrees sharing one issue id, issue closed, both get disposed
   (not just the first).

## VERIFY

- `just build` (Rust) — never raw `cargo build`.
- `cargo test --workspace` via its `just` target — confirm existing
  `orphan_reconciler` tests pass with updated ledger shape, plus the new
  shared-issue-id test.
- `just pre-commit`.
- Manual sanity check acceptable in the PR description (not required to
  reproduce against a live Forgejo instance): describe how the fix behaves
  for the exact observed case (issue 33, two worktrees) if a live repro
  isn't practical in this environment.

## DONE CRITERIA

- Two worktrees sharing one Chainlink issue id are each independently
  reconciled once that issue closes — neither is silently skipped because
  the other was disposed first.
- The persisted ledger records enough to make that guarantee true on
  restart (not just within one process's in-memory state).
- Tests pass; no change to `dispose_agent_resources`, `cleanup_agent`, or
  any other reconciler responsibility (session timeouts) beyond what's
  listed above.

comments.content: Implemented per-worktree reconciliation: active_issue is preferred over slug parsing, issue_closed.jsonl records (issue_id, slug), same-issue worktrees are independently checked, and INFO logs identify prior worktrees. Added ledger/active_issue tests. Verified with just build, just check-fmt, and just rust-test (852 passed, 3 skipped).

issues.title: Orphan reconciler leaks leaf worktrees when multiple leaves share one Chainlink issue id
issues.description:
## Symptom (observed live)

In a consuming project (`RustDebuggerRepo`), 50 of ~103 leaf worktrees under
`.exo/worktrees/` are stale: their tmux windows are long dead, their PRs are
closed (merged or abandoned), yet the worktree directories, `.exo/agents/`
registry entries, and (for merged cases only) git worktrees still sit on disk.
Cross-referencing against Forgejo (`/repos/exomonad/RustDebuggerRepo/pulls?state=all`)
shows a clean split:

- Every PR that actually **merged** had its exact-match worktree removed
  correctly (e.g. PR #38 `issue-33-performance-debugging-replacement-opencode`,
  merged, worktree gone).
- Every worktree still on disk belongs to a PR that was **closed unmerged** —
  overwhelmingly the "abandoned original, replaced by a respin" pattern this
  codebase explicitly supports (`replace_close_pr`, `-followup`/`-v2`/`-ci-repair`
  naming). Concrete example: PR #24 (`issue-33-performance-debugging-opencode`)
  was closed unmerged when its replacement PR #38 landed under the *same*
  Chainlink issue id (33) instead — but the original worktree is still on
  disk, clean (no uncommitted changes), doing nothing.

## Root cause chain

There is an automatic sweep already running — `reconcile_issue_worktrees`
in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs:54-83`, ticked
from a background loop started in `rust/exomonad/src/serve.rs:1320`. For each
`.exo/worktrees/{slug}` dir it: parses an issue id out of the slug via
`issue_id_from_slug` (`orphan_reconciler.rs:112-120`, expects an
`issue-<N>...` prefix), checks `chainlink show <N>` for `Status: closed`
(`orphan_reconciler.rs:85-104`), and if closed calls
`dispose_agent_resources` (`agent_resources.rs:51-80`: kills the tmux
window, removes the git worktree, removes `.exo/agents/{slug}`) — then
permanently records the disposal in `.exo/events/issue_closed.jsonl`
(`orphan_reconciler.rs:122-165`) so it never re-checks that issue id again.

**Bug 1 — idempotency guard is keyed by bare issue id, not by
`(issue_id, slug)`.** When an original attempt and its replacement share one
Chainlink issue number — exactly the supported respin pattern
(`issue-33-performance-debugging-opencode` and
`issue-33-performance-debugging-replacement-opencode` both resolve to issue
id 33) — the directory scan visits both slugs in the same `issue_id_from_slug`
issue. Whichever slug the scan reaches first for that issue id gets disposed
and the closure gets recorded; the *second* slug for the same issue id is
skipped that tick (`issue_closed_event_already_recorded` at
`orphan_reconciler.rs:73` short-circuits before re-checking `chainlink show`)
and, because the event is now permanently in `issue_closed.jsonl`, is never
revisited on any future tick either. One of the two worktrees leaks forever.

**Bug 2 — no coverage for worktrees whose slug doesn't embed `issue-<N>`.**
`issue_id_from_slug` returns `None` for anything not prefixed `issue-`
(`ci-gdb-install-review-fix-opencode`, `pr52-golden-alignment-ci-followup-opencode`,
`rdb-step-count-fix-opencode`, etc. — roughly half the leaked worktrees in
the observed session). These are invisible to the automatic reconciler
regardless of their PR/issue state. The graceful manual path,
`dispose_leaf` (`haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/DisposeLeaf.hs:62-73`),
has the identical `inferIssueId` limitation and refuses to act unless
`force=true` is passed to fall through to `cleanup_orphan`
(`haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/CleanupOrphan.hs`) — and
nothing in `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md`'s TL protocol calls either
tool for the "leaf superseded/abandoned without merging" case. The TL
protocol only wires disposal into the `[MERGE READY]` -> `merge_pr` ->
`dispose_leaf` success path (`root.md` "Dev-leaf signals").

Per-agent `.exo/agents/{slug}/active_issue` files already exist and are read
elsewhere (`orphan_reconciler.rs:234`, in `reconcile_session_timeouts`) —
this is a more reliable issue-id source than slug regex parsing and isn't
restricted to any naming convention.

## Direction (decided, do not relitigate)

Two independently workable tracks, matching the existing
`dispose_agent_resources` / `cleanup_agent` mechanism rather than inventing a
parallel one (Single Code Path):

1. Fix the automatic reconciler in place: stop keying the idempotency guard
   by bare issue id; resolve issue id from `active_issue` first, slug parsing
   as fallback; re-evaluate every worktree independently regardless of
   whether its issue id was already reconciled via a *different* worktree.
2. Add a manual, on-demand reconciliation MCP tool (candidate name
   `cleanup_leaf`) so a TL (or human) can trigger the same disposal logic
   immediately for a specific leaf, and/or run a full sweep, rather than
   waiting on the ticker — this is also the only path that can ever cover
   leaves with no Chainlink issue association at all (ad-hoc `spawn_leaf`
   names), which structurally cannot be inferred from a background sweep
   keyed on issue ids.

Do not implement a third disposal code path. Both tracks must bottom out in
the existing `dispose_agent_resources` (Rust) / `cleanup_agent`. All MCP
tool schema and dispatch logic for track 2 lives in Haskell WASM per
CLAUDE.md's "All Tools and Hooks in Haskell WASM" rule — Rust only executes
the effect.

## Subissues

See linked subissues. They are independent and can be worked in parallel.

comments.content: Audit complete: landed #555/#556 behavior satisfies per-(issue_id, slug) reconciliation, active_issue-first lookup, shared dispose_agent_resources path, manual ad-hoc/sweep cleanup safety checks, Haskell-only cleanup_leaf schema/dispatch, and paginated state=all PR lookup. Found and fixed one integration-doc gap: added cleanup_leaf to docs/architecture/agent-system.md role matrix. Commit bae24ac0. Verified cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib services::orphan_reconciler (7 passed), cleanup_pr_state (2 passed), paginated Forgejo regression (1 passed), just check-fmt, just haskell-test (566 passed), just wasm-all, just build, and serialized WASM visibility test (1 passed). Full just test-wasm-integration build succeeded but its parallel phase timed out 24 tests at 60s; no assertions ran. #547 files untouched. Parent remains open.

Completed and verified on main. Integrated docs fix 00191d5c (cleanup_leaf role visibility). Reconciler: 7 passed; file_pr helper tests: 14 passed under TMPDIR=/tmp and repo TMPDIR; claude-teams-bridge inbox tests: 8 passed under both TMPDIR values; git grep confirms one definition of each shared helper; just check-fmt and just build passed. Prior worker verification also passed just test-fast (853 passed, 3 skipped), just haskell-test (566), just wasm-all, pagination and cleanup-state tests. Full parallel WASM integration timed out at its 60s test limit before assertions.

issues.title: Add open-PR equivalent of replace_close_pr for unrecoverable-by-name leaves
issues.description:
## ANTI-PATTERNS (read first)

- Do NOT make dev-leaf sessions persistent/long-running as a way to dodge
  this problem. Direction was explicitly decided against that: it fights the
  ephemeral-worker cost model and the Fire-and-Forget/hook-injection review
  architecture documented in CLAUDE.md. This issue is about a resume/replace
  tool, not about keeping agents alive.
- Do NOT let this tool auto-fire from the worktree event watcher without
  human approval, mirroring `replace_close_pr`'s existing
  `human_approved: true` gate (`ReplaceClosedPr.hs`). Silently respawning
  work against a still-open PR without a human/TL decision point is exactly
  the kind of undocumented heuristic CLAUDE.md's top-level rules forbid
  ("Always prefer failure to an undocumented heuristic or fallback").
- Do NOT duplicate `replace_close_pr`'s logic in a parallel code path.
  CLAUDE.md's "Single Code Path" rule applies: either extend
  `replace_close_pr` to accept open PRs under an explicit flag/precondition,
  or factor the shared "continue from source_head_sha, base_branch =
  original PR base" logic into one function both tools call. Do not
  copy-paste `handlers/agent.rs`'s replace-PR handler body into a new
  function.
- ZERO new external dependencies.
- Do not silently merge/close/touch the PR being replaced -- this tool only
  creates the continuation leaf; merge/close remains a separate, explicit TL
  action as with every other flow in this codebase.
- All tool/hook logic lives in Haskell WASM
  (`haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/`); Rust only executes
  effects. Do not add tool schema or dispatch logic directly in Rust.

## READ FIRST

- `/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad/CLAUDE.md` -- "All Tools and Hooks in
  Haskell WASM", "Single Code Path", "Logging" sections.
- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/ReplaceClosedPr.hs` in full --
  this is the tool to extend or use as the template. Note the
  `human_approved: true` requirement and the "Never use this for an open or
  merged PR" guard (around line 60 as of this writing -- confirm current
  line with `rg -n "open or merged" haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/ReplaceClosedPr.hs`).
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs` -- the `replace_close_pr`
  handler (was around lines 1019-1148): captures `source_head_sha` from the
  closed PR's exact head SHA, computes `new_branch` as a child of
  `original_base_branch` (the OLD PR's own base, not the caller's birth
  branch), and passes `start_point: Some(source_head_sha)` +
  `base_branch: Some(original_base_branch)` into `SpawnLeafOptions`.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/mod.rs` -- `SpawnLeafOptions`
  struct (around lines 538-539), specifically the existing `base_branch`
  field this issue will reuse (it is Rust-side complete; the gap is only in
  what's exposed/wired through Haskell for the open-PR case).
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs` lines ~1617-1710
  -- `spawn_leaf_subtree`'s existing resume-by-slug and
  replacement-leaf-via-`base_branch` code paths, so the new open-PR path
  reuses rather than reimplements this.
- `.exo/review-policy.toml` -- `reviewer_max_rounds`, and the "Stuck" state
  semantics referenced in CLAUDE.md's "Review Policy" section, to understand
  where in the existing state machine an open-PR-dead-leaf currently
  surfaces (it currently looks identical to `dev_not_pushing`).
- `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` -- leaf lifecycle
  invariants (issues can't close while the caller's worktree is dirty,
  etc.) that any new replace/resume path must not violate.

## CONTEXT

`replace_close_pr` already solves "continue a dead leaf's work without
losing its last commit, correctly re-parented onto the original PR's base
branch" -- but only for PRs that are CLOSED. There is no equivalent for a PR
that is still OPEN whose owning agent's session died in a way that
`spawn_leaf`'s same-name resume-by-slug cannot recover (e.g. the worktree
itself is corrupted/gone, or the TL genuinely cannot determine/re-derive the
original agent name). Today that situation is indistinguishable at the
watcher level from ordinary `dev_not_pushing` staleness and dead-ends at
human Chainlink `review-stuck` escalation with no structured recovery tool
-- the human has to manually intervene rather than the TL having a supported
one-call path (still gated by human approval, matching `replace_close_pr`'s
existing pattern).

This is a smaller, more scoped fix than "expose `base_branch` generally on
`spawn_leaf`" -- keep it scoped to extending the existing
closed-PR-replacement pattern to also accept open PRs, reusing the same
Rust-side `SpawnLeafOptions.base_branch` + `start_point` mechanism that
already works correctly for the closed case.

## STEPS

1. Decide (and document the decision in the PR description) whether to (a)
   relax `replace_close_pr`'s "must be closed" precondition to also accept
   open PRs when `human_approved: true` is set, or (b) add a distinct tool
   (e.g. `replace_open_pr` / `resume_pr_leaf`) that shares the Rust handler
   logic via a common function. Given CLAUDE.md's "Single Code Path" rule,
   prefer (a) unless there's a concrete reason open-PR semantics need to
   diverge (e.g. should the old open PR be auto-closed when the replacement
   files a new one, to avoid the exact orphan-PR proliferation this whole
   issue chain is about? If yes, that behavior difference alone may justify
   a distinct flag rather than a distinct tool).
2. In `ReplaceClosedPr.hs`, update (or branch) the tool schema/args to allow
   the target PR to be open, still gated by `human_approved: true`. Update
   the tool's description/doc comment to state both cases explicitly.
3. In `handlers/agent.rs`, extend the `replace_close_pr` handler to accept
   an open source PR: still capture `source_head_sha` and
   `original_base_branch` the same way; additionally decide (per step 1)
   whether to close the original PR as part of this flow to prevent the
   orphan-PR-proliferation pattern from the parent issue recurring (an open
   PR left behind alongside its replacement is exactly the bug this whole
   issue chain exists to prevent).
4. Log aggressively at each step per CLAUDE.md's "Logging" rule: before
   spawning the replacement (source PR number, head SHA, base branch), and
   on success/failure (new branch, new PR number if filed).
5. Update `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md`'s Chainlink Coordination /
   Worker Correction Loop sections (coordinate with subissue A's docs
   change -- if A has already landed, extend it rather than re-writing; if
   not, note the dependency) to point the TL at this tool for the specific
   "resume-by-name didn't work, PR still open" case identified there.

## VERIFY

- `just wasm-all` (WASM build for the Haskell schema change) -- never raw
  `wasm32-wasi-cabal`.
- `just build` (Rust) -- never raw `cargo build`.
- `cabal test all` / `cargo test --workspace` via their `just` targets, not
  invoked directly.
- New tests: (a) Haskell-side schema/arg parsing test accepting an open PR
  when `human_approved: true`; (b) Rust-side handler test asserting the
  replacement leaf's branch is `{original_base_branch}.{new_slug}` with
  `start_point` set to the open PR's exact head SHA (mirror whatever test
  pattern already covers the closed-PR case for `replace_close_pr` --
  `rg -n "replace_close_pr" -g "*test*"` to find it); (c) if step 3 decides
  to auto-close the original PR, a test confirming that closure happens and
  is logged.
- `just pre-commit`.

## DONE CRITERIA

- A TL can recover an open PR whose owning leaf is unrecoverable-by-name,
  via one gated (`human_approved: true`) tool call, producing a replacement
  leaf correctly parented onto the ORIGINAL PR's base branch and continuing
  from its last commit -- not a sibling of the TL's own branch.
- The orphan-PR-proliferation failure mode from the parent issue (multiple
  live PRs for the same underlying problem, all basing against main) cannot
  recur through this path: either the original PR is closed as part of
  replacement, or the PR description explains why leaving it open is safe
  and how a human/TL is expected to reconcile the two.
- Tests pass; `root.md` documents when to reach for this tool versus plain
  `spawn_leaf` resume-by-name versus `replace_close_pr`.

issues.title: Fix spawn_leaf/fork_wave response branch_name to report the real dot-prefixed branch
issues.description:
## ANTI-PATTERNS (read first)

- Do NOT change `spawn_leaf`'s branch-naming logic itself
  (`BirthBranch::child`, `spawn.rs:1697-1706`). That logic is correct. This
  issue is ONLY about the value reported back in the MCP tool response.
- Do NOT add a new field to the response as a workaround -- fix the existing
  `branch_name` field to report the truth. Adding a second, "actually
  correct" field alongside a known-wrong one is exactly the kind of
  redundant-path bug CLAUDE.md's "Single Code Path" rule forbids.
- Do NOT touch `fork_wave`'s response unless you confirm (via grep) it has
  the identical bug -- if so, fix both in this same issue since they are the
  same root cause; if fork_wave is unaffected, say so in the PR description
  and leave it alone.
- ZERO new external dependencies.
- No `todo!()`, `unwrap_or_default()`-style silent fallbacks that hide a
  missing branch name -- if the real branch name cannot be determined,
  that's a bug to surface (log + error), not paper over.

## READ FIRST

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs` -- find
  `leaf_subtree_result_to_proto` (was around line 2653; confirm with
  `rg -n "fn leaf_subtree_result_to_proto"`) and its caller (was around line
  1310, `rg -n "leaf_subtree_result_to_proto\("`).
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs` -- find
  `spawn_leaf_subtree` and specifically where it constructs `child_birth`
  (was around lines 1697-1706: `effective_birth.child(agent_name)` /
  `existing_identity_record.birth_branch` / `base_branch.child(agent_name)`).
  This `child_birth` (or equivalent `BirthBranch`/`BranchName` value) is the
  TRUE branch that was actually created -- it must be what flows into the
  proto response, not the raw request argument.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/domain.rs` -- `BirthBranch` type (around lines
  191-203: `.child()` and `.parent()`) to understand the string this
  produces (e.g. `"main.fix-pr97-ci"`).
- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/Spawn.hs` lines ~501-512 --
  the tool schema's own doc comment for `name`: "Branch name suffix (e.g.,
  'fix-clippy' -> 'main.fix-clippy')" -- this confirms the intended/documented
  behavior that the current code violates.

## CONTEXT

`spawn_leaf`'s MCP response includes a `branch_name` field. Today it is set
directly from the caller's raw, un-prefixed `name` argument (e.g.
`"fix-pr97-ci"`), not from the actual dot-prefixed git branch the service
created (e.g. `"main.fix-pr97-ci"`, or, when resuming an existing agent,
whatever branch that agent already owns). This is misleading: a TL reading
its own tool-call response cannot tell what branch/lineage was actually
created, which was one contributing factor in a live incident where a TL
spawned a disconnected sibling branch/PR while believing it had done
something scoped to an existing PR. See parent Chainlink issue for the full
incident.

## STEPS

1. In `spawn_leaf_subtree` (`spawn.rs`), locate the `SpawnResult` (or
   equivalent return struct) that is passed to `leaf_subtree_result_to_proto`.
   Confirm it either already carries the real computed branch (`child_birth`
   or similar) as a field, or add one if it currently discards it after
   worktree creation.
2. In `leaf_subtree_result_to_proto` (`handlers/agent.rs`), change the
   `branch_name` assignment to read from that real branch field on the
   result, not from the `&req.branch_name` / raw request argument passed in
   today.
3. Trace the same for the `mux_window`/tab-name derivation
   (`tab_display_name`, referenced near the same call site) -- if it also
   derives from the raw un-prefixed name, decide whether that's intentional
   (short tab labels are a reasonable UX choice) or should also reflect
   reality; if intentional, leave it and note why in the PR description.
4. Grep `fork_wave`'s equivalent result-to-proto conversion for the same
   pattern (`rg -n "branch_name" rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs`)
   and fix it too if it shares the bug.

## VERIFY

- `cargo build -p exomonad-core` (via `just build`, per this repo's
  standing rule to never invoke raw `cargo build`/`cabal` directly -- see
  `justfile` targets).
- Add or extend a Rust test in `rust/exomonad-core` (find existing tests for
  `spawn_leaf_subtree` or `leaf_subtree_result_to_proto`, likely under
  `services/agent_control/` or `handlers/` `#[cfg(test)]` modules) that
  asserts: given a `name` of `"fix-pr97-ci"` and a caller birth branch of
  `"main"`, the returned `branch_name` is `"main.fix-pr97-ci"`, not
  `"fix-pr97-ci"`. Also cover the resume-by-slug case: given an existing
  agent whose real branch is `"main.rebase-pr95-main-conflicts-opencode"`,
  a repeat `spawn_leaf` call with that same `name` returns that full branch,
  not the bare name.
- `cargo test --workspace` (via `just` target, not raw cargo) must pass.
- `just pre-commit`.

## DONE CRITERIA

- `spawn_leaf`'s MCP response `branch_name` field always reports the actual
  dot-prefixed git branch that was created or resumed, never the raw `name`
  argument.
- New/updated tests cover both the fresh-spawn case and the resume-by-slug
  case, and pass.
- `fork_wave` is either confirmed unaffected (documented in the PR) or fixed
  identically.

issues.title: Protocol guardrail: resume PR-owning agent by name instead of inventing a new spawn_leaf name
issues.description:
## ANTI-PATTERNS (read first)

- Do NOT touch any Rust or Haskell source in this issue. This is a docs-only
  change to TL-facing protocol files.
- Do NOT invent a new MCP tool or new prompt section unrelated to this
  specific behavior. Scope is exactly: "how the TL decides what to call
  `spawn_leaf` when fixing an existing PR's problem."
- Do NOT weaken or remove the existing "Worker Correction Loop" or
  "Chainlink Coordination" sections in `root.md` -- add to them, don't
  restructure them.
- Do NOT claim `spawn_leaf`'s resume-by-slug is guaranteed reliable in every
  case -- it is the correct default path, but the doc must also point at the
  escalation fallback (Chainlink `review-stuck`) for when it doesn't apply
  (see the parent issue's "genuine gap" -- that gap is fixed by a separate
  subissue, not this one).

## READ FIRST

- `/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad/CLAUDE.md` -- section "Branch Naming
  as Coordinate System" (the `{parent}.{name}` convention, "last dot-segment
  IS the AgentName").
- `/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad/.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md`
  -- full file, especially "Worker Correction Loop" and the paragraph noting
  `spawn_leaf` is "also the resume path for an existing leaf worktree...
  ExoMonad reuses that worktree and starts a fresh session instead of
  duplicating the task."
- `/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad/.claude/rules/exomonad.md` -- section
  "Convergence Protocol" and "Branch Naming".
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs` around lines
  1617-1698 (resume-by-slug lookup) and 1789-1862 (resume injects PR review
  context instead of re-filing) -- confirm current line numbers with
  `rg -n "lookup_by_slug|find_existing_leaf_worktree_by_slug"
  rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs` since they may
  have drifted.
- The `watcher_pr_state` MCP tool's response shape (search
  `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/` for `watcher_pr_state` or
  `WatcherPrState`) -- confirm it returns `head_branch` as documented.

## CONTEXT

Live incident: a root TL, told PR #97 was CI-red, called
`spawn_leaf({"name":"fix-pr97-ci", ...})` -- inventing an unrelated new name.
This created a disconnected sibling branch/worktree/PR (based against
`main`, since `spawn_leaf` always children off the caller's own branch)
instead of resuming the agent that actually owned PR #97
(`rebase-pr95-main-conflicts-opencode`, derivable from PR #97's
`head_branch` field: `main.rebase-pr95-main-conflicts-opencode` -- last
dot-segment is the owning agent's name). Nothing in the TL's protocol docs
told it to do that lookup first. This produces an ever-growing chain of
orphan PRs that all target main regardless of which PR they were meant to
fix.

## STEPS

1. In `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md`, add a new subsection under (or
   near) "Worker Correction Loop" -- title it something like "Fixing an
   Existing PR's CI/Review Problem" -- with this rule, stated as an explicit
   DO/DO NOT pair:
   - DO NOT call `spawn_leaf` with a new, unrelated `name` to fix another
     PR's CI failure, review comments, or merge conflicts. This always
     creates a disconnected sibling branch that bases against the TL's own
     branch (often `main`), never against the PR it was meant to fix.
   - DO first resolve the name of the agent that owns the target PR's
     branch: call `watcher_pr_state` (or `list_agents`) for the PR number,
     read `head_branch`, and take its last dot-segment -- that string IS the
     owning agent's name (per CLAUDE.md's branch-naming convention).
   - DO call `spawn_leaf` again with that EXACT SAME `name`. This resumes
     the existing worktree/branch (slug-based lookup) instead of creating a
     new one, and if the PR already exists, injects resume context with
     review comments rather than filing a duplicate PR.
   - If resuming by name does not work (agent/worktree is genuinely gone,
     not just session-dead) and the PR is still OPEN (not closed), this is
     the one case `spawn_leaf` cannot currently handle by itself -- do not
     work around it by inventing a new leaf name. Escalate via the existing
     Chainlink `review-stuck` surface, or use whatever tool exists for
     resuming an open PR after this issue's sibling subissue (open-PR
     replace/resume capability) lands. Link that subissue's Chainlink ID
     here once known.
2. Mirror the same rule, condensed to 3-4 sentences, into
   `.claude/rules/exomonad.md` under "Convergence Protocol" (this file is
   the crosscutting rules file per the top-level CLAUDE.md's "Crosscutting
   Rules" policy -- it must stay in sync with any TL-behavior rule that
   applies across projects, not just root.md's project-local copy).
3. Cross-check: does `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md`'s existing
   sentence about `spawn_leaf` being "the resume path for an existing leaf
   worktree" already say enough, and this issue's job is just to make the
   DO-NOT half explicit (spawning a NEW name for someone else's problem),
   plus the name-resolution recipe (parse `head_branch`)? If so, keep the
   diff minimal -- don't rewrite the whole section.

## VERIFY

- No build/test commands apply (docs-only). Verification is manual review:
  re-read the full diff of both files and confirm (a) the new text is
  internally consistent with the rest of root.md/exomonad.md's voice and
  structure, (b) it does not contradict "Never wait silently" or the
  existing Worker Correction Loop steps, (c) it gives a concrete, executable
  recipe (call X tool, read Y field, do Z) rather than a vague admonition.

## DONE CRITERIA

- `root.md` and `.claude/rules/exomonad.md` both explicitly forbid spawning
  a new, unrelated `spawn_leaf` name to fix another PR's problem, and both
  give the exact recipe (derive owning agent name from `head_branch`'s last
  dot-segment, resume by calling `spawn_leaf` with that same name).
- The text names the escalation fallback for when resume-by-name doesn't
  apply (open PR, unrecoverable agent) instead of leaving it unaddressed.
- Diff is reviewed and committed with a message referencing this Chainlink
  issue id.
