issues.title: TL spawns disconnected fix-PRs instead of resuming the owning agent
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Symptom (observed live)

In a consuming project (`RustDebuggerRepo`), the root TL saw PR #97 CI-red and
called `spawn_leaf({"name":"fix-pr97-ci", ...})` to fix it. This created a
brand-new sibling branch/worktree/PR instead of resuming the agent that
actually owned PR #97's branch. Result: an ever-growing chain of orphan PRs
(#95 -> #97 -> would-be #98...), each one a sibling of the TL's own branch,
each therefore auto-basing against `main` via `file_pr`'s dot-hierarchy
walk-up (`file_pr.rs:61-71`) -- never against the PR they were spawned to fix.
The user does not want "PR merges into another PR's branch" as a normal
workflow either; the fix is to stop spawning disconnected fix-PRs in the
first place.

## Root cause chain

1. `spawn_leaf` always children a new branch off the CALLER's (TL's) own
   birth branch (`spawn.rs:1697-1706`, `BirthBranch::child` at
   `domain.rs:191-193` unconditionally does `format!("{}.{}", self.0, slug)`
   using the TL's own branch as `self`).
2. `spawn_leaf` DOES already have a correct resume path: calling it again
   with the SAME `name` does slug-based lookup (`agent_resolver().lookup_by_slug`,
   `spawn.rs:1617-1698`), reuses the existing worktree/branch, and if a PR
   already exists for that branch, injects resume context with review
   comments instead of filing a duplicate PR (`spawn.rs:1789-1862`).
3. The TL in the observed session did NOT use the same name -- it invented
   `"fix-pr97-ci"`, unrelated to the branch-owning agent's actual name
   (`rebase-pr95-main-conflicts-opencode`, derivable from PR #97's
   `head_branch` field returned by `watcher_pr_state`: the last dot-segment
   of `head_branch` IS the owning agent's name, per CLAUDE.md's branch-naming
   convention: "The last dot-segment IS the AgentName -- one namespace, zero
   translation"). Nothing in `root.md` / `.claude/rules/exomonad.md` tells
   the TL to do this lookup before spawning a fix.
4. Compounding confusion: `spawn_leaf`'s MCP response reports the raw,
   un-prefixed `name` argument as `branch_name` (`handlers/agent.rs:2653`,
   sourced from `handlers/agent.rs:1310`'s `&req.branch_name`), never the
   real dot-prefixed git branch computed inside the service. So even reading
   the tool's own response, the TL cannot see that it just created a
   disconnected sibling.
5. The one genuine gap: `replace_close_pr` (`ReplaceClosedPr.hs:32-90`) is
   the correct "continue from a dead worktree's last commit, correctly
   re-parented onto the ORIGINAL PR's base" tool (`handlers/agent.rs:1019-1148`:
   captures `source_head_sha`, uses `original_base_branch`, passes
   `start_point`+`base_branch` into `SpawnLeafOptions`) -- but it only fires
   for CLOSED, unmerged PRs (`ReplaceClosedPr.hs:60`) and requires
   `human_approved: true`. There is no equivalent for "owning agent is
   unrecoverable by name, but the PR is still OPEN" -- today that case is
   indistinguishable from ordinary `dev_not_pushing` staleness and dead-ends
   at human Chainlink escalation.

## Direction (decided, do not relitigate)

Leaves stay ephemeral / Fire-and-Forget. Do NOT make dev-leaf sessions
persistent -- that fights the cost model (leaves are cheap/disposable Gemini
or OpenCode sessions) and the documented architecture where reviewer
round-trips are watcher/hook-injection driven, not live TL<->leaf
conversation (CLAUDE.md "Fire-and-Forget Execution"). The fix is narrower:
make the TL resume the correct agent by name, make the tool response honest
about what branch it created, and close the one real gap (open-PR
resume-by-replacement) with a small, explicitly-gated extension of the
existing `replace_close_pr` pattern -- not new "persistent leaf" machinery.

## Subissues

See linked subissues. They are independent and can be worked in parallel
except where noted (#3 should land after #2 exists as prior art, but does
not strictly require it).

issues.title: Add --reset-inbox flag to exomonad init
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Add `exomonad init --reset-inbox` to clear stale ExoMonad inbox messages.

## Background

ExoMonad's cross-agent inbox (`InboxStore`, `.exo/inbox.db`) is a project-local
SQLite file, not part of tmux session state. `exomonad init --recreate` tears
down and recreates the tmux session but never touches `.exo/inbox.db`, so
unread/stale messages from prior runs accumulate indefinitely with no way to
clear them. This issue adds a standalone `--reset-inbox` flag (not folded into
`--recreate`, since the two have different lifecycles — someone may want a
fresh tmux session while keeping pending cross-agent messages).

## ANTI-PATTERNS (read first)

- Do NOT add new crate dependencies. `rusqlite` is already a dependency of
  `exomonad-core`; nothing else is needed.
- Do NOT fold this behavior into `--recreate`. It must be an independent
  `--reset-inbox` boolean flag.
- Do NOT `DROP TABLE` anything. Use `DELETE FROM` so the schema/indexes
  created by `migrate()` are left intact — the store must still work
  immediately after a reset.
- Do NOT rename or touch existing `InboxStore` methods (`write_message`,
  `drain_unread`, `peek_unnotified`, `has_unread`, etc.). Add one new method
  only.
- Do NOT touch tmux session logic, WASM, or anything else in `init.rs` beyond
  the single insertion point described below.
- No stream-of-consciousness comments. `clear_all` needs no doc comment beyond
  what's shown — its name says what it does.

## READ FIRST

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs` — full file. Note
  `fn connection(&self) -> Result<MutexGuard<'_, Connection>>` (~line 338) and
  the existing `migrate()` method (~line 305) for the `execute_batch` pattern.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs` test module at the bottom
  (~line 620 onward) — follow the existing `InboxStore::open_in_memory()` +
  `write_message` test pattern for the new test.
- `rust/exomonad/src/main.rs` lines ~40-129 (the `Commands::Init { ... }` CLI
  struct — note the `set_git_remote: Option<String>` field as the most recent
  precedent for how a new Init flag is documented and declared) and lines
  ~344-380 (the match arm that destructures `Commands::Init` and calls
  `init::run(...)`).
- `rust/exomonad/src/init.rs` lines ~841-870 (the `pub async fn run(...)`
  signature and the `cwd` / `config_path` resolution at the top of the
  function body — `cwd` is the project dir, same value `InboxStore::open`
  expects).
- `rust/exomonad/src/serve.rs` line ~1098 for the existing
  `InboxStore::open(&project_dir)` call, confirming `InboxStore` is
  reachable as `exomonad_core::services::InboxStore`.
- `rust/exomonad/CLAUDE.md` — "Init Command" section, to extend with the new
  flag per the project's "always update CLAUDE.md" rule (root `CLAUDE.md` §
  Style).

## STEPS

1. **Add `clear_all` to `InboxStore`** in
   `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs`. Insert it as a new method
   near `has_unread`/`last_check_inbox_at` (before `fn migrate`, ~line 304):

   ```rust
   pub fn clear_all(&self) -> Result<()> {
       let conn = self.connection()?;
       conn.execute_batch("DELETE FROM messages; DELETE FROM agent_inbox_meta;")
           .context("failed to clear inbox database")?;
       Ok(())
   }
   ```

issues.title: refactor: share outside-repo tempdir test helper instead of duplicating it
issues.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

## Summary

Follow-up to #546 (`5d279c65`). The test helpers `tempdir_outside_any_repo` and
`git_repository_root` were duplicated **byte-for-byte** into two crates instead of
shared:

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr.rs:277-310`
- `rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/inbox.rs:270-305`

Both copies hash identically (`md5 9260dc98d470` over the helper block). #546's spec
asked for reuse rather than duplication; this closes that gap.

This is the two-code-paths pattern `CLAUDE.md` § Single Code Path prohibits: a fix or
hardening applied to one copy will silently miss the other. The helper is a **test
correctness guard** — if it drifts, tests start silently asserting the wrong thing,
which is exactly the class of failure #546 existed to fix.

Low urgency, small scope. Filed for later.

### Why it was duplicated

`claude-teams-bridge` does not depend on `exomonad-core` (checked
`rust/claude-teams-bridge/Cargo.toml` — no such dependency in either `[dependencies]`
or `[dev-dependencies]`), so there was no existing home both crates could reach. That
makes the duplication understandable but not correct.

---

## 1. ANTI-PATTERNS

- **DO NOT** make `claude-teams-bridge` depend on `exomonad-core` to share a test
  helper. That inverts the dependency direction for a test-only concern and drags a
  large crate into a small one's build.
- **DO NOT** put the helper in `exomonad-core`'s public API behind a feature flag.
  It is test scaffolding, not product surface.
- **DO NOT** change the helper's behavior. It is correct as written: try the ambient
  tempdir, fall back to `/tmp` then `/var/tmp`, and panic with the offending `.git`
  path plus `TMPDIR` if none is outside a repo. Move it, do not redesign it.
- **DO NOT** weaken the panic into a `skip`, a warning, or a silent fallback. Failing
  loudly is the point.
- **DO NOT** add external dependencies.
- **DO NOT** touch the tests' assertions or any non-test code.

## 2. READ FIRST

- `CLAUDE.md` — § Rules (Single Code Path; prefer failure to an undocumented fallback)
- `rust/CLAUDE.md` — § Testing (documents the helper requirement, added by #546)
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr.rs:270-330` — one copy plus its caller
- `rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/inbox.rs:265-320` — the other copy plus its caller
- `Cargo.toml` (repo root) — workspace `members` list
- `git show 5d279c65` — the change that introduced the duplication

## 3. STEPS

### Step 1 — Add a workspace test-support crate

Create `rust/exomonad-test-support/` with:

`rust/exomonad-test-support/Cargo.toml`
```toml
[package]
name = "exomonad-test-support"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false

[dependencies]
tempfile = { workspace = true }
```

`rust/exomonad-test-support/src/lib.rs` — move the helper verbatim from either copy
(they are identical), made `pub`, with the module doc explaining why it exists:

```rust
//! Shared test scaffolding for the ExoMonad workspace.
//!
//! Not published; `publish = false`. Consumed only as a dev-dependency.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// The git repository root containing `path`, if any.
pub fn git_repository_root(path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    // ... verbatim from the existing helper ...
}

/// A temp directory guaranteed not to sit inside any git repository.
///
/// `tempfile::tempdir()` honors `TMPDIR`, which in a dev shell can point at the
/// project root — silently placing "no git repo" fixtures inside the repo. Fail
/// loudly rather than let a test assert the wrong thing.
pub fn tempdir_outside_any_repo() -> tempfile::TempDir {
    // ... verbatim from the existing helper ...
}
```

The existing panic message in `inbox.rs` is inbox-specific ("failed to create an inbox
test directory..."). Generalize it to "failed to create a test directory outside any
git repository", keeping the `.git` path and `TMPDIR` detail.

Register the crate in the root `Cargo.toml` `members` list, after
`rust/exomonad-proto`.

### Step 2 — Consume it from both crates

Add to the `[dev-dependencies]` of **both** `rust/exomonad-core/Cargo.toml` and
`rust/claude-teams-bridge/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
exomonad-test-support = { path = "../exomonad-test-support" }
```

### Step 3 — Delete both copies

Remove `git_repository_root` and `tempdir_outside_any_repo` from
`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr.rs` and
`rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/inbox.rs`, replacing each with an import:

```rust
use exomonad_test_support::tempdir_outside_any_repo;
```

Call sites are unchanged. Drop any `use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};` import that
becomes unused, and let the compiler confirm.

### Step 4 — Documentation

Update `rust/CLAUDE.md` § Testing — it currently says tests "must use the
outside-repository tempdir helper" without naming a location. Point it at
`exomonad-test-support`. Add the crate to the Workspace Members table in
`rust/CLAUDE.md` with type "Library (dev-only)".

## 4. VERIFY

```bash
just build
just check-fmt
just test-fast
nix develop --command cargo clippy --workspace --lib --all-features
```

`just test-fast` must stay at **840 passed, 3 skipped** — this is a pure move, so the
count must not change.

Prove the helper still does its job under both TMPDIR values:

```bash
TMPDIR=/tmp cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib -- services::file_pr
TMPDIR=$PWD cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib -- services::file_pr
TMPDIR=/tmp cargo test -p claude-teams-bridge --lib -- inbox
TMPDIR=$PWD cargo test -p claude-teams-bridge --lib -- inbox
```

All four pass, each in under a second.

Confirm the duplication is gone:

```bash
git grep -n "fn tempdir_outside_any_repo\|fn git_repository_root" -- rust/
```

Exactly one definition of each, both in `rust/exomonad-test-support/src/lib.rs`.

## 5. DONE CRITERIA

- [ ] `exomonad-test-support` crate exists, `publish = false`, in workspace `members`.
- [ ] Exactly one definition of each helper, in that crate.
- [ ] Both consuming crates use it via `[dev-dependencies]`; no dependency added
      between `claude-teams-bridge` and `exomonad-core`.
- [ ] Helper behavior unchanged; panic still reports the `.git` path and `TMPDIR`.
- [ ] `just test-fast` still reports 840 passed, 3 skipped.
- [ ] All four TMPDIR permutations pass in under a second each.
- [ ] `rust/CLAUDE.md` § Testing names the crate; Workspace Members table updated.
- [ ] No new external dependencies; no non-test code changed.
- [ ] **PR filed** with title: `refactor: share outside-repo tempdir helper via test-support crate`
      (#543, #545 and #546 all landed directly on `main` with no PR — do not repeat that).

issues.title: fix: test temp dirs depend on ambient TMPDIR; remove stale Codex-Fugu docs
issues.description:
## Summary

Test isolation silently depends on the ambient `TMPDIR`. When `TMPDIR` points inside
the repository, `tempfile::tempdir()` creates test scratch directories **inside the
exomonad git repo**, and tests that assume "a directory outside any git repo" or "a
shallow path" break.

Observed with `TMPDIR=/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad`:

| Test | Symptom |
|---|---|
| `exomonad-core services::filesystem::tests::test_path_traversal_rejected` | FAIL |
| `exomonad-core services::file_pr::tests::test_file_pr_async_no_git_repo` | SLOW 30s → TIMEOUT 60s |
| `claude-teams-bridge inbox::tests::test_concurrent_writes_no_lost_messages` | FAIL |

All three pass under `TMPDIR=/tmp`.

**Scope note:** the `filesystem` failure is a **real security bug**, tracked separately
as its own issue — it is a canary, not an isolation problem, and its fix is not part of
this issue. This issue covers the environment guard and the other two tests.

### Root cause 1 — the flake guard is too narrow

`flake.nix:100-106`:

```nix
# nix mkShell overrides TMPDIR to /tmp/nix-shell.*, which breaks
# tmux and other tools socket discovery.
# Restore native TMPDIR — devShells are interactive, not hermetic builds.
if [[ "$TMPDIR" == /tmp/nix-shell.* ]]; then
  export TMPDIR="$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR 2>/dev/null || echo /tmp)"
fi
```

`nix mkShell` derives its scratch dir from the **ambient** `TMPDIR`, not from `/tmp`.
So when the ambient value is the repo root, nix produces
`/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad/nix-shell.UVmLia` — which the `/tmp/nix-shell.*`
pattern does not match. The guard silently does nothing and the bad value propagates
into every test process.

Confirmed: inside `nix develop`, `TMPDIR=/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad/nix-shell.UVmLia`.

### Root cause 2 — `test_file_pr_async_no_git_repo` has an unenforced precondition

`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr.rs:427-444` creates a tempdir and asserts
`result.is_err()`. With a repo-nested `TMPDIR`, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` inside
that tempdir returns `/home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad` — the premise "no git repo"
is simply false. `file_pr_async` then proceeds to a real HTTP request to
`http://forgejo.local`, which does not resolve, and the test hangs until nextest's 60s
timeout.

`assert!(result.is_err())` passes for the wrong reason in the good case and hangs in
the bad one. The assertion is too weak to distinguish them.

---

## 1. ANTI-PATTERNS

- **DO NOT** fix the `filesystem` path-traversal test here. It is a genuine security
  bug with its own issue. If it still fails after your change, that is expected —
  leave it.
- **DO NOT** set `TMPDIR` from Rust code, `build.rs`, or a test harness global. The
  environment is process-global and mutating it races across parallel tests.
- **DO NOT** paper over root cause 2 by raising the nextest timeout, marking the test
  `#[ignore]`, or adding a retry. The test must fail fast and deterministically.
- **DO NOT** let any test reach the network. `http://forgejo.local` must never be
  contacted.
- **DO NOT** hardcode `/tmp` in Rust test code without a fallback — use a helper that
  fails loudly if it cannot find a directory outside any git repository.
- **DO NOT** add external dependencies.
- Scope is roughly 50 lines: one nix guard, one test helper, two test fixes.

## 2. READ FIRST

- `CLAUDE.md` — § Rules (Always prefer failure to an undocumented heuristic or fallback)
- `flake.nix:95-115` — the devShell `shellHook`
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr.rs:420-445` — the failing test and
  `file_pr_async`'s early git checks
- `rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/inbox.rs` — `test_concurrent_writes_no_lost_messages`

## 3. STEPS

### Step 1 — Widen the flake TMPDIR guard

In `flake.nix`, replace the guard condition so it matches a nix-created scratch dir
**anywhere**, not only under `/tmp`:

```nix
              # nix mkShell points TMPDIR at a per-shell scratch dir derived from the
              # ambient TMPDIR, which breaks tmux socket discovery and puts test
              # tempdirs inside the repo when the ambient value is the project root.
              # Restore a real system temp dir — devShells are interactive, not
              # hermetic builds.
              if [[ "$TMPDIR" == */nix-shell.* ]]; then
                export TMPDIR="$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR 2>/dev/null || echo /tmp)"
              fi
```

Verify afterwards:

```bash
nix develop --command bash -c 'echo "$TMPDIR"'
```

It must print a system temp dir (`/tmp` on Linux), **not** a path under the repo.

### Step 2 — A test helper that guarantees isolation

Tests that need "a directory outside any git repository" must state and enforce that,
rather than inheriting it from the environment.

Add to `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr.rs` inside `mod tests` (or a shared
test-support module if one already exists — check before creating a new one):

```rust
    /// A temp directory guaranteed not to sit inside any git repository.
    ///
    /// `tempfile::tempdir()` honors `TMPDIR`, which in a dev shell can point at the
    /// project root — silently placing "no git repo" fixtures inside the repo. Fail
    /// loudly rather than let the test assert the wrong thing.
    fn tempdir_outside_any_repo() -> tempfile::TempDir {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("failed to create temp dir");
        let mut cursor = Some(dir.path());
        while let Some(current) = cursor {
            assert!(
                !current.join(".git").exists(),
                "temp dir {} is inside a git repository (found .git at {}). \
                 TMPDIR={:?} — see flake.nix TMPDIR guard.",
                dir.path().display(),
                current.display(),
                std::env::var("TMPDIR").ok(),
            );
            cursor = current.parent();
        }
        dir
    }
```

### Step 3 — Make `test_file_pr_async_no_git_repo` deterministic

Rewrite the test at `file_pr.rs:427-444`:

```rust
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn test_file_pr_async_no_git_repo() -> Result<()> {
        let temp_dir = tempdir_outside_any_repo();
        let git_wt = Arc::new(GitWorktreeService::new(temp_dir.path().to_path_buf()));
        let input = FilePRInput {
            title: "Test PR".to_string(),
            body: "Test Body".to_string(),
            base_branch: None,
            working_dir: Some(temp_dir.path().to_string_lossy().to_string()),
            author_agent: Some("test-agent".to_string()),
            author_role: Some("dev".to_string()),
        };

        let forgejo = ForgejoClient::new("http://forgejo.local", "token").unwrap();
        let err = file_pr_async(&input, git_wt, forgejo.as_ref())
            .await
            .expect_err("filing a PR outside a git repo must fail");

        // Must fail on git repo detection, before any network call. A connection
        // error here means the git precondition was not enforced.
        let message = err.to_string().to_lowercase();
        assert!(
            message.contains("git") || message.contains("repo") || message.contains("branch"),
            "expected a git-repo detection error, got: {err}"
        );

        Ok(())
    }
```

Tighten the substring assertion to whatever `file_pr_async` actually returns — read the
error path rather than guessing, and assert on the specific message. The requirement is
that the test distinguishes "failed because there is no git repo" from "failed because
the network timed out."

The test must complete in well under a second. If it still takes tens of seconds, the
git precondition is not being checked before the HTTP client is used — say so in the PR
rather than working around it.

### Step 4 — `claude-teams-bridge` concurrent-writes test

`rust/claude-teams-bridge/src/inbox.rs::test_concurrent_writes_no_lost_messages` fails
under a repo-nested `TMPDIR` and passes under `/tmp`. Diagnose the actual dependency
before changing it — likely a path-length, nesting, or file-locking assumption.

Fix the underlying assumption. If it turns out to need isolation from the repo, reuse
the same helper pattern from Step 2 rather than duplicating it. **Do not** simply
retry-loop the assertion.

### Step 5 — Documentation

Add a short note to `rust/CLAUDE.md` § Testing recording that tests requiring a
directory outside any git repository must use the helper, and why the flake pins
`TMPDIR`. Two or three sentences.

### Step 6 — Remove stale Codex-Fugu documentation (folded in from #538)

`AgentType::CodexFugu` was removed; no Fugu references remain in any `.rs`/`.hs`
source. Two docs still describe effort-level behavior for the removed harness, which
CLAUDE.md § Style requires cleaning up alongside the change.

- `CLAUDE.md:224` — currently reads
  `# CLI flags override these values. Omitted effort is medium, except Fugu (high).`
  Drop the Fugu clause: `# CLI flags override these values. Omitted effort is medium.`
- `rust/exomonad/CLAUDE.md:72` — currently reads
  `tl_effort_level = "medium"    # CLI overrides config; Fugu omitted => high`
  Drop the Fugu clause: `tl_effort_level = "medium"    # CLI overrides config`

Check the surrounding prose in both files for any other Fugu mention and remove it.

**Leave `docs/decisions/codex-integration.md` § "Codex-Fugu (removed)" untouched.** That
section is a deliberate ADR record of why the harness was dropped and must survive.

`EFFORT_AND_CODEX_FUGU_PLAN.md` has already been deleted from the repo root — do not
re-add it or reference it.

Verify no live references remain outside the ADR:

```bash
git grep -in fugu -- . ':!docs/decisions/codex-integration.md' ':!CHANGELOG.md'
```

This must return no results.

## 4. VERIFY

```bash
just build
just check-fmt
nix develop --command bash -c 'echo TMPDIR=$TMPDIR'   # must NOT be under the repo
```

Then prove independence from the ambient value:

```bash
TMPDIR=/tmp cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib -- services::file_pr
TMPDIR=$PWD cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib -- services::file_pr
TMPDIR=/tmp cargo test -p claude-teams-bridge --lib -- inbox
TMPDIR=$PWD cargo test -p claude-teams-bridge --lib -- inbox
```

All four must pass, and each must finish in seconds — no 30s+ runs.

Finally:

```bash
just test-fast
```

The only acceptable remaining failure is
`services::filesystem::tests::test_path_traversal_rejected`, which belongs to the
separate security issue. Everything else must be green.

## 5. DONE CRITERIA

- [ ] `flake.nix` guard matches `*/nix-shell.*`; `nix develop` yields a system `TMPDIR`.
- [ ] A helper enforces "outside any git repository" and fails loudly with the
      offending `.git` path and the `TMPDIR` value.
- [ ] `test_file_pr_async_no_git_repo` asserts the specific git-detection error, makes
      no network call, and completes in under a second.
- [ ] `test_concurrent_writes_no_lost_messages` passes under both `TMPDIR` values, with
      the real assumption fixed rather than retried around.
- [ ] `just test-fast` green except the separately-tracked filesystem security test.
- [ ] `rust/CLAUDE.md` § Testing documents the requirement.
- [ ] Stale Fugu effort-level docs removed from `CLAUDE.md` and
      `rust/exomonad/CLAUDE.md`; the `codex-integration.md` ADR section preserved;
      `git grep -in fugu` clean outside the ADR and CHANGELOG.
- [ ] No new dependencies; no test marked `#[ignore]`; no timeout raised.
- [ ] **PR filed** with title: `fix: make test temp dirs independent of ambient TMPDIR`

issues.title: Wire and verify TL review recovery commands and operator guidance
issues.description:
Goal: expose both recovery workflows through the correct MCP role surfaces and make the human approval boundary unambiguous. This subissue owns the Haskell tool/schema/role wiring, generated protocol regeneration where required, documentation, and end-to-end assertions; it must consume the backend contracts from the restart and replacement subissues without duplicating lifecycle logic.

ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Do not expose recovery commands to dev leaves or reviewers. They are TL/root tools only.
- Do not let role prompts tell the TL to auto-restart, auto-close issues, or reuse the old leaf slug.
- Do not describe replace_close_pr as a same-PR reset or restart_review as a closed-PR replacement.
- Do not hide the PR number, Chainlink issue id, old/new leaf names, round count, source SHA, or target base branch from the human escalation message.
- Do not update docs without matching tool schemas, role tool lists, and WASM integration tests.

READ FIRST:
- .exo/roles/devswarm/RootRole.hs and TLRole.hs
- .exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md and tl.md
- CLAUDE.md review policy, Stuck escalation, lifecycle, and MCP tool matrix
- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/RestartReview.hs
- existing tool patterns for structured responses and effect suspension
- proto/effects/agent.proto, proto generation recipes, and rust/exomonad-core/tests/wasm_integration.rs

STEPS:
1. Define the public MCP schema and descriptions for restart_review and replace_close_pr. Clearly state that a human must approve the action and that the TL records the approval in its operator-facing message or Chainlink comment.
2. Keep restart_review available only to TL/root and describe its precondition: the PR is open and unmerged; it preserves the author worktree and resets only the same PR review cycle.
3. Add replace_close_pr to TL/root only. Require explicit old and new leaf identities and Chainlink issue continuity; require a closed, unmerged old PR; explain that it retires the old worktree and starts a fresh dev leaf from the preserved old head toward the original base.
4. Update root/TL guidance for [STUCK] handling: report reviewer_max_rounds, PR state, Chainlink issue, and exact next choices; ask the human whether to restart the same open PR or replace a closed PR; never perform either action without approval.
5. Ensure the watcher notification contains enough data for the TL to ask the human, including PR number, issue metadata when available, head branch/SHA, review rounds, and whether the PR is open or closed.

issues.title: Add TL-approved closed-PR replacement workflow
issues.description:
Goal: add the separate TL/root MCP workflow replace_close_pr for a Forgejo PR that the human has approved for replacement after it was closed without merging. The Chainlink issue continues; the old PR review counter and leaf identity must not leak into the replacement.

Suggested request shape:
- chainlink_issue_id: positive Chainlink issue id that remains open
- closed_pr_number: positive Forgejo PR number
- old_leaf_name: explicit author leaf identity to retire
- new_leaf_name: required fresh leaf slug; it must differ from old_leaf_name and be unique
- replacement_task: complete task/spec for the new dev leaf
- optional agent_type and operator context
The implementation may refine field names, but the old PR, issue, old identity, new identity, source branch, and base branch must be explicit in the response.

ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Do not accept an open PR; use restart_review instead.
- Do not accept a merged PR as a replacement target.
- Do not rename a live agent or worktree in place. Agent identity, resolver keys, tmux routing, and worktree directory are coupled.
- Do not reuse old_leaf_name, silently create a new slug, or let spawn_leaf discover and reuse the old worktree.
- Do not dispose the old worktree before capturing and validating the remote source branch and exact head SHA.
- Do not lose old-PR commits. The replacement leaf must start from the old PR head or exact head SHA.
- Do not make the old PR head branch the new PR base. The new PR must target the old PR base branch, with the old head used only as the source/start point.
- Do not close the Chainlink issue or manufacture a new issue.
- Do not claim success if cleanup or spawn fails; preserve enough branch metadata for a retry.

READ FIRST:
- proto/effects/agent.proto and generated Rust/Haskell bindings
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs, agent-control cleanup, resolver, and reviewer cleanup paths
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr.rs
- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/Spawn.hs and role tool wiring
- Chainlink metadata helpers and existing close_issue_and_cleanup behavior

STEPS:
1. Validate request ids/names and query Forgejo. Require closed_pr_number to be closed and unmerged. Capture head branch, base branch, exact head SHA, PR metadata, and author identity. If available, verify the PR metadata points to chainlink_issue_id and old_leaf_name; reject mismatches rather than disposing an unrelated leaf, with an explicit override only if the project already has an established safe pattern.
2. Verify the source branch/head is reachable locally or fetch it from the configured remote before cleanup. Keep the old branch as a recoverable source; never delete it as part of replacement.
3. Dispose reviewer resources and clear old PR watcher/review artifacts. Retire the old author leaf through the normal cleanup path, including tmux window, resolver record, config directory, and git worktree. Do not close the Chainlink issue.
4. Create a fresh author identity and worktree using new_leaf_name. Extend the spawn/worktree API as needed to distinguish PR base_branch from worktree start_point: the new branch must be based on the old PR head SHA while the new PR base remains the old PR base branch. Preserve normal dot-separated branch naming and ensure the new slug cannot match an existing worktree.
5. Start the new dev leaf with replacement_task plus explicit context: Chainlink issue id, old PR number/state, source branch/SHA, target base branch, review history, and instruction to file a new PR. The new leaf must not resume the closed PR as if it were open.
6. Make the operation idempotent. A retry after partial cleanup must detect an existing replacement identity/branch and resume or return its details instead of creating duplicate leaves. If spawning fails, return old/new identity, source SHA, cleanup status, and a retry-safe error.
7. Return structured response data: old PR and state, Chainlink issue id, retired author/reviewer resources, source branch/SHA, new leaf name, new branch, worktree path, base branch, spawn status, and next operator action. Emit an audit event linking old PR to replacement identity without changing the Chainlink issue status.
8. Add tests for closed/open/merged validation, mismatched author or issue metadata, branch preservation, fresh slug enforcement, source-versus-base branch separation, cleanup failure, spawn failure, and idempotent retry.

VERIFY:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- focused handler, agent-control, git-worktree, and file-pr tests
- cargo test --workspace
- just wasm-all and WASM integration coverage for the new effect/tool
- a Forgejo-backed or deterministic fixture test proving a closed PR can produce a new PR with a fresh watcher key

DONE CRITERIA:
A TL-approved closed, unmerged PR can be replaced without stale worktree/event identity, without losing commits, without closing the Chainlink issue, and without carrying the old PR review counter into the new PR. Failure and retry behavior is explicit and safe.

issues.title: Add explicit recovery workflows for same-PR restarts and closed-PR replacement
issues.description:
Problem: the existing restart_review(pr_number) resets reviewer state but does not model author-leaf lifecycle. If a TL closes a Forgejo PR and starts another leaf, the old agent slug and worktree can be reused, leaving stale identity and event-routing state. Same-PR continuation and closed-PR replacement need separate explicit workflows.

Scope:
- Keep same-PR recovery for an open, unmerged PR through TL/root MCP tool restart_review.
- Add a TL/root MCP tool named replace_close_pr for a closed, unmerged PR. It must preserve Chainlink issue continuity, retire the old author leaf safely, and create a fresh author identity/worktree/branch for the replacement PR.
- Preserve the old reviewed branch as the source of the replacement work so fixes are not lost, while the new PR targets the old PR base branch rather than accidentally targeting the old head branch.
- Never auto-reset after max rounds and never rename a live worktree in place.

ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Do not use restart_review on a closed or merged PR.
- Do not reuse the old leaf slug when creating a replacement leaf.
- Do not dispose the old worktree before recording and validating its source branch and head SHA.
- Do not silently discard old-branch commits or create a replacement PR against the old PR head as its base.
- Do not close the Chainlink issue as part of replacement; the issue remains active until the replacement PR converges and merges.
- Do not make either workflow an automatic escape from reviewer_max_rounds; the TL calls it only after human approval.

- CLAUDE.md sections on review policy, Stuck escalation, PR workflow, and tool role matrix

- proto/effects/agent.proto and generated Rust/Haskell bindings

1. Harden restart_review for same-PR recovery and explicit open/unmerged validation.
2. Implement replace_close_pr as a separate closed-PR replacement lifecycle, including source-branch preservation and fresh identity/worktree creation.

issues.title: Fix watcher review comments delivery to the TL

comments.content: Diagnosis and acceptance criteria: The watcher currently emits review_commented/review_received but routes the event through the PR author's dev branch and the dev handler returns InjectMessage, so the TL handler is never selected. For every new reviewer comment or requested-change review on an open/unmerged PR, deliver one actionable parent/TL notification containing the PR number, head branch, review kind, author branch when available, and full review text; the TL must receive it through its inbox/tmux route and be able to spawn a replacement dev leaf. Add Rust/Haskell regression tests covering watcher event generation, parent/TL routing, payload preservation, deduplication, and delivery-target resolution. Diagnosis: Chainlink-Issue metadata is not used as the reviewer-spawn key; watcher state is keyed by Forgejo PR number/head SHA. A fresh spawn_leaf from the TL creates a child branch/PR, so fixes do not change the original reviewed PR unless the exact existing leaf worktree/branch is resumed. The watcher also skips reviewer spawn when the PR's recorded author worktree is absent. This explains why a dev leaf can push fixes under another Chainlink task/PR without triggering a reviewer for the original PR.

Live diagnosis confirmed: /home/goya/storage/RustDebuggerRepo/.exo/review-policy.toml sets reviewer_max_rounds = 2. At the affected cycle, PRs #48/#49/#50/#51 had changes_requested_rounds=2 and PR #52 had 3; the watcher gate is state.rounds < max_rounds, so no new reviewer is spawned after another fix push. The Chainlink task/PR association is not consulted by the spawn gate. Logs show stale review commits being dropped by SHA, but historical requested-change rounds still count toward the max. The TL manually spawned reviewers because the automatic round gate was exhausted.

issues.title: Fix cross-backend git remote confusion: add exomonad init --set-git-remote
issues.description:
## Bug

`exomonad serve` conflates git remotes across backends. When a repo has two
remotes configured (e.g. `origin` -> GitHub, plus a second remote pointing at
a local Forgejo instance), owner/repo resolution for Forgejo API calls picks
up the GitHub owner instead of the Forgejo owner, and every Forgejo PR/CI
call 404s:

```
WARN exomonad_core::services::worktree_event_watcher: Watcher cycle failed:
list Forgejo pull requests failed with HTTP 404 Not Found:
{"message":"GetUserByName","url":"http://localhost:3000/api/swagger",
 "errors":["user redirect does not exist [name: nanonite]"]}
```

(`nanonite` here is the GitHub username on `origin`, not a Forgejo user —
the `url` field in the error body is Gitea/Forgejo's generic swagger-docs
pointer, not the request URL; it's a red herring.)

Confirmed as an exomonad bug, not a user config mistake — there is currently
no config knob that lets a project disambiguate which remote belongs to
which backend.

## Root cause

`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/repo.rs`:
- `select_remote()` (line 67) always prefers a remote literally named
  `origin` if one exists, else falls back to the first remote `git remote`
  lists. It has no concept of "which remote is the Forgejo one."
- `get_repo_info()` (line 22) calls `detect_first_remote` ->
  `select_remote`, then parses `(owner, repo)` out of whatever URL that one
  remote has, via the host-agnostic `parse_github_url`.

That single, backend-blind `(owner, repo)` pair is used verbatim by
**every** caller of `repo::get_repo_info()` — confirmed via grep, this is
18 call sites, not a handful: `services/file_pr.rs`, `services/merge_pr.rs`,
`services/worktree_event_watcher.rs` (x3), `services/copilot_review.rs`,
`services/github_poller.rs` (hibernated, zero active call sites),
`services/agent_control/spawn.rs` (x3), `handlers/file_pr.rs` (x3),
`handlers/session.rs`, `handlers/forgejo_as_github.rs`, `handlers/agent.rs`
(x2), `exomonad/src/serve.rs`.

Push is hardcoded to `origin` too:
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs`: `push_bookmark_with_token`
  (used by `file_pr_async`) always runs `git push origin {branch}` via
  `push_origin_command` (line 91), optionally injecting the Forgejo token as
  an `http.extraheader`. There is already a separate, tested
  `push_to_remote(workspace_path, branch, remote: &str)` (line 308) that
  pushes to an arbitrary named remote (tests already cover pushing to a
  remote named `"forgejo"`, see `test_push_to_remote_with_remote`) — but it
  does **not** inject the Forgejo token auth header.

And `exomonad init` bakes the same "origin is the Forgejo remote" assumption
into its one-time setup:
- `rust/exomonad/src/init.rs:168` `configure_forgejo_remote` runs
  `git remote get-url origin` / `git remote set-url origin <token-url>` to
  embed the Forgejo PAT into `origin`'s URL. If `origin` is GitHub and
  Forgejo lives on a second remote, this function never looks at that second
  remote at all.

## Proposed design (revised — see history for the original config.toml/Services plan)

The original plan (new `git_remote` config.toml field + `HasGitRemote`
capability trait threaded through `Services` + updating every one of the 18
call sites individually) was scoped before the call-site count was known.
That's a large, error-prone diff for a small fix. Revised design:

**Use `git config --local exomonad.remote <name>` as the override,
read directly inside `repo::get_repo_info()`.** This fixes all 18 call
sites transparently with a change to a single function, because every
caller already just calls `get_repo_info(working_dir)` — none of them need
to change.

1. `exomonad init --set-git-remote <name>`:
   - Validate `<name>` is an existing git remote (`git remote` in the
     project dir must list it) — fail fast with a clear error otherwise,
     per the "prefer failure to an undocumented heuristic" rule in
     `CLAUDE.md`.
   - Run `git config --local exomonad.remote <name>` in the project root.
     Git worktrees share the main repo's `.git/config` for repo-level
     config, so every spawned agent worktree picks this up automatically —
     no config.toml, no per-worktree propagation needed.
   - Update `configure_forgejo_remote` (init.rs:168) to target this
     resolved remote name (default `"origin"` when unset) instead of the
     hardcoded `git remote get-url origin` / `git remote set-url origin`.

2. `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/repo.rs`: `get_repo_info()` reads
   `git config --get exomonad.remote` first (git exits 1 when the key is
   absent — that is not an error, it just means "unset", fall through to
   today's `detect_first_remote`/`select_remote` auto-detect). When the key
   is set, use that literal remote name directly for
   `get_remote_url` -> `parse_github_url`, skipping auto-detect entirely.
   **Default (key unset): zero behavior change** — every existing
   single-remote-named-`origin` workflow behaves identically to today.

3. `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs`: add a sync
   equivalent of the same git-config lookup (this module uses
   `std::process::Command`, not async), and a
   `push_to_remote_with_token(workspace_path, branch, remote, forgejo_token)`
   that generalizes `push_origin_command`'s token-header injection to an
   arbitrary remote name (merging it with the existing
   `push_to_remote`'s named-remote arg). `push_bookmark_with_token`
   resolves the configured remote (default `"origin"`) and delegates to it.

No new config.toml field. No `Services` field. No capability trait. No
changes to `file_pr.rs`, `merge_pr.rs`, `worktree_event_watcher.rs`,
`handlers/*.rs`, `spawn.rs`, `github_poller.rs`, `copilot_review.rs`,
`serve.rs` — they all keep calling `get_repo_info(dir)` exactly as today.

## Anti-patterns (read before implementing)

- Do NOT thread a remote-name parameter through the 18 `get_repo_info`
  call sites. The whole point of the git-config approach is that none of
  them change.
- Do NOT change `select_remote()`'s default "prefer origin" auto-detect —
  it remains the fallback when `exomonad.remote` is unset.
- Do NOT add a `config.toml` field, `Services` field, or capability trait
  for this. Git config is the persistence layer; nothing else needs to
  know about it.
- Do NOT remove or rename `push_origin_command`, `push_bookmark_with_token`,
  `push_to_remote`, or `get_repo_info` — extend, don't replace.
- Do NOT add the flag to `exomonad new` — this is an `exomonad init`-time
  operational setting, not one-time project bootstrap.
- Do NOT silently accept a `--set-git-remote` value that isn't a real git
  remote — validate against `git remote` output and fail loudly.

## Read first

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/repo.rs` (full file — small, ~193 lines)
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs:85-332`
- `rust/exomonad/src/init.rs:160-300` (`configure_forgejo_remote` and
  helpers)
- `rust/exomonad/src/main.rs:66-121` (`Init` command CLI args — follow the
  `--tl` / `--worker` pattern for the new flag's declaration/doc comment)

## Verify

```bash
just build                          # Rust workspace build (never raw cargo build)
cargo test -p exomonad-core         # repo.rs, git_worktree.rs unit tests
cargo test -p exomonad              # init.rs CLI + remote config tests
just pre-commit                     # full check suite
```

Add unit tests mirroring existing coverage:
- `repo.rs`: `get_repo_info` honors `exomonad.remote` when set (temp git
  repo, `git config --local exomonad.remote <name>`, non-origin remote
  added, assert parsed owner/repo comes from the named remote not origin)
  and falls back to auto-detect when unset (existing tests must still
  pass unchanged).
- `git_worktree.rs`: `push_to_remote_with_token` injects the auth header
  for an HTTP remote and omits it for SSH (mirror
  `push_origin_command_injects_forgejo_token_extraheader` /
  `test_push_to_remote_with_remote`); `push_bookmark_with_token` respects
  `exomonad.remote` when set.
- `init.rs`: `--set-git-remote` rejects a nonexistent remote name; sets
  `git config --local exomonad.remote` correctly for a valid one;
  `configure_forgejo_remote` targets the configured remote instead of
  hardcoded `origin` when set (mirror
  `forgejo_token_remote_url_rewrites_matching_ssh_origin`).

## Done criteria

- `exomonad init --set-git-remote forgejo` validates the remote exists,
  then runs `git config --local exomonad.remote forgejo` in the project
  root.
- With `exomonad.remote` unset, all existing single-remote (`origin`)
  workflows behave identically to today (no regression) — verified by
  existing `repo.rs`/`git_worktree.rs` tests passing unchanged.
- With `exomonad.remote` set to a remote distinct from `origin`,
  `get_repo_info()` (and therefore file_pr, merge_pr, the worktree event
  watcher, and every other current caller) resolves owner/repo from the
  named remote instead of `origin`; push goes to the named remote too.
- A repo with `origin` = GitHub and a second remote pointing at a local
  Forgejo instance, configured via `--set-git-remote`, no longer produces
  the `GetUserByName ... user redirect does not exist` 404.
- All new code has unit tests per the Verify section; `just pre-commit`
  passes clean.

In progress — implementing per the git-config design above (approved to
proceed after confirming call-site count and revised approach with the

issues.title: exomonad models: bring gemini/claude/codex/codex-fugu up to opencode's live-query standard
issues.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

`exomonad models` only queries live for opencode (rust/exomonad/src/models.rs:18-34,
shells out to `opencode models [provider]`). gemini, claude, codex, and codex-fugu
each print a hardcoded static list (models.rs:36-69) with a disclaimer that the list
may be stale. Bring the other harnesses up to opencode's standard: live discovery
where the harness/provider exposes it, otherwise keep a static fallback but make it
easy to keep current.

## Per-harness investigation (do this first, one leaf/worker each)

- **claude**: Anthropic exposes a `GET /v1/models` API endpoint. Check whether the
  `claude` CLI has an equivalent subcommand, or whether we should hit the Anthropic
  API directly (needs an API key — check what auth is already available to the
  harness, e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or the CLI's own auth). If the CLI has no
  subcommand and calling the API directly requires credentials we can't assume are
  present, document that and keep the static list but make it easy to regenerate.
- **codex**: Check `codex --help` / `codex models` / OpenAI's `GET /v1/models` API for
  a discovery path. Same credential caveat as claude.
- **gemini**: Check `gemini --help` for a models subcommand, and whether the
  Gemini API exposes a `models.list` endpoint reachable with existing CLI auth.
- **codex-fugu**: Current comment says "model discovery is not exposed, static list
  is provider-defined" — verify that's still true before assuming it stays static.

## Implementation

For each harness where live discovery is confirmed possible without new credential
requirements, mirror `run_opencode`'s pattern in `rust/exomonad/src/models.rs`:
shell out to the harness CLI (or call the provider API if the CLI has no
subcommand) and stream/print the live result, with the same
`.context("Failed to spawn ... — is X on PATH?")` style error handling and
graceful "unavailable" fallback in `run_all`.

Where live discovery isn't possible (no CLI subcommand, no API without extra
credentials), leave the static list but note it explicitly is a fallback in the
same style as today's disclaimers — do not silently keep it looking equivalent to
a live-queried harness.

## Anti-patterns
- Do not invent a live-discovery mechanism that doesn't exist — verify via
  `--help` output or actual docs, not assumption.
- Do not require new credentials/config the user hasn't already set up just to
  make `exomonad models` work — that regresses the zero-config UX.
- Keep `run_all`'s per-harness error isolation (one harness failing must not
  break the others' output).

## Verify
`cargo build -p exomonad` then manually run `exomonad models` (no harness arg,
and with `--harness claude|codex|gemini|codex-fugu`) and confirm output.

## Done criteria
Each harness either queries live (matching opencode's behavior) or, if that's
genuinely not possible, has that constraint documented in the issue and in the
disclaimer text — no harness silently stays stale without a stated reason.

comments.content:

issues.title: spawn_leaf cannot resume from existing remote branch when local worktree was deleted
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

When a dev-leaf's local worktree is deleted (cleanup after context loss, manual removal, etc.) but the remote branch and open PR still exist on Forgejo, spawn_leaf has no recovery path.

Current behavior in spawn_leaf_subtree (spawn.rs:1743-1758):
- worktree exists + tmux alive → return early (idempotent) ✓
- worktree exists + tmux gone → reuse worktree, start new session ✓
- worktree missing → calls create_worktree_checked which calls git worktree add <path> <branch>

The third path fails when the branch only exists on the remote (not fetched locally). git worktree add requires the branch to exist locally. It does not fetch from remote automatically. Result: spawn fails with a git error, or succeeds but on a new branch if the base branch is used instead.

Even if create_worktree_checked is made to fetch first (the fix below), the respawned leaf also needs to know not to file a new PR — it should be told the existing PR number and that it is resuming reviewer feedback, not starting fresh.

Concrete scenario that triggered this:
- Leaf rework-pr22-bp-model-opencode filed PR #23
- Leaf context was lost mid-review (session timeout)
- Worktree deleted during cleanup
- Remote branch main.rework-pr22-bp-model-opencode and PR #23 still open
- TL respawn attempt hits the missing-local-branch gap

Fix:
1. Before create_worktree_checked, check if the branch exists on the remote (git ls-remote origin <branch>). If it does, run git fetch origin <branch>:<branch> to create the local tracking branch, then call git worktree add normally.
2. After creating the worktree, check if an open PR already exists for the branch (via Forgejo API). If one does, include the existing PR number and review comments in the task context injected into the new leaf session so it resumes rather than re-files.

The second part (PR context injection on resume) is what prevents the leaf from filing PR #24, #25, etc. on repeated respawns.

issues.title: Ghost poke loop: check_inbox drains wrong agent key, unread messages never cleared
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

The watcher pokes the TL repeatedly ('You have 1 unread message(s)') but check_inbox returns 0 every time. The inbox is never cleared and the poke loop is infinite.

ROOT CAUSE:
agents_needing_poke() queries WHERE m.read_at IS NULL and returns to_agent as the agent_id (the literal stored value, e.g. 'root-claude').

check_inbox calls drain_unread(canonical_check_agent_key(ctx.agent_name)).

canonical_check_agent_key('root'): if 'root' is a registered AgentName in AgentResolver, it returns 'root' immediately (first branch, inbox_store.rs handlers/inbox.rs canonical_check_agent_key). Then drain_unread('root') runs and normalize_agent_id('root') produces 'root'. The SQL WHERE to_agent = 'root' finds 0 rows because messages were stored as to_agent = 'root-claude'.

The mismatch: messages are written by notify_parent_delivery using the parent's canonical suffixed name ('root-claude' from supervisor registry), but check_inbox drains under the bare name ('root' from ctx.agent_name). Neither is marked read. agents_needing_poke sees the same rows every poll and pokes again.

DIAGNOSTIC:
Check inbox.db in live session:
  sqlite3 .exo/inbox.db 'SELECT to_agent, read_at FROM messages WHERE read_at IS NULL LIMIT 20;'
This will confirm whether stored to_agent values include the harness suffix.

FIX OPTIONS:
1. canonical_check_agent_key: when AgentResolver has 'root' registered, return the CANONICAL name from the registry record (e.g. 'root-claude'), not the input key. The current code returns agent_key.to_string() when resolver.get(&name).is_some() -- this is wrong.
2. Or: normalize_agent_id used in write_message and drain_unread should strip harness suffixes so both sides agree on the canonical key.
3. Or: drain_unread should also drain messages stored under slug aliases (query by slug OR canonical name).

The safest fix is option 1: canonical_check_agent_key should return the canonical AgentName from the resolver record, not the input key.

FILES:
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/inbox.rs (canonical_check_agent_key function)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs (normalize_agent_id, drain_unread)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/delivery.rs (write_message to_agent value)

issues.title: Reviewer task prompt instructs notify_parent but tool is not in reviewer role
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:

The Codex reviewer workflow in spawn.rs (line 466) says:
  '6. Call notify_parent with status=success after submitting the review, then stop.'

The Key Rules also say:

The Key Rules failure case ('PR author is you') is also broken for the same reason -- and the direct Forgejo API section already explains the reviewer may have no .exo/server.sock, so notify_parent (which requires MCP socket) can't be reliable there either.

FIX:
Remove step 6 from the reviewer workflow prompt. Replace with: 'Exit after submitting. The ExoMonad watcher reads Forgejo reviews and routes the result to the dev and TL automatically.'

Remove the notify_parent failure instruction from Key Rules. The reviewer's only failure signal is the stop hook being blocked -- the stuck escalation path handles the case where the reviewer cannot proceed.

FILES:
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs -- reviewer workflow step 6 and Key Rules
- docs/architecture/agent-system.md -- verify tool matrix row for reviewer is consistent

issues.title: Reviewer stuck: CommitsPushedEv resets ReviewerDone back to ReviewerReviewing after verdict posted
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Symptom

Reviewer agent posts a valid APPROVED verdict (via approve_pr tool, which calls applyEvent ReviewerApprovedEv and transitions to ReviewerDone), then immediately gets blocked on the stop hook:
  'PR #N is under review. Post an approval or requested-changes verdict before exiting.'

Reviewer then loops, trying additional API calls that don't help.

## Root cause

ReviewerPhase.transition ignores the current phase entirely for ALL events:
  transition _phase event = case event of
    ReviewerFixesPushedEv prNum _ci -> Transitioned (ReviewerReviewing prNum)
    ReviewerCommitsPushedEv prNum _ci -> Transitioned (ReviewerReviewing prNum)
    ReviewerApprovedEv _ -> Transitioned ReviewerDone
    ...

This means the watcher's CommitsPushedEv or FixesPushedEv can fire AFTER the reviewer has posted its verdict, transitioning ReviewerDone back to ReviewerReviewing:

1. approve_pr called -> applyEvent ReviewerApprovedEv -> KV = ReviewerDone
2. Watcher polls Forgejo, detects commits on the PR -> fires ReviewerCommitsPushedEv
3. transition ReviewerDone (ReviewerCommitsPushedEv prNum ci) -> Transitioned (ReviewerReviewing prNum)
4. KV = ReviewerReviewing prNum
5. Stop hook: canExit (ReviewerReviewing prNum) = MustBlock -> reviewer blocked

The reviewer already did its job, but the watcher reactivated it. ReviewerDone and ReviewerFailed must be terminal states that reject further transitions.

## Key files

- .exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerPhase.hs — transition function ignores current phase
- .exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs — reviewerPRReviewHandler fires applyEvent for CommitsPushed/FixesPushed events
- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/StateMachine.hs — applyEvent applies transition without terminal state guards

## Fix

In ReviewerPhase, guard terminal states before the wildcard match:
  transition ReviewerDone _ = InvalidTransition "reviewer already completed"
  transition (ReviewerFailed _) _ = InvalidTransition "reviewer already failed"
  transition _phase event = case event of
    ReviewerFixesPushedEv prNum _ci -> Transitioned (ReviewerReviewing prNum)
    ...

This makes ReviewerDone and ReviewerFailed truly terminal — once posted, no watcher event can re-activate the reviewer.

## Secondary: silent applyEvent failure

applyEvent uses 'void $ applyEvent ...' in tool handlers. If setPhase fails (KV write error), the error is silently discarded and the phase is not updated. This is a secondary failure mode: consider logging the failure or propagating it to the tool result.

comments.content: Implemented in commit 31166eb5. Added terminal ReviewerDone/ReviewerFailed guards before wildcard reviewer event transitions; verified with just fmt and just wasm-all.

issues.title: Secondary reviewer intermittently not spawned / review not completed
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Symptom

Secondary review (reviewer agent re-spawned after dev pushes fixes, or second reviewer triggered by external_review_threshold / external_review_paths) sometimes does not happen or does not produce a result. Observed as PRs stalling without a second review verdict.

## Suspected causes

1. reviewer_spawned flag set before spawn confirms success (worktree_event_watcher.rs ~line 1318/1382):
   The reviewer is launched via tokio::spawn (fire-and-forget), then ws.reviewer_spawned = true is set immediately after, regardless of whether spawn_reviewer_for_pr inside the task actually succeeds. If the inner future fails, reviewer_spawned stays true, blocking any re-spawn on the next watcher cycle.

2. should_spawn_reviewer_for_new_head guard (line 240-241):
   fn should_spawn_reviewer_for_new_head(state, max_rounds) -> bool {
     !state.reviewer_spawned && state.rounds < max_rounds
   }
   If reviewer_spawned was set true by a prior failed spawn (see #1), this returns false and no second spawn happens until reviewer_spawned is reset (only happens on new head detection at line 1294).

3. terminal_review_observed gate (line ~1363):
   The new-PR reviewer spawn is guarded by !terminal_review_observed. If the watcher restarts and replays events out of order, terminal_review_observed could be true before the second reviewer is spawned.

4. External review threshold / path matching:
   review_policy.rs lines_trigger_external_review and path_triggers_external_review are evaluated against PR metadata. If PR metadata (lines changed, file paths) isn't fetched yet when the spawn decision runs, the second reviewer may be skipped.

## Key files

- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:240 — should_spawn_reviewer_for_new_head
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:1294-1320 — reviewer_spawned reset + first spawn
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:1364-1382 — second/new-PR spawn path
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/review_policy.rs:133,147 — external review trigger checks

## Investigation needed

- Verify reviewer_spawned is only set true when spawn_reviewer_for_pr succeeds (fix: move set inside tokio::spawn, after Ok())
- Add logging at each reviewer spawn guard branch to surface which condition is blocking
- Check whether reviewer_spawned needs a timeout reset if the spawned reviewer task never completes

issues.title: Stale inbox poke loop: check_inbox drains 'root' but messages stored under 'root-claude'
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Symptom

Root TL enters an infinite loop: poke fires → TL calls check_inbox → returns {count:0,messages:[]} → poke fires again. Reproducible on branch harness-agnostic-teams-inbox-messaging after a child agent notifies the parent.

## Root cause

Two code paths use different identifiers for the same agent:

Write path (delivery.rs ~line 590, record_inbox_delivery):
  canonical_recipient_key('root', resolver) checks if 'root' is a known agent_name — it is NOT (root TL is stored as 'root-claude'). Slug lookup: slug='root' → agent_name='root-claude'. Message stored as to_agent='root-claude'.

Drain path (handlers/inbox.rs, check_inbox handler):
  drain_unread(ctx.agent_name.as_str()) where ctx.agent_name='root' (from MCP URL /agents/root/root/tools/call). Queries WHERE to_agent='root'. No match. Returns empty.

Consequence:
- Message with to_agent='root-claude' sits with read_at=NULL forever
- agents_needing_poke finds it (read_at IS NULL), routes poke to TL window via 'root-claude' routing.json
- TL calls check_inbox → drain('root') → empty → poke fires again after backoff
- Suppression never triggers: drain_unread('root') updates agent_inbox_meta for 'root', not 'root-claude'
- The actual message IS delivered correctly via Teams inbox (native CC). The stuck ExoMonad inbox_store copy is the problem.

## Key files

- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/delivery.rs:590 — canonical_recipient_key call in record_inbox_delivery
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/inbox.rs — check_inbox drain uses ctx.agent_name
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs:151 — agents_needing_poke (read_at IS NULL)

## Fix options

A (recommended): Fix check_inbox handler to use canonical_recipient_key before draining so drain matches write path.

B: Fix record_inbox_delivery to store under bare agent_key (no slug resolution). Update poke routing to canonicalize candidate.agent_id before route_tmux_notification.

C (root fix): Align agent_name in MCP config and routing.json as the FIXME in close_self describes. Write routing.json under bare slug 'root' so canonical_recipient_key('root') hits the first branch and returns 'root' — both paths then use same key.

issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:

Expected: 
Actual: 

# Symptom
`just role-hook-tests` fails:
```
role-hook-tests.wasm: Uncaught exception ... user error (PR review event unexpectedly suspended)
```
This was masked until 2026-06-17 by an earlier assertion failure at Main.hs:300 (fixed in commit d07ed859, #506). With that fixed, the suite now runs further and reveals THIS pre-existing failure.

# Root cause
`assertMergeReadyReviewNotifiesParent` / `assertMergeReadyCIStatusNotifiesParent` call `runPRReviewEvent` / `runCIStatusEvent` (.exo/roles/devswarm/test/Main.hs ~l.434-446), which interpret the handler with:
```
runM $ runC $ runFileSystemSuspend $ runAgentControlSuspend (onPRReview (eventHandlers cfg) event)
```
`runAgentControlSuspend` and `runFileSystemSuspend` SUSPEND (yield `C.Continue`) whenever the handler invokes an AgentControl or FileSystem effect. The test expects `C.Done`.

The `DevRole` MergeReady handler (.exo/lib/PRReviewHandler.hs:107-111) now performs effects before returning:
```haskell
prReviewHandler (MergeReady n ci branch_) = do
  logHandler ...
  branch <- getCurrentBranch                 -- AgentControl/StopHook effect -> SUSPENDS under the test interpreter
  void $ applyEvent @DevPhase @DevEvent branch DevSpawned (MergeReadyEv n ci branch_)  -- state/KV effect
  pure (NotifyParentAction (Tpl.mergeReady n ci branch_) n)
```
`getCurrentBranch` (haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Effects/StopHook.hs:73) was added to the handler by the sequential-CI-dev-phase work AFTER this test was written; the test harness still suspends on those effects, so the handler can never reach `Done`. The CIStatus path has the same shape.

This is NOT caused by the #508 notify_parent work (pure Rust) nor by the #506 assertion fix — it predates both. It is genuine test rot: role-hook-tests has been red across several commits, with failures stacked behind one another (HUnit's `fail` throws and aborts the executable on the first failure).

# Fix direction (decide with reviewer)
Option 1 (preferred): give `runPRReviewEvent`/`runCIStatusEvent` a NON-suspending interpreter that PROVIDES the effects the handler legitimately uses — return a stub branch for `getCurrentBranch` and a no-op/in-memory interpreter for the state effect behind `applyEvent` — so the handler runs to `Done` and the test can assert `NotifyParentAction`. Look for existing pure/stub interpreters (analogous to `runAgentControlSuspend`) in haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Effects/{AgentControl,FileSystem}.hs and StateMachine.hs; add stub runners if none exist.
- Verify whether `applyEvent` (haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/StateMachine.hs:108) needs FileSystem/KV and provide a matching stub.

Option 2: if the phase transition + getCurrentBranch are NOT meant to run during event dispatch in production either, that's a deeper handler-design question — escalate.

After fixing, AUDIT the whole role-hook-tests suite for further stacked failures (run to completion, not just first-failure) so we do not uncover yet another masked break later.

- .exo/roles/devswarm/test/Main.hs (l.221-234 hook tests for the pattern; l.421-454 the failing event tests + helpers)
- .exo/lib/PRReviewHandler.hs (l.107-123 DevRole MergeReady/etc; l.126+ TL handler)

- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Effects/AgentControl.hs (runAgentControlSuspend l.200), FileSystem.hs (runFileSystemSuspend l.116), StopHook.hs (getCurrentBranch l.73), StateMachine.hs (applyEvent l.108)

# VERIFY
- `just role-hook-tests` exits 0 and runs ALL assertions to completion.
- `just test` green overall.

# DONE CRITERIA
- MergeReady + CIStatus event tests pass by exercising the real handler effects via stub interpreters (no assertion weakened to accept suspension).
- Whole role-hook-tests suite audited and green.

# FILES
- .exo/roles/devswarm/test/Main.hs
- possibly haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Effects/*.hs (stub interpreters)

issues.title: notify_parent/send_message: canonicalize inbox recipient key via AgentResolver
issues.description:
# Goal
Make the durable inbox `to_agent` key ALWAYS equal the recipient's own drain key (its AgentName), so cross-agent messages are never orphaned. The structural notify_parent case (top-level branch -> `root`) was fixed in commit 00bccc4a (#508 first pass). This task closes the REMAINING gaps on the send/peer path.

# Background (already done — do NOT redo)
- `delivery::canonical_parent_recipient` collapses a top-level parent branch (`main`/`master`, no dot) to `root`. Applied at the 3 notify_parent sources (events.rs structural, worktree_event_watcher.rs, github_poller.rs).
- `inbox_store::normalize_agent_id` is now a PURE last-dot-segment strip (the `main->root` heuristic was removed). It canonicalizes a dotted branch (`main.foo-codex`) to its bare last segment (`foo-codex`).
- Agents drain their inbox under their SUFFIXED AgentName (e.g. `fix-ci-fmt-opencode`, `review-pr-5-codex`), confirmed against `.exo/inbox.db` `agent_inbox_meta`.

# Remaining bugs to fix

## Bug A — send-side slug-vs-suffix mismatch (PRIMARY)
`send_message`/peer routing writes the raw `agent_key` as `to_agent`. When the caller passes a bare SLUG (no type suffix), it never matches the recipient's suffixed drain key.
Evidence (`.exo/inbox.db`): `to_agent = "patch-step-over"` from `root`, but the real agent drains as `patch-step-over-opencode`. `normalize_agent_id` cannot fix this — `patch-step-over` has no dot, so it passes through unchanged and stays orphaned.

Root path: `services/delivery.rs` -> `record_inbox_delivery(ctx, agent_key, ...)` (currently `fn`, bound only `HasInboxStore`) writes `agent_key` verbatim via `inbox_store().write_message(from, agent_key, ...)`.

## Bug B — literal "parent" recipient (INVESTIGATE then fix)
Evidence: `to_agent = "parent"` from `m1-breakpoints-step-opencode` (an OpenCode leaf). Not produced by the structural path (that emits a branch or `root`). Origin is caller-supplied: either an `override_recipient` Address, or the OpenCode/Codex notify_parent shim emitting the literal string "parent". Find the source and make it resolve to the real parent AgentName (or fail loudly — see Bug C). This is harness-agnostic work: check the OpenCode TS plugin and Codex hook wire path, not just Claude.

## Bug C — silent orphaning (POLICY)
Today an unresolvable recipient is silently recorded under a bad key and never delivered. Per CLAUDE.md ("prefer failure to an undocumented heuristic", "silent failures are unacceptable"), an unresolved recipient MUST log a loud WARN with the unresolved key and the resolver candidates tried. Decide with reviewer whether to also fail the delivery or record-and-warn; default recommendation: record-and-warn (don't lose the message) but emit a WARN-level log + OTel event.

# ANTI-PATTERNS (read FIRST)
- DO NOT reintroduce a hardcoded string mapping (no `if key == "parent" { "root" }`, no `main->root`). Resolve via `AgentResolver`, fail/​warn otherwise.
- DO NOT add a second normalization code path. There is exactly one inbox keying chokepoint: the write in `record_inbox_delivery`. Canonicalize there, once.
- DO NOT change `inbox_store::normalize_agent_id` — it stays a pure dot-strip. Slug->suffix resolution needs the resolver and does NOT belong in inbox_store (no resolver access there).
- DO NOT touch `canonical_parent_recipient` or the 3 notify sources — they are correct.
- DO NOT broaden bounds you don't use. `record_inbox_delivery` only needs `HasInboxStore + HasAgentResolver`.

# READ FIRST
- rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md (Delivery Pipeline, Has* capability traits, Routing Resolution)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/delivery.rs: `record_inbox_delivery` (~l.533), `deliver_to_agent` (~l.1068, bounds incl `HasAgentResolver`), `deliver_to_agent_for` (~l.427, same bounds), `route_message` (~l.281).
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resolver.rs: `get(&AgentName)` (l.126), `lookup_by_slug(&Slug)` (l.131), `all()` (l.215), `AgentIdentityRecord { agent_name, slug, ... }`.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs: `normalize_agent_id` (do not edit), `write_message`, `drain_unread`.
- docs/decisions/opencode-hooks.md, docs/decisions/codex-hook-wire-format.md (for Bug B shim investigation).

# STEPS
1. Add an async resolver helper in delivery.rs:
   `async fn canonical_recipient_key(resolver: &AgentResolver, agent_key: &str) -> String`
   - If `AgentName::try_from_str(agent_key)` is a known agent (`resolver.get(&name).is_some()`) -> return `agent_key` (already canonical, incl. dotted branches handled later by inbox strip).
   - Else if `Slug::try_from_str(agent_key)` resolves (`resolver.lookup_by_slug(&slug)`) -> return `record.agent_name.to_string()`.
   - Else: WARN log (Bug C) listing the key tried; return `agent_key` unchanged (record-and-warn).
2. Make `record_inbox_delivery` async, add `HasAgentResolver` bound, and canonicalize before writing:
   `let to = canonical_recipient_key(ctx.agent_resolver(), agent_key).await;`
   `ctx.inbox_store().write_message(from.as_str(), &to, message, Some(summary))`
   Update the 3 call sites (`deliver_to_agent` l.1083, `deliver_to_agent_for` TmuxOnly l.444 + MailboxOnly l.450) to `.await`. All callers already have `HasAgentResolver` in scope.
3. Bug B: grep the OpenCode/Codex notify_parent path for a literal "parent"/"main" recipient. Likely in the runtime shim that builds the notify_parent call for non-Claude agents. Fix it to pass the structural parent (reuse the same resolution) or drop the override so the structural fallback runs. If it is a WASM-side override, fix in haskell/wasm-guest or the role lib. Document what you found.
4. Bug C: ensure the unresolved-recipient WARN is emitted once at the chokepoint with `tracing::warn!` + an OTel-style event line (match existing `[event] message.delivery` style in delivery.rs).

# VERIFY
- `just build`
- `just test` (must be green; note: a separate pre-existing role-hook-tests MergeReady failure is tracked in its OWN issue — confirm THIS work doesn't add new failures)
- New unit tests in delivery.rs:
  - slug recipient (`patch-step-over`) with a registered `patch-step-over-opencode` agent -> inbox `to_agent == "patch-step-over-opencode"` and `drain_unread("patch-step-over-opencode")` returns it.
  - already-canonical suffixed name round-trips unchanged.
  - unresolved key -> recorded unchanged + WARN emitted (assert via log capture or returned value).
- Manual repro: in a live run, `send_message` to a leaf by slug, then check `.exo/inbox.db`: `SELECT to_agent FROM messages ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 3;` shows the suffixed AgentName; the leaf's `check_inbox` drains it.

# DONE CRITERIA
- No inbox row is ever written with a slug-only or literal placeholder (`parent`/`main`) recipient for a resolvable agent.
- Bug B origin documented and fixed (or, if truly external caller garbage, made to fail loudly).
- Tests above pass; `just build` + `just test` green (modulo the separately-tracked MergeReady issue).
- Update rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md "Routing Resolution" to note recipient canonicalization happens at inbox write via AgentResolver.

# FILES
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/delivery.rs (primary)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resolver.rs (read only)
- OpenCode/Codex notify shim (Bug B — locate via grep)
- rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md (doc update)

comments.content: Bug B investigation: searched OpenCode plugin, Codex config hook wire path, Haskell wasm guest/.exo role libs, proto, and Rust event handler for literal parent recipient construction. The delivery chokepoint fix will make any future unresolved parent placeholder loud via WARN + OTel event while preserving the message.
