issues.title: Inbox poke loop: identity mismatch spams agents + needs backoff cadence
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Symptom
Spawned dev-leaves (observed: opencode leaf `m1-process-regs-mem-opencode` in the live RustDebuggerRepo run) are spammed indefinitely with `You have N unread message(s). Call check_inbox.` The count climbs (2 -> 6) while every `check_inbox` the agent runs returns `{"count":0,"messages":[]}`. The agent eventually gives up and stops responding. PRs stall because the agent can't see its mail.

## Root cause: AgentName identity mismatch (write side vs drain side)
The inbox InboxStore keys `to_agent` inconsistently:

- WRITE side (event-handler delivery, notify_parent recipient resolution) stores `to_agent` as the FULL branch-qualified name, e.g. `main.m1-process-regs-mem-opencode`.
- DRAIN side (`check_inbox` -> `drain_unread`) and `agent_inbox_meta` use the BARE AgentName (last dot-segment), e.g. `m1-process-regs-mem-opencode`.

Per the architecture (CLAUDE.md Branch Naming), AgentName IS the last dot-segment — one namespace, zero translation. The write side is violating that.

Consequence chain (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs):
1. `drain_unread("m1-process-regs-mem-opencode")` matches 0 rows — the unread rows are keyed `main.m1-process-regs-mem-opencode`. `read_at` is never set.
2. `agents_needing_poke` (inbox_store.rs:147) finds those rows (`read_at IS NULL`) joined against `agent_inbox_meta` where the full-name agent has NO meta row -> `last_check_inbox_at IS NULL` -> always considered stale -> poke fires every cycle.
3. New mail keeps arriving addressed to the full name, so the count climbs.
4. The poke (worktree_event_watcher.rs:1145 `poke_unread_inbox_agents`, routed via `route_tmux_notification` to `Address::Agent(full-name)`) resolves to the leaf's pane and injects the message forever.

Evidence from live DB `/home/goya/storage/RustDebuggerRepo/.exo/inbox.db`:
- Unread `to_agent` values: `main.m1-process-regs-mem-opencode` (6), `main.m1-breakpoints-step-opencode` (5), `main.m0-xtask-fixtures-opencode` (3), `main.review-pr-4-codex` (2), etc. — all branch-qualified, mostly from `event-handler`.
- `agent_inbox_meta.agent_id` values: `m1-process-regs-mem-opencode`, `m0-xtask-fixtures-opencode`, ... — all BARE. None match the unread `to_agent` keys.

## Secondary bug (same investigation)
Some `to_agent` values are literal unresolved placeholders: `parent` (1), `main` (4), `patch-step-over` (1). `notify_parent` is recording the recipient as a raw string ("parent"/"main") instead of resolving to the parent's real AgentName. These will never be drained either.

## Fix direction (needs design sign-off before implementing)
1. Canonicalize AgentName to the bare last-dot-segment at EVERY inbox boundary: `write_message` to_agent, `drain_unread`, `agents_needing_poke`, `agent_inbox_meta`, and the poke routing address. Single normalization helper; one code path. Must be harness-agnostic (Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Gemini/Shoal all go through the same store).
2. Fix `notify_parent` recipient resolution so it never stores literal `parent`/`main`.
3. Backfill/migrate or accept that existing mismatched rows are orphaned (decide).

## Poke cadence redesign (requested alongside the fix)
Current: `DEFAULT_INBOX_POKE_INTERVAL = 300s` fixed (worktree_event_watcher.rs:26). User wants the poke to back off, NOT poll at a fixed rate:
- Base cadence ~30s.
- Exponential decay: if no NEW messages have arrived since the last poke for an agent, lengthen the wait each cycle (cap at some max, e.g. 600s). Reset to base when new mail arrives.
- Rationale: forcing cadence via agent prompt instructions ("poll every 30s") is unreliable — agents disobey. Cadence must be enforced server-side in the poke loop, which is harness-agnostic.

Note: even a perfect backoff only masks the identity-mismatch infinite loop. The mismatch is the primary fix; backoff is correct behavior on top of it.

## Files
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/inbox_store.rs (drain/poke/meta keying)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs (poke loop + interval/backoff, ll. 26, 1145-1187)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/delivery.rs (notify_parent recipient resolution)

## Verify
- Repro: spawn a non-Claude leaf on a branch-qualified name, send it event-handler mail, confirm `check_inbox` drains it and the poke stops after one drain.
- New test in inbox_store.rs asserting write/drain/poke agree on a branch-qualified AgentName.
- Backoff unit test: no-new-mail lengthens interval; new mail resets it.

comments.content: Implemented inbox identity canonicalization and backoff cadence. Durable inbox now normalizes branch-qualified recipients to bare agent IDs, maps root birth branch 'main' to agent 'root', migrates legacy inbox rows/meta on open, and persists per-agent poke backoff state. Added regressions for branch-qualified drain, root TL drain, migration backfill, backoff reset/doubling, and handler-level check_inbox on branch-qualified mail. Verification: cargo fmt --all; cargo test -p exomonad-core inbox_store -- --nocapture; cargo test -p exomonad-core handlers::inbox::tests -- --nocapture; cargo test -p exomonad-core worktree_event_watcher::tests::test_inbox_poke_message -- --nocapture. Full cargo test -p exomonad-core remains blocked in sandbox because wiremock tests cannot bind localhost (Operation not permitted). cargo clippy -p exomonad-core -- -D warnings also fails on pre-existing unrelated warnings in codex_config.rs, protocol/hook.rs, handlers/agent.rs, handlers/lifecycle.rs, services/agent_control/internal.rs, services/pr_registry.rs, services/review_policy.rs, and services/worktree_event_watcher.rs.

issues.title: Prefer fj CLI over curl in reviewer/dev/root Forgejo interaction prompts
Reviewer/spawned-agent envs lack FORGEJO_URL/FORGEJO_TOKEN/FORGEJO_REVIEWER_TOKEN when config changes after init
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Problem

Spawned agent processes (especially reviewer agents) can lack `FORGEJO_URL` /
`FORGEJO_TOKEN` / `FORGEJO_REVIEWER_TOKEN` in their environment even though
`config.toml` / `config.local.toml` have these values configured correctly.

## Root cause

There are two divergent sources of truth for Forgejo credentials:

1. **`rust/exomonad/src/serve.rs:1041-1090`** — the watcher's Forgejo client and
   the reviewer-token Forgejo client are built **directly from the loaded
   `Config` struct** (`config.forgejo_url` / `config.forgejo_token` /
   `config.forgejo_reviewer_token`, merged from `config.toml` +
   `config.local.toml`). This always reflects the current config file state.

2. **`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs:214-237`**
   (`common_spawn_env`) — the env vars shell-prefixed onto every spawned
   agent's command (including reviewers, via
   `spawn_reviewer_subtree_named` -> `spawn_subtree` ->
   `common_spawn_env(.., role=reviewer)`) are read from
   **`std::env::var("FORGEJO_URL")` / `std::env::var("FORGEJO_TOKEN")` /
   `std::env::var("FORGEJO_REVIEWER_TOKEN")` etc — the server PROCESS's own
   OS environment.**

The server process's OS env is populated **only once**, at `exomonad init`
time, by **`rust/exomonad/src/init.rs:1005-1016`**, which calls
`std::env::set_var(...)` (and `tmux set-environment`) for each Forgejo var
present in the config at that moment.

If `forgejo_token` / `forgejo_reviewer_token` / `forgejo_url` are added or
changed in `config.local.toml` (or `config.toml`) **after** the last
`exomonad init` (without `--recreate`/restart), the running server's OS env
never picks up the new value. From then on:

- The watcher / reviewer MCP tools keep working fine (they read `Config`
  directly).
- But `common_spawn_env` keeps returning a stale/missing `FORGEJO_URL` /
  `FORGEJO_TOKEN` / `FORGEJO_REVIEWER_TOKEN` for **every newly spawned agent**
  (reviewers and dev leaves alike), because it's still reading the server
  process's original `std::env::var` snapshot from init time.

This produces exactly the symptom observed in `backrooms-workspace`: spawned
reviewer agents report missing `FORGEJO_URL`/Forgejo token env vars and
cannot submit PR reviews via the Forgejo API, despite `config.toml` /
`config.local.toml` being correctly configured.

## Relationship to #502/#503

This is **independent** of #502/#503 (the `forgejo_review_parts` SHA-filter
state-corruption bug in `worktree_event_watcher.rs`). #502/#503 is a pure
watcher state-machine bug that affects whether/when a reviewer gets
(re)spawned at all. This issue (#504) is about the **environment a reviewer
agent process inherits once spawned** — a config-to-spawned-agent-env
propagation gap. Both bugs can independently cause "PR stuck with no
effective review," but via different mechanisms, and both need fixing.

## Fix direction

`common_spawn_env` (internal.rs:214-237) should source `FORGEJO_HOST` /
`FORGEJO_TOKEN` / `FORGEJO_REVIEWER_TOKEN` / `FORGEJO_URL` / `FORGEJO_OWNER` /
`FORGEJO_REPO` / `REPO` from the same loaded `Config` that `serve.rs` uses for
its Forgejo clients (config.toml + config.local.toml merged), not from
`std::env::var`. `std::env::var` can remain a fallback for vars that have no
config-file equivalent (e.g. `GH_HOST`, `GH_TOKEN` outside the
forgejo_token/forgejo_reviewer_token override), but anything with a
`config.toml` field must be sourced from the live `Config`, so config edits
take effect on the next spawn without requiring `exomonad init --recreate`.

## Verify

- Add a unit test for `common_spawn_env` (or whatever it's refactored into)
  that constructs a context with a `Config`/forgejo fields set via the config
  struct (not `std::env::set_var`), and asserts the resulting env map contains
  `FORGEJO_URL` / `FORGEJO_TOKEN` / `FORGEJO_REVIEWER_TOKEN` (with the
  reviewer-role override) sourced from that struct.
- Manual repro: change `forgejo_reviewer_token` in `config.local.toml` without
  restarting the server, spawn a reviewer, confirm its env now has the new
  token (previously would still have the old/missing value).

comments.content: Implemented config-sourced Forgejo spawn env propagation. AgentControlService now accepts ForgejoSpawnEnv from the loaded serve Config and common_spawn_env applies it after process-env fallback, so config values override stale/missing FORGEJO_* env vars; reviewer role still maps FORGEJO_REVIEWER_TOKEN onto FORGEJO_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN. Verification: cargo fmt --all; cargo test -p exomonad-core services::agent_control::internal::tests::test_common_spawn_env; cargo test -p exomonad-core services::agent_control; just build.

GOAL: drive a real PR through reviewer_max_rounds (=2, per
.exo/review-policy.toml) distinct ChangesRequested verdicts and assert the
watcher's Stuck/human-escalation path actually fires:

1. Dev leaf opens PR, reviewer #1 posts ChangesRequested (round 1).
2. Dev leaf pushes a fix addressing round 1.
3. Reviewer #2 (fresh reviewer per .exo/review-policy.toml identity
   discipline) posts ChangesRequested again (round 2) -- on the SAME PR,
   different reviewer identity, simulating the real PR #29 sequence

4. Assert:
   - watcher sets the PR's stuck flag (old_state.stuck / WriteRegistryStuck

   - a chainlink issue with label 'review-stuck' and priority 'high' is

     containing the PR number, branch, rounds, and head_sha in its
     diagnostic body
   - per root.md, the TL does NOT receive [STUCK: ...] / does not auto-merge
     and does NOT auto-close/respawn/replace the dev leaf -- the review-stuck
     chainlink issue is the human-facing surface

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION (raise with the human operator before writing the test's
'done' assertions, do not assume): the operator's request for this e2e test
also said the watcher 'should probably tell forgejo to abandon the PR, clean
up [worktrees/agents] and summarize the issue to the human operator.' This
is NOT current behavior -- file_review_loop_escalation only files a chainlink
issue today. It also appears to conflict with the existing root.md
instruction: 'Treat Chainlink review-stuck issues as human-clarification
inputs. Do not automatically close, respawn, or replace the dev leaf that
owns the PR worktree.'

Before adding assertions for PR-closure/worktree-cleanup, confirm with the
human operator whether:
  (a) Stuck handling should gain new behavior (e.g. close/mark-draft the
      Forgejo PR, post a closing comment summarizing the two rounds of
      feedback, and leave worktree cleanup to the human), or
  (b) the current 'file a review-stuck issue, leave the PR/worktree alone
      for human triage' behavior is correct and root.md/this issue's
      framing in the operator's message was describing the *desired human
      workflow* (operator manually abandons after reading the chainlink
      issue), not new automation.

If (a), this issue should be split: a small implementation task for the new
Forgejo-abandon + summary behavior (with its own unit tests in
worktree_event_watcher.rs), landed BEFORE the e2e test is finalized to match.

VERIFY: just check-e2e-<name> (bash -n syntax check) and, if a live run is
feasible in CI, just e2e-<name>.

Resolved: operator confirmed (b) — current behavior (file_review_loop_escalation files a 'review-stuck' chainlink issue, PR/worktree left untouched for human triage) is correct and matches root.md's existing 'do not auto-close/respawn/replace the dev leaf' instruction. The 'abandon the PR' phrasing in the original report described the human's manual follow-up after reading the chainlink issue, not new automation.

Scope for this e2e test is now fixed to the original goal list (steps 1-4): drive a PR through 2 distinct ChangesRequested rounds (post-#502 fix), assert WriteRegistryStuck fires with rounds>=2, assert a 'review-stuck'/high-priority chainlink issue is filed with PR number/branch/rounds/head_sha in its diagnostic, and assert the TL does NOT receive [STUCK:...] and does not auto-close/respawn/replace the dev leaf. No Forgejo PR-closure or worktree-cleanup assertions needed.

issues.title: Fix: watcher loses ChangesRequested review rounds when dev pushes multiple times between polls, never reaches reviewer_max_rounds
issues.description:
Root cause analysis for: TL kept spawning fresh reviewers for PR #29 round
after round instead of the watcher firing Stuck/human-escalation, even though
two separate reviewers had already posted ChangesRequested.

ROOT CAUSE (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs):

forgejo_review_parts() (around line 2113-2126) drops any Forgejo review whose
commit_id != current head_sha:

    if let Some(review_commit) = review.commit_id.as_deref()
        .filter(|commit| !head_sha.is_empty() && *commit != head_sha)
    {
        // ... logged and dropped
        continue;
    }

This is correct for deciding the *current* approve/changes-requested verdict,
but compute_pr_actions_with_context() also derives the round counter from this
same SHA-filtered list:

    let observed_request_change_rounds = reviews.iter()
        .filter(|r| r.state == ForgejoReviewVerdict::ChangesRequested)
        .count() as u32;
    let next_review_round = observed_request_change_rounds.max(old_state.rounds + 1);

and old_state.rounds is only bumped inside the 'changes_requested' block
(line ~2451), which only runs if the *current-SHA* reviews contain a
ChangesRequested entry.

FAILURE SEQUENCE (matches the PR #29 transcript):
1. Round 1: reviewer reviews sha A -> ChangesRequested. rounds=1.
2. Dev pushes sha B (addresses round 1). pr_sha change -> fixes_pushed,
   last_review_state reset to None. rounds stays 1.
3. New reviewer reviews sha B -> ChangesRequested (round 2).
4. Dev leaf, without the watcher polling in between, ALSO pushes sha C
   before the next poll.
5. Watcher polls: head_sha=C. forgejo_review_parts drops BOTH the sha-A
   review AND the sha-B ChangesRequested review (neither commit_id == C).
   reviews=[] for this poll.
6. pr_sha (C) != old_state.last_sha (A, never updated to B because the
   watcher never polled at B) -> was_changes_requested=true (last state was
   CR from round 1) -> fires fixes_pushed, rounds stays 1.
7. changes_requested block does not run (reviews=[] for sha C) -> rounds
   never reaches reviewer_max_rounds=2 -> WriteRegistryStuck /
   FileHumanEscalation never fire.

Round 2's ChangesRequested verdict (against sha B) is silently and
permanently lost. The dev/reviewer loop continues indefinitely instead of
escalating to a human after reviewer_max_rounds genuinely-distinct
ChangesRequested rounds.

FIX DIRECTION:
old_state.rounds must count *every* distinct ChangesRequested verdict the PR
has ever received, not just ones still visible against the current head_sha.
Likely fix: increment old_state.rounds inside the 'was_changes_requested'
branch (pr_sha change while last_review_state == ChangesRequested) -- i.e. a
push that addresses a ChangesRequested review IS the completion of that
round, regardless of whether a later poll can still see the stale review
object. The 'changes_requested' block's own increment (for the
still-on-current-sha case) and this push-triggered increment must not
double-count the same round -- needs careful state-machine design across
both branches plus the existing test_request_changes_then_approve_does_not_trip_stuck
and test_request_changes_history_preserves_round_when_poll_sees_only_approval
tests (both of which currently call compute_pr_actions directly with
synthetic, non-SHA-filtered review lists and do NOT exercise this gap).

REQUIRED:
1. Fix the round-counting state machine in compute_pr_actions_with_context
   (and/or forgejo_review_parts) so that N distinct ChangesRequested verdicts
   across any sequence of pushes/polls reliably drives old_state.rounds to N.
2. Add a unit test reproducing the exact 'two pushes between polls, skipping
   an intermediate SHA that had a ChangesRequested review' sequence above,
   asserting WriteRegistryStuck + FileHumanEscalation fire once
   reviewer_max_rounds is reached.
3. Run existing round/stuck tests (test_changes_requested_at_max_rounds_fires_stuck,
   test_request_changes_then_approve_does_not_trip_stuck,
   test_request_changes_history_preserves_round_when_poll_sees_only_approval,
   test_new_sha_after_approval_reopens_review_round,
   test_first_approval_increments_review_rounds,
   test_approval_after_new_sha_increments_review_rounds_once) and confirm they
   still pass.

Verify: just build && cargo test -p exomonad-core worktree_event_watcher (run
via just/nix per project convention, not raw cargo).

comments.content: Implemented historical ChangesRequested round counting in worktree_event_watcher. Verification: cargo test -p exomonad-core services::worktree_event_watcher passed (81 tests).

LIVE REPRODUCTION (backrooms-workspace, PR #29, 2026-06-10 21:30-22:22Z):

Confirms this bug also breaks reviewer re-spawn, not just the Stuck/escalation
path that #503's e2e test targets.

Timeline from .exo/logs/watcher.log:
- 21:30:43 "terminal review observed for PR #29; disposing reviewer slugs: review-pr-29-codex"
- 21:36:44 same dispose message again
- 21:44-21:53 review=ChangesRequested (round against an earlier head SHA)
- 21:54-22:01 review=PendingReview (head changed to 8f3e0087, dev pushed fix;
  prior CR review dropped by SHA filter -> local_reviews empty -> PendingReview)
- 22:02:45 review=ChangesRequested again (new review against 8f3e0087);
  "terminal review observed for PR #29; disposing reviewer slugs: review-pr-29-codex"
- 22:03-22:06 review=ChangesRequested (head still 8f3e0087)
- 22:07:45 head changes to 1553374 (dev pushes second fix). All 3 historical
  reviews (against the two earlier SHAs and 8f3e0087) get dropped by the
  commit_id==head_sha filter -> local_reviews=[] -> review_state=PendingReview,
  forgejo_review_present=false
- 22:07:46 onward (through at least 22:22): review=PendingReview, steady state.

Result: NO "Spawning reviewer agent for new PR head SHA" log line ever appears
for PR #29 after the initial spawn -- despite 3 separate dispose events and a
head SHA change at 22:07:45 that should satisfy
should_spawn_reviewer_for_new_head() (reviewer_spawned reset to false on
head_sha_changed, rounds presumably < reviewer_max_rounds=2).

Persisted .exo/watcher-state.json for PR 29 at 22:21 (14 min after the push):
  {"rounds": 0, "stuck": false, "needs_human_review": false,
   "last_head_sha": "15533745afff29797d06037cdd08e9a5117f0bd2"}

rounds=0 despite at least one (likely two) ChangesRequested verdicts having
been observed against earlier SHAs -- consistent with the SHA-filter dropping
those reviews before compute_pr_actions_with_context ever sees them with a
matching SHA, so `rounds` and `last_review_state` never advance the way the
round-counting logic (next_review_round, lines ~2429) assumes.

Net effect on this live PR: the dev leaf pushed a second fix, notify_parent
succeeded (informational), but no reviewer was respawned and no Stuck/
escalation fired either -- the PR is now silently stuck in PendingReview with
no reviewer assigned, and the TL has no signal to act on.

Recommend the #502 fix (and #503's test) explicitly cover the reviewer-respawn
gating (should_spawn_reviewer_for_new_head / old_state.rounds /
old_state.reviewer_spawned) in addition to the Stuck/escalation path -- both
derive from the same rounds/last_review_state/last_sha triple that the SHA
filter corrupts.

Added regression coverage for the live reproduction's reviewer-respawn failure: stale historical ChangesRequested rounds on a new head now re-spawn the reviewer and persist recovered rounds. Verification: cargo test -p exomonad-core services::worktree_event_watcher passed (82 tests).

issues.title: Add e2e test for root TL idle/shutdown convergence flow
issues.description:
Follow-up to #494-#499 (Root TL idle/shutdown convergence) and #500 (handler
unit tests). Plan verification item 6 from TL_IDLE_SHUTDOWN_PLAN.md is still
unaddressed: "drive a root TL through a full chainlink backlog to empty,
confirm it eventually calls has_pending_work then shutdown_server rather than
looping indefinitely."

No e2e test currently exercises this. tests/e2e/lifecycle/ is unrelated
(pre-existing, covers agent lifecycle invariants from #302-#305 / dirty
worktree stop-hook checks).

New test: tests/e2e/idle-shutdown/ following the established pattern (see
tests/e2e/messaging/ as reference):

- run.sh: temp repo + bare remote, exomonad new, config.toml with yolo=true,
  a small Chainlink backlog (1-2 trivial issues that a worker/leaf can close
  quickly), GITHUB_TOKEN dummy, exomonad init as the last line.
- e2e-test.md: root TL rules — process the backlog to completion via the
  normal scaffold-fork-converge flow, then rely on the existing idle/shutdown
  convergence prompt section (see "You are the root TL.md" /
  .exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md) to call has_pending_work and
  shutdown_server once check_inbox returns empty 20x with no pending work.
- testrunner.md: a Claude (haiku) companion that observes (read-only bash):
    1. Chainlink backlog reaches 0 open issues.
    2. has_pending_work / shutdown_server tool calls appear in server logs
       (or via OTel spans if otlp_endpoint is configured).
    3. The exomonad server process actually exits (no longer listening on
       .exo/server.sock) within a bounded timeout.
  Reports pass/fail via notify_parent.
- Add `just e2e-idle-shutdown` recipe to justfile.

Note: the 20-empty-check threshold makes this slow in real time (root TL must
observe 20 empty check_inbox calls). Consider whether the test should
temporarily lower the threshold via a prompt override in e2e-test.md, or
accept a long-running test — flag this tradeoff for review rather than
guessing.

Verify: just e2e-idle-shutdown completes and testrunner reports all 3
assertions pass.

comments.content: Implemented tests/e2e/idle-shutdown with run.sh, e2e-test.md, testrunner.md, validate.sh, plus just recipes e2e-idle-shutdown and check-e2e-idle-shutdown. The harness uses an E2E-only 3-empty-check_inbox threshold override to keep runtime bounded while preserving the convergence path. Verification run here: just check-e2e-idle-shutdown passed and git diff --check passed. I did not run just e2e-idle-shutdown in this root session because the active server-management instruction forbids running exomonad init; the new recipe is the full launch verification path.

Full verification now run after user confirmed exomonad init is allowed outside an active ExoMonad session. issues.title: Fix watcher notification delivery for non-WASM agent runtimes
issues.description: merge_ready/fixes_pushed/etc. notifications never reach the TL when the PR's owning agent has no WASM plugin and isn't covered by the narrow Codex/OpenCode dev-only fallback. Root cause identified; fix direction: generalize the existing native EventActionResponse fallback path to compute-and-deliver via notify_parent_delivery directly, regardless of agent_type or role — bypassing WASM dispatch entirely as a Rust-side capability rather than an agent-shaped one.

comments.content:
## Root Cause (confirmed by code reading, not speculation)

`call_handle_event_for_role` in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs`
(~line 1557) is the single dispatch point for all `pr_review`/`ci_status`/`sibling_merged`/
`issue_closed` events. Its control flow:

```rust
let plugin = match plugins_guard.get(&agent_name) {
    Some(p) => p.clone(),
    None => {
        if (agent_type == AgentType::Codex || agent_type == AgentType::OpenCode)
            && role == "dev"
        {
            if let Some(action) = codex_dev_fallback_event_action(event_type, &payload) {
                return Ok(Some(action));   // <-- only escape hatch
            }
        }
        log_missing_event_plugin(branch, &agent_name, agent_type, role, event_type);
        return Ok(None);                  // <-- everything else: silently dropped
    }
};
```

`event_target_has_wasm_runtime` (line ~226) gates which agent types even *have* a WASM
plugin to look up:

```rust
fn event_target_has_wasm_runtime(agent_type: AgentType) -> bool {
    matches!(agent_type, AgentType::Claude | AgentType::Gemini)
}
```

So **Codex, OpenCode, Shoal, and Process agents structurally never have a plugin**. The
only fallback that exists (`codex_dev_fallback_event_action`, lines ~518-650) is gated on
BOTH:
1. `agent_type == Codex || agent_type == OpenCode`, AND
2. `role == "dev"`

This fallback is otherwise complete — it already contains a fully generalized,
agent-agnostic mechanism: an `EventActionResponse` enum (`InjectMessage` /
`NotifyParent` / `NoAction`) that `handle_event_action` (line ~1708) turns into real
delivery by calling `crate::services::delivery::deliver_to_agent` or
`crate::services::delivery::notify_parent_delivery` **directly, with no WASM
involvement**. The `merge_ready` case is already handled correctly inside
`codex_dev_fallback_pr_review_action` (line ~569):

```rust
"merge_ready" => {
    let pr_number = value_u64(payload, "pr_number")?;
    Some(EventActionResponse::NotifyParent {
        message: merge_ready_message(pr_number, value_str(payload, "ci_status")?, value_str(payload, "branch")?),
        pr_number: pr_number as i64,
    })
}
```

**The bug is the gate, not the mechanism.** Any of the following silently drops the
notification today, with only a `tracing::debug!` (not even `error!`) on the floor:

- A Shoal or Process dev leaf reaches `merge_ready` / `fixes_pushed` / `review_received`
  / `stuck` / etc. — falls through `log_missing_event_plugin` at `debug` level (because
  `event_target_has_wasm_runtime` returns false for Shoal/Process too) and the action is
  `Ok(None)`.
- A Codex or OpenCode **sub-TL** (`role == "tl"`, not `"dev"`) hits any pr_review event —
  same silent drop, because the fallback's `role == "dev"` guard excludes it.
- The reviewer fan-out path (line ~1354, same `call_handle_event_for_role` call against
  `reviewer_branch`/`reviewer_agent_type`/`reviewer_role`) has the identical gap for
  non-WASM reviewer agents.

This is exactly the symptom Roger observed live: `merge_ready: true` independently
confirmed via Forgejo (approved review + green CI), but `[MERGE READY]` never arrived in
the TL's inbox — because the dev leaf (or the path resolving its parent) was an
agent_type/role combination that the narrow Codex+dev gate doesn't cover.

## User's Proposed Fix Direction (verbatim framing — this is the spec north star)

> "this should be a matter of the watcher sending a MCP message but, not as an agent,
> just using it as a thread that wants to use a command in the API the exomonad MCP
> server offers"

In other words: **notification delivery should not be conditioned on the target having a
WASM runtime at all.** The watcher is a Rust-side background task with direct access to
`crate::services::delivery::notify_parent_delivery` / `deliver_to_agent` — the exact
functions the WASM-driven path eventually calls anyway via `handle_event_action`. There
is no structural reason this capability should be agent-shaped (gated behind
`PluginManager::call("handle_event", ...)`)  — it is a Rust API the watcher can call
directly, the same way `merge_pr` and `notify_parent` effects ultimately resolve to Rust
function calls.

## Fix Plan

1. **Promote the fallback computation to the universal path, not an escape hatch.**
   Rename/generalize `codex_dev_fallback_event_action` (and its
   `codex_dev_fallback_pr_review_action` / `codex_dev_fallback_ci_status_action` helpers)
   into a `native_event_action(event_type, payload, role) -> Option<EventActionResponse>`
   that has zero dependency on `agent_type`. It already produces the correct
   `EventActionResponse` for every `pr_review`/`ci_status`/`sibling_merged`/`issue_closed`
   kind — strip the Codex/OpenCode-only framing from its name and doc comments.

2. **Restructure `call_handle_event_for_role` so the native computation is the
   fallback for ALL agent types when no plugin exists — not a Codex/OpenCode/dev-only
   carve-out:**

   ```rust
   let plugin = match plugins_guard.get(&agent_name) {
       Some(p) => p.clone(),
       None => {
           if let Some(action) = native_event_action(event_type, &payload, role) {
               tracing::info!(
                   branch, lookup_key = %agent_name, ?agent_type, role, event_type,
                   "No WASM plugin for event target; using native Rust-side delivery"
               );
               return Ok(Some(action));
           }
           log_missing_event_plugin(branch, &agent_name, agent_type, role, event_type);
           return Ok(None);
       }
   };
   ```

   This covers Shoal, Process, Codex, OpenCode — and any future non-WASM runtime — for
   BOTH `role == "dev"` and `role == "tl"` (sub-TL) targets, and for the reviewer
   fan-out call site at line ~1354 (same function, same fix, free).

3. **Decide WASM-vs-native precedence explicitly for Claude/Gemini.** Currently
   Claude/Gemini always go through the WASM `handle_event` path (because they always
   have a plugin). Leave that untouched — this fix only changes behavior for agent types
   that have NO plugin today, so there is no risk of double-delivery or behavior change
   for Claude/Gemini.

4. **Make the silent-drop case loud.** If `native_event_action` ALSO returns `None`
   (i.e., a genuinely unhandled `event_type`/`kind` combination for a non-WASM agent),
   upgrade `log_missing_event_plugin`'s non-WASM branch from `debug!` to `warn!` — a
   dropped notification is never a `debug`-level event; it is a correctness gap that
   should be visible in default log output.

5. **Audit `codex_dev_fallback_*` for `role == "tl"` gaps.** Walk every `event_type`/
   `kind` combination currently routed to a sub-TL via WASM `handle_event` in
   `.exo/lib/PRReviewHandler.hs` (`tlPrReviewHandler`) and confirm `native_event_action`
   produces an equivalent `EventActionResponse` for each — `merge_ready`, `fixes_pushed`,
   `stuck`, `review_timeout`, `pr_ready`, `sibling_merged`. Any kind missing from the
   native function for `role == "tl"` is a second-order silent-drop bug waiting to
   reproduce this exact issue for a different agent shape.

## Anti-Patterns (DO NOT)

- DO NOT add a second, parallel "non-WASM notification" code path alongside the
  existing `EventActionResponse` → `handle_event_action` → `notify_parent_delivery`
  chain. The fallback functions ALREADY produce `EventActionResponse`; reuse that type
  and that delivery function. Two paths that do "the same thing" is exactly the
  single-code-path violation this codebase forbids (see root `CLAUDE.md` § Single Code
  Path).
- DO NOT gate the generalized native path on `agent_type` at all. The whole point of
  this fix is that delivery is a Rust-side capability, not an agent-runtime-shaped one.
  Any `match agent_type` inside the new `native_event_action` is a regression to the
  same bug shape with a different enum arm.
- DO NOT special-case `role` inside `native_event_action` beyond what the payload
  already encodes (e.g., `merge_ready` always notifies the parent regardless of whether
  the target is a dev leaf or a sub-TL — the message format and delivery target derive
  from the event payload + branch hierarchy, not from the role string).
- DO NOT silently widen `event_target_has_wasm_runtime` to claim Codex/OpenCode/Shoal
  "have" a WASM runtime — they don't, and pretending otherwise just moves the bug. The
  fix is to stop *requiring* a WASM runtime for delivery, not to fake one.
- DO NOT touch the Claude/Gemini WASM dispatch path. It works; this issue is scoped to
  the no-plugin fallback branch only.

## Read First

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs`:
  - `event_target_has_wasm_runtime` (~line 226)
  - `log_missing_event_plugin` (~line 228)
  - `EventActionResponse` enum + `codex_dev_fallback_*` functions (~lines 458-650)
  - `call_handle_event_for_role` (~line 1557) — the function to restructure
  - `handle_event_action` (~line 1708) — confirms `notify_parent_delivery` /
    `deliver_to_agent` are already reachable natively; reuse, do not duplicate
  - Reviewer fan-out call site (~line 1354) — second beneficiary of the same fix
- `rust/exomonad-core/CLAUDE.md` § Delivery Pipeline — `notify_parent_delivery` /
  `deliver_to_agent` contracts and the "any code path that notifies a parent MUST use
  `notify_parent_delivery`" rule
- `.exo/lib/PRReviewHandler.hs` — `tlPrReviewHandler`/`prReviewHandler`, the Haskell-side
  source of truth for what `EventAction` each `pr_review` kind should produce; the
  generalized native function must stay in parity with this for every kind it claims to
  handle

## Verify

```bash
cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib worktree_event_watcher
```

Existing tests at lines ~3151, ~3320-3500, ~3560-3668, ~3825-3872 already assert
`PendingAction`/`EventActionResponse` shapes for `merge_ready`/`approved`/CI-status
combinations — extend them with cases where `agent_type` is `Shoal`/`Process` and
`role` is `"tl"`, asserting `Ok(Some(EventActionResponse::NotifyParent { .. }))` is
returned (not `Ok(None)`).

## Done Criteria

- `call_handle_event_for_role` returns a populated `EventActionResponse` (not `Ok(None)`)
  for every `(agent_type, role, event_type, kind)` combination that the Haskell
  `PRReviewHandler.hs` would have produced a `NotifyParentAction`/`InjectMessage` for,
  regardless of whether the target has a WASM plugin.
- `[MERGE READY]`, `[FIXES PUSHED]`, `[PR READY]`, `[REVIEW TIMEOUT]`, `[STUCK]` all
  reach the parent TL's inbox for Codex/OpenCode/Shoal/Process dev leaves AND sub-TLs,
  verified by new unit tests asserting `EventActionResponse::NotifyParent` is produced
  (not silently dropped).
- The non-WASM "no plugin, no native handler" case logs at `warn!`, not `debug!`.
- No new code path duplicates `notify_parent_delivery`/`deliver_to_agent` — the fix
  reuses the existing `EventActionResponse` → `handle_event_action` chain end to end.
- `cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib worktree_event_watcher` passes.

## Relationship to #491

Distinct root cause from #491 (the `head_sha_changed` self-comparison bug that prevents
reviewer respawn). #491 is about *triggering* the right watcher state transition; this
issue is about *delivering* the resulting notification once the watcher has already
correctly determined `merge_ready: true`. Both can land independently; fixing this one
does not require #491 to land first, and vice versa.

Implemented universal native EventActionResponse fallback for no-plugin event targets. Removed Codex/OpenCode dev-only and process-role gates, preserved existing EventActionResponse -> handle_event_action delivery path, added TL/native parity for pr_review and ci_status signals, upgraded non-WASM unmatched-handler logging to warn, and added no-plugin Shoal/Process/sub-TL regression tests. Verified: cargo fmt; cargo test -p exomonad-core --lib worktree_event_watcher; just build; git diff --check.

issues.title: Fix reviewer respawn after PR head SHA changes
issues.description:
Symptom: After a dev-leaf addresses reviewer feedback and pushes fixes (new head SHA, e.g. PR #21 commit 2c1e0aa), no second-round reviewer is automatically spawned. The watcher continues to show the PR's review state as 'request_changes' (stale verdict against the OLD pre-fix commit) even though CI is green on the new commit. TL never receives [FIXES PUSHED]-triggered re-review or [MERGE READY]; the loop silently stalls until a human force-respawns a reviewer.

ROOT CAUSE (structural, not a one-off flake): in rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs

1. build_registry() (~line 880-919) sets PrEntry.last_head_sha = pr.head_sha.clone() — i.e. the LIVE current head SHA fetched from Forgejo on THIS cycle. It carries over persisted.rounds/stuck/needs_human_review from the watcher's saved state, but NEVER reads back persisted.last_head_sha. The persisted value is effectively write-only.

2. collect_observations() (~line 1037-1043) sets Observation.head_sha = pr.last_head_sha (i.e. the same live SHA just stored in step 1).

3. process_observations() (~line 1092) computes:
     let head_sha_changed = pr.last_head_sha.as_deref() != Some(obs.head_sha.as_str());
   But pr.last_head_sha and obs.head_sha are THE SAME VALUE derived in the SAME rebuild cycle (both ultimately = pr.head_sha from Forgejo's live PR listing). This comparison is structurally always false — it compares a freshly-fetched value to itself, never to a previous observation.

Consequence: head_sha_changed is permanently false, so the entire branch at line 1104-1136 (reviewer_spawned/reviewer_disposed reset + should_spawn_reviewer_for_new_head + spawner.spawn_reviewer_for_pr) NEVER executes. A fresh reviewer is only ever spawned on first sighting of a brand-new PR (line ~1152-1199); subsequent rounds after fixes-pushed get no automatic re-review.

Why [FIXES PUSHED] still fires correctly: that's a SEPARATE detection path inside compute_pr_actions_with_context — 'if pr_sha != old_state.last_sha' (line ~2154), which compares against WatchState.last_sha, the watcher's own in-memory per-cycle bookkeeping (self.state.prs), NOT the registry's last_head_sha. That path works fine, which is why the leaf got [FIXES PUSHED] notifications and the TL saw 'fixes pushed' — but it does not drive reviewer respawn; only the (broken) head_sha_changed path does.

Net effect: the leaf+reviewer convergence loop silently stalls after round 1 on every PR, every time. The only reason this hasn't been caught before is that humans have been manually force-respawning reviewers (as happened on PR #21) or merging directly off a stale-but-actually-passing review state.

comments.content:
## Scaffolding / Fix Plan

### Where to look
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs
  - struct PrEntry (likely in rust/exomonad-core/src/services/pr_registry.rs) — currently has a single last_head_sha field doing double duty (both 'live current SHA' and 'last observed SHA for change detection')
  - build_registry() ~880-919 — overwrites last_head_sha with the live pr.head_sha every cycle, discarding persisted.last_head_sha
  - collect_observations() ~1037-1043 — derives Observation.head_sha FROM pr.last_head_sha (the just-overwritten live value)
  - process_observations() ~1092 — head_sha_changed comparison that is structurally always false
  - persist_last_head_shas() ~1451 — writes the new SHA to watcher_state.prs[n].last_head_sha (currently write-only; never read back)

### Fix direction
Split the single overloaded last_head_sha into two distinct concepts:
1. A 'live/current head SHA' — fetched fresh from Forgejo each cycle (what collect_observations should use to fetch reviews/CI/comments for the right commit).
2. A 'last observed head SHA' — the watcher's own persisted bookkeeping from the PREVIOUS cycle, read from persisted.last_head_sha in build_registry() and compared against the live SHA to compute head_sha_changed.

Concretely:
- In build_registry(): keep storing the live pr.head_sha (e.g. rename to current_head_sha or similar so the field's role is unambiguous), AND separately retain persisted.last_head_sha (e.g. as last_observed_head_sha) carried over from watcher_state — the same way persisted.rounds/stuck/needs_human_review are already carried over.
- In collect_observations(): fetch reviews/CI against the LIVE sha (current_head_sha), not the persisted one.
- In process_observations(): compute head_sha_changed = persisted_last_observed_sha != live_current_sha. After processing, persist_last_head_shas() should write the live sha into last_observed_head_sha for the next cycle (this part of the plumbing already exists and is correct — it just needs to feed into a comparison that is read back).

### Anti-patterns
- Do NOT just rename the field without separating the two concepts — a rename alone won't fix the self-comparison.
- Do NOT remove the WatchState.last_sha-based fixes_pushed detection — it works correctly and is independent; leave it as-is. The fix is scoped to the registry-level head_sha_changed -> reviewer-respawn path only.
- Do NOT change reviewer_spawned/reviewer_disposed reset semantics (lines ~1108-1110) or should_spawn_reviewer_for_new_head's gating logic (!reviewer_spawned && rounds < max_rounds) — those are correct; they just never get a chance to run because head_sha_changed is always false.

### Verify
- Add/extend a unit test in worktree_event_watcher.rs that: seeds watcher_state with a persisted last_head_sha = 'old_sha', rebuilds the registry against a live PR reporting head_sha = 'new_sha', and asserts head_sha_changed evaluates true and a reviewer-spawn is triggered (mock ReviewerSpawner call count == 1, with should_spawn_reviewer_for_new_head returning true given rounds < max_rounds).
- Add a regression test asserting that on a cycle where the live SHA has NOT changed since the last persisted observation, head_sha_changed is false and no duplicate reviewer is spawned.
- Manually verify against a live PR: push a fix commit after a 'changes requested' review, confirm the watcher logs 'Spawning reviewer agent for new PR head SHA' and a fresh reviewer agent appears without human intervention.

### Done criteria
A dev-leaf pushing fixes after 'changes requested' automatically triggers a fresh reviewer respawn (when rounds < reviewer_max_rounds), with no human force-respawn required, end to end through to [MERGE READY] or [STUCK].

Implemented persisted last-head-SHA comparison for reviewer respawn. issues.title: Fix generated Claude settings self-disabling exomonad MCP
issues.description:
Root TL session in /home/goya/backrooms-workspace (tmux 'backrooms-workspace', window 1) has no exomonad MCP tools — check_inbox, spawn_leaf, poll_workers etc. all missing. 'claude mcp get exomonad' shows Status: Rejected (see disabledMcpjsonServers in settings).

Root cause: /home/goya/backrooms-workspace/.claude/settings.local.json is marked _exomonad_generated: true (written by exomonad init / fork_wave) and contains:
  "disabledMcpjsonServers": ["exomonad"]
This is self-defeating — the generated settings file disables the very MCP server the agent needs. The exomonad server process is healthy (exomonad serve running, .exo/server.sock present, hooks flowing fine for agent=root in server logs), so this is a Claude Code MCP-registration/trust problem, not a server-side bug.

Likely trigger: .mcp.json in that worktree has an UNCOMMITTED diff changing role/name/command (reviewer/backrooms-workspace/'exomonad' -> root/root/'/home/goya/.cargo/bin/exomonad'). When Claude Code detects a changed server definition (different command/args than what it last approved), it marks the server Rejected and persists that into settings.local.json. If exomonad's settings-generation path then preserves/re-emits that disabled entry on subsequent writes (instead of clearing it once exomonad itself wrote a matching .mcp.json), every later session in that worktree starts with its own MCP server pre-disabled — silent, persistent breakage.

comments.content:
## Scaffolding / Investigation Plan

### Reproduce
1. Inspect /home/goya/backrooms-workspace/.claude/settings.local.json — confirm disabledMcpjsonServers: ["exomonad"] is present alongside _exomonad_generated: true.
2. Run 'claude mcp get exomonad' from /home/goya/backrooms-workspace — confirm Status: Rejected (see disabledMcpjsonServers in settings).
3. Diff .mcp.json (uncommitted change present: role reviewer->root, name backrooms-workspace->root, command exomonad -> absolute cargo path) — this mismatch vs. what Claude Code last trusted is the likely trigger for the Rejected state.

### Where to look in the codebase
- Whatever Rust path writes .claude/settings.local.json for spawned/init'd agents — search for _exomonad_generated and settings.local.json (likely rust/exomonad-core/src/.../init or fork_wave settings-writer).
- Confirm whether exomonad reads-and-merges the EXISTING settings.local.json (preserving Claude Code's own disabledMcpjsonServers/enabledMcpjsonServers keys) vs overwriting wholesale:
  - If it merges/preserves: a stale Rejected entry from a prior mismatched .mcp.json persists forever.
  - If it overwrites: something is actively WRITING disabledMcpjsonServers: ["exomonad"] — that would be even more clearly a bug (no generator should ever disable its own server).

### Fix directions (pick after root-causing)
A) When exomonad (re)writes .mcp.json for a worktree/session, also clear/reconcile any disabledMcpjsonServers/enabledMcpjsonServers entry for 'exomonad' in the corresponding settings.local.json, OR
B) Stop persisting .mcp.json mismatches across re-inits — ensure generated .mcp.json is stable (same command/args) across init/fork_wave runs so Claude Code never re-prompts/rejects, OR
C) If Claude Code itself writes the disabled entry on trust-change, document that operators must reset project MCP choices after any exomonad-driven .mcp.json change, and have exomonad init do this automatically before launching the TL session.

### Verify
- After fix: fresh 'exomonad init --recreate' in a test project; confirm 'claude mcp list' shows exomonad Connected and check_inbox/spawn_leaf/etc. available to root TL on first session start, no manual claude mcp intervention.
- Add an E2E assertion that fails if disabledMcpjsonServers ever contains "exomonad" in a freshly generated settings.local.json.

### Done criteria
Root TL sessions reliably get exomonad MCP tools on first connect after exomonad init/--recreate, across re-inits where .mcp.json content changes (role/name/command). Regression covered by an E2E check.

Implemented settings reconciliation so generated Claude settings remove exomonad from disabledMcpjsonServers while preserving other disabled MCP servers. Added hooks unit coverage and a claude-only E2E harness assertion. Verified: cargo fmt; cargo test -p exomonad-core hooks; bash -n tests/e2e/claude-only/run.sh; git diff --check; just build.

Fixed by commits b5e4a7bd ("Fix generated Claude settings self-disabling exomonad MCP") and 38e04169 (changelog entry), landed on harness-agnostic-teams-inbox-messaging.

Fix: rust/exomonad-core/src/hooks.rs adds remove_self_from_disabled_mcp_servers(), which strips only the 'exomonad' entry out of disabledMcpjsonServers (preserving any other disabled servers), called from both settings-write paths (write_persistent for exomonad init, generate for mid-session/fork_wave regeneration). Two new unit tests cover the merge/preserve behavior.

E2E regression coverage: tests/e2e/claude-only/run.sh now asserts (assert_exomonad_mcp_not_disabled) that a freshly generated settings.local.json has _exomonad_generated=true and does NOT list 'exomonad' in disabledMcpjsonServers, checked immediately after tmux session creation.

Verified live: the backrooms-workspace root TL session is no longer blocked on exomonad MCP access — check_inbox/spawn_leaf/poll_workers etc. are available as expected.

issues.title: fix: chainlink_relate passes invalid relation argument to CLI
issues.description:
## Root Cause

buildRelateArgs in haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/Chainlink/Pure.hs builds:

  ["relate", show (crIssue1 args), show (crIssue2 args), T.unpack (crRelation args)]

The CLI signature is: chainlink relate [OPTIONS] <ID> <RELATED>

There is no positional relation argument. The third argument is rejected with exit 2:

Drop the relation argument from buildRelateArgs. The ChainlinkRelateArgs struct has a crRelation field that doesn't map to anything in the CLI. Either:

(a) Remove the relation field from ChainlinkRelateArgs and buildRelateArgs entirely, since the CLI has no concept of relation types.
(b) Check if relation can be expressed as a --flag (run chainlink relate --help to verify).

If the CLI adds relation types in a future version, the field can be re-added then.

- chainlink_relate tool call with any relation value succeeds
- buildRelateArgs only passes ["relate", id1, id2]

issues.title: file_pr push_bookmark doesn't inject Forgejo token for HTTP remote auth
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

push_bookmark in services/git_worktree.rs:257 runs 'git push origin' via headless_git_command() which sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_ASKPASS='', GCM_INTERACTIVE=never. This correctly prevents interactive prompts in headless agents. But it provides no credentials either — the ForgejoClient token used for REST API calls is never passed to the git subprocess. SSH remotes work via ssh-agent/key. HTTP Forgejo remotes (http://localhost:3000/owner/repo) fail with 'terminal prompts disabled' because git needs a username/password and cannot ask. Fix: pass the Forgejo token to the git push via -c http.extraheader='Authorization: token <FORGEJO_TOKEN>' (git 2.x+), or by rewriting the push URL to http://<token>@host/owner/repo for the duration of the push. The token is available in the FilePRHandler context via self.ctx.forgejo_client() — it needs to flow down into push_bookmark.

issues.title: Remove local bare path remote support from get_repo_info — Forgejo HTTP/SSH only
issues.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

get_repo_info/parse_github_url silently accepts local bare path remotes (e.g. /home/goya/bare/backrooms.git) and parses filesystem directory names as owner/repo. This produces wrong results that cause downstream HTTP 404s from both file_pr and spawn_reviewer. The fallback exists but should never be valid: all exomonad-managed repos must have a Forgejo HTTP or SSH remote. Refactor: (1) Remove the local path acceptance path — detect non-URL strings (no :// and no @host:) early and fail with a clear error: 'Remote is a local path. Set your remote to the Forgejo HTTP URL: git remote set-url origin http://<forgejo>/owner/repo'. (2) Handle generic SSH format git@<host>:owner/repo.git by stripping the git@<host>: prefix before splitting, not just git@github.com:. (3) Add a test asserting local paths are rejected with a useful error message. This is a strict improvement: there is no legitimate use case for a local bare path in an exomonad workflow.

issues.title: parse_github_url fails on local bare path remotes and non-GitHub SSH URLs
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

services/repo.rs::parse_github_url hardcodes git@github.com: normalization. Two failure modes: (1) Local bare path remote (e.g. /home/goya/bare/backrooms.git): no normalization applies, function splits on '/' and takes last two path segments, extracting filesystem directory as owner instead of the Forgejo org — this is what caused 'user goya not found' in the backrooms dev-leaf. (2) Forgejo SSH (git@localhost:owner/repo.git): git@localhost: prefix is not stripped, so owner becomes 'git@localhost:owner'. Forgejo HTTP remotes (http://localhost:3000/owner/repo) already parse correctly. Fix: handle generic SSH format by stripping git@<host>: prefix before splitting, and fail early with a clear error on local paths (no :// and no @) rather than silently parsing wrong path segments as owner/repo. Consider adding forgejo_owner/forgejo_repo config overrides as an escape hatch.

issues.title: fj CLI backend for Forgejo: auto-detect when HTTP config absent
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

When forgejo_url + forgejo_token are absent from config.toml, exomonad should detect the fj binary (Forgejo's official CLI) and use it as the Forgejo backend. If neither is configured, Forgejo remains unavailable (current behavior). Clean mutual exclusion — only one backend active, no dual-path debugging.

## Selection logic (server startup)

  if forgejo_url + forgejo_token configured → HTTP API client (current, unchanged)
  else if `fj` found in PATH → fj CLI client (new)
  else → forgejo_client = None (current behavior)

Explicit config ALWAYS wins. fj is only used when HTTP config is absent.

## exomonad init behavior

On startup, if fj backend is selected, log clearly:
  [Forgejo] Using fj CLI backend (forgejo_url/forgejo_token not configured)
If fj not found and HTTP not configured, log:
  [Forgejo] Not configured — spawn_reviewer, watcher_pr_state, file_pr will be unavailable

## Implementation

1. Add FjForgejoClient struct in rust/exomonad-core/src/services/forgejo.rs (or a new fj_client.rs)
   - Implements the same interface as ForgejoClient
   - Each method shells out to fj commands:
     get_pull_request → fj pr view <number> --json
     list_open_pull_requests → fj pr list --state open --json
     create_pull_request → fj pr create --title ... --body ... --base ...
     update_pull_request → fj pr edit <number> ...
     commit_status_for_head → fj api GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/statuses

2. ForgejoClient becomes an enum or the HasForgejoClient trait is backed by a boxed trait object

3. In serve.rs: extend the Forgejo client initialization block with fj detection:
   (None, None) => {
       if which::which("fj").is_ok() {
           info!("[Forgejo] fj binary detected, using fj CLI backend");
           Some(FjForgejoClient::new())
       } else {
           None
       }
   }

4. exomonad init: run fj detection early, surface in startup banner

## Constraint

Do NOT add a config option to select between backends — the selection is fully automatic and deterministic. This keeps debugging focused: if forgejo_url is set, you are on the HTTP path. If not, check for fj.

comments.content: Implemented deterministic Forgejo backend selection: HTTP config wins; otherwise fj in PATH selects the fj CLI backend; otherwise Forgejo remains unavailable. exomonad init now reports fj availability and fj auth status when HTTP config is absent. Verified with cargo test -p exomonad-core forgejo::tests::commit_status_for_head_reads_forgejo_combined_status and cargo test -p exomonad --lib forgejo.

issues.title: OpenCode dev-leaf review loop stalls: missing event dispatch fallback
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

The reviewer agent IS spawned correctly for OpenCode dev-leaf PRs (guard passes, preflight passes). The stall happens in the event dispatch step AFTER the reviewer submits comments.

## Root cause

call_handle_event_for_role (worktree_event_watcher.rs ~line 1474) dispatches pr_review events to dev agents via their WASM plugin. OpenCode dev-leaves have no WASM plugin entry because they have no SessionStart hook to register one.

When no plugin is found, the code has a Codex-specific fallback:
  if agent_type == AgentType::Codex && role == 'dev' {
      codex_dev_fallback_event_action(...)
  }

OpenCode is NOT included. It falls through to:
  tracing::error!('No plugin found for event target; skipping event dispatch')
  return Ok(None)

So reviewer comments are dropped silently. The OpenCode dev-leaf never sees them. It never pushes fixes. The review loop stalls indefinitely. The TL never gets [MERGE READY].

## Why Codex works

Codex has the same no-plugin situation but is explicitly handled by codex_dev_fallback_event_action. The fallback injects review comments into the Codex pane via tmux and routes merge_ready/ci_blocked events to the TL.

## Fix

In call_handle_event_for_role (worktree_event_watcher.rs), extend the fallback guard to include OpenCode:

  // Before:
  if agent_type == AgentType::Codex && role == 'dev' {

  // After:
  if (agent_type == AgentType::Codex || agent_type == AgentType::OpenCode) && role == 'dev' {

No other changes needed. codex_dev_fallback_event_action already handles all required event kinds (review_received, reviewer_requested_changes, merge_ready, ci_blocked, stuck, etc.) and is agent-type-agnostic in its logic.

## Files

- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs ~line 1477
  Change: if agent_type == AgentType::Codex && role == 'dev'
  To:     if (agent_type == AgentType::Codex || agent_type == AgentType::OpenCode) && role == 'dev'

## Verification

After fix: spawn an OpenCode dev-leaf, file PR, verify reviewer window appears (already works), verify reviewer comment appears injected into the OpenCode pane, verify the agent addresses it and gets [MERGE READY] to the TL.

comments.content:
Additional finding: upstream config bug in write_agent_mcp_config.

The missing OpenCode fallback in call_handle_event_for_role is a real bug, but the deeper upstream cause is that write_agent_mcp_config for OpenCode uses generate_mcp_config which produces an incomplete opencode.json — missing both "instructions" and "plugin" sections.

Comparison:

generate_mcp_config (used for dev-leaves):
  { "mcp": { "exomonad": {...} } }

generate_opencode_tl_settings (used for workers):
  { "mcp": {...}, "instructions": ["..."], "plugin": ["./.exo/opencode-plugin"] }

Missing "plugin" means the TypeScript hook bridge (opencode_plugin.rs) is never loaded for dev-leaves. The plugin is what routes exomonad hook event calls back through WASM dispatch. Without it, the event channel from OpenCode to the server is broken.

Missing "instructions" means the OpenCode dev-leaf gets no protocol instructions at all (no knowledge of the review loop, file_pr, notify_parent, etc.).

COMPLETE FIX requires two changes in write_agent_mcp_config for AgentType::OpenCode:

1. Replace:
     fs::write(agent_dir.join("opencode.json"), mcp_content).await?;
   With:
     let opencode_config = Self::generate_opencode_tl_settings(agent_name, role.as_str(), extra_mcp_servers);
     fs::write(agent_dir.join("opencode.json"), serde_json::to_string_pretty(&opencode_config)?).await?;

2. Also call after:
     Self::write_opencode_plugin_files(agent_dir).await?;

This mirrors exactly what spawn_worker does for OpenCode workers (spawn.rs ~1118-1126).

The fallback bug in call_handle_event_for_role (~line 1477) is still worth fixing as defense-in-depth, but the config is the root cause.

Files:
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs  AgentType::OpenCode arm of write_agent_mcp_config (~line 739)

Implemented OpenCode dev-leaf fallback guard extension. Verification: cargo test -p exomonad-core test_codex_dev_fallback_injects_review_received passed. Note: cargo test -p exomonad-core codex_dev_fallback also compiled but has an existing unrelated failure where merge_ready returns NotifyParent while the test expects InjectMessage.

Implemented the OpenCode dev-leaf opencode.json root-cause fix: write_agent_mcp_config now writes full OpenCode config with instructions/plugin and creates .exo/opencode-plugin files. Verified with cargo test -p exomonad-core test_write_agent_mcp_config_opencode_writes_full_config_and_plugin.

issues.title: Reviewer not spawned for OpenCode dev-leaf PRs: wrong Authoring-Agent in PR body

issues.title: Fix TL-to-worker messaging E2E validator launch
Stale routing registry: TL cannot detect dead worker panes or terminate OpenCode worker sessions
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

The TL believes a worker is alive because routing.json exists and tmux STDIN injection returns success=true — but the pane is already gone. The routing registry is never cleaned up when a worker exits on its own. The TL then blocks waiting for a handoff that will never arrive.

Observed in practice: Codex TL sent a correction to an OpenCode worker via send_message (tmux_stdin delivery), got success=true, then waited indefinitely because the pane was already closed.

## Root cause

1. **routing.json is never cleaned up on worker exit** — OpenCode (and other) workers do not delete their routing.json when they exit. The file persists pointing to a dead window/pane ID.

2. **tmux STDIN injection does not verify pane liveness** — send_tmux_message loads a buffer and pastes it to the target pane. tmux returns exit 0 even if the target is a shell prompt with no agent running, or if the window/pane no longer exists (some tmux versions silently swallow paste-buffer to dead targets).

3. **No TL-side termination path for OpenCode workers** — The TL has no tool to explicitly end a worker session (kill its pane/window and clean up its registry entry). dispose_leaf exists in Haskell but its behavior for OpenCode pane-based workers (vs window-based leaves) is untested.

## What should happen

1. **Pane liveness check before send_message** — Before injecting via tmux STDIN, verify the target pane/window is alive and running an agent (not a bare shell prompt). If dead, surface `[WORKER GONE: {name}]` to the TL instead of returning success=true.

2. **routing.json TTL / cleanup on worker exit** — Worker Stop hook should remove routing.json (or write a `exited_at` sentinel). Orphan reconciler already cleans up timed-out agents — same logic should apply when a worker exits cleanly.

3. **TL-side session termination tool** — A tool (or dispose_leaf extension) that: checks pane liveness, kills the pane/window if alive, removes routing.json, and optionally ends the Chainlink session for that agent. Must work for both window-based leaves (spawn_leaf) and pane-based workers (spawn_worker).

## Affected paths
- send_tmux_message effect handler (Rust): add pane liveness check before paste-buffer
- Worker Stop hook (WASM): write exited_at to agent dir, remove or tombstone routing.json
- dispose_leaf tool (Haskell WASM): verify it handles pane-based OpenCode workers correctly
- Orphan reconciler: pick up exited_at tombstones as a cleanup trigger alongside spawned_at timeout

## Related
- #437 (poll_workers: proactive TL visibility into agent state)
- #436 (E2E test: TL-to-worker pane messaging round-trip)

issues.title: Proactive TL worker monitor: poll spawned agent state instead of waiting passively
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

The TL currently sits idle between spawning workers/dev-leaves and receiving event notifications. When tmux delivery fails (pane injection drops, Teams inbox misses), the TL never wakes up — it just waits forever with no visibility into what its workers are doing.

## Current state tracking (what exists)

### Server-side (not TL-visible)
- **Orphan reconciler** — polls `.exo/agents/{slug}/spawned_at` on an interval, kills windows that exceed session timeout, injects timeout notification via tmux STDIN to TL. Reactive, not proactive.
- **Worktree event watcher** — watches Forgejo PR state (reviews, CI, approvals), fires WASM event handlers → injects messages into agent panes. Forgejo-focused, not worker-process-focused.

### Agent state files on disk (readable by anyone)
Per agent in `.exo/agents/{slug}/`:
- `spawned_at` — unix timestamp
- `active_issue` — chainlink issue ID the agent is working on
- `routing.json` — tmux window_id or pane_id
- `.birth_branch` — git branch

These files are written by spawn infrastructure and updated by agents. The TL has no loop that reads them.

### What the TL sees today
Only terminal events via push: `[MERGE READY]`, `[STUCK]`, `[FAILED]`, `[TIMED OUT]` from orphan reconciler. Intermediate worker state is invisible unless the worker explicitly calls notify_parent.

## Proposed: TL-owned worker watcher

A lightweight polling loop the TL can invoke after spawning a wave. It reads the agent state files and chainlink session status for each spawned agent and injects a summary into the TL's context if something looks stale or stuck.

### What to poll (per spawned agent)
1. **Pane/window alive?** — `tmux list-windows` or `tmux list-panes` against the routing.json target
2. **Chainlink session status** — `chainlink session status --agent {slug}` (shows started/attached/ended + handoff notes)
3. **Chainlink issue progress** — `chainlink issue show {active_issue}` (status, comments count, last updated)
4. **Age** — now - spawned_at

### Delivery to TL
If any worker looks stale (alive but no chainlink session activity in N minutes, or pane is a shell prompt with no agent running), inject a structured status report into the TL's pane so it can decide to re-spec, send a correction, or escalate.

## Design options

**Option A: WASM tool (preferred — follows architecture)**
New MCP tool `poll_workers` in Haskell WASM. TL calls it explicitly after spawning or on a timer. Tool reads agent state files + chainlink CLI, returns structured status. Keeps all logic in WASM, Rust executes the filesystem/process effects.

**Option B: Server-side background poller (like orphan reconciler)**
New service in Rust that runs per-TL-session, polls on interval, injects status updates into TL pane automatically. No TL action needed, but harder to scope per-wave.

**Option C: TL-side bash loop (no framework changes)**
TL uses bash in a worker pane to poll and notify_parent when something looks wrong. Works today, brittle, no semantic model.

## Recommendation
Option A — `poll_workers` MCP tool. The TL calls it at the start of each idle period after spawning. Returns per-agent: pane_alive, chainlink_session_state, issue_status, age_minutes. TL decides what to do with the information. Fits the existing WASM tool architecture exactly.

## Implementation notes
- New tool `poll_workers` in `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/`
- Rust effect handler reads `.exo/agents/` dir, runs chainlink CLI per agent
- TL role context updated to call poll_workers after fork_wave when idling
- No new server-side background service needed for Option A

issues.title: Add exomonad revert command
issues.description:
Add `exomonad revert` CLI command that undoes workspace changes made by `exomonad init`, allowing a workspace to run an interactive Claude session without role enforcement or hook interception.

## Files written by init (confirmed from init.rs source)

### Root workspace — Claude root agent
- `.mcp.json` — MCP server config (written at line 860–894)
- `.claude/settings.local.json` — hooks via `HookConfig::write_persistent` (line ~680)
- `.claude/rules/exomonad_role.md` — symlink to role context file

### Root workspace — agent-type-specific
- `.codex/config.toml` — Codex root config (`write_codex_root_config`)
- `.gemini/settings.json` — Gemini root MCP config
- `opencode.json` — OpenCode TL config written to repo root
- `.exo/agents/root/opencode.json` — OpenCode agent config
- `.exo/agents/root/.birth_branch` — root agent birth branch marker

### Companion worktrees (Claude companions)
Per companion `{name}` from config `[[companions]]`:
- `.exo/companions/{name}/` — git worktree (`git worktree add`)
- `.exo/companions/{name}/.mcp.json`
- `.exo/companions/{name}/.claude/settings.local.json`
- `.exo/companions/{name}/.claude/rules/exomonad_role.md`
- `.exo/companions/{name}/.exo/server.sock` — symlink to project server socket

### Companion agent dirs (all companion types)
- `.exo/agents/{name}/routing.json` — window_id for all companions
- `.exo/agents/{name}/settings.json` — Gemini companions
- `.exo/agents/{name}/opencode.json` — OpenCode companions

## What revert must NOT remove
- `.exo/config.toml` — written by `new`, not `init`
- `.exo/wasm/` — WASM plugins
- `.claude/rules/exomonad.md` — written by `new`, not `init`
- `.gitignore` entries
- `.chainlink/` — issue tracker data
- `.exo/logs/` — log files
- The tmux session itself (default; use `--kill-session` to opt in)

## Implementation plan

### New files
- `rust/exomonad/src/revert.rs` — `pub async fn run(kill_session: bool) -> Result<()>`

### Changes to existing files
- `rust/exomonad/src/main.rs` — add `Commands::Revert { kill_session: bool }` variant and dispatch arm
- `rust/exomonad/CLAUDE.md` — add Revert Command section

### revert.rs logic
1. Load `Config::discover()` to get session name and companion list
2. Remove root files (skip silently if missing): `.mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/rules/exomonad_role.md`, `opencode.json`, `.codex/config.toml`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `.exo/agents/root/opencode.json`, `.exo/agents/root/.birth_branch`
3. For each companion in config:
   - If Claude type: `git worktree remove --force .exo/companions/{name}` then `fs::remove_dir_all` if still present
   - Remove `.exo/agents/{name}/routing.json`, `settings.json`, `opencode.json`
4. Remove `.exo/server.sock` and `.exo/sockets/` if server is not running (check socket liveness)
5. If `--kill-session`: `TmuxIpc::kill_session(&session)`
6. Print what was removed; skip missing files silently (not an error)

### Behavior notes
- Non-destructive by default — tmux session left running
- Idempotent — safe to run multiple times
- Skips files not present (no error)
- Reads companion list from `config.toml` so it knows which worktrees to remove

issues.title: Reviewer must submit reviews directly via Forgejo API — no local file or socket dependency
issues.description:
Reviewers are currently blocked in two ways: (1) PreToolUse hooks fail with ENOENT because .exo/server.sock is absent from the reviewer worktree, and (2) the approve_pr MCP tool routes through the exomonad server which also needs the socket. Both are avoidable — the reviewer does not need local infrastructure at all.

A reviewer's entire job is:
  1. Read the PR diff: GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/files
  2. Read changed file content: GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/raw/{sha}/{filepath}
  3. Submit a review: POST /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews
     body: {state: 'APPROVED' | 'REQUEST_CHANGES', body: '...'}

All three are direct Forgejo API calls using FORGEJO_TOKEN. No exomonad server, no MCP tools, no local file reads beyond the credentials in env.

The Codex reviewer task spec should give the reviewer:
  - FORGEJO_URL, FORGEJO_TOKEN, FORGEJO_REVIEWER_TOKEN
  - The PR number and repo slug
  - Explicit curl/gh commands to perform each step
  - No hooks needed if we do not block tool use (or reviewer runs in yolo mode)

For Claude reviewers: the reviewer should also prefer direct API calls. The PreToolUse hook guard (which denies Edit/Write) can remain as a safety rail, but the hook should not be required for approval to succeed.

Milestone: reviewer can approve a PR in a fresh Codex session with no .exo/ directory present, using only curl and env vars.

issues.title: Codex shared_dir agents missing routing.json — TL cannot deliver messages
issues.description:
Codex agents spawned with shared_dir topology (working_dir='.', birth_branch matches parent) have no routing.json in their .exo/agents/{name}/ directory. Only identity.json, active_issue, and spawned_at are written.

Without routing.json, deliver_via_tmux cannot find the tmux window_id for the agent. All message delivery from TL falls through to tmux_target guess-based injection, which fails silently or hits the wrong target.

Observed: .exo/agents/issue-65-divergence-investigation-codex/ has no routing.json.

Root cause: The Codex spawn path that sets topology=SharedDir likely uses a different code path that either (a) does not call new_tmux_window and thus has no window_id, or (b) calls finalize_spawn with an empty RoutingInfo (all None fields), which write_to_dir serializes as {} and routing_tmux_target returns None for.

Fix: Identify the SharedDir spawn path, ensure it records the tmux window_id (or pane_id for pane-based agents) in the RoutingInfo passed to finalize_spawn. If Codex shared_dir agents run in the project root, the routing.json should still record the window_id so TL can target the correct tmux window.

issues.title: Reviewer Codex worktree missing .exo/server.sock — all PreToolUse hooks fail
issues.description:
Reviewer Codex agents are spawned into their own worktree (.exo/worktrees/issue-N-*-codex/) but the worktree has no .exo/ directory at all. The Codex PreToolUse hook calls `exomonad hook pre-tool-use` which tries to connect to .exo/server.sock relative to its CWD. Without that socket, EVERY tool call fails with 'No such file or directory (os error 2)'.

Observed: worktree .exo/worktrees/issue-68-pr16-ci-fix-codex/ has no .exo/ subdir and no server.sock symlink. Reviewer cannot execute bash, read files, call MCP tools, or submit an approve_pr. CI can pass and fixes can be pushed but the reviewer is permanently blocked.

Root cause: create_socket_symlink() in spawn_subtree is supposed to create a .exo/server.sock symlink in the child worktree. Either it is not being called for Codex reviewer worktrees, the symlink path is wrong, or the symlink target no longer resolves (project moved). Also needs .exo/tmp/ created in the worktree for file-indirect injection.

Fix: ensure spawn_reviewer_subtree_named (or the Codex reviewer spawn path) always creates .exo/server.sock as an absolute-path symlink to the project root server socket. Verify with: ls -la .exo/worktrees/*/exo/server.sock

issues.title: TL needs restart_review tool to re-trigger the review cycle when a PR is stuck on CI or reviewer failure
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

## Problem

When a PR's CI fails and then gets fixed (e.g., the dev pushes a CI fix commit), the watcher may not automatically restart the review cycle. If the PR's WatchState has stuck=true, notified_parent_timeout=true, or the reviewer was disposed, the convergence loop is stalled. The TL has no tool to reset this state and restart from scratch.

Specific case observed: nemotron-port PR with CI bugs that were fixed by a subsequent commit. The TL needs to re-trigger a fresh review round.

## What to do

Add a restart_review MCP tool available to root and tl roles. It should:

1. Accept pr_number as input.
2. Reset the WatchState for that PR in the watcher's in-memory state:
   - stuck = false
   - notified_parent_timeout = false
   - notified_parent_approved = false
   - merge_ready_notified = false
   - addressed_changes = false
   - rounds = 0
   - reviewer_spawned = false
   - reviewer_disposed = false
3. Clear stuck and needs_human_review from watcher-state.json for that PR number.
4. If a reviewer worktree exists for this PR, dispose it (kill the tmux window, remove the worktree) so a fresh reviewer gets spawned on the next watcher poll cycle.
5. Return a summary of what was reset.

The watcher's next poll cycle (within 60s) will then see the PR as if newly observed — reviewer_spawned=false triggers a fresh reviewer spawn, and compute_pr_actions processes it with a clean state.

## Alternative considered

Exposing a 'force restart poll cycle now' trigger. This is weaker — it doesn't reset WatchState, so the stale flags remain.

## Architecture note

This tool is a Rust effect (new effect type in the agent namespace or a new watcher namespace). The Haskell tool definition lives in TLRole.hs/RootRole.hs. The Rust handler calls into the watcher service directly (the watcher is already shared via Arc<RwLock<...>>).

## Files

- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/ -- new RestartReview.hs tool
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs -- expose reset_pr_watch_state() method
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/ -- new handler for the restart_review effect

comments.content: Implemented restart_review as an agent effect/tool. Verification: cargo test -q -p exomonad-core reset_reviewer_restart_artifacts -- --nocapture; cargo test -q -p exomonad-core watcher_runtime_state_resets_review_cycle_flags -- --nocapture; cargo test -p exomonad-core --test wasm_integration wasm_tl_tools_include_spawn_and_merge -- --nocapture; cargo test -p exomonad-core --test wasm_integration wasm_chainlink_tools_are_scoped_by_role -- --nocapture; just build. Full just test-wasm-integration built WASM but nextest timed out at its 60s per-test limit with many tests still running.

issues.title: Reviewer spawned without Edit/Write deny in AgentPermissions — WASM hook alone is insufficient guard
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Problem

spawn_reviewer_subtree_named() sets AgentPermissions.deny to only MCP tool names:
  ['fork_wave', 'spawn_leaf', 'spawn_worker', 'merge_pr', 'file_pr']

It does NOT deny 'Edit', 'Write', 'MultiEdit', 'NotebookEdit'. These are Claude Code built-in tools, not MCP tools, and are supposed to be blocked by the WASM PreToolUse hook in ReviewerRole.hs.

But the WASM hook is the wrong layer for this. AgentPermissions.deny is enforced by Claude Code's harness settings directly — it is reliable. The WASM hook requires the exomonad server to be reachable (hook fires via UDS), which can fail. Reviewers are currently able to modify code when either:
  a) The WASM hook fails (ENOENT, UDS unreachable), or
  b) The WASM reviewer role doesn't deny those tools explicitly.

## Root cause of hook ENOENT

The reviewer agent's PreToolUse hook calls 'exomonad hook pre-tool-use', which connects to .exo/server.sock. From the reviewer's working directory (.exo/worktrees/review-pr-N-{type}/), the socket discovery crawls up the directory tree. On some configurations (NixOS, or when the worktree is inside .exo/ itself), either the exomonad binary isn't on PATH in the tmux environment, or the socket path resolution fails. This causes the hook to exit with ENOENT (os error 2), bypassing all WASM deny logic.

## Fix

Add 'Edit', 'Write', 'MultiEdit', 'NotebookEdit' to AgentPermissions.deny in spawn_reviewer_subtree_named(). This enforces read-only at the harness level, independent of the WASM hook. The WASM hook remains as defense-in-depth but is no longer the primary guard.

Also diagnose the ENOENT path: add a preflight check in the hook binary (or the reviewer spawn) to verify the socket is reachable before the reviewer session starts. Log a clear error if not.

## File

- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs -- spawn_reviewer_subtree_named() AgentPermissions (~line 1625)
