issues.title: Evaluate and adopt fj/Forgejo CLI for one-shot Forgejo operations — replace custom HTTP client calls where appropriate
issues.description:
Question: 

Context: 

Findings: 

## Background

exomonad maintains a bespoke ForgejoClient (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/forgejo.rs, ~600 lines) that hand-rolls every Forgejo API call with raw reqwest HTTP. This includes auth header management, URL construction, response deserialization, and error handling for each endpoint. A Forgejo CLI (fj or equivalent) can replace the one-shot operations with subprocess calls, reducing the HTTP client surface we own and maintain.

The Forgejo admin CLI docs are at https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/command-line/ — this is the server-side CLI. Also evaluate the Gitea/Forgejo community client CLI ('tea') which is the user-facing equivalent of 'gh' for GitHub. Identify which tool is available and appropriate for the local docker-compose Forgejo environment exomonad ships with.

## Current ForgejoClient surface (forgejo.rs)

Operations that are ONE-SHOT (called once per agent action, good candidates for CLI replacement):

| Method | Endpoint | Used by |
|--------|----------|---------|
| create_pull_request | POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls | file_pr handler |
| update_pull_request | PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n} | file_pr handler (update) |
| merge_pull_request | POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/merge | merge_pr service |
| get_pull_request | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n} | merge_pr service, watcher |
| submit_pull_request_review | POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews | approve_pr / copilot_review |

Operations that are HIGH-FREQUENCY POLLING (keep as HTTP client — CLI subprocess overhead is too high):

| Method | Endpoint | Used by |
|--------|----------|---------|
| list_open_pull_requests | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls | watcher (every 60s) |
| list_pull_request_reviews | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews | watcher (every 60s, per PR) |
| list_commit_statuses | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/statuses | watcher (every 60s, per PR) — see also #419 |
| commit_status_for_head | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status | watcher fallback |
| actions_status_for_head | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs | watcher |
| latest_actions_status_for_branch | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs | watcher, dashboard |
| list_workflow_runs_for_branch | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs | watcher |
| list_global_runners | GET /repos/runners | dashboard |
| find_open_pull_request | GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls | watcher |

## gh CLI usage to migrate

- copilot_review.rs uses 'gh' (GitHub Copilot review — this is GitHub-specific, not Forgejo). Needs separate treatment.
- services/mod.rs checks 'gh --version' as a presence check.

## Research tasks

1. Determine which CLI tool is available for Forgejo in the local docker-compose environment:
   - Is 'fj' (https://codeberg.org/forgejo/fj) installable and stable?
   - Is 'tea' (the Gitea CLI, https://gitea.com/gitea/tea) usable with Forgejo?
   - Can the Forgejo server admin CLI (accessible via docker exec on the forgejo container) handle user-facing operations like PR creation?
   - Does the local Forgejo instance expose an API that 'gh' (configured with --hostname) can use?

2. For each one-shot operation above, prototype the equivalent CLI command and verify it works against the local Forgejo docker-compose instance (see /home/goya/rust-workspace/nemotron-port/forgejo/ for the reference setup).

3. Document auth: the CLI will need FORGEJO_TOKEN or equivalent. Verify the CLI respects the same env var exomonad already exports, or document the mapping.

4. Prototype: replace file_pr handler's create_pull_request and update_pull_request calls with CLI subprocess. Measure: is the result simpler and more maintainable than the current reqwest code?

## Decision criteria

Keep ForgejoClient for high-frequency polling (watcher). The 60s poll cycle with multiple API calls per PR cannot absorb subprocess overhead. For one-shot operations (file_pr, merge_pr, approve_pr), CLI replacement is appropriate if:
- Auth is handled transparently from env vars
- JSON output is available and stable (for result parsing)
- Error messages are machine-readable
- The CLI is available on the platforms exomonad targets (NixOS, Ubuntu, macOS)

## Expected outcome

A decision doc (docs/decisions/forgejo-cli-adoption.md) with:
- Which CLI tool was chosen and why
- Which ForgejoClient methods are replaced
- Which are kept as HTTP calls
- Auth approach
- Install/availability story for NixOS

If adoption is viable: follow-on implementation issue for each replaced method. Do not implement during this research issue.

comments.content: Decision documented in docs/decisions/forgejo-cli-adoption.md. Finding: do not adopt a CLI path yet. tea is the first future prototype candidate, but tea/fj are not installed in this workspace, and Forgejo's bundled CLI is server/admin-oriented. No implementation follow-up created because adoption is not currently viable.

issues.title: exomonad models: add codex harness, make opencode failure non-fatal, fix NixOS WAL checkpoint error
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Problem

exomonad models shells out to 'opencode models' as the first step in run_all(). OpenCode opens a SQLite database on startup and runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) to merge its write-ahead log. On NixOS this fails because the XDG state/data dirs are either read-only or not fully initialized, producing a WAL checkpoint error that aborts the entire command.

Two compounding issues:
1. run_all() propagates the opencode failure — the entire command fails even if the user only cares about codex or claude models.
2. There is no 'codex' harness in models.rs at all. Codex-installed systems have no way to query available models.

## What to do

1. Add run_codex() to models.rs with a static list (same pattern as run_gemini() and run_claude()). Wire it to --harness codex and include it in run_all(). Codex does not expose programmatic model discovery; a static list with a staleness note is correct.

2. Make run_opencode() failure non-fatal in run_all(). If 'opencode models' exits non-zero or fails to spawn, print a warning line ('opencode: unavailable ({error})') and continue to the next harness. A missing or broken opencode install should not prevent listing claude or codex models.

3. Consider whether opencode model discovery via SQLite is worth keeping at all. A static list (like gemini/claude) avoids the SQLite dependency entirely and is more robust across environments. The opencode model list rarely changes and is well-documented upstream.

## Files

- rust/exomonad/src/models.rs -- run_opencode(), run_all(), run_gemini(), run_claude()

issues.title: Remove persist_review_states and watcher file writes for review_state — WatchState is the state machine
issues.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

## Context

persist_review_states() is called each poll cycle when review state changes, but it does not actually persist review_state anywhere. It only clears stuck/needs_human_review flags in watcher-state.json when a PR is approved. The review_state values in the update vec are silently ignored.

The watcher already has the correct state machine: WatchState (in-memory HashMap<PRNumber, WatchState>) holds last_review_state, rounds, notified_parent_approved, merge_ready_notified, addressed_changes, stuck, needs_human_review, etc. These fields are re-derived correctly on each poll cycle via compute_pr_actions. No file write is needed to track review state across poll cycles — Forgejo is the source of truth and is queried live each cycle.

## What to do

1. Delete persist_review_states() entirely. It is dead code for its stated purpose.

2. The only fields that need to survive server restarts are rounds, stuck, and needs_human_review (so the TL does not re-receive stuck notifications). These are already read from watcher-state.json on startup (load_registry_from_forgejo, lines ~786-817). Keep that read path. The watcher-state.json write path should only be triggered by set_pr_stuck() and set_pr_rounds() — not by review_state observations.

3. Remove the review_state field from WatcherStateFile if it exists there. Review state is not worth persisting: it is fetched live from Forgejo on the first poll cycle after restart (forgejo_review_parts), so the watcher re-derives it correctly without any file.

4. Remove the review_state field from PrEntry / pr_registry.json if it is only written by persist_review_states and read by merge_pr. After #418 is fixed (merge_pr queries Forgejo directly), this field is unused on both ends.

5. Update tests that assert on review_state writes to watcher-state.json.

## Depends on

#418 (merge_pr must stop reading local registry review_state before that field can be removed)

## Files

- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs -- persist_review_states(), review_state_updates vec, WatcherStateFile
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/pr_registry.rs -- review_state field on PrEntry
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/file_pr.rs -- local_pr_get review_state in response

issues.title: combine_commit_statuses uses /statuses list endpoint causing false Pending from historical entries
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Problem

commit_status_for_head() calls list_commit_statuses() which hits /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/statuses (paginated list). combine_commit_statuses() then checks: if any entry is 'pending' -> return Pending.

The /statuses list endpoint returns ALL historical status entries, not deduplicated by context. Forgejo appends a new entry for each CI run, so after a completed run there are both 'pending' (old) and 'success' (new) entries for the same context. combine_commit_statuses finds a pending entry and returns Pending indefinitely, even though the latest run succeeded.

## Observed evidence

Watcher log shows PR#18 ci=Pending and PR#19 ci=Pending for 30+ minutes. Direct API check of the same SHAs via /commits/{sha}/status (combined endpoint) returns state=success, total=2.

The /statuses list for PR#18 head SHA contained:
  success (push, 05:44), pending (push, 05:43), success (pr, 05:43), pending (pr, 05:42), pending (waiting, 05:42)

combine_commit_statuses sees pending entries -> returns Pending. But the latest per context are both success.

## Fix

Switch commit_status_for_head to use the combined /status endpoint (/api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/status, singular) instead of /statuses (plural). The combined endpoint deduplicates by context server-side and returns the aggregate state field directly. Parse that field instead of running combine_commit_statuses on a raw list.

Alternatively: deduplicate the /statuses list by context before passing to combine_commit_statuses (keep only the latest updated_at per context). The combined endpoint approach is simpler.

## Impact

CI status is permanently wrong (stuck at Pending) for any PR where the CI ran multiple times (push + pull_request events). This prevents merge_ready events from firing because the watcher never sees CI as success.

## Files

- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/forgejo.rs -- commit_status_for_head(), list_commit_statuses(), combine_commit_statuses()

issues.title: merge_pr gates on stale local registry review_state instead of live Forgejo state
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Problem

mergeFromLocalPr (MergePR.hs ~line 202) blocks merges using the local PR registry's review_state field:

  if force || reviewState == "approved"
    then doMerge args
    else Left "Local PR #N is not approved yet (review_state=pending_review)"

The local review_state is written by the watcher's poll cycle via persist_review_states. It defaults to pending_review and is only updated when the watcher observes a state change. This makes merge_pr dependent on the watcher having successfully propagated the review state.

## Failure modes

1. SHA-drop filter (forgejo_review_parts, watcher ~line 1865): the watcher drops a review if the review commit SHA doesn't match pr.last_head_sha in the local registry. If last_head_sha is stale, the approval is silently discarded and the registry never advances past pending_review.

2. Poll cycle gap: watcher polls every 60s. If merge_pr is called within that window after an approval, the registry hasn't been updated yet.

3. Server restart: WatchState is in-memory. After restart, merge_ready_notified resets; the registry write requires the poll to have completed at least once post-restart.

## Observed symptom (nemotron-port, 2026-05-26)

PR #19 shows APPROVED + CI success via direct Forgejo API. Watcher has been polling for hours (poll cycle pr_count=3 logged every 60s). merge_pr still returns: 'Local PR #19 is not approved yet (review_state=pending_review).'

## Fix

In mergeFromLocalPr, when the local registry says pending_review and force is false, fall through to a live Forgejo review query rather than blocking. Mirror what mergeFromGitHub already does: call GitHubGetPullRequest with includeReviews=true, then pass to checkCopilotReadinessFromPR.

The local registry review_state is appropriate as a cached view for event delivery. It is NOT appropriate as an authoritative gate for an irreversible operation like merge. Forgejo is the source of truth at merge time.

Note: The watcher's observed_ci_status() already does the right thing for CI -- it calls commit_status_for_head() (live Forgejo API) every poll cycle. Review state needs the same treatment at merge time.

## Files

- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/MergePR.hs -- mergeFromLocalPr (~line 195)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs -- forgejo_review_parts, persist_review_states
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/pr_registry.rs -- ForgejoReviewState

investigate: should close_self / shutdown tool exist? narrow or remove unsafe self-teardown
issues.description:
Question: 

Context: 

Findings: 

Investigate whether the close_self effect / shutdown MCP tool should exist, and narrow or remove the unsafe surface. See docs/decisions/agent-teardown-ownership.md.

FINDINGS (audited 2026-05-25):
- close_self has exactly ONE live caller: the WorkerExit hook (haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tool/Runtime.hs, handleWorkerExit) -- ephemeral worker pane self-cleanup. Defensible (no PR/worktree/review loop).
- The shutdown MCP tool (Guest/Tools/Events.hs, shutdownCore) is defined+exported in the SDK but wired to NO role in .exo/roles/. It is dormant. 1. Decide: delete the dormant shutdown tool entirely, OR re-scope it worker-only behind a canExit check.
2. If kept for workers, route any self-close through the stop-hook canExit so it can never bypass review gating.
3. Confirm no role config exposes shutdown/close_self to dev/reviewer leaves; add a test asserting that.

issues.title: fix: forgejo CI stack must come up cleanly from docker-compose (survive host restart)
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Forgejo CI broke after a host restart and required manual recovery (docker start forgejo-dind + docker restart forgejo-runner). Make the stack come up cleanly and reproducibly from docker-compose so a reboot auto-recovers with zero manual steps.

ROOT CAUSE (observed 2026-05-25):
- forgejo-dind (image docker:dind, runs `dockerd -H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375 --tls=false`) was Exited(0) ~13h after a restart and never came back.
- runner has DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-in-docker:2375 and depends_on docker-in-docker; with dind down it could not ping the docker daemon, exited 1, and crash-looped (269 restarts, ~1/min).
- Forgejo server stayed healthy and kept queuing Actions jobs, so all CI sat pending with no live runner.

EVIDENCE THE LIVE STACK DIVERGED FROM COMPOSE (debugged out-of-band):
- `docker compose -f forgejo/docker-compose.yml ps -a` lists only forgejo + forgejo-runner, NOT forgejo-dind -> compose no longer tracks the dind container, so `up -d` may recreate/rename instead of resuming.
- Running dind image is docker:28-dind while compose pins docker:dind (floating tag).

WORK:
1. Reconcile forgejo/docker-compose.yml with the live working config (fold in whatever was hand-tweaked outside compose). Pin dind image to docker:28-dind (the tag that works), not floating docker:dind.
2. Add `restart: unless-stopped` (or always) to forgejo, docker-in-docker, and runner so a host reboot brings them all back.
3. Gate the runner on dind readiness: dind healthcheck + runner `depends_on: { docker-in-docker: { condition: service_healthy } }`. This kills the crash-loop at the source (runner never starts before dockerd is reachable).
4. Confirm runner registration (runner-data/.runner, runner-config.yml) persists across container recreation via the volume.

VERIFY/DONE: from a clean `docker compose -f forgejo/docker-compose.yml down` then `up -d` (and ideally a real host reboot), all three services come up, the runner reaches idle, and a pushed commit gets its CI job picked up and completed -- with NO manual docker start/restart.

comments.content: Implemented compose hardening: pinned docker-in-docker to docker:28-dind, added no-TLS dind healthcheck, changed runner dependency to service_healthy, documented persisted runner registration. Verified docker compose config, clean compose down/up after one-time removal of the previously untracked forgejo-dind drift container, all three containers compose-managed with restart=unless-stopped; dind/forgejo healthy and runner declared local-runner. EXOMONAD_FORGEJO_TOKEN missing, so full pushed-commit CI smoke was not run.

Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Three loosely-coupled fixes surfaced while debugging a Codex dev leaf whose PR was correctly tracked by the Forgejo watcher, but which session_status reported as "no live agents" (the leaf had timed out/cleaned up while waiting on the reviewer, and the reviewer was waiting on CI).

Root cause is a vocabulary collision across three orthogonal state sources:
- session_status -> .exo/agents/ dirs + tmux (actor liveness only)
- chainlink_session_status -> .chainlink/issues.db (issue work-state)
- watcher / [MERGE READY] -> Forgejo (load_registry_from_forgejo): PR/review/CI

issues.title: Fix cleanup_reviewer_leaf and live_reviewer_for_pr to use tmux window scan instead of dead filesystem scan
Stop hook block response injects conversation message causing agent to loop and burn tokens
issues.description: When the Stop hook blocks dev leaf exit (e.g. dev_ci_triggered phase), it returns a block reason string that gets injected into the agent conversation. The agent reads this injected message, generates a response, then tries to stop again, gets blocked again, generates another response — infinite token-burning loop. Fix: the Stop hook block response should either (1) return a silent block with no injected message, letting the agent sit idle until the watcher delivers the real event, or (2) the block reason message should not trigger a new agent turn. The agent should be in true idle after file_pr+notify_parent — the Stop hook should block silently, not inject conversation content.

issues.title: Watcher never evicts closed/merged PRs from watcher-state.json — stale state blocks dev leaf exit indefinitely
issues.description: When a PR is merged, the watcher poll_cycle correctly stops seeing it in the open PR list (pr_count drops). But watcher-state.json is never cleaned up — the PR entry persists with its last known phase (e.g. dev_ci_triggered). The dev leaf Stop hook reads this stale phase and blocks exit forever, even after the PR is closed in Forgejo. Fix: at the end of each poll_cycle, remove any PR from watcher-state.json whose number no longer appears in the open PR list from Forgejo. When a PR disappears from the open list, it was merged or closed — evict it from state and allow the dev leaf to exit.

issues.title: Watcher dashboard window closure gives false impression of dead watcher — needs persistence or respawn path
issues.description: The ratatui watcher dashboard runs in a dedicated tmux window. When that window is accidentally closed the watcher service keeps running inside the server process, but there is no visual heartbeat. The operator reads the missing window as watcher death. Fix: either (1) register the watcher dashboard as a companion in config.toml so init always owns its lifecycle and can revive it, or (2) make exomonad init --attach detect a missing watcher window and reopen it without tearing down the session. The poll cycle logs are visible in the server window at INFO level but are buried in hook traffic — not viable as a heartbeat substitute.

issues.title: Add watcher_pr_state MCP tool so TL can query PR review and CI state to decide merge directly
issues.description: When the watcher event chain is broken (no plugin for Codex, failed delivery, stale merge_ready_notified), the TL has no way to query current PR state and must wait indefinitely or escalate to human. Add a new MCP tool watcher_pr_state that takes pr_number, queries Forgejo for review state and CI status, and returns merge_ready bool plus a blocker description. TL can call this to self-diagnose and proceed with merge_pr when merge_ready=true without needing the watcher notification. Workaround today: TL queries Forgejo directly via bash curl against /pulls/N/reviews and /commits/SHA/statuses.

issues.title: Watcher pr_review events not dispatched to Codex dev leaves — no WASM plugin registered
issues.description: Codex dev agents do not register a WASM plugin at startup (no SessionStart hook equivalent). Watcher lookup finds the branch but no plugin entry, logs error and drops the event. Reviewer feedback and merge-ready signals are silently lost for all Codex leaves. Fix: either pre-load dev WASM plugin for Codex worktrees at spawn time keyed by birth_branch, or bypass WASM dispatch for Codex entirely and route pr_review events straight to tmux injection (consistent with Codex tmux-first delivery model).

issues.title: Dev-leaf burns tokens polling after file_pr — needs explicit IDLE instruction like root TL protocol
issues.description:
## Problem

After filing a PR, dev-leaf agents (Codex/Gemini) burn tokens in an active polling loop — checking CI status, printing state updates, re-checking git — instead of going idle. This is the opposite of the root TL protocol which says 'After spawning, STOP. End your turn with no further output.'

## Root cause

dev.md step 7 says 'Stay alive for watcher-delivered reviewer comments, CI status, and merge-ready.' No explicit stop instruction. LLM interprets 'stay alive' as 'keep generating output.' The watcher injects events into the pane when they arrive — the agent does not need to poll.

## Fix

Update dev.md steps 6-9 to mirror the TL IDLE pattern:

6. file_pr to create the PR
7. notify_parent with PR number and branch
8. IDLE: After notify_parent, STOP. End your turn. Do not generate any further output. Do not check CI. Do not poll git. Do not print status. The watcher will inject reviewer comments and merge-ready signals directly into this pane — your next turn begins only when a message arrives.
9. When a message arrives: act on it (fix review comments, push, etc.). Then STOP again.
10. Stop only after the watcher injects [MERGE READY].

## Impact

Every dev-leaf run currently burns idle tokens for the full review+CI wait window (can be 5-30 minutes). Fix is a doc change to dev.md.

issues.title: Reviewer Forgejo API identity: token user cannot review own PRs — need separate reviewer account or per-agent token
issues.description:
## Problem

When the reviewer calls POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews via the Forgejo API, it uses the same configured forgejo_token as the PR author. Forgejo rejects this: 'approve your own pull is not allowed'.

Observed in nemotron-port: TL merged PRs #8 and #9 but could not create Forgejo approval records because the token identity matched the PR author.

## Root cause

The reviewer role is identified by a distinct git identity (user.name=exomonad-reviewer-{name}) at the commit layer, but all Forgejo API calls use the single project-level forgejo_token. Forgejo enforces review identity at the API token level, not the git identity level.

## Fix options

1. Configure a second Forgejo user account (e.g. exomonad-reviewer) with its own token; store as forgejo_reviewer_token in config.toml; use this token when approve_pr / request_changes call the Forgejo review API.
2. Per-agent token: each spawned reviewer gets its own token injected at spawn time. More flexible but requires more config surface.

Option 1 is simpler. The reviewer account needs read access to the repo and permission to submit reviews.

## Impact

Without this, approve_pr / request_changes can never create Forgejo review records when the reviewer shares a token with the PR author — which is the common case since all dev-leaf agents use the same Forgejo identity.

issues.title: Watcher ci_status always Neutral — observed_ci_status never polls Forgejo commit statuses API, depends only on webhooks that are never delivered
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

observed_ci_status() never queries the Forgejo commit statuses API. It reads exclusively from ci_status_map, which is populated only by incoming webhook events. Since no Forgejo webhook is configured to deliver CI pipeline events to the exomonad server, ci_status_map is always empty.

Result: every PR forever shows ci=Neutral, regardless of actual CI outcome. CI passing on Forgejo has zero effect on the watcher's merge gate.

Root cause (worktree_event_watcher.rs ~L467):
  if !self.policy.ci.gate.enabled(self.ci_source_configured()) {
      return CIStatus::Neutral;  // hits this unconditionally
  }

ci_source_configured defaults to false (L423). Even if set to true, the ci_status_map lookup always misses because no webhooks populate it.

Confirmed: Forgejo /api/v1/repos/exomonad/nemotron-port/commits/{sha}/statuses returns status=success for both PR #8 and #9 head SHAs. Watcher shows ci=Neutral.

Fix: in collect_observations, after resolving head_sha, call:
  forgejo.list_commit_statuses(owner, repo, &head_sha).await
Map the combined result to CIStatus::Success (all success), CIStatus::Failure (any failure), CIStatus::Pending (any pending, no failures), CIStatus::Neutral (empty list). Use this directly as obs.ci_status — no ci_status_map, no webhook dependency.

This replaces the webhook-fed ci_status_map path entirely. The watcher already polls Forgejo every 60s for PR state; adding one commit-statuses call per open PR per cycle is consistent with that pattern and eliminates the webhook infrastructure requirement.

Also: set ci_source_configured = true when a Forgejo client is present, so the gate activates correctly. Or remove ci_source_configured entirely once the poll path is the only path.

Files:
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs (collect_observations ~L697, observed_ci_status ~L466)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/ (Forgejo client — add list_commit_statuses if not present)

Note: this fix is also required for #398's cleanup to be complete — the webhook-fed ci_status_map is another local-state path that should be replaced by Forgejo API polling.

4. Observation struct: remove review_file_seen and review_file_mtime fields

5. WatchStateDiagnostic: remove review_file_seen and review_file_mtime fields

6. .exo/reviews/ directory: can be deleted from all projects

API call volume: forgejo_review_parts is one list_pull_request_reviews call per open PR per poll cycle (60s). The watcher already polls Forgejo every cycle for PR metadata. This is one additional call per PR per cycle — acceptable. The local file was not a meaningful optimization; it was a workaround for not having Forgejo API submission.

Prerequisite: verify forgejo.create_pull_request_review() exists or add it to the Forgejo client.

- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/ (approve_pr, request_changes, post_review_comment tools)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs (approve_pr handler)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs (collect_observations, Observation, compute_pr_actions_with_context, ReviewFile, review_file_parts, etc.)

This also unblocks #395/#396: with Forgejo as source of truth, cleanup_reviewer_leaf just needs to delete the Forgejo review (or let the new reviewer submit a new one), no local file to manage.

issues.title: Add cleanup_reviewer_leaf MCP tool to kill, clean, and reset a stuck reviewer before respawn
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

TLs currently have no explicit way to clean up a stuck or zombie reviewer before respawning. spawn_reviewer(force=true) patches over this by reusing the existing worktree and window, leaving stale state behind (see #395).

A dedicated cleanup_reviewer_leaf(pr_number) MCP tool would:
1. Kill the reviewer's tmux window (if alive) — force-close the Codex/Gemini session
2. Delete .exo/reviews/pr_N.json — remove stale approval/request-changes state
3. Reset the reviewer worktree to the current PR branch tip (git fetch + reset --hard) — or dispose the worktree entirely if full recreation is preferred
4. Reset the watcher's in-memory WatchState for that PR number (clear merge_ready_notified, review_approved_at, notified_parent_approved, notified_parent_timeout) so the next reviewer spawn is seen as a fresh first observation
5. Update agent registry to mark the reviewer as inactive

Usage pattern:
  cleanup_reviewer_leaf(pr_number: 8)   // cleans up
  spawn_reviewer(pr_number: 8)           // spawns fresh — watcher sees first approval as new transition

This is the TL-facing surface for the fix in #395. The spawn_reviewer --force path should call cleanup_reviewer_leaf internally, or it can be a standalone tool the TL calls explicitly before respawn.

Haskell tool definition: haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/ (new file CleanupReviewerLeaf.hs or added to existing reviewer tools file)
Rust handler: rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs (new handler) + effect to reset WatchState in worktree_event_watcher.rs
Role: tl, root

comments.content: Reopened: tool was invoked in nemotron-port but did not close reviewer tmux panes. User had to close them manually. Tool may have returned success without actually killing the windows, or the pane identifiers were stale/mismatched. Needs investigation against the actual binary running in nemotron-port — may be a stale binary (built before the commit landed) or a logic bug in the pane kill path.

Root cause confirmed: cleanup_agent reads RoutingInfo from .exo/agents/{name}/ only. Reviewer agents are worktrees — their routing.json lives in .exo/worktrees/{name}/. cleanup_agent never checks the worktree path, finds no window_id, does nothing, returns success. Fix: in cleanup_agent, if .exo/agents/{name}/routing.json is missing or has no window_id, also try .exo/worktrees/{name}/routing.json before giving up on the window kill.

Second occurrence confirmed with review-pr-12-codex. cleanup_reviewer_leaf returned success, registry was clean, but tmux window @7 was still alive. TL had to manually run tmux kill-window -t @7 as workaround. Root cause is the same: cleanup_agent looks in .exo/agents/{name}/ for routing.json, reviewer worktrees put it in .exo/worktrees/{name}/. Fix must check both paths before giving up on the window kill.

Third occurrence with review-pr-15-codex. filesystem scan found zero entries in .exo/agents/ and .exo/worktrees/ (worktree was already cleaned up) but tmux window @4 was still alive. cleanup_reviewer_leaf returned cleaned_reviewers=[] and did nothing. Required manual tmux kill-window -t @4. Fix must add a second path: when filesystem scan returns empty, scan EXOMONAD_TMUX_SESSION windows directly for review-pr-{N}-* pattern and kill matches.
Superseded by #407. Root fix is a full rewrite to tmux window scan — patching the filesystem path is wrong since .exo/agents/ and .exo/worktrees/ no longer hold reviewer state post-#398.

issues.title: spawn_reviewer --force: stale worktree, stale review file, and no watcher state reset — force-respawn cannot unblock a stuck reviewer
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

spawn_reviewer(force=true) has three gaps that prevent it from actually recovering a stuck reviewer:

1. STALE WORKTREE: spawn_reviewer_subtree_named skips worktree creation if the path already exists (line 1604 in spawn.rs: 'unless it already exists'). The reviewer starts in a worktree that may be at a stale HEAD SHA, not the current PR branch tip. If the PR has been pushed to since the worktree was created, the reviewer reviews old code.

2. STALE REVIEW FILE: .exo/reviews/pr_N.json is NOT deleted before spawning the new reviewer. The existing approval/request-changes state is still on disk. The new reviewer either re-approves (redundant) or sees a confusing pre-existing state.

3. WATCHER STATE NOT RESET: The watcher's in-memory merge_ready_notified = true (set from the first approval cycle) is never reset. Even if the force-respawned reviewer produces a fresh approval, the watcher sees the Approved state, finds merge_ready_notified = true, and returns early. The PR stays stuck. There is no API or mechanism to reset per-PR watcher state without a full server restart.

Additionally: spawn_subtree reuses the existing tmux window for the same agent name, so from the user's perspective 'the panes look the same' — no new window appears. This is confusing operationally.

Fix:
- force=true path should: delete .exo/reviews/pr_N.json, reset worktree to current PR tip (git fetch + reset to head_sha), kill the existing tmux window, create a fresh window
- Add a watcher reset endpoint or effect: reset_pr_watch_state(pr_number) clears merge_ready_notified + review_approved_at + notified_parent_approved in the in-memory WatchState for that PR
- Expose reset_pr_watch_state as an effect called by spawn_reviewer_for_recovery so reviewer force-respawn automatically resets the watcher state

Files: rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs (spawn_reviewer_subtree_named ~L1604), rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs (WatchState, process_observations)

issues.title: Watcher: approved PR suppresses timeout escalation path — no recovery when merge_ready delivery also fails
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

In compute_pr_actions_with_context, the timeout escalation path (line ~2059) is:

  if !notified_parent_timeout && !notified_parent_approved && first_seen.elapsed() > max_wait_seconds { ... }

The notified_parent_approved guard means: once a PR has been approved, the timeout path is permanently suppressed — even if the watcher restarted and the approval was already present when it first observed the PR. If merge_ready delivery also fails (Bug #392), the PR is fully stuck: merge_ready never retries, timeout never fires, no human escalation path.

This creates a deadlock: approval suppresses timeout, broken delivery suppresses merge_ready retry, and there is no recovery path short of a human reading the watcher log.

Fix: decouple the timeout guard from notified_parent_approved. The timeout path should check whether the TL has actually been notified of a terminal event (merge_ready or stuck), not just whether an approval was locally observed. A notified_parent_merge_ready flag (checked after confirmed delivery) would be the correct gate.

Files: rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs (compute_pr_actions_with_context ~L2059)

comments.content: Fixed approved-PR timeout deadlock: stale guard now treats only merge-ready delivery, timeout escalation, or stuck state as terminal. Timeout escalation no longer checks local approval, so approved PRs can still escalate if merge_ready delivery was never confirmed. Verified with cargo test -p exomonad-core worktree_event_watcher --lib.

issues.title: Watcher: reviewer windows not disposed on restart when PR already approved (no state transition)
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

dispose_reviewers_for_pr is called only on review state transitions (process_observations line ~905). When the watcher restarts with a PR already in Approved state, pr.review_state == obs.review_state so no transition is detected, review_state_updates is empty, and dispose_reviewers_for_pr is never called. Reviewer Codex windows remain alive indefinitely at idle prompts.

Confirmed in nemotron-port: review-pr-8-codex and review-pr-9-codex both at Codex CLI idle prompt, phase=reviewer_done in KV, but tmux windows alive for 5+ hours.

Fix: in process_observations, after building watch state for an existing PR (the else branch for new PRs, or on the initial observation pass), check if review_file_seen && local_review_state == Approved and the reviewer window is still alive — if so, call dispose_reviewers_for_pr. Alternatively: call dispose on any observation where review is already Approved, gated by a disposed flag in WatchState to avoid repeated calls.

Files: rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs (process_observations ~L781, ~L905)

comments.content: Fixed watcher restart reviewer cleanup: terminal review observations now set a reviewer_disposed guard and dispose reviewer resources even without a review-state transition. Reviewer spawning is skipped when the first post-restart observation is already terminal. Verified with cargo test -p exomonad-core worktree_event_watcher --lib.

issues.title: Watcher: merge_ready_notified set before delivery confirmation — no retry on failed delivery
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

In worktree_event_watcher.rs, merge_ready_notified is set to true inside compute_pr_actions_with_context (pure logic, no I/O) before delivery is even attempted. The WasmEvent is pushed to pending_actions, then dispatched later via call_handle_event_for_role → handle_event_action → deliver_to_agent. If delivery fails (e.g. broken tmux path for Codex TL — no Enter sent), the flag is permanently committed and the watcher never retries. On every subsequent poll: merge_ready_now = !merge_ready_notified = false, notified_parent_approved = true → early return. Confirmed in nemotron-port: both PRs approved for 3+ hours, watcher polling every 60s doing nothing, TL never received MERGE READY.

Fix: move merge_ready_notified = true to after confirmed delivery in handle_event_action/deliver_release_message. Or: add a delivery-confirmed callback that sets the flag only on success, with a bounded retry window.

Files: rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs (compute_pr_actions_with_context ~L1928, deliver_release_message ~L1515)

comments.content: Fixed merge_ready_notified gating so pure watcher computation no longer marks it before async delivery. The dispatch loop now marks merge_ready_notified only after a successful event action delivery, and merge-ready notifications retry while unconfirmed. Verified with cargo test -p exomonad-core worktree_event_watcher --lib.

issues.title: Split send_message MCP tool into send_tmux_message and send_mailbox_message
issues.description:
Rename and split the send_message Haskell WASM MCP tool into two explicit tools:

send_tmux_message: always delivers via tmux STDIN injection. No mailbox, no ACP, no smart routing. The tool the TL uses to reach workers/Codex agents mid-session.

send_mailbox_message: delivers via Teams inbox (Claude-to-Claude). Hard-fails with a clear error if the mailbox protocol is not configured or has not passed e2e validation for the current session's role/runtime combination. Error: 'Mailbox protocol not available in this session: Teams inbox is not configured or has not passed e2e validation for this role/runtime combination.'

Requires a session-level capability flag for mailbox availability, set during exomonad init based on configured runtimes. send_mailbox_message checks this flag before attempting delivery — no silent fallback.

Files: haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/ (new tools), rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/events.rs (new effect handlers), session capability flag in server init.

comments.content: Implemented split message delivery: send_tmux_message uses tmux-only routing, send_mailbox_message uses Teams inbox-only routing guarded by EXOMONAD_MAILBOX_PROTOCOL_AVAILABLE. Verified cargo check, focused delivery/events tests, devswarm role-hook-tests, and e2e-test WASM build.

issues.title: Fix tmux injection for non-Claude agent runtimes (Codex/OpenCode)
issues.description:
Two bugs in the tmux delivery path that break TL→worker messaging for Codex agents:

1. File-indirect pointers: multiline messages are stored in .exo/tmp/{uuid}.txt and a [label] @path pointer is injected. Only Claude Code has a hook to expand these. Codex/OpenCode receive a useless pointer string. Fix: skip file-indirect for non-Claude runtimes, always inject full content inline.

2. No Enter after paste: tmux paste-buffer puts text in the input field but never submits it. Fix: inject_input gains a 'submit: bool' flag — when true, sends 'tmux send-keys Enter' after paste. send_tmux_message passes submit=true for non-Claude runtimes.

Additional cleanup:
- Add 'codex' to routing candidates suffix list in deliver_via_tmux (currently only has gemini/claude/shoal/opencode)
- Rename DeliveryMethod::AgentInbox → DeliveryMethod::Tmux (misleading: this variant is returned for tmux delivery, not mailbox delivery)

Files: rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_events.rs, rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs, rust/exomonad-core/src/services/delivery.rs

comments.content: Implemented runtime-aware tmux injection: queued tmux messages now carry InjectionOptions, non-Claude runtimes use inline submitted payloads, TmuxIpc has submit flag support, Codex routing suffix is included, and tmux delivery reports tmux_stdin instead of agent_inbox. Verified cargo check -p exomonad-core and cargo test -p exomonad-core tmux.

issues.title: Split send_message into send_tmux_message and send_mailbox_message
issues.description:
The current send_message MCP tool has opaque smart-routing that hides which delivery method is actually used. DeliveryResult::Tmux maps to DeliveryMethod::AgentInbox (misleading label), and the tool silently falls through delivery methods without clear caller control.

Split into two explicit tools in Haskell WASM:
- send_tmux_message: always injects directly via tmux STDIN (the current fallback path). Reliable for workers/Codex agents mid-session. No mailbox, no ACP.
- send_mailbox_message: Teams inbox delivery path (currently partially implemented — Claude-only via write_to_inbox). For when the mailbox mechanism is fully wired.

Also fix the misleading DeliveryResult::Tmux -> DeliveryMethod::AgentInbox mapping — rename AgentInbox to Tmux in the DeliveryMethod enum.

Routing candidates in deliver_via_tmux also missing 'codex' suffix (only has gemini/claude/shoal/opencode) — fix that too.

comments.content:
Additional requirement: send_mailbox_message must guard against unconfigured/untested mailbox.

If the mailbox protocol is not configured or has not passed e2e tests between all roles and their respective agent runtimes in the current exomonad session, send_mailbox_message should return an explicit error:
  'Mailbox protocol not available in this session: Teams inbox is not configured or has not passed e2e validation for this role/runtime combination.'

No silent fallback to tmux. No partial delivery. Hard fail with a clear message.

This means the server needs a session-level capability flag for mailbox availability — set during init based on configured runtimes and verified via the e2e messaging test. send_mailbox_message checks the flag before attempting delivery.

Root cause analysis complete.

The asymmetry: notify_parent (worker→TL) works because TL is Claude → Teams inbox path. send_message (TL→Codex worker) falls to tmux → broken.

Two concrete bugs in the tmux path for Codex agents:

1. File-indirect pointers: multiline messages are stored in .exo/tmp/{uuid}.txt and a [label] @path pointer is injected. Codex has no hook to expand @file pointers — that's Claude Code-only. Codex receives a useless pointer string instead of content.

2. No Enter after paste: tmux paste-buffer puts text into Codex's input field but never sends a keystroke to submit it. Text sits in the prompt unsubmitted. Affects single-line messages too.

Fix for send_tmux_message targeting Codex workers:
- Skip file-indirect: always inject full content inline (truncate if needed, or chunk)
- Send explicit Enter keystroke after paste-buffer (tmux send-keys Enter)
- This needs to be conditioned on agent_type == Codex (or a broader 'needs_enter' flag per runtime)

Alternatively: inject_input gains a 'submit' boolean — when true, sends Enter after paste. send_tmux_message passes submit=true for non-Claude runtimes.
Split into #390 (Rust tmux injection fix) and #391 (Haskell WASM tool rename/split). Closing this umbrella issue.

issues.title: Fix CI workflow to not fetch actions from internet — use inline git clone instead of actions/checkout
issues.description:
## Problem

docker-compose.yml line 19 sets:

  FORGEJO__actions__DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL=https://code.forgejo.org

This causes the forgejo-runner to fetch action definitions (actions/checkout@v4, etc.) from the public internet on every CI run. In a fully local setup this either fails (no network access from container) or is unreliable. All 25 existing CI runs show status=failure, and the runner logs confirm it is contacting code.forgejo.org for each task.

## Fix Part 1: Update workflow to avoid external action fetch

File: /home/goya/rust-workspace/nemotron-port/.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml

Replace the 'uses: actions/checkout@v4' step with an inline git clone:

Current:
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        fetch-depth: 1
        submodules: false
    - name: Install pkg-config
      run: apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq pkg-config
    - name: test
      run: cargo test --lib

Replace with:
  steps:
    - name: checkout
      run: |
        git clone --depth 1 http://172.17.0.1:3000/exomonad/nemotron-port.git .
        git checkout ${{ github.sha }}
    - name: Install pkg-config and openssl
      run: apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq pkg-config libssl-dev
    - name: test
      run: cargo test --lib

Note: 172.17.0.1 is the Docker bridge gateway — reachable from inside the runner container to the host's Forgejo instance. Alternatively use the forgejo service name if the runner container is on the same Docker network.

Also add libssl-dev to the apt-get step — cargo build of many Rust crates requires it and its absence causes link failures.

## Fix Part 2: Update DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL in docker-compose.yml

File: /home/goya/agent-workspace/exomonad/forgejo/docker-compose.yml line 19

Change:
  - FORGEJO__actions__DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL=https://code.forgejo.org

To:
  - FORGEJO__actions__DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL=http://localhost:3000

This prevents Forgejo from directing the runner to code.forgejo.org for any remaining 'uses:' steps. Combined with Part 1 (no 'uses:' steps at all), the CI pipeline becomes fully offline.

## Apply to exomonad new scaffold too

The exomonad new command generates a .github/workflows/ci.yml or .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml scaffold for new projects (rust/exomonad/src/new.rs). That scaffold should also use the inline git clone pattern instead of actions/checkout@v4 so new projects work offline by default.

Search for the scaffold template in new.rs and update accordingly.

## After fix

1. docker compose -f forgejo/docker-compose.yml up -d (to pick up DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL change)
2. Commit the updated ci.yml to nemotron-port master and all open PR branches
3. Push — should trigger new CI runs that pass without any internet access
4. Verify runner log no longer shows code.forgejo.org

comments.content: Implemented in exomonad commit 74265d4b and nemotron-port commit d4702f8. Verified cargo test -p exomonad scaffolds_gitea_ci_placeholder_workflow; pushed nemotron-port master to Forgejo.

issues.title: Fix watcher Forgejo Actions API field name mismatch — commit_sha/prettyref vs head_sha/head_branch
issues.description:
## Problem

The watcher's actions_status_for_head function in rust/exomonad-core/src/services/forgejo.rs (line ~241) matches runs using:

    run.head_sha.as_deref() == Some(head_sha)
        && run.head_branch.as_deref() == Some(branch.as_str())

But the Forgejo Actions API (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs) returns these fields with different names. Inspecting the actual response:

  keys: ['id', 'title', 'repository', 'workflow_id', 'index_in_repo', 'trigger_user',
         'ScheduleID', 'prettyref', 'is_ref_deleted', 'commit_sha', 'is_fork_pull_request',
         'need_approval', 'approved_by', 'event', 'event_payload', ...]

The actual field names are:
- commit_sha  (not head_sha)
- prettyref   (not head_branch) — this is the full ref string e.g. 'refs/heads/master.issue-22-...'

The WorkflowRunResponse struct in forgejo.rs deserializes head_sha and head_branch but the API sends commit_sha and prettyref. Both deserialize as None/empty, so no run ever matches → CIStatus::Unknown is always returned → watcher treats CI as neutral → [MERGE READY] never fires based on CI state.

## Evidence

- 25 CI runs exist for exomonad/nemotron-port, all showing status=failure
- cargo test --lib passes locally (39 tests, 0 failed) — the code is correct
- Watcher always reports neutral/unknown because it cannot match any run to a PR head SHA

## Fix

In rust/exomonad-core/src/services/forgejo.rs, update WorkflowRunResponse struct (~line 97):

Current:
  struct WorkflowRunResponse {
      head_sha: Option<String>,
      head_branch: Option<String>,
      status: Option<String>,
      conclusion: Option<String>,
  }

Change to (with serde rename):
  struct WorkflowRunResponse {
      #[serde(rename = "commit_sha")]
      head_sha: Option<String>,
      #[serde(rename = "prettyref")]
      head_branch_ref: Option<String>,
      status: Option<String>,
      conclusion: Option<String>,
  }

Then update the matching logic in actions_status_for_head (~line 241):

  let Some(run) = runs.workflow_runs.into_iter().find(|run| {
      let sha_matches = run.head_sha.as_deref() == Some(head_sha);
      // prettyref is a full git ref like 'refs/heads/branch-name', strip prefix
      let branch_matches = run.head_branch_ref.as_deref()
          .map(|r| r.trim_start_matches("refs/heads/"))
          == Some(branch.as_str());
      sha_matches && branch_matches
  }) else {
      return Ok(CIStatus::Unknown);
  };

Also add a debug log when no match is found to make future debugging easier:
  tracing::debug!(
      head_sha,
      branch = %branch,
      total_runs = runs.workflow_runs.len(),
      "[Forgejo] No Actions run matched branch+SHA — CI status unknown"
  );

## Also fix: CI failures are infra-related, not code

The current CI runs fail because actions/checkout@v4 is fetched from code.forgejo.org
which may be unreachable from inside the runner container, or the container image
(rust:slim) lacks the required toolchain dependencies.

Consider switching the workflow to use a local action or a self-contained step:
- Replace 'uses: actions/checkout@v4' with a direct git clone step (no external fetch)
- Or mirror the action locally

This is tracked separately from the field name fix.

## Verify

After fix:
1. Push a commit to a PR branch
2. Wait for watcher poll cycle
3. watcher.log should show 'ci=Success' or 'ci=Failure' (not 'ci=Unknown')
4. If CI passes: watcher fires [MERGE READY] correctly

issues.title: Add spawn_reviewer MCP tool so TL can trigger reviews on demand without clearing watcher state
issues.description:
## Problem

Reviewer spawning is entirely watcher-driven. When a TL needs to trigger a fresh review — after original reviewer agents are gone, after stale review files are cleared, or after a PR is updated — there is no MCP tool to do it. The only current path is:

1. Manually delete .exo/reviews/pr_N.json files
2. Manually reset .exo/watcher-state.json
3. Wait up to 60s for the watcher poll cycle to detect the gap and spawn a reviewer

This is fragile: it requires filesystem access from outside the agent, it races with the watcher's state model, and it is not something a TL agent can do itself via MCP tools.

## Solution

Expose a spawn_reviewer MCP tool to TL and root roles that triggers an immediate reviewer spawn for a specific PR number, bypassing the watcher poll cycle.

## Tool spec

Name: spawn_reviewer
Role: root, tl
Location: haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/SpawnReviewer.hs

Input:
- pr_number: Int — the PR to review
- force: Bool (default false) — spawn even if a reviewer is already registered for this PR in the watcher state

Output:
- reviewer_name: Text — the spawned reviewer agent slug
- already_active: Bool — true if a reviewer was already running and force=false prevented a duplicate spawn

## Rust effect: agent.spawn_reviewer

Add to rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs:

Effect: agent.spawn_reviewer
Input: { pr_number: u64, force: bool }

Implementation:
1. Read the PR from Forgejo (get_pull_request) to verify it is open
2. Check if a reviewer agent for this PR is already alive (check .exo/agents/review-pr-{N}-* routing, verify window alive). If alive and force=false, return already_active=true without spawning.
3. If force=true or no live reviewer: clear .exo/reviews/pr_{N}.json if it exists, clear the PR entry from .exo/watcher-state.json
4. Call the existing AgentControlService reviewer spawning logic (same path the watcher uses internally — ReviewerSpawner trait)
5. Return the reviewer agent name

## Why clearing the review artifacts is the right approach

The watcher's state model for a PR is:
- review_file_seen=true (local .exo/reviews/pr_N.json exists) → treat as reviewed, no new reviewer needed
- review_file_seen=false + Forgejo has no reviews → needs reviewer → spawn

spawn_reviewer must clear the local review file before spawning so the watcher does not immediately re-detect the PR as already-reviewed and kill the new reviewer's work. The watcher state rounds counter should also be reset to 0 for the PR so the new review round is counted fresh.

## Alternative considered: watcher-only approach

The watcher could be smarter about detecting dead reviewer agents and re-spawning. But that only helps when the reviewer dies mid-review. The spawn_reviewer tool is needed for the deliberate case: 'the review is done, I disagree with it, spawn a second reviewer' or 'the original reviewer agents are gone, I need fresh eyes.'

## Verify

1. File a PR. Wait for watcher to spawn reviewer. Let reviewer complete.
2. Call spawn_reviewer pr_number=N — should spawn a fresh reviewer
3. Call spawn_reviewer pr_number=N again immediately — should return already_active=true (reviewer still running)
4. Call spawn_reviewer pr_number=N force=true — should spawn a second reviewer despite one running

Add cleanup_orphan MCP tool and fix dispose_leaf force=true to actually clean up filesystem
issues.description:
## Problem

Two related gaps:

### Gap 1: dispose_leaf force=true does nothing

In haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/DisposeLeaf.hs (~line 74):

    Nothing
      | dlaForce args ->
          pure $ Right $ object ["success" .= True, "agent" .= dlaName args, ...]
      | otherwise -> pure $ Left "Could not infer a Chainlink issue id..."

When force=true and no issue ID can be inferred, it returns success immediately without touching anything. The .exo/agents/ directory and the worktree both remain. This is the ORPHAN case — agents that crashed, were manually killed, or were spawned without a Chainlink issue.

### Gap 2: No tool for direct orphan cleanup

When session_status reports an ORPHAN (window_alive=false, no open issue), the TL has no tool to remove the stale .exo/agents/ entry and worktree. dispose_leaf won't work. The orphan reconciler will eventually clean it up on the next session timeout cycle, but that can be 30+ minutes away and the stale entry blocks spawn_worker in the meantime (see issue #376).

## Solution

### Part 1: Fix dispose_leaf force=true

In DisposeLeaf.hs, change the force=true + no-issue-id path to yield an agent.dispose_orphan effect instead of returning success silently:

    Nothing
      | dlaForce args ->
          do
            result <- send (DisposeOrphan (dlaName args))
            case result of
              Left err -> pure $ Left err
              Right () -> pure $ Right $ object ["success" .= True, "agent" .= dlaName args, "force" .= True]
      | otherwise -> pure $ Left "..."

Add DisposeOrphan to the agent effects in the Haskell effects module.

### Part 2: Add cleanup_orphan MCP tool

New tool: cleanup_orphan
Role: root, tl
Location: haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/CleanupOrphan.hs

Input:
- name: Text — agent slug to clean up (e.g. "inspect-forgejo-prs-codex")
- dry_run: Bool (default false) — if true, report what would be removed without removing it

Behavior:
1. Check window_alive for the agent (via session.list_agents effect from #375, or a simpler session.check_agent_alive effect)
2. REFUSE if window_alive=true — never clean up a live agent. Return error: "Agent {name} window is still alive. Use dispose_leaf to close it gracefully."
3. If window_alive=false (or routing.json missing): call agent.dispose_orphan effect
4. Return what was cleaned up: worktree path removed, agent dir removed

### Part 3: Rust effect agent.dispose_orphan

Add to rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs (or agent_resources handler):

Effect: agent.dispose_orphan
Input proto: { agent_slug: string }
Output proto: { removed_worktree: bool, removed_agent_dir: bool }

Implementation:
1. Verify the agent's window/pane is NOT alive (same tmux check as session_status). If alive, return error — refuse to clean up a live agent.
2. Call dispose_agent_resources(project_dir, git_wt, agent_slug).await
3. Return what was removed

The liveness check inside the Rust handler is the safety gate — even if the Haskell caller skips the check, the Rust side verifies.

## Proto additions needed

Add to proto/effects/agent.proto and rust/exomonad-proto/proto/effects/agent.proto:

message DisposeOrphanRequest {
  string agent_slug = 1;
}

message DisposeOrphanResponse {
  bool removed_worktree = 1;
  bool removed_agent_dir = 2;
  string message = 3;
}

## Safety invariant

cleanup_orphan and dispose_leaf force=true must BOTH refuse to act if the agent's tmux window/pane is currently alive. This is enforced at the Rust effect handler level, not just the Haskell tool level. An agent must be verifiably dead before its resources are removed.

## Verify

1. Spawn a worker, kill its pane manually
2. session_status shows it as ORPHAN
3. cleanup_orphan removes .exo/agents/{slug} and .exo/worktrees/{slug}
4. spawn_worker unblocked immediately after
5. cleanup_orphan dry_run=true reports what would be removed without removing
6. cleanup_orphan on a live agent returns an error, removes nothing

issues.title: spawn_worker sequential guard gets stuck when previous worker pane closes without cleanup
issues.description:
## Symptom

spawn_worker is blocked with:

  BLOCKED: workers are sequential per CLAUDE.md. Active worker in this TL worktree: `inspect-forgejo-prs-codex` (spawned 3m ago).

Even though the previous worker's pane is already closed/gone. The sequential guard checks the registry for an active worker but does not verify whether that worker's tmux pane is actually alive.

## Root cause

When a worker pane closes (agent exits normally, window killed manually, or session timeout), the active worker registration in .exo/agents/{slug}/ is not cleaned up. The sequential guard in spawn_worker reads the registry and sees an active worker slug, finds a spawned_at timestamp, and blocks — without checking whether the window/pane still exists.

The orphan reconciler (issue #372) eventually cleans up timed-out agents, but:
1. The reconciler only runs every 60s
2. Workers that exit early (before the timeout limit) are never cleaned up by the reconciler
3. A worker that finishes in 2 minutes leaves a stale registry entry for up to 30 minutes (default max_reviewer_session_seconds)

## Where to fix

### Option A: spawn_worker guard does liveness check before blocking

In the Rust handler for spawn_worker (rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs or the spawn path), when the sequential guard finds an active worker:
1. Read the worker's routing.json for its window_id/pane_id
2. Check if that window/pane is actually alive in the current tmux session
3. If NOT alive: log warn, clean up the stale registry entry, allow the spawn to proceed
4. If alive: block as normal with the existing error message

This is the most defensive fix — the guard self-heals when it detects a dead worker.

### Option B: worker stop hook clears the registry

When a worker agent's session ends (Stop hook fires), call an exomonad effect that removes the active worker registration from the parent TL's worktree state. This requires the Stop hook to know the parent identity (EXOMONAD_SESSION_ID env var is the parent's birth branch).

Option A is simpler and handles cases where the Stop hook doesn't fire (crash, manual kill).

## Files to check

- rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/agent.rs — spawn_worker handler, look for active worker check
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/ — worker spawning logic
- Look for the sequential guard: grep for 'sequential' or 'active_worker' or 'BLOCKED'

## What 'active worker' state looks like on disk

Check .exo/agents/{tl-slug}/ for a file tracking the active worker. May be:
- active_worker file containing the worker slug
- A lock file
- Part of routing.json or a separate state file

## Verify

1. Spawn a worker, let it finish or kill its pane manually
2. Immediately try spawn_worker again — should succeed, not block
3. The stale worker's .exo/agents/ entry should be cleaned up

issues.title: Add session_status MCP tool so TL can see all live tmux windows cross-referenced with agent registry
issues.description:
## Problem

The TL has no visibility into what tmux windows are currently open. It only learns about agents when they call notify_parent. A stale agent whose window is gone but whose registry entry persists is invisible to the TL — it cannot know to call dispose_leaf or re-assign the issue.

The orphan reconciler (issue #372) now sends [STALE REGISTRY: agent] notifications, but only after the session timeout fires. The TL needs an on-demand tool to inspect current session state proactively.

## Tool spec

Name: session_status
Role: root, tl
Location: haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/SessionStatus.hs

## Tool input

No required fields. Optional:
- include_dead: bool (default false) — include agents whose windows are confirmed gone

## Tool output

Returns a structured list of agents with fields:
- name: agent slug (e.g. issue-22-streaming-compare-v2-codex)
- role: dev | reviewer | worker | tl
- issue: chainlink issue id if known (from active_issue file)
- window_id or pane_id: from routing.json
- window_alive: bool — whether the tmux window/pane actually exists right now
- age_mins: how many minutes since spawned_at
- birth_branch: the agent's birth branch

## Rust effect needed

Add a new effect: session.list_agents

Handler in rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/session.rs (or a new session_status.rs):

1. Read all entries from .exo/agents/ directory
2. For each agent directory, read:
   - routing.json (window_id or pane_id)
   - spawned_at (timestamp)
   - active_issue (optional)
   - .birth_branch
3. For each window_id/pane_id, check if it actually exists in the current tmux session:
   tmux list-windows -t {session} -F '#{window_id}' to get live window IDs
   tmux list-panes -t {session} -a -F '#{pane_id}' to get live pane IDs
4. Cross-reference: window_alive = routing window_id is in the live set
5. Return a proto list of AgentStatus entries

## Proto type needed

Add to proto/effects/session.proto (and rust/exomonad-proto/proto/effects/session.proto):

message AgentStatus {
  string name = 1;
  string role = 2;
  string issue = 3;
  string window_id = 4;
  string pane_id = 5;
  bool window_alive = 6;
  uint64 age_mins = 7;
  string birth_branch = 8;
}

message ListAgentsRequest {
  bool include_dead = 1;
}

message ListAgentsResponse {
  repeated AgentStatus agents = 1;
}

## Haskell tool implementation

The tool calls session.list_agents effect, formats the response as a readable table for the TL:

  AGENT                               ROLE      ISSUE  WINDOW   ALIVE  AGE
  issue-22-streaming-compare-v2-codex dev       22     @6       yes    47m
  review-pr-1-codex                   reviewer  -      @7       yes    12m
  retrigger-pr-ci-41-43-codex         worker    -      %4       NO     38m

Dead agents (window_alive=false) are shown with a note suggesting dispose_leaf or manual cleanup.

## Why this is important

1. TL can call session_status at any time to get a full picture
2. After receiving [STALE REGISTRY: agent] from the reconciler, TL can call session_status to confirm the state before acting
3. Makes the TL's decision-making grounded in actual session state rather than stale notifications

## Verify

In an active session with mixed live/dead agents:
- session_status returns all agents
- window_alive correctly reflects actual tmux state
- Dead agents are flagged clearly
- Age is computed correctly from spawned_at

comments.content:
Additional context after reading DisposeLeaf.hs:

dispose_leaf does NOT kill tmux windows. It only closes the Chainlink issue. Worktree deletion happens at the next orphan reconciler tick (~60s). The tmux window keeps running.

Two risks the session_status tool must guard against:
1. TL calls dispose_leaf on a live agent (window_alive=true) — premature issue close + eventual worktree deletion while agent is still running. session_status should surface window_alive so TL knows not to dispose a live agent.
2. force=true orphans (no issue ID) — dispose_leaf returns success but does nothing to clean up .exo/agents/ or the worktree. Need a separate cleanup path for these.

The session_status output should clearly distinguish:
- LIVE: window_alive=true, has issue — normal running agent, do not dispose
- FINISHING: window_alive=false, has open issue — agent exited, safe to dispose_leaf
- ORPHAN: window_alive=false, no issue or issue already closed — stale registry entry, needs direct filesystem cleanup (dispose_agent_resources by slug), not dispose_leaf

Consider adding a cleanup_orphan tool or extending dispose_leaf force=true to actually call dispose_agent_resources when no issue is found.

issues.title: Auto-configure git remote to HTTP token auth during exomonad init when Forgejo is configured
issues.description:
## File to modify

rust/exomonad/src/init.rs

## Where to add

After the root agent birth branch is written (~line 470) and before the tmux session creation (~line 701). This is a pure git config operation — no tmux dependency.

## Logic

Add a function configure_forgejo_remote(cwd: &Path, forgejo_url: &str, forgejo_token: &str) -> Result<()>:

1. Run: git -C cwd remote get-url origin
   - If this fails (no remote named origin), log a warn and return Ok(()) — non-fatal.

2. Parse the host + path from the existing remote URL using the same parse_github_url logic already in crate::services::repo (supports both SSH git@host:owner/repo.git and HTTPS https://host/owner/repo.git).

3. Parse the host from forgejo_url (strip scheme, trailing slash, port).

4. If the remote host does not match the Forgejo host, log info and return — do not clobber a remote pointing at a different host.

5. Construct the new URL:
   - Parse owner/repo from the existing remote
   - Construct: {forgejo_url_base}/{owner}/{repo}.git
   - Inject token: replace scheme://host with scheme://forgejo_pat:{token}@host
   - Example: http://localhost:3000/exomonad/nemotron-port.git
     becomes: http://forgejo_pat:<token>@localhost:3000/exomonad/nemotron-port.git

6. If the existing remote URL already contains the token (idempotent check): log debug and return.

7. Run: git -C cwd remote set-url origin <new_url>

8. Log: info!(old_url = %old, new_url = %new_url_redacted, "Configured git remote to use Forgejo HTTP token auth")
   IMPORTANT: redact the token in the log line — log the URL with <token> in place of the actual token value.

## Call site in run()

In run(), after writing root agent birth branch:

    if let (Some(forgejo_url), Some(forgejo_token)) = (
        config.forgejo_url.as_deref(),
        config.forgejo_token.as_deref(),
    ) {
        if let Err(e) = configure_forgejo_remote(&cwd, forgejo_url, forgejo_token) {
            warn!(error = %e, "Failed to auto-configure Forgejo remote URL (non-fatal)");
        }
    }

## Idempotent

Running exomonad init multiple times must not break anything. If the remote is already using the token URL, detect this (URL contains the token or already uses http://*@host form) and skip silently.

## Security note

Add a comment in the code:
// Token is embedded in the URL and visible in local-knot	git@local-tangled:repositories/owner/exomonad.git (fetch)
local-knot	git@local-tangled:repositories/owner/exomonad.git (push)
origin	git@github.com:nanonite/exomonad.git (fetch)
origin	git@github.com:nanonite/exomonad.git (push)
upstream	https://github.com/tidepool-heavy-industries/exomonad.git (fetch)
upstream	https://github.com/tidepool-heavy-industries/exomonad.git (push) and .git/config.
// Acceptable for local Forgejo instances. Do not use for public hosts.

## Verify

1. Start with SSH remote: git remote set-url origin git@localhost:2222/exomonad/nemotron-port.git
2. Run exomonad init
3. git remote -v should show the HTTP token URL
4. Run exomonad init again (idempotent) — should not duplicate or corrupt the URL
5. git fetch origin && git push origin HEAD — no prompts

issues.title: Configure git remote to use Forgejo HTTP token auth so all agents can push/fetch without prompts
issues.description:
## Problem

ssh-agent is not inherited by tmux windows created after the agent starts, nor by git worktrees spawned by fork_wave. This means every git push from a dev-leaf or reviewer agent either hangs waiting for an SSH passphrase or fails silently.

The only solution that works uniformly across all agents (main repo, worktrees, reviewer worktrees) is to use HTTP with the token embedded in the remote URL, since:
- git worktrees share .git/config with the parent repo, so the remote URL is inherited automatically
- No per-process environment setup required
- Works in any tmux window, any worktree, any agent type

## Solution

### Part 1: Set the remote URL in the nemotron-port repo

Manually or via script:

  git remote set-url origin http://forgejo_pat:<token>@localhost:3000/exomonad/nemotron-port.git

Replace <token> with the value of forgejo_token from .exo/config.toml. Verify with:

  git remote -v
  git fetch origin   # should succeed with no prompts
  git push origin HEAD  # should succeed with no prompts

### Part 2: Verify git worktrees inherit the URL

After setting the remote on the main repo:
  1. Check an existing worktree: cd .exo/worktrees/<any-leaf>; git remote -v
     Should show the same token URL, not the old SSH URL.
  2. git fetch origin from within the worktree should succeed without prompts.
  3. git push origin HEAD from within the worktree should succeed without prompts.

If a worktree has its own remote override (unlikely but possible with git worktree -b), check git -C <worktree> config remote.origin.url.

### Part 3: Verify reviewer agents can pull PR branches

Reviewer worktrees are created at .exo/worktrees/review-pr-N-codex. They do:
  git fetch origin <pr-branch>
  git checkout <pr-branch>
to get the PR content. With the token URL set on the main repo, worktrees inherit it, so this should work. Confirm by checking a reviewer pane after a PR is created.

### Part 4 (optional): Have exomonad init auto-configure the remote URL

If forgejo_url and forgejo_token are both set in .exo/config.toml, exomonad init could automatically rewrite the git remote URL to use token auth. This would be idempotent and remove the manual step for new projects.

Location: rust/exomonad/src/init.rs, after the tmux session is created (or before — this is a git config change, not tmux-dependent).

Logic:
  1. If config.forgejo_url and config.forgejo_token are both Some:
  2. Run: git remote get-url origin
  3. If the URL is SSH (starts with git@ or ssh://) or is an HTTP URL without a token:
  4. Parse the host/path from forgejo_url
  5. Construct: http://{token}@{forgejo_host}/{path}.git
  6. Run: git remote set-url origin <new_url>
  7. Log: info!("Configured git remote to use Forgejo HTTP token auth")

This should only rewrite if the current remote URL is for the same host as forgejo_url (avoid clobbering if the repo has a different remote).

## Security note

The token appears in git remote -v output and in .git/config. This is acceptable for local Forgejo instances. For public hosts, use a git credential helper instead. Document this in the change.

## Verify

After Part 1:
  git push origin HEAD   # no prompts
After Part 2-3:
  cd .exo/worktrees/<leaf>; git fetch origin   # no prompts
  Reviewer agent completes a review cycle end-to-end without SSH prompt

comments.content: Closed #374 with auto-configure support in exomonad init. Did not rewrite this workspace's origin because it points at git@github.com:nanonite/exomonad.git, not the configured local Forgejo host; the new init logic intentionally skips non-Forgejo origins to avoid clobbering unrelated remotes.

Implemented in commit 7897a7a0. Verified cargo test -p exomonad forgejo_token_remote_url_ignores_empty_token; verified nemotron-port git fetch origin and git push origin HEAD over authenticated Forgejo HTTP remote.

issues.title: Fix orphan reconciler: stop retrying dead agents and notify TL of stale registry entries
issues.description:
## Problem

The orphan reconciler (reconcile_session_timeouts in rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs) produces this log spam every 60 seconds indefinitely:

  Session timeout: killing agent agent=retrigger-pr-ci-41-43-codex age_secs=2182
  can't find window: %4
  kill-pane returned non-zero agent=retrigger-pr-ci-41-43-codex

Two bugs:
1. After a kill attempt (whether the window was alive or already gone), the agent's routing info is never cleaned up. So the next tick finds the same agent, same age (still > limit), and tries again — forever.
2. notify_tl_of_timeout is always called, even when the window was already gone. The TL gets [TIMED OUT: agent] for agents it may have never seen alive in this session.

## Files to modify

rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs

## Change 1: kill_agent_window returns bool

Change signature from:
  async fn kill_agent_window(session: &str, agent_dir: &Path, slug: &str)
to:
  async fn kill_agent_window(session: &str, agent_dir: &Path, slug: &str) -> bool

Return true if we successfully killed a live window/pane. Return false if:
- routing.json could not be read (no routing info — agent may never have had a window)
- kill-window or kill-pane returned non-zero (window/pane already gone)

## Change 2: clean up routing.json after kill attempt

In reconcile_session_timeouts, after kill_agent_window returns, remove routing.json so the next reconciler tick skips this agent:

  let was_alive = kill_agent_window(session, &agent_dir, &slug).await;
  // Remove routing.json so the reconciler doesn't retry this agent next tick
  let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(agent_dir.join("routing.json")).await;
  notify_tl_about_agent(project_dir, session, &slug, &active_issue, limit_mins, was_alive).await;

## Change 3: differentiated TL notification

Rename notify_tl_of_timeout to notify_tl_about_agent and add was_alive: bool parameter:

  async fn notify_tl_about_agent(
      project_dir: &Path,
      session: &str,
      slug: &str,
      active_issue: &Option<String>,
      limit_mins: u64,
      was_alive: bool,
  )

Message when was_alive = true (we killed a running agent):
  [TIMED OUT: {slug}] Exceeded {limit_mins}min session limit — killed.{issue_hint}

Message when was_alive = false (window was already gone, stale registry):
  [STALE REGISTRY: {slug}] Agent window was already gone — registry entry cleaned up.{issue_hint}

The issue_hint for stale entries: if active_issue is Some, suggest the TL check the issue status: " Issue #{id} — verify status with chainlink show {id} and re-spec or close if done."

## Context for reviewer

The TL already receives [TIMED OUT] messages. The new [STALE REGISTRY] message is informational — tells the TL an agent exited without the normal session teardown path (e.g. agent crashed, window closed manually). No action is strictly required from the TL, but it can use the info to close or re-assign the issue.

## Verify

cargo test -p exomonad-core orphan_reconciler
After fix: run exomonad init and let an agent time out. Confirm the server log shows the kill attempt exactly once, not every 60 seconds.
