Register ForgejoAsGitHubHandler in groups.rs when GitHub client is absent
Create ForgejoAsGitHubHandler in forgejo_as_github.rs
issues.description:
## File to create

rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/forgejo_as_github.rs

## Struct

pub struct ForgejoAsGitHubHandler<C> { ctx: Arc<C> }

where C: HasForgejoClient + HasProjectDir + Send + Sync + 'static

## EffectHandler impl

- namespace() -> "github"
- handle() dispatches on effect_type:
  - "github.get_pull_request" -> handle_get_pull_request
  - "github.list_pull_requests" -> handle_list_pull_requests
  - "github.create_pull_request" -> handle_create_pull_request
  - "github.get_pull_request_review_comments" -> return empty GetPullRequestReviewCommentsResponse
  - "github.list_issues" -> return empty ListIssuesResponse
  - "github.get_issue" -> return GetIssueResponse { issue: None, comments: vec![] }
  - _ -> EffectError::not_found(format!("github/{effect_type}: not supported via Forgejo"))

## resolve_owner_repo helper

If owner_str and repo_str are non-empty, use them directly. Otherwise call crate::services::repo::get_repo_info(self.ctx.project_dir()).await to get owner/repo from the git remote. This handles the case where WASM passes empty owner/repo proto fields.

## handle_get_pull_request

1. Decode GetPullRequestRequest from payload (prost::Message)
2. Get forgejo client from self.ctx.forgejo_client().ok_or(not_found)
3. Call resolve_owner_repo(&req.owner, &req.repo)
4. let pr_number = PRNumber::new(req.number as u64)
5. Call forgejo.get_pull_request(&owner, &repo, pr_number).await
6. Convert ForgejoPullRequest to proto PullRequest via forgejo_pr_to_proto()
7. Return GetPullRequestResponse { pull_request: Some(proto_pr), reviews: vec![] }.encode_to_vec()

## handle_list_pull_requests

1. Decode ListPullRequestsRequest
2. Call forgejo.list_open_pull_requests(&owner, &repo).await
3. Map each ForgejoPullRequest through forgejo_pr_to_proto
4. Return ListPullRequestsResponse { pull_requests }

## handle_create_pull_request

1. Decode CreatePullRequestRequest
2. Parse head and base as BranchName (default base to "main" if empty)
3. Call forgejo.create_pull_request(&owner, &repo, &req.title, &req.body, &base, &head).await
4. Return CreatePullRequestResponse { pull_request: Some(proto), url: pr.url }

## forgejo_pr_to_proto free fn

Converts ForgejoPullRequest -> proto PullRequest:
- state = if pr.state == "closed" || pr.merged { IssueState::Closed } else { IssueState::Open }
- author: None (ForgejoPullRequest has no author field)
- head_sha: pr.head_sha.unwrap_or_default()
- All other fields map directly

## Imports needed

use crate::domain::{GithubOwner, GithubRepo, PRNumber};
use crate::effects::{EffectContext, EffectError, EffectHandler, EffectResult};
use crate::services::forgejo::ForgejoPullRequest;
use crate::services::{HasForgejoClient, HasProjectDir};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use exomonad_proto::effects::github::{
    CreatePullRequestRequest, CreatePullRequestResponse,
    GetIssueRequest, GetIssueResponse,
    GetPullRequestRequest, GetPullRequestResponse,
    GetPullRequestReviewCommentsRequest, GetPullRequestReviewCommentsResponse,
    IssueState, ListIssuesRequest, ListIssuesResponse,
    ListPullRequestsRequest, ListPullRequestsResponse, PullRequest,
};
use prost::Message;
use std::sync::Arc;

## Tests (in mod tests)

1. forgejo_open_pr_maps_to_open_state — creates ForgejoPullRequest with state="open", merged=false, asserts proto state == IssueState::Open, head_sha maps correctly
2. forgejo_merged_pr_maps_to_closed_state — state="closed", merged=true, head_sha=None, asserts proto state == IssueState::Closed, head_sha==""

## Verify

issues.title: Route github.* effects to Forgejo when GitHub client is not configured
issues.description:
## Problem

The Haskell WASM merge_pr tool calls github.get_pull_request for a self-merge check. In Forgejo-only deployments (no GitHub client configured), the github namespace handler is never registered, causing:

  [wasm] MergePR: Failed to fetch PR #16 for self-merge check — handler/github unavailable: hosted PR effect handler is not registered

## Root cause

In rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/groups.rs (git_handlers fn, ~line 43), GitHubHandler is only registered when services.github_client is Some. When only Forgejo is configured, the github namespace has no handler at all.

## Solution

Create a ForgejoAsGitHubHandler that implements EffectHandler for namespace "github" by routing calls to the Forgejo API. Register it in git_handlers when github_client is None but forgejo_client is Some.

## Files to change

1. NEW: rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/forgejo_as_github.rs
2. MODIFY: rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/mod.rs — add pub mod forgejo_as_github; pub use forgejo_as_github::ForgejoAsGitHubHandler;
3. MODIFY: rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/groups.rs — register ForgejoAsGitHubHandler in git_handlers when github is absent

## Architecture note

All github.* effect calls should route to Forgejo in a Forgejo-only deployment. The github.* and forgejo flow are not the same — Forgejo has its own API. The handler translates github proto types into Forgejo API calls and converts the response back to GitHub proto format, so existing WASM tools work without modification.

Watcher-internal state (rounds, stuck, needs_human_review): move to a thin .exo/watcher-state.json keyed by PR number. merge_blocked_on_ci and approved_at_sha are derivable from Forgejo review history and CI run state, not stored flags.

issues.title: TL preflight: verify clean worktree + passing CI on base branch before spawning
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Add a 'preflight' check that runs automatically at TL session start (SessionStart hook or early in the TL role's init logic) before any planning or spawning. It should: (1) verify the main worktree is clean (no uncommitted changes, no untracked files that would conflict); (2) check that CI is passing on the base branch by querying the Forgejo API for the latest run on that branch; (3) if CI is failing or absent, report exactly which step failed and block the TL from spawning children until the user acknowledges; (4) deliver the result as a clear summary to the user — green means ready to work, red means the baseline is broken and must be fixed first. This prevents agents from forking off a broken baseline and compounding the problem. The check should be non-blocking if CI is simply absent (no workflow file configured yet), but blocking if CI is present and failing.

All agent spawn entry points now check git status --porcelain before spawning, require clean/untracked-free worktree, and when .gitea/workflows exists query Forgejo Actions for the latest run on the base branch. Success/neutral passes; failure/pending/unknown/missing run blocks unless EXOMONAD_TL_PREFLIGHT_ACK=1 is set. Added Forgejo latest_actions_status_for_branch helper and tests. Verification: cargo fmt; cargo check -p exomonad-core; focused Forgejo tests passed. Full cargo test -p exomonad-core still has existing merge_pr_local CI-unknown failures.

issues.title: Reviewer should exit after writing review; watcher owns CI gating and merge_ready
issues.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

The reviewer agent is staying alive after writing its review, waiting on CI status. This is wrong — the reviewer's job ends when it writes its verdict to the review file and the watcher records review_state in prs.json. After that the reviewer should close. CI gating and the merge_ready signal are exclusively the watcher's responsibility: the watcher observes approved review_state + CI status from the ci_status_map (populated by Forgejo webhook) and fires merge_ready when both conditions are met. The current coupling keeps reviewer Stop hooks blocked indefinitely (visible now with issue-35: 'PR #8 approved, waiting for CI to be triggered'), duplicates responsibility that already lives in the watcher, and conflates two distinct jobs. Fix: reviewer Stop hook should not gate on CI; watcher owns the full merge_ready path.

issues.title: exomonad init: surface orphaned agent windows for TL review rather than auto-killing
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

On exomonad init, detect agent tmux windows left over from a prior session and surface them as a startup report rather than auto-killing. The human or TL decides what to close.

Rationale: auto-kill on init is too destructive — orphaned windows may contain valuable state (in-progress analysis, diffs, notes). Err on the side of caution.

Proposed behavior:
1. On init, scan the tmux session for windows that are not the Server or TL/root windows
2. Cross-reference against .exo/agents/ entries — windows with no live agent process (process has exited, window is at shell prompt) are 'orphaned'
3. Print a startup report listing orphaned windows: name, age (from spawned_at if available), associated issue ID (from active_issue if available)
4. Do NOT auto-kill. The human uses close_worker_pane or dispose_leaf to clean up explicitly.

For --recreate: same behavior — kill the tmux session, but do not touch worktrees or agent dirs. The TL starts fresh but all prior work is recoverable via spawn_leaf (which reuses existing worktrees).

The background orphan reconciler continues to handle logical cleanup (issue-closed worktrees, reviewer disposal, session timeouts) independently.

This gives TL/dev-leaves a clean mental model: init shows you what was left behind, you decide what to keep.

issues.title: orphan reconciler: enforce max session age to stop long-running leaves and reviewers
issues.description:
Extend the orphan reconciler to kill any agent (dev-leaf or reviewer) whose session has exceeded max_session_seconds (configurable in review-policy.toml, default 1800s = 30 min).

Mechanism:
- Reconciler checks .exo/agents/ entries for session age
- If age > max_session_seconds: kill the tmux window, then notify TL

Two-part implementation:

1. spawn_leaf / spawn_worker write the assigned issue ID to .exo/agents/{name}/active_issue at spawn time. Reconciler reads this file when killing an agent so it can include the issue ID in the notification.

2. Reconciler kills the tmux window and fires send_message to the TL: '[TIMED OUT: {agent-name}] Issue #{id} exceeded {limit}min session limit — killed. Call chainlink_timer_stop #{id} and decide whether to re-spec or escalate.' TL handles chainlink_timer_stop and any issue bookkeeping with its existing tools.

Reconciler stays simple — it does not touch chainlink directly. Issue ID from .exo/agents/{name}/active_issue is purely for the notification message.

Config knobs: max_leaf_session_seconds (default 1800) and max_reviewer_session_seconds (default 600) in review-policy.toml.

issues.title: discover and document knot HTTP API for repo registration (installs git hooks)

Manual git init --bare does NOT install the git hooks that trigger triggerPipeline() on push — only API-created repos get hooks. Repos created via the API show up in repo_keys with did:web:... format (e.g. backrooms-workspace). Need to: (1) reverse-engineer or read knot source to find the repo creation endpoint, (2) document the required auth (owner DID + key), (3) implement the API call in exomonad new so repos are registered via API by default. This is a blocker for #334 and for #337 (CI on approval).

issues.title: DevPhase: add sequential CITriggered and CIBlocked states after reviewer approval
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

DevPhase currently has no explicit states for the post-approval CI step. Reviewer approval and CI status are checked concurrently in the watcher. The intended sequential flow is: FiledPR -> ReviewerApproved -> CITriggered -> CIPassed -> MergeReady. With a CI failure path: CITriggered -> CIFailed -> CIBlocked (TL escalation). Adding explicit CITriggered and CIBlocked states to DevPhase enforces the ordering structurally: (1) the watcher can only fire CITriggered from ReviewerApproved, not from an earlier state; (2) MergeReady can only be reached from CIPassed, never from an unresolved CI state; (3) CIBlocked is a terminal non-merge state that surfaces to the TL as a Chainlink review-stuck issue. This makes the reviewer's contract clear: they approve, CI runs, CI result determines merge. Depends on #337 (knot manual trigger on approval).

issues.title: watcher: trigger CI via knot manual API on reviewer approval, block issue on CI failure
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Current flow: CI triggers on branch push to knot. Problem: branches pushed before spindle was configured never get CI, and CI runs on every push regardless of review state (noise). Proposed flow: when reviewer fires ReviewerApproved, the watcher calls the Tangled knot manual trigger API (already supported in ci.yml via 'event: [manual]') for that branch+SHA. Spindle picks up the resulting sh.tangled.pipeline event and reports back. If CI passes: merge-ready fires normally. If CI fails: watcher creates a Chainlink review-stuck issue (or a new ci-blocked issue type) and notifies the TL. TL surfaces this to the human and decides next steps. This also fixes the Unknown CI state problem: if CI was never triggered for a PR, the watcher now knows to trigger it on approval rather than waiting forever for an event that will never come. Implementation needs: (1) knot HTTP manual-trigger API call from the watcher on ReviewerApprovedEv, (2) CI failure path that surfaces to TL as a blocked state, (3) CIStatus::Unknown should not permanently block merge-ready — it should trigger a CI run instead.

Causes spurious 'repo knot does not match' errors. Fix in exomonad init (not spindle binary): after spindle starts, prune any repos from spindle.db that were not explicitly seeded by exomonad new/init. No spindle binary change required.

issues.title: TL tool: close_issue_and_cleanup — close Chainlink issue + dispose leaf and reviewer worktrees
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

After merge_pr succeeds, the TL currently needs to call dispose_leaf and chainlink_issue_close separately, and reviewer worktrees are cleaned up lazily by the orphan reconciler. Add a single TL-role MCP tool (working name: close_issue_and_cleanup or issue_done) that atomically: (1) closes the Chainlink issue via the issue close effect, (2) disposes the dev-leaf worktree and tmux window, (3) disposes all reviewer worktrees associated with that leaf's PRs (any worktrees in .exo/worktrees/ whose name matches review-pr-N-* for PRs owned by the leaf). This gives the TL a single post-merge call that leaves no orphan worktrees. The tool takes issue_id and leaf_name (or infers leaf_name from the issue's assigned agent). Add to TLRole.hs and RootRole.hs (once #329 is resolved). Implementation: new Haskell tool in ExoMonad.Guest.Tools/, new Rust effect handler that combines the existing dispose-leaf and dispose-reviewer logic.

issues.title: exomonad new: attempt Tangled integration by default
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Currently all Tangled config in config.toml is commented-out template text — Tangled integration is opt-in. The intended behavior is: exomonad new probes for a local Tangled knot, registers the git repo with it, discovers tangled_owner_did, and writes the populated Tangled fields into config.toml. If the knot is unreachable, fall through and leave the fields commented (ci.gate=auto handles no-CI gracefully). Steps: (1) probe tangled_knot_url (default localhost:5555) or discover via tangled_knot_container docker lookup; (2) register the repo with the knot HTTP API; (3) resolve tangled_owner_did from the knot response or local Tangled identity; (4) write tangled_knot_url, tangled_spindle_url, tangled_appview_url, tangled_owner_did into config.toml as active fields; (5) exomonad init then auto-starts spindle as a companion (already gated on tangled_owner_did being set). The .tangled/workflows/ci.yml scaffold from exomonad new feeds the CI pipeline once the repo is registered. Failure to reach the knot is non-fatal — log a warning and continue with the commented template.

issues.title: reviewer pane does not exit after writing verdict
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

The ReviewerPhase stop hook correctly returns Clean after ReviewerDone (allowing exit). But Codex reviewers keep running after approve_pr/request_changes because nothing signals them to stop. The stop hook only fires when the agent tries to exit; if Codex keeps the session alive post-verdict, the hook is never invoked. The afterModel hook is a no-op (AfterModelAllow Nothing). Fix: use the postToolUse hook on approve_pr and request_changes to return an exit nudge, or inject a 'verdict written — exit now' instruction via AfterModelOutput so the next model turn sees it and terminates the session.

issues.title: runtime-hook-parity: extend agent inbox with structural deduplication for convergent delivery paths
issues.description:
Extend the per-agent FIFO inbox from #317 with structural deduplication, so multiple delivery paths converging on the same agent for the same logical event don't produce redundant messages in the agent's context window.

## Why this is worth doing even with #327 in place

#327 fixes the *intentional* double-delivery (handler-auto NotifyParent + leaf model's voluntary notify_parent both targeting the TL). But other convergence paths remain:

- **#327's TL InjectMessage backstop + leaf's voluntary notify_parent**: both deliver `[MERGE READY]` for the same PR to the TL pane. If both succeed (the common case after #314/#317 stabilize), the TL sees the signal twice.
- **Retry storms** from #314's send-keys retry policy or #317's FIFO consumer retry-on-failed-verification could deliver the same message multiple times if the verifier wobbles.
- **Watcher tick + cron-like re-evaluation** firing the same event payload before the recipient has processed the first one.

Deduplication catches all of these as one structural rule, rather than per-failure-mode patches.

## Dedup key — structural, not byte-equal

Hashing the full payload is brittle (any wording change defeats it). Instead, key on the **structural identity** of the event:

```
DedupKey = {
  recipient: AgentName,
  event_type: "MergeReady" | "ReviewApproved" | "FixesPushed" | ... | "notify_parent_freeform",
  scope_key: optional u64,   # PR number for PR events, issue number for IssueClosed, etc.
}
```

For freeform `notify_parent` messages with no event_type, fall back to a sender+recipient+payload-hash key with a short TTL — these are agent-composed text that can legitimately repeat (status updates), so dedup must be permissive.

For structured event-handler-driven deliveries (the InjectMessage / NotifyParentAction outputs from `prReviewHandler`), the (event_type, scope_key) tuple is the canonical key.

## Behavior

In `services/agent_inbox.rs` (the FIFO inbox from #317):

```rust
struct AgentInbox {
    queue: VecDeque<Message>,
    recent: HashMap<DedupKey, Instant>,  // last-delivered timestamp per dedup key
}

fn enqueue(msg: Message) -> Result<EnqueueOutcome> {
    let key = msg.dedup_key();
    let now = Instant::now();
    if let Some(last) = self.recent.get(&key) {
        if now.duration_since(*last) < self.dedup_window {
            tracing::debug!(?key, "Dropping duplicate message within dedup window");
            return Ok(EnqueueOutcome::DroppedAsDuplicate);
        }
    }
    self.recent.insert(key.clone(), now);
    self.queue.push_back(msg);
    Ok(EnqueueOutcome::Enqueued)
}
```

`dedup_window`: configurable, default 30 seconds. Tracked in `.exo/config.toml`.

Periodic pruning of `recent` based on TTL keeps memory bounded.

## Observability

Every dropped duplicate increments a metric: `agent_inbox.duplicates_dropped{recipient, event_type, scope_key}`. If this spikes for a particular agent/event combination, that's evidence of a delivery-path-convergence bug worth investigating at the source.

Importantly: **dedup must never silently mask a real bug**. Failed deliveries (the inbox couldn't actually inject) should NOT participate in the dedup window — only successful deliveries update `recent`. Otherwise a stuck-delivery scenario would deduplicate the retry attempts and the agent would never see the message.

## Files to touch

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_inbox.rs` (created by #317) — add `recent` map + `enqueue` dedup check + pruning.
- Define `DedupKey` and `dedup_key()` method on `Message`. For structured deliveries, the EventAction needs to carry enough context (event_type + scope_key) — extend the WASM Event types if needed.
- `.exo/config.toml` — add `inbox_dedup_window_secs` (default 30).

## Tests

- Unit: enqueueing two messages with the same DedupKey within the window → second returns `DroppedAsDuplicate`, queue has 1 entry.
- Unit: enqueueing two messages with the same DedupKey outside the window → both queued.
- Unit: enqueueing with different DedupKey (different PR, or different event_type) → both queued.
- Unit: failed delivery doesn't update `recent` — retry of the same message still goes through.
- Integration: simulate the #327 backstop scenario — TL handler InjectMessage + leaf voluntary notify_parent target the same TL with the same `[MERGE READY]` event for the same PR. Assert TL's pane gets the message ONCE. Metric `duplicates_dropped` increments by 1.

## Done criteria

- Per-agent inbox dedupes by (recipient, event_type, scope_key) within configurable window.
- Failed deliveries do NOT participate in dedup.
- Metric exposed for dropped duplicates.
- #327's structural backstop + leaf voluntary delivery converges to one message at the recipient (integration test demonstrates).
- Freeform `notify_parent` messages dedupe permissively (hash-based, short TTL) so legitimate repeats aren't silently lost.

## Relationship

- **#317** — per-agent FIFO inbox; this is a behavioral extension to that inbox.
- **#327** — TL backstop + leaf voluntary delivery; dedup at the recipient is the natural cleanup so the backstop doesn't produce duplicate context.
- **#326** — orthogonal (merge gate semantics); not coupled.
- **Future sub-TL behavior** — dedup is even more important when sub-TL cascading is enabled, since multiple agents in a chain might surface the same event independently. The structural dedup key handles this without per-tree-depth logic.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: PRReview handler must branch by role — TL gets InjectMessage (backstop), leaf drops auto NotifyParent
issues.description:
`TLRole.hs:312` registers `eventHandlers = prReviewEventHandlers` — the SAME handler `DevRole.hs` uses. On `MergeReady`, both roles return `NotifyParentAction(text, pr#)` per `PRReviewHandler.hs:87-91`. That's wrong for the TL role and creates three structural problems:

## Problem 1: TL cascades MergeReady up the tree

When the watcher fires `MergeReady` on the TL, the TL's handler returns `NotifyParentAction` → runtime tries to deliver to TL's parent (a grandparent TL, or root). For a sub-TL in an intermediate position, the message bubbles UP the tree to the root — every TL on the chain inherits the same redundant notification path. For a root TL, the upward delivery is a no-op or self-routed. Either way the TL's own pane gets nothing from its own handler.

## Problem 2: TL relies entirely on the leaf's delivery (which can fail)

Because the TL handler doesn't `InjectMessage` to its own pane, the only way the TL receives `[MERGE READY]` is via the dev-leaf's notify_parent chain. That delivery fails silently in tmux-fallback territory (#314 Enter-drop, #317 pile-up). Observed live 2026-05-20: nemotron-port TL never received `[MERGE READY]` for PR #1 despite the leaf seeing the signal in its own pane and calling `notify_parent` voluntarily. No structural backstop existed.

## Problem 3: Double-delivery path to TL from the leaf

The dev-leaf's pane shows the actual sequence:
1. Watcher fires `MergeReady` event → leaf's handler returns `NotifyParentAction` → **runtime auto-delivers** template text to TL.
2. Same handler ALSO injects the template into the leaf's own pane (the `›` prefix is visible — leaf's model now reads it as input).
3. Leaf's model decides to act → **voluntarily calls `notify_parent`** as an MCP tool with its own composed message.

Two notifications to the TL on the same event: one automatic from the handler, one model-driven from the leaf's voluntary `notify_parent`. If both succeed, the TL gets the message twice (different text, same semantic event). Currently both fail because of unrelated delivery bugs — so the TL gets nothing — but the design is wrong regardless.

## Fix

PRReview handler branches by role:

| Role | `MergeReady` returns | Effect |
|------|----------------------|--------|
| Dev-leaf | `InjectMessage(text)` | Leaf model sees `[MERGE READY]`, decides to call `notify_parent` voluntarily. ONE delivery path to TL. |
| TL | `InjectMessage(text)` | TL's own pane sees `[MERGE READY]` directly from the watcher — structural backstop against leaf's delivery failure. No upward cascade. |
| Reviewer | (already correct, no-op after verdict) | Reviewer already terminated per #311. |

Drop the automatic `NotifyParentAction` entirely from the shared handler. The leaf model voluntarily notifying the parent (via its own `notify_parent` tool call after reading the InjectMessage) is the canonical path; the auto-NotifyParentAction was redundant.

## Implementation

Split `prReviewEventHandlers` into role-aware versions, or accept a role parameter:

```haskell
-- pseudocode
mkPRReviewHandler :: Role -> EventHandlerConfig
mkPRReviewHandler role = defaultEventHandlers
  { onPRReview = case role of
      Dev -> prReviewHandlerForDev      -- InjectMessage on MergeReady
      TL  -> prReviewHandlerForTL       -- InjectMessage on MergeReady (self-targeted, structural backstop)
      Root -> prReviewHandlerForTL      -- same as TL
      Reviewer -> reviewerPRReviewHandler  -- unchanged
      Worker -> defaultEventHandlers.onPRReview  -- workers don't care about PR events
  }
```

Then `TLRole.hs:312` calls `mkPRReviewHandler TL`, `DevRole.hs` calls `mkPRReviewHandler Dev`, etc.

## Other PRReview events to check

Audit each event the shared handler currently dispatches:

- `MergeReady` — covered above
- `ReviewReceived` — leaf needs to see comments; TL probably wants `InjectMessage` (informational) too
- `ReviewApproved` — same pattern
- `ReviewTimeout`, `Stuck` — TL should see (already routes via NotifyParent up); reviewer's lifecycle bound here
- `FixesPushed` — informational for both
- `CommitsPushed` — same

For each, the leaf and TL handlers may want different actions. The audit produces the role-aware table — most cases probably collapse to "leaf returns NoAction or InjectMessage; TL returns InjectMessage."

## Tests

- Unit: TL handler on `MergeReady` returns `InjectMessage`, not `NotifyParentAction`.
- Unit: Dev-leaf handler on `MergeReady` returns `InjectMessage`, not `NotifyParentAction`.
- Integration: simulate the nemotron-port scenario (PR merge-ready, watcher fires event). Assert:
  - Leaf's pane receives `[MERGE READY]`.
  - Leaf's model voluntarily calls `notify_parent` (existing behavior).
  - TL's pane receives `[MERGE READY]` from BOTH paths (watcher-injected via TL handler, AND leaf's voluntary notify_parent).
  - No upward cascade beyond the TL.

## Subagent / sub-TL note (NOT this issue's scope)

Roger flagged 2026-05-20: sub-TL behavior on PR events hasn't been fully hashed out. A sub-TL is an intermediate TL that is itself a child of a root TL. When a sub-TL's dev-leaf hits MergeReady, the sub-TL needs to:
1. See the event (this issue's `InjectMessage` to TL's pane covers it)
2. Decide whether to merge locally OR escalate to its parent root TL

Today's `NotifyParentAction` blanket-cascades all the way up, which is wrong. After this issue's fix, the cascade is removed. Whether sub-TLs should explicitly escalate via their own `notify_parent` call after seeing `[MERGE READY]` is a separate design question — track in a follow-up issue when sub-TL flows become a focus.

## Done criteria

- TL and dev-leaf have distinct `MergeReady` handlers.
- TL handler `InjectMessage`s to TL's own pane (structural backstop).
- Dev-leaf handler `InjectMessage`s to leaf's own pane (no auto-NotifyParent).
- Leaf's voluntary `notify_parent` call remains the canonical delivery path to TL.
- Upward cascade through intermediate TLs is gone for `MergeReady`.
- All PRReview event types audited; per-role action table documented in code comments or a small `docs/decisions/pr-review-event-routing.md` ADR.

## Relationship

- **#311** — reviewer ephemerality; reviewer handler stays as-is (no-op after verdict).
- **#314 / #317** — delivery layer; this issue adds the structural backstop so a delivery failure on the leaf's notify_parent path doesn't leave the TL blind.
- **#324** — verdict file lock; orthogonal but in the same review-loop cluster.
- **#326** — round-counting; orthogonal but related (both gate the merge_pr success path).

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: merge gate rounds counter never increments on verdict write (option B: rounds = unique reviewed SHAs)
issues.description:
The merge gate in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/merge_pr_local.rs:116` refuses a PR when `pr.rounds < policy.min_review_rounds` (default `min_review_rounds = 1`). But production code paths **never increment `pr.rounds`** — the field is initialized to 0 at 5 sites in `file_pr_local.rs` and only set to non-zero values inside unit tests (lines 548, 563, 577, 592, etc. in `merge_pr_local.rs`). First-pass approvals — the most common case — therefore stay at `rounds=0` forever, and the gate rejects them even when the watcher correctly identifies the PR as merge-ready and sends `[MERGE READY]`.

Observed live 2026-05-20 in nemotron-port PR #1: `review_state=approved`, `approved_at_sha == last_head_sha`, watcher sent `[MERGE READY]`, TL retried `merge_pr` repeatedly (including with hallucinated `force: true`), every attempt produced:

```
WARN exomonad_core::services::merge_pr_local: Merge gate failed: PR #1: 0 review round(s) completed, 1 required blocked_on_ci=false
```

#297 (`3323fa1a Add reviewer round escalation coverage`) addressed escalation when rounds exceeds `reviewer_max_rounds` but did NOT address this root semantic — the rounds counter is never incremented in healthy operation, so neither the lower nor upper bound is functional.

## Fix — Option B with SHA uniqueness

Roger's preference (logged 2026-05-20): the `rounds` field should track **unique reviewed SHAs**, not raw verdict count. Each new head SHA push that receives at least one verdict bumps `rounds` by 1; subsequent verdicts on the same SHA do not bump it again.

This semantic supports future multi-reviewer flows naturally: multiple reviewers contributing verdicts to one SHA still count as one round. Combined with #324 (one verdict per `(PR, SHA)` round), the structural picture is:
- `#324` enforces: at most one verdict per `(PR, SHA)`
- This issue enforces: `rounds` = count of unique SHAs that have received any verdict
- `min_review_rounds = 1` then means "at least one reviewer has weighed in on the current SHA before merge" — which is the natural intent

## Implementation

The increment happens at the **verdict-write path** in `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs`, specifically in `approve_pr`, `request_changes`, and `post_review_comment` handlers. After writing the verdict to `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json`:

```haskell
-- pseudocode
let prev_head_sha = lookup prNumber pr_registry |> .last_head_sha
let already_reviewed_this_sha = any (\v -> verdictHeadSha v == prev_head_sha) (existing_verdicts_for_pr prNumber)
when (not already_reviewed_this_sha) $ do
  bump_pr_rounds prNumber  -- writes .exo/prs.json: pr.rounds += 1
```

Requires `ReviewVerdict` to carry the head SHA at write time (already proposed in #324). The increment is idempotent — re-running the same approve at the same SHA does not double-bump.

Alternative implementation: the watcher could detect SHA changes and bump rounds when it sees a new verdict file for a new SHA. Less coupled to the reviewer's tool path but adds asymmetry between reviewer-write and the registry update.

## Files to touch

- `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs` — extend approve_pr / request_changes to bump rounds after write.
- New effect / handler to atomically update `.exo/prs.json.rounds` from the WASM side; alternatively, the Rust runtime processes a `bump_rounds` effect emitted by the WASM after verdict write.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr_local.rs` — add `bump_rounds(pr_number)` API; ensure idempotency when `(pr_number, head_sha)` already counted.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/merge_pr_local.rs:116` — no change to the gate logic itself; just verify it accepts a properly-incremented rounds value.

## Tests

- Unit (Rust): `bump_rounds` is idempotent for the same `(pr_number, head_sha)`.
- Unit (Rust): `bump_rounds` increments when head_sha changes.
- Unit (Haskell): reviewer `approve_pr` on a fresh PR results in `pr.rounds = 1`.
- Integration: spawn a dev-leaf, file a PR, drive a reviewer to approve once; assert `pr.rounds = 1` in `.exo/prs.json`; assert `merge_pr` succeeds against current HEAD.
- Integration: same flow but reviewer first requests changes, dev pushes fix, reviewer approves; assert `pr.rounds = 2`; assert merge succeeds.
- Integration: regression for the nemotron-port symptom — fresh PR, single approval, `merge_pr` succeeds (currently fails).

## Done criteria

- A first-pass-approved PR has `pr.rounds = 1` immediately after the reviewer's `approve_pr`.
- `merge_pr` accepts such a PR (no `InsufficientRounds` error).
- Multiple verdicts on the same SHA do not double-bump rounds.
- Existing tests in `merge_pr_local.rs` (which manually set rounds) continue to pass; new tests cover the production-path increment.

## Relationship

- **#297** — closed without fixing this; this issue is the actual semantic fix.
- **#285** — addressed CI gating per SHA, complementary, not overlapping.
- **#324** — one verdict per `(PR, SHA)` round; combined with this issue, gives the clean "review rounds" semantic.
- **Future multi-reviewer flows** — scaffolding lever Roger called out: with rounds = unique-reviewed-SHAs, additional reviewers per round are a natural extension (each contributes a verdict to the same SHA without inflating rounds).

issues.title: E2E test: reviewer ephemerality (verdict-triggered disposal, per-round lock, fresh-reviewer-per-round, branch identity)
issues.description:
#311 (reviewer ephemerality) is closed/landed but the live observation on PR #2 (two distinct verdicts from what should be ephemeral reviewers — see #324) shows ephemerality may not actually be holding. We need an automated regression guard so this class of bug surfaces in CI rather than in real test sessions.

## What the test asserts

For each runtime that spawns reviewers (Claude, Codex, OpenCode):

1. **Verdict-triggered disposal.** Spawn a reviewer, drive it to write `approve_pr` to `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json`. Within one event-router tick (≤ a few seconds), assert:
   - `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-N-<runtime>/` is removed.
   - The reviewer's tmux window is killed.
   - `.exo/agents/review-pr-N-<runtime>/` is removed (if it existed).
   - The reviewer's git branch is cleaned up.

2. **Per-round verdict lock (paired with #324).** Attempt to spawn a SECOND reviewer instance against the same PR/SHA after the first wrote `approved`. Either:
   - Spawn refuses (preferred — first-line defense), OR
   - Spawn succeeds but the second reviewer's `approve_pr`/`request_changes` call is refused at the tool layer per #324's per-round lock.

   Test asserts ONE of these two paths fires, with a clear error mentioning the existing verdict. If both succeed and a second verdict lands, **the test must fail loudly** — that's the PR #2 nemotron-port symptom verbatim.

3. **Fresh reviewer per round on SHA change.** Push a new SHA to the PR (simulated — `git commit --allow-empty` on the PR branch, then `git push`). Assert a fresh reviewer agent spawns for that round, with a distinct agent slug or distinct invocation identity. The first reviewer's resources stay gone (their worktree shouldn't reappear).

4. **Reviewer branch identity captured.** When the reviewer writes a verdict, assert `verdict.author_branch` matches the reviewer's actual birth-branch (e.g., `master.review-pr-N-codex`), NOT `'unknown'` (the bug in #324 Part B).

## Companion layout

Follows `tests/e2e/messaging/` pattern:

- `tests/e2e/reviewer-ephemerality/run.sh` — temp repo + `exomonad new` + `exomonad init`. Sets `default_role=tl`, spawns a TL companion + a mock-dev-leaf that files a PR.
- `tests/e2e/reviewer-ephemerality/testrunner.md` — Claude haiku companion observing via read-only bash: `ls .exo/worktrees/`, `cat .exo/reviews/pr_*.json`, `tmux list-windows`. Reports pass/fail per phase via `notify_parent`.
- `tests/e2e/reviewer-ephemerality/e2e-test.md` — root TL rules: create team, idle.

## Concrete pseudocode for the testrunner

```
Phase 1: spawn reviewer → wait for approved verdict → poll .exo/worktrees for review-pr-N-* removal (timeout 30s)
Phase 2: try to spawn a second reviewer on the same PR/SHA → assert refusal OR refused-write (≤ 1 reviewer can land verdicts)
Phase 3: simulate fix push → wait for new reviewer worktree to appear → assert it's a new agent identity, not the old one
Phase 4: cat .exo/reviews/pr_N.json | jq '.verdicts[].author_branch' → assert no 'unknown' values
```

## Why high priority despite "deferred" being the typical E2E posture

Other E2E placeholders (#301, #305, #320) were filed at low/deferred because their corresponding unit tests provided most of the safety. This case is different: we have a **live observation** that ephemerality is not holding (#324's PR #2 evidence), so this E2E is the regression guard for an active bug class, not speculative coverage.

## Done criteria

- `just e2e-reviewer-ephemerality` runs the four phases in a temp repo.
- All four phases pass against current HEAD.
- The test fails on a synthetic regression where a second verdict is allowed to write (paired with #324).
- The test fails on a synthetic regression where reviewer disposal is skipped.
- The test fails on `author_branch=unknown`.

## Relationship

- **#311** — reviewer ephemerality landed; this test verifies it works in practice.
- **#324** — per-round verdict lock and author_branch fix; this test is the acceptance criterion for both.
- **#320** — generic MCP tool visibility E2E (closed). This is the targeted reviewer-lifecycle E2E.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: enforce one verdict per (PR, SHA) round; fix reviewer author_branch=unknown
issues.description:
Two-reviewer race observed 2026-05-19 nemotron-port on PR #2:

```
verdict[0]: state='approved'            author_branch='unknown'  body='Looks good. The encoder layer-prefix fallback...'
verdict[1]: state='changes_requested'   author_branch='unknown'  body='This PR's RNNT greedy decode refactor in src/model/candle/d...'
```

Two distinct review passes on different aspects of the same PR (encoder fallback vs RNNT greedy decode). The MergeReady event correctly fired on verdict[0] — the dev-leaf received `[MERGE READY]` and stopped. Then verdict[1] arrived, overwrote `reviewState` to `changes_requested`, and the registry now disagrees with the leaf's terminal state. Leaf has exited; PR is "open with changes requested" but no one is going to address them.

Two compounding bugs:

## Bug A: No per-round verdict lock

`ReviewerRole.hs::appendVerdict` always appends — every call adds to the verdicts list, and `reviewState` overwrites. Nothing enforces "one verdict per (PR, head SHA) round." Whoever calls `approve_pr` / `request_changes` / `post_review_comment` writes regardless of prior verdicts at the same SHA. Combined with the unknown-author-branch bug below, multiple reviewer instances can stomp each other without conflict detection.

## Bug B: Reviewer branch identity captured as 'unknown'

Both verdicts in the example show `author_branch='unknown'`. The verdict write path calls `getCurrentBranch` (in `ReviewerPhase.hs` or `ReviewerRole.hs`), which is falling back to `'unknown'` rather than returning the reviewer's actual birth branch (should be `master.review-pr-2-codex` or similar per the agent-identity-model).

This means: even if we add the per-round lock from Bug A, we can't tell which reviewer wrote which verdict — provenance is lost. Also, the verdict file's audit trail is useless for debugging the multi-reviewer race.

## Proposed fix

**For Bug A**: extend `appendVerdict` (or its callers in `ReviewerApprovePR`, `ReviewerRequestChanges`, `ReviewerPostReviewComment`) with a pre-write check:

```haskell
-- Pseudocode
existing <- readExistingReviewFile prNumber
let currentSha = ... -- read from PR registry or args
if any (\v -> verdictHeadSha v == currentSha) (reviewVerdicts existing)
  then pure $ errorResult $ "Refused: verdict for PR #" <> showT prNumber <> " at SHA " <> currentSha <> " already exists. Reviewers are ephemeral per round; if you believe the PR needs re-review, the dev-leaf must push a new SHA first."
  else writeVerdict ...
```

This requires the verdict record to carry the head SHA — currently `ReviewVerdict` has `verdictState`, `verdictBody`, `verdictComments`, `verdictAuthorBranch` but no SHA field. Add it.

**For Bug B**: investigate why `getCurrentBranch` returns 'unknown' in the reviewer's context. Possibilities:
- The reviewer worktree's `.git/HEAD` isn't a proper branch ref (detached HEAD per `git worktree list` output earlier — reviewer worktrees are detached)
- The reviewer's env var `EXOMONAD_AGENT_ID` or `EXOMONAD_SESSION_ID` isn't being read where it should
- The `getCurrentBranch` function's fallback chain reaches 'unknown' silently

Trace through the call path; surface a clear error or use the agent's birth-branch from the env var rather than git HEAD.

## Files to touch

- `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs`: add SHA field to `ReviewVerdict`; add per-round duplicate check before write.
- `.exo/lib/ReviewerPhase.hs` (or wherever `getCurrentBranch` is resolved for reviewer context): fix the unknown-branch fallback.
- The verdict file schema: bump version or add migration if needed for the new SHA field.

## Tests

- Unit: `appendVerdict` refuses a second verdict at the same SHA.
- Unit: `appendVerdict` allows a verdict at a new SHA (different round).
- Unit: reviewer's branch identity comes back as `review-pr-N-<runtime>` (or whatever the canonical reviewer slug format is), not `unknown`.
- Integration: simulate two reviewer instances spawning concurrently on the same PR/SHA; assert only the first verdict lands and the second is refused with the correct error message.

## Done criteria

- A single (PR, head SHA) round has exactly one verdict.
- Verdict files written today (with the new schema) carry a SHA field per verdict.
- Reviewer branch identity is captured correctly — `'unknown'` never appears in healthy operation.
- The two-verdict scenario from PR #2 is structurally impossible.

## Relationship

- **#311 (reviewer ephemerality)** — if #311 fully prevented a reviewer from writing a second verdict by terminating after the first, this bug would be impossible. The PR #2 observation says #311 either has a gap or hasn't fully shipped — the new E2E test in the paired issue (next ticket) will confirm.
- **#319 (sequential workers)** — sibling principle: one verdict per round mirrors one worker per worktree. Both enforce "exclusive access" structurally rather than via discipline.

issues.title: ensure_gitignore must cover all runtime scaffold paths (.codex/, .tangled/state/, .claude/settings.local.json, .opencode/)
issues.description:
`rust/exomonad/src/init.rs::ensure_gitignore` only adds entries for `.exo/*` (with allowlists for `config.toml`, `roles/`, `lib/`, `rules/`). Spawn paths for non-Claude runtimes drop additional scaffold files into the worktree that aren't covered, causing #316's clean-tree spawn precondition to refuse on a fresh project until the user manually fixes their `.gitignore`.

Observed 2026-05-19 nemotron-port: TL blocked from spawning leaves because `.codex/`, `.tangled/` (state, not workflows), and `.claude/settings.local.json` appear as untracked in `git status --porcelain`. All three are exomonad-managed runtime artifacts.

## Paths to add

Most agents' per-instance configs already live under `.exo/agents/{name}/` (covered by `.exo/*`). The gaps are at the project root and the worktree root where some runtimes write directly:

| Path | Created by | Tracked? | Ignore rule |
|------|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `.codex/` | spawn path (per-agent + project root Codex config) | no — runtime state | `.codex/` |
| `.tangled/workflows/` | exomonad new (CI config) | yes — project | (keep tracked) |
| `.tangled/*` (other) | runtime | no | `.tangled/*` + `!.tangled/workflows/` |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | spawn path | no — machine-specific | `.claude/settings.local.json` |
| `.claude/rules/` | exomonad new + user | yes — project rules | (keep tracked) |
| `.opencode/` (if at project root) | check whether opencode CLI writes here for session state, history, cache | no if so | `.opencode/` |
| `opencode.json` at project root | not currently written there (lives under `.exo/agents/{name}/`), but verify | TBD | TBD per verification |

## Implementation

Extend `rust/exomonad/src/init.rs::ensure_gitignore` to append all rows above. Same pattern as the existing `.exo/*` block — guard with `has_line()` so re-runs are idempotent.

```rust
let needed: Vec<&str> = [
    ".exo/*",
    "!.exo/config.toml",
    "!.exo/roles/",
    "!.exo/lib/",
    "!.exo/rules/",
    ".codex/",
    ".tangled/*",
    "!.tangled/workflows/",
    ".claude/settings.local.json",
    ".opencode/",  // verify against opencode CLI behavior first
].into_iter().filter(|line| !has_line(line)).collect();
```

## Investigation step (do first)

Before adding `.opencode/`, verify: does the OpenCode CLI write any project-root files outside `.exo/agents/{name}/`? Grep the OpenCode docs or run a smoke session and check `git status` after `exomonad init` with OpenCode as worker. If yes, include the path; if no, omit and document why.

## Tests

- Unit: `ensure_gitignore` on a fresh repo writes all expected entries; re-run is a no-op.
- Unit: `ensure_gitignore` on an existing `.gitignore` with some entries already present only appends missing ones.
- Integration: `exomonad new` + `exomonad init` on a fresh repo leaves `git status --porcelain` empty — #316 spawn precondition passes immediately without manual intervention.

## Done criteria

- Fresh project bootstrapped via `exomonad new` + `exomonad init` produces a clean worktree per `git status --porcelain`.
- All runtime-managed scaffold paths exomonad creates are either tracked deliberately (CI configs, rules) or gitignored.
- #316's spawn precondition fires only on actual user work, never on exomonad's own runtime artifacts.

## Relationship

- #316 — this issue removes the false-positive trigger that's currently blocking spawn in fresh projects.
- Harness-agnosticism design priority — every supported runtime's scaffold paths must be in the template, not just `.exo/`.

issues.title: Codex MCP tool list is stale and namespaced; bare-name docs/prompts/deny-messages don't match exposed tools
issues.description:
Observed 2026-05-19 in nemotron-port: a Codex TL session's exposed MCP tool list contains only 7 tools (spawn_worker, spawn_leaf, spawn_codex, fork_wave, send_message, merge_pr, close_worker_pane) — all of them namespaced as `mcp__exomonad__<tool>`. **Missing entirely** despite being registered in `TLRole.hs:253-256, 290-293` and `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/Chainlink.hs`:

- `file_pr`, `notify_parent`, `task_list`/`task_get`/`task_update`
- All `chainlink_issue_*`, `chainlink_session_*`, `chainlink_timer_*`, `chainlink_subissue_*`, `chainlink_milestone_create`
- Newly added `dispose_leaf` (#303), `discard_worker_output` (#304)

Pattern: exposed tools are the **core orchestration set that existed early**. Missing tools are **chainlink integration + recently-added (today's lifecycle work)**. Two distinct bugs compound:

## Bug 1: Stale tool list

Either the running server's plugin cache holds an older WASM that pre-dates the chainlink + lifecycle registrations, OR (more likely) the MCP handshake between exomonad's mcp-stdio and the Codex client caches the `tools/list` response at session start — even if WASM hot-reloads, the agent's view doesn't refresh.

**Fix paths:**
- Emit the MCP `notifications/tools/list_changed` notification (per MCP spec) whenever WASM mtime changes. Codex's MCP client should re-fetch the tool list on receipt.
- Or: drop the per-session tool cache on the exomonad mcp-stdio side and serve `tools/list` fresh on every request. Trade slight cost for guaranteed freshness.
- Document the operational fallback: `exomonad reload` clears WASM cache, but agents must re-handshake (which may require session restart on some runtimes) to see new tools.

## Bug 2: Tool namespace mismatch

Codex exposes every MCP tool prefixed with `mcp__exomonad__` (e.g., `mcp__exomonad__spawn_worker` rather than `spawn_worker`). But:

- CLAUDE.md references bare names (`fork_wave`, `merge_pr`, etc.).
- `docs/architecture/agent-system.md`'s role × tool matrix uses bare names.
- The `#310` deny message tells agents *"Use the chainlink_* MCP tool equivalents instead"* — also bare names.
- Agent runbooks at `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md` use bare names.

When the agent reasons *"I should call chainlink_timer_start,"* and scans its tool list for that string, it never matches the namespaced version. Even when the tool IS exposed, the agent doesn't recognize it as the thing the doc told it to use. This is partially why the TL in nemotron-port reported *"no chainlink_* MCP timer/session tools are exposed to me"* — even tools that aren't missing-from-registration may be unfindable from the agent's perspective.

**Fix paths (pick one and apply uniformly):**
- **(a) Strip the prefix at the exomonad mcp-stdio layer.** Agents see bare names matching docs. Compatible with everything written today. Risk: collision if a future MCP server exposes a tool of the same name.
- **(b) Rewrite all prompts, docs, deny messages, runbooks to use the namespaced form.** Agent sees `mcp__exomonad__chainlink_timer_start` everywhere. Higher friction now, more accurate forever.
- **(c) Per-runtime alias table**: exomonad mcp-stdio detects which runtime is connecting and exposes either bare or namespaced names as the runtime expects. Most flexible, most code.

My read: **(a) is the right answer** — it keeps the canonical name space coherent with the docs and removes a cross-runtime presentation gap. The namespacing was a Codex display choice, not a semantic one; strip it at our wrapper.

## Files to touch (assuming fix (a))

- `rust/exomonad/src/mcp_stdio.rs` (or wherever tools/list response is built) — strip any `mcp__<server>__` prefix from outgoing tool names. Verify Claude path unaffected (Claude already sees bare names today, so the strip should be a no-op for Claude clients).
- For bug 1: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/` plugin cache invalidation; emit `notifications/tools/list_changed` on WASM reload.

## Tests

- Unit: tools/list response from mcp-stdio uses bare names regardless of runtime.
- Integration: spawn Codex TL → query its exposed tool list → assert every tool in `agent-system.md`'s TL row is present, in bare-name form (this is exactly the test from #320, which catches both bugs).
- Manual: with a Codex session running, touch a WASM file → assert agent's `tools/list` view refreshes within reasonable time without session restart.

## Done criteria

- Codex (and any other runtime that namespaces by default) sees bare tool names matching docs.
- WASM mtime change triggers a tool-list refresh visible to running agents.
- Every tool documented in `agent-system.md` for a given role × runtime is actually exposed at that surface.
- #320's E2E test passes (it directly verifies both fixes).

## Relationship

- #320 (MCP tool visibility E2E) — directly tests both bugs. Should be bumped to high alongside this issue; passing #320 IS the structural acceptance test for this fix.
- #310 (block bash chainlink CLI) — depends on this being fixed for agents to actually use the MCP equivalents the deny message points them to. Without this fix, agents see "use chainlink_* MCP tools" but can't find any matching name, so they get permanently stuck.
- harness-agnosticism (memory: feedback_harness_agnosticism.md) — this is exactly the kind of presentation gap that breaks the agnostic-workflow goal.

comments.content:
Roger 2026-05-19: For Bug 1, force tool-list refresh — emit MCP `notifications/tools/list_changed` on WASM mtime change (per MCP spec). Drop the alternative of clearing per-session cache and serving tools/list fresh on every request; the spec-compliant notification path is the right answer because it actively pushes the change to connected clients instead of relying on them to ask again.

For Bug 2, fix (a) remains my recommended approach (strip `mcp__exomonad__` prefix at the exomonad mcp-stdio layer) — pending Roger's confirmation. Cross-reference #320 (E2E test) as the structural acceptance test.

Roger 2026-05-19 (sequencing update):

Land Bug 1 (force tool-list refresh via `notifications/tools/list_changed`) FIRST and observe whether Bug 2 still manifests. Modern LLMs often match `chainlink_timer_start` against `mcp__exomonad__chainlink_timer_start` on suffix — the missing-tools symptom in nemotron-port may have been entirely a Bug 1 staleness issue wearing a Bug 2 costume.

Per-runtime stripping at the mcp-stdio wrapper layer is rejected as sloppy: it creates a new wrapper branch per harness namespace convention. If Bug 2 genuinely blocks agents after Bug 1 lands, the structural answer is alias-at-MCP-server (expose every tool under both `<name>` AND `<namespace>__<name>`), which generalizes across runtimes without per-harness logic. But that's speculation — only build it if observed.

Scope adjustment for this issue: implement Bug 1 fully. Mark Bug 2 as deferred pending evidence after Bug 1 lands. #320 (E2E visibility test) is the falsifier — if it passes with bare-name assertions after Bug 1 alone, Bug 2 is closed by transitivity.

issues.title: runtime-hook-parity: investigate ACP support for Codex agents (low — tmux fallback works today)
issues.description:
Exploratory investigation. The tmux STDIN fallback path is the harness-agnostic baseline that works across every runtime, and it's getting structurally harder (#314 Enter verification, #317 FIFO inbox). ACP gives Gemini a much cleaner delivery channel via structured JSON-RPC; if Codex supports ACP (or could be invoked in an ACP-speaking mode), Codex agents could opt onto the same upgraded delivery and skip several classes of tmux-layer bug entirely.

This is opportunistic, not urgent. The tmux fallback handles Codex today and will continue to. The investigation may also conclude "Codex doesn't speak ACP, not worth it" — that's a valid outcome and the work stops there.

## Investigation questions

1. **Does Codex CLI expose an ACP server?** Search Codex docs (https://developers.openai.com/codex/) for any ACP mention. OpenCode has a `--acp` / "ACP port from opencode acp stdout" pattern (referenced in exomonad chainlink #10) — does Codex have an analogue?
2. **If yes, how is it invoked?** A flag, an env var, a subcommand. What does Codex print on stdout/stderr to advertise the port/socket?
3. **What does Codex's ACP surface support?** ACP defines `Agent` and `Client` traits with specific methods (`new_session`, `prompt`, `request_permission`, `session_notification`). Does Codex implement all the ones exomonad needs (mostly `prompt` + `session_notification`)?
4. **Does Codex's auto-permission story match ours?** Today our ACP client (`services/acp_client.rs`) auto-approves all permissions. If Codex enforces approval prompts differently in ACP mode, that may be a friction point.

## If supported — implementation sketch

- Extend `services/acp_registry.rs::connect_and_prompt` to accept a runtime variant. Codex spawn path captures the ACP port (similar to OpenCode's pattern) and registers an `AcpConnection` for the agent.
- Update `services/delivery.rs` priority chain so Codex agents use ACP when a connection exists, fall back to tmux otherwise. The order becomes: Teams inbox → ACP prompt → HTTP-over-UDS → tmux STDIN (same as Gemini today).
- Verify the vendored ACP SDK at `vendor/acp-rust-sdk/` handles Codex's protocol version / capabilities advertisement (Send-safety patches per CLAUDE.md were specifically for tokio multi-threaded runtime; should compose).
- Add Codex row to the per-runtime table in `docs/decisions/cross-runtime-message-inbox.md` (created by #318): change from "tmux fallback only" to "ACP preferred, tmux fallback."

## What it does NOT replace

- The MCP server / tool dispatch path (Codex uses MCP for tool calls regardless of delivery mechanism).
- The Codex sandbox profiles (#309) — those constrain filesystem writes, independent of message delivery.
- The per-runtime hook policy (#308) — runs at hook layer, independent of message delivery.
- The agent FIFO inbox (#317) — ACP delivery still benefits from per-agent serialization at the exomonad layer.

## Done criteria

Either:
- **(a) Codex supports ACP**: implementation sketch above is fleshed out into a follow-up issue (or this issue is reclassified as the implementation issue). Codex delivery path includes ACP between Teams inbox and tmux.
- **(b) Codex does not support ACP**: investigation document at `docs/decisions/codex-acp-investigation.md` records the findings (what was checked, where the gap is, whether it could be added upstream), and this issue is closed with that doc as the artifact.

Either outcome is acceptable. The win is having the investigation on the record so we're not guessing later.

## Why low priority

Tmux fallback works for Codex today. Every bug we've filed at the tmux layer (#314, #317) makes that path more reliable, not less. ACP would be strictly better for the Codex case, but it's not gating anything currently running. Pick this up when there's bandwidth and no higher-impact runtime-parity work is in flight.
