issues.title: E2E test: assert per-role per-runtime MCP tool visibility matches agent-system.md matrix
issues.description:
Observed 2026-05-19 nemotron-port: TL (Codex) reported *"no chainlink_* MCP timer/session tools are exposed to me"* despite those tools being registered in `TLRole.hs:253-256, 290-293` (landed in commits `bdaa28ea` and `5ebcd3ac`, pre-dating today's burst). Root cause could be agent hallucination, stale WASM cache, or tool-name namespacing mismatch — and we have no automated way to tell which, or to catch the next instance of the same class of bug.

The canonical role × tool matrix is documented at `docs/architecture/agent-system.md` (lines 50-71 cover MCP + chainlink tools per role). We need an E2E test that asserts the live MCP server's actual tool list per role × runtime exactly matches the matrix. Documentation drift, stale WASM, and runtime-specific name mangling all fail this test.

## Scope

A new `tests/e2e/mcp-tool-visibility/` test following the existing pattern (`tests/e2e/messaging/` as reference).

## What it does

1. **Parse the canonical matrix** from `docs/architecture/agent-system.md` — extract the role × tool table programmatically (it's a markdown table, parseable). Build an expected `{role: set<tool_name>}` map.
2. **For each role** in `{root, tl, dev, reviewer, worker}` and **for each runtime** in `{claude, codex, opencode, gemini}` (skip combinations that don't exist):
   - Spawn an agent with that role + runtime in a sandboxed temp directory.
   - Query the MCP server for that agent's tool list (`exomonad mcp-stdio --role <role> --agent-id <test-id>` then JSON-RPC `tools/list` request, OR via a small test helper that exercises the same path the agent runtime uses).
   - Capture the actual exposed tool name set.
3. **Diff** actual vs expected:
   - **Missing tool**: matrix says role has X, actual list doesn't → test fails with the missing tool name.
   - **Unexpected tool**: actual list has Y, matrix doesn't list it for this role → test fails (catches accidentally over-exposed tools).
   - **Name-mangled tool**: actual list has `mcp__exomonad__X` but matrix says `X` → test fails on the prefix.
4. **Report** the full diff matrix as a markdown table in the test output, so a failure makes the gap obvious without reproducing.

## Sample assertions (illustrative — full set generated from the matrix)

- `assert "chainlink_timer_start" in tools_for(role=tl, runtime=codex)` — would have caught the 2026-05-19 nemotron-port symptom.
- `assert "chainlink_timer_start" not in tools_for(role=worker, runtime=codex)` — catches over-exposure.
- `assert "chainlink_issue_close" in tools_for(role=root, runtime=claude)` — coordinator authority.
- `assert "fork_wave" not in tools_for(role=dev, runtime=any)` — leaf role can't spawn subtrees.

## Companion layout (per `tests/e2e/messaging/` reference)

- `run.sh` — temp-repo + exomonad init + spawn test harness.
- `testrunner.md` — instructions for the testrunner Claude that drives the assertions.
- `e2e-test.md` — root TL rules for this test (idle / observe).

## Done criteria

- `just e2e-mcp-tool-visibility` runs the test against a temp project.
- All 5 roles × 4 runtimes exercise (skipping any combo that's structurally invalid, e.g., reviewer not having `chainlink_*` tools per the matrix).
- Test fails loudly with a diff table when the matrix and reality disagree.
- Re-runs idempotently.

## What this test gives us

- Catches future stale-WASM regressions (server returns old tool list because cache wasn't reloaded).
- Catches name-mangling drift (a runtime starts namespacing tools differently and the matrix becomes wrong without us knowing).
- Catches accidental over-exposure (a tool gets registered for the wrong role).
- Provides a concrete falsification target for any "I don't have tool X" agent report — if the test passes for that role × runtime × tool, the agent was hallucinating; if it fails, there's a real registration/exposure bug.

## Relationship

- #308 (per-runtime hook policy) — peer at the enforcement layer. This is the discovery / visibility layer.
- #310 (block bash chainlink) — the deny message that redirected to MCP tools is only useful if the MCP tools are actually visible. This test is the regression guard for that contract.
- `docs/architecture/agent-system.md` is the matrix this test reads. Keeping that doc accurate IS the test's job; if doc drifts from reality the test fails and you update one or the other.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: spawn_worker refuses if another worker is active in TL worktree (enforce sequential)
issues.description:
CLAUDE.md and `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` (Out of scope section) both document workers as sequential: *"Workers stay sequential and one-off. Parallelization is dev-leaf turf."* But `spawn_worker` doesn't enforce it. Parallel worker spawning produces ambiguous dirty state at session end — multiple workers share the TL's worktree, and the strict #304 stop hook can't tell whose changes are whose without per-worker attribution (which is explicitly out of scope per the ADR, re-confirmed by Roger 2026-05-19).

Observed cascade in nemotron-port 2026-05-19: TL spawned four verification workers in parallel into the same worktree → all four hit dirty-state confusion at session end → notification pile-up in TL pane. Each chained symptom (#316 spawn precondition, #317 FIFO inbox) addresses one layer; this issue closes the root: workers are sequential, full stop.

## Decision

`spawn_worker` MCP tool refuses if there's already an active worker registered to the calling TL's worktree. Workers are spawned **one at a time** per TL worktree. For parallel work, the TL uses `spawn_leaf` (own worktree, own branch, own PR).

## Mechanism

A worker registers in `.exo/agents/{worker-name}/routing.json` with a `parent_tab` field identifying its TL. Active workers = entries whose `parent_tab` matches the calling TL's slug. `spawn_worker` precondition:

```
let active = list_agents_dir(".exo/agents")
    .filter(|a| routing_json(a).parent_tab == calling_tl.slug)
    .count();
if active > 0 {
    refuse with deny_message
}
```

Reuses the same `routing.json` reader pattern already in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resources.rs:cleanup_worker_agents_in_dir`.

## Files to touch

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn_worker.rs` (or wherever `spawn_worker` core lives): add the active-worker check before spawn.
- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/SpawnWorker.hs` (or equivalent): update tool description to mention the sequential constraint.
- `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md`: promote the sequential-workers rule from "Out of scope" prose to a named architectural rule; cross-reference this issue as the structural enforcement.

## Deny message

> BLOCKED: workers are sequential per CLAUDE.md and docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md. Active worker in this TL worktree: `{worker_name}` (spawned {duration} ago).
>
> Options:
> 1. Wait for the active worker's handoff before spawning the next.
> 2. Use `spawn_leaf` for parallel work that warrants its own PR — dev-leaves have their own worktrees and don't share state.
>
> Per-worker attribution to allow parallel workers in one worktree is explicitly out of scope (see ADR § Out of Scope).

## Tests

- Unit: spawn_worker with no active workers → succeeds.
- Unit: spawn_worker when one worker is registered with matching parent_tab → refused with the deny message; refusal includes the active worker's name.
- Unit: spawn_worker when one worker is registered with DIFFERENT parent_tab (e.g., from a sibling TL) → succeeds (constraint is per-TL, not global).
- Unit: spawn_worker after a previous worker's `dispose_agent_resources` cleanup → succeeds.
- Integration: spawn worker A, attempt to spawn worker B before A exits → B refused; A exits cleanly via session_end; spawn worker B → succeeds.

## Done criteria

- spawn_worker refuses on active-worker collision with actionable deny message.
- Refusal scope is per-TL (siblings can have their own active workers concurrently).
- ADR updated to promote the sequential rule from "Out of scope" to a named structural constraint.
- Per-worker attribution stays out of scope; deny message points readers there.

## Relationship

- #316 — spawn-time clean-tree precondition. Complementary: #316 ensures clean state at spawn, this ensures only one worker spawns per worktree at a time.
- #317 — FIFO inbox. Mitigates symptom (pile-up); this issue closes the root cause for the worker case.
- ADR `agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` § Out of Scope: "Parallel workers in one TL worktree" — this issue is the structural enforcement of that rule.

issues.title: ADR: cross-runtime message inbox — codify exomonad-provides-inbox rule for non-Claude runtimes
issues.description:
Peer ADR to `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md`, codifying the architectural rule that surfaces from #317: **for agent runtimes without a native inbox + poller (Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, future), exomonad provides one.**

This is the harness-agnosticism design priority (see `~/.claude/projects/-home-goya-agent-workspace-exomonad/memory/feedback_harness_agnosticism.md`) showing up structurally: Claude Code's Teams inbox already serializes message delivery via InboxPoller; non-Claude runtimes must get the same guarantees from exomonad.

## Files to create

`docs/decisions/cross-runtime-message-inbox.md`

## Structure (follow agent-lifecycle-invariants.md style)

**Status:** Proposed (flip to Accepted once #317 lands)
**Date:** 2026-05-19
**Chainlink:** #314, #317, this issue

**Context** — Observed pile-up in nemotron-port (concatenated `[from issue-N]` markers in TL input box). Root cause analysis: INJECTION_LOCKS serializes calls not messages; Codex multi-line input mode breaks the absence-heuristic in #314.

**Decision** — Per-runtime inbox parity. Exomonad provides a per-agent FIFO inbox + single-consumer task for any runtime that lacks a native equivalent. Claude path stays on Teams inbox.

**Invariants** —
1. Every message addressed to an agent enters a per-agent FIFO before reaching the runtime.
2. The FIFO has a single consumer per agent; in-flight count is at most 1 per agent.
3. Consumption verification uses a per-runtime positive signal (TUI rendered a response), not absence-of-payload heuristics.
4. Queue depth is observable; bounded with explicit rejection at cap (no silent drops).

**Per-runtime table** —
| Runtime | Inbox source | Consumer | Notes |
|---------|--------------|----------|-------|
| Claude Code | Teams inbox (`~/.claude/teams/{team}/inboxes/`) | InboxPoller (native) | Already serialized; exomonad path unchanged |
| Codex | exomonad `AgentInbox` | exomonad consumer task | Tmux injection; multi-line input mode needs positive-signal verification |
| Gemini | exomonad `AgentInbox` (fallback) OR ACP prompt (when connection live) | exomonad consumer task | ACP delivery is preferred when available — separate from tmux fallback |
| OpenCode | exomonad `AgentInbox` | exomonad consumer task | Stub until OpenCode integration matures |

**Out of scope** —
- Persisting the inbox across exomonad restarts. In-memory is fine; senders use `notify_parent` retries.
- Cross-agent fanout (broadcast to many recipients) — that's `send_message` territory and uses the same per-recipient inboxes underneath.

**Related** —
- agent-lifecycle-invariants.md (peer ADR)
- agent-identity-model.md (birth-branch identity used as inbox key)
- teams-roadmap.md, claude-teams-integration.md (Claude's native path)
- chainlink #314 (per-message Enter verification, complementary)
- chainlink #317 (implementation)

**Implementation tracking** — table mapping chainlink issues to invariants, following the convention from agent-lifecycle-invariants.md.

## Done criteria

- File exists at `docs/decisions/cross-runtime-message-inbox.md`.
- Status flips to Accepted once #317 merges.
- Cross-references added to agent-lifecycle-invariants.md and to the architecture docs (`docs/architecture/agent-system.md` should mention the inbox in its messaging section).
- The harness-agnosticism design priority is named explicitly in the rationale.

issues.title: Per-agent FIFO inbox for tmux-injection runtimes (Codex/Gemini/OpenCode); serialize delivery + positive-signal consumption
issues.description:
Multiple worker `notify_parent` calls in flight at once can pile into the TL's input box rather than being delivered as discrete messages. Observed 2026-05-19 nemotron-port: four workers' messages concatenated as `[from issue-19-...] [from issue-21-...] [from issue-20-...] [from issue-22-...]` in a single visible input line, none submitted individually.

Root cause: `INJECTION_LOCKS` in `tmux_ipc.rs` serializes inject CALLS but doesn't queue MESSAGES. Even with #314's capture-pane verification, Codex's multi-line input mode (Enter inserts newline rather than submitting) keeps the pasted payload "visible," so verification incorrectly retries — adding more Enters that don't flush.

Claude Code agents are immune because the Teams inbox + InboxPoller drips one message at a time into the agent's context as `<teammate-message>` blocks. Codex/Gemini/OpenCode have no equivalent — every notify_parent falls back to direct tmux injection. The fix: exomonad provides an inbox+poller for runtimes that lack one natively.

## Architecture

- **`AgentInbox<AgentName>`** keyed by recipient agent. In-memory `VecDeque<Message>` with bounded depth (configurable, default 64).
- **One consumer task per agent** spawned lazily on first message. Pops head, injects via `tmux_ipc::inject_input`, waits for **strict consumption** (see below), then pops the next.
- **`deliver_to_agent`** in `services/delivery.rs` enqueues to the inbox instead of calling `inject_input` directly for tmux-fallback runtimes. Claude path (Teams inbox) unchanged.
- **Bounded queue with backpressure**: when depth exceeds threshold, log warning with queue depth + oldest-message-age; reject new enqueues at hard cap. Caller of `notify_parent` gets a failure result and can retry.

## Strict consumption verification

Today's #314 verification ("is payload no longer visible in input area") fails in Codex multi-line mode. Stronger verification needs a positive signal:

- Capture-pane after Enter, look for the **TL's response area** showing a new block of generated text (the TUI rendered something in reaction). The exact pattern is TUI-specific (Codex's `• Called exomonad...`-style bullets, Claude Code's box-bordered messages).
- Per-runtime consumption-pattern table in `tmux_ipc.rs` (mirrors `implementerToolsFor` from #308): each runtime declares the regex/substring that means "TUI consumed my input and rendered a response."
- Timeout: if no positive signal after N seconds, treat as failed delivery; head stays in queue; consumer retries with backoff.

## Files to touch

- New: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_inbox.rs` (queue + consumer task)
- New: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tui_consumption.rs` (per-runtime consumption-pattern table)
- Modify: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/delivery.rs` — route tmux-fallback deliveries through inbox
- Modify: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs` — replace `verify_input_consumed`'s "absence" heuristic with the new positive-signal verification helper
- Modify: `rust/exomonad/src/serve.rs` — wire inbox registry into server services
- Add: `.exo/config.toml` keys for inbox depth cap, consumption verification timeout

## Test plan (be descriptive — per Roger)

**Unit tests (`agent_inbox.rs`):**
1. `enqueue_dequeue_fifo_order` — enqueue 10 messages with distinct IDs, dequeue 10 times, assert order is exactly enqueue order.
2. `bounded_queue_rejects_at_cap` — set cap=3, enqueue 4, assert 4th returns `Err(QueueFull)` with queue depth in the error.
3. `independent_queues_per_agent` — enqueue to agent A (3 msgs) and agent B (5 msgs) concurrently, drain both, assert no cross-contamination.
4. `queue_depth_metric_visible` — enqueue 5, drain 2, assert depth metric reads 3.

**Integration tests (`services/agent_inbox/tests/`):**
5. `four_concurrent_workers_no_pile_up` — spawn a mock TL pane (script that prints "RECEIVED: {msg}\n" for each input line); fire 4 concurrent `notify_parent` calls with distinct payloads; assert TL pane log shows exactly 4 separate `RECEIVED: ...` lines in enqueue order, not 1 concatenated line. Reproduces the nemotron-port symptom.
6. `multi_line_codex_input_mode_consumed_correctly` — mock pane that mimics Codex multi-line input (Enter inserts newline, prompt `> ` indicates ready-for-next); inject a 3-line payload; assert verification recognizes consumption from the `>` prompt return, NOT from "payload absent" (which would be false because multi-line keeps it visible).
7. `consumer_retries_on_failed_verification` — mock pane that swallows the first Enter, accepts the second; assert message is eventually delivered (1 retry) and metric `verify_failure_count` increments by 1.
8. `consumer_gives_up_loudly_after_timeout` — mock pane that swallows all Enters; assert after N attempts the consumer logs an error AT WARN level with the queue head's message id, message stays in queue, alert is observable via OTel.
9. `backpressure_warning_at_depth_threshold` — set threshold=10, cap=20; enqueue 11; assert WARN log with queue depth; 12th still accepted; 21st rejected.
10. `restart_documented_as_lossy` — explicit test asserting that dropping the inbox registry loses queued messages (this is the documented behavior). Pair with documentation in the ADR that `notify_parent` callers must treat delivery as best-effort and rely on idempotency for retries.

**Cross-runtime tests:**
11. `codex_consumption_pattern_matches` — fixture with real Codex output (saved from a capture); assert the Codex-row of `tui_consumption.rs` regex matches the "response started" signal.
12. `claude_path_unchanged` — fire `notify_parent` against a Claude-runtime recipient; assert delivery goes through Teams inbox path, NOT the new agent_inbox (Claude already has its own inbox).
13. `opencode_consumption_pattern_stub` — placeholder test asserting OpenCode row exists in the table even if its pattern is TODO. Catches regression where a new runtime is added but consumption pattern is forgotten.

**Observability tests:**
14. `otel_metrics_emitted` — assert spans/events for: enqueue, drain attempt, verify success, verify failure, queue depth sample.

## Done criteria

- Per-agent FIFO inbox prevents the nemotron-port-style pile-up; integration test #5 demonstrates this against the documented failure mode.
- Strict consumption verification recognizes per-runtime "TUI responded" signals; test #6 demonstrates this against Codex multi-line mode.
- Backpressure visible via OTel; bounded queue rejects loudly at cap.
- Claude Teams inbox path untouched; harness-agnosticism preserved.
- All 14 tests above pass.

## Relationship

- #314 (Enter consumption verification) — complementary. #314 fixes single-message verification; this fixes multi-message serialization and replaces the absence-heuristic with positive-signal verification.
- Teams inbox (Claude Code) — prior-art / structural inspiration.
- Sibling ADR (separate chainlink issue, paired) — codifies the "for runtimes without native inbox, exomonad provides one" rule.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: spawn_worker / spawn_leaf must refuse on dirty TL worktree (invariant 4)
issues.description:
Workers run in-place in the TL's worktree per CLAUDE.md § Architecture. When the TL has uncommitted changes at spawn time, workers inherit that dirty state and cannot end their session cleanly per #304's stop hook — they correctly refuse to commit files they didn't author and escalate to the TL.

Observed 2026-05-19 nemotron-port: TL spawned four verification workers (#19, #20, #21, #22) into a worktree with uncommitted `CHANGELOG.md` and `src/model/candle/decoder.rs`. All four stuck on the inherited dirty state, escalations piled in TL's input box.

## Invariant 4 (proposed addition to agent-lifecycle-invariants.md)

`spawn_worker` and `spawn_leaf` refuse on dirty TL worktree. The TL commits its scaffolding (per scaffold-fork-converge in CLAUDE.md § Tech Lead Praxis) or runs `discard_worker_output` before spawning. Same boundary discipline as #304 invariant 2 (issue close refuses on dirty), applied to spawn.

## Why both spawn tools

- **spawn_worker** (in-place): worker shares TL's worktree → inherited dirty state breaks #304's stop hook. Direct symptom of the bug observed.
- **spawn_leaf** (own worktree): leaf forks from TL's branch HEAD. Uncommitted TL scaffold work is invisible to the leaf → it works on stale code. Same precondition prevents the silent staleness.

## Files to touch

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/` — spawn_worker and spawn_leaf handlers: pre-flight `git status --porcelain` in TL's CWD, refuse on non-empty.
- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/` — update TL spawn tool descriptions to mention the precondition.
- `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` — add invariant 4 with cross-references to #304.

## Deny message

> BLOCKED: cannot spawn agent into a dirty TL worktree. {N} file(s) have uncommitted changes:
>   {file list}
> Commit the scaffold (per scaffold-fork-converge) or run `discard_worker_output` if throwaway, then retry. Workers spawn in-place and would inherit this state; dev-leaves fork from your branch HEAD and would not see your uncommitted work.

## Tests

- Unit: spawn handler refuses with dirty worktree, succeeds with clean. File list appears in error message.

## Done criteria

- spawn_worker and spawn_leaf refuse on dirty TL worktree with actionable error.
- ADR invariant 4 added; ADR's "Out of scope" section gets one more entry removed (no longer needs to handwave about workers inheriting state — the precondition handles it).

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: orphan_reconciler must dispose dev-leaf worktrees, not just log the event
issues.description:
#313 (background orphan reconciler) landed but only half-wired the dev-leaf path. Verified against the diff at `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs`:

- `reconcile_reviewer_worktrees` (lines 58-73) correctly calls `dispose_reviewers_for_pr` → `dispose_agent_resources` for each merged/closed PR. **Working.**
- `reconcile_issue_worktrees` (lines 31-56) detects a closed chainlink issue for a live worktree, calls `append_issue_closed_event` (writes to `.exo/events/issue_closed.jsonl`), and **stops there**. It does NOT call `dispose_agent_resources` for the dev-leaf slug.

Grep confirms `.exo/events/issue_closed.jsonl` has only writers in the codebase (`orphan_reconciler.rs:148` and `merge_pr_local.rs:469`) — no readers. Nothing consumes the jsonl to fire the WASM `IssueClosed` event. So the dev-leaf worktree stays orphaned indefinitely even after the reconciler "notices" the closed issue.

## Fix

In `reconcile_issue_worktrees`, alongside the existing `append_issue_closed_event` call, also call `dispose_agent_resources(project_dir, git_wt.clone(), &slug).await`. The event log remains for idempotency (already checked at line 47); the disposal does the actual cleanup.

Requires plumbing `git_wt: Arc<GitWorktreeService>` into `reconcile_issue_worktrees` (today only `reconcile_reviewer_worktrees` receives it from `reconcile_once`).

## Files to touch

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs`:
  - Add `use crate::services::agent_resources::dispose_agent_resources;` to the imports.
  - Change `reconcile_issue_worktrees` signature to `(project_dir: &Path, git_wt: Arc<GitWorktreeService>)`.
  - After `append_issue_closed_event`, call `dispose_agent_resources(project_dir, git_wt.clone(), &slug).await`.
  - Update `reconcile_once` to clone `git_wt` when passing to `reconcile_issue_worktrees`.

## Tests

- Unit: existing tests at lines 161-184 cover slug parsing, chainlink output parsing, and idempotency — still pass.
- Manual verification: create a worktree dir for an agent whose chainlink issue is closed; run one reconciler tick; assert the worktree and agent dir are removed.

## Done criteria

- Dev-leaf worktrees disposed within one reconciler tick of their assigned issue closing via any path (bash CLI, manual sqlite edit, etc.).
- Event log remains as the idempotency check (don't re-fire IssueClosed for the same issue).
- No regression in reviewer reconciliation path.

## Why medium not high

The primary disposal paths (MCP `chainlink_issue_close` → IssueClosed event from #302, and `merge_pr_local` post-merge cleanup) cover the common cases. The reconciler is the safety net for bash-CLI bypass and operator manual edits — both of which are now also blocked structurally by #310. So this gap is real but narrowly exposed.

issues.title: tmux inject_input: Enter keystroke sometimes dropped; agent receives paste but never submits
issues.description:
Roger observed 2026-05-19: tmux messages get pasted into agent panes but the Enter keystroke doesn't always execute the submission. Text sits visible in the agent's input box waiting for a human to hit Enter manually. Affects message delivery to Claude Code, Codex, and likely OpenCode panes alike.

This is a runtime correctness bug in the only fallback delivery path we have for inter-agent messaging. When it fires, messages are silently undelivered — they're visible in the pane but the agent's model never sees them.

## Current injection sequence

`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs:412-554` (`inject_input`):

1. Acquire per-target `INJECTION_LOCKS` mutex.
2. If pane in copy/scroll mode: cancel + 50ms sleep.
3. Write payload (trailing newlines stripped) to `/tmp/exomonad_buf_<uuid>`.
4. `tmux load-buffer -b <buf> <tmp>`.
5. `tmux paste-buffer -b <buf> -t <qualified-target>`.
6. `tmux delete-buffer`.
7. Sleep **150 ms** (fixed debounce).
8. `tmux send-keys -t <target> Enter` (with 3-attempt linear backoff @ 200 ms).
9. `wake_pane` (SIGWINCH) — AFTER Enter, non-fatal.

## Why the retry doesn't catch this

`send-keys` returns success once tmux has written the Enter keystroke to the pane's PTY. The retry policy at line 523-545 only fires on `send-keys` itself errroring. If the TUI was mid-render or hadn't yet processed the pasted bytes when the Enter arrived, the Enter is silently dropped by the TUI's input handler — tmux reports success, retry never triggers.

## Likely root causes

1. **Paste-to-Enter race.** The 150 ms debounce is shorter than some TUI render cycles, especially Codex on heavier panes. Bytes from `paste-buffer` are still in flight through the PTY when Enter is sent.
2. **`send-keys` success ≠ TUI ingestion.** Tmux returning 0 only confirms byte-write to the PTY, not that the application accepted the keystroke. The retry policy guards the wrong layer.
3. **SIGWINCH wake happens AFTER Enter, not before.** Line 549 — if the pane's TUI was parked/idle, waking it after the Enter means the Enter arrived during a dormant input loop.
4. **Multi-line paste edge case.** Payloads with embedded `\n` may put the TUI into multi-line input mode where the first Enter inserts a newline rather than submitting. We strip *trailing* newlines (line 462) but not internal ones.

## Investigation tasks

- Instrument `inject_input` to log: paste-buffer wall-clock duration, time between paste-buffer return and Enter send, total bytes pasted.
- Reproduce against a Codex pane with a known-multiline message (~500 char, contains `\n`). Compare against single-line ≤80 char message. Measure failure rate per payload shape.
- Capture pane content via `tmux capture-pane -p -t <target>` after the Enter send and after a 500 ms wait. Compare. If the payload text is still in the input box after the wait, the Enter was dropped.

## Proposed fix shape (pick after investigation)

**Option A (post-Enter verification, recommended):** After step 8, sleep ~300 ms and capture-pane. If the last N lines still contain the payload text (indicating it's still in the input box, not consumed), send Enter again. Bounded retry (max 3 confirmations). True self-healing — works regardless of root cause.

**Option B (SIGWINCH before Enter):** Move `wake_pane` from line 549 to BEFORE the Enter send. Wakes the TUI event loop, then Enter arrives to a listening handler.

**Option C (defensive double-Enter):** Send Enter, sleep 100 ms, send Enter again. Risks phantom empty submission on TUIs that accept the first one but ignore the second (most TUIs are tolerant — empty submit at idle prompt is a no-op).

**Option D (adaptive debounce):** Replace fixed 150 ms with payload-size-aware sleep. Larger pastes get longer settle time.

A + B together is probably the right combination: SIGWINCH-then-Enter as the primary path; post-Enter capture-pane verification as the safety net.

## Files to touch

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/tmux_ipc.rs` — modify `inject_input` per the chosen fix.
- New helper: `verify_input_consumed(target, payload) -> bool` that captures the pane and checks if the payload text is still in the input area.

## Tests

- Unit: mock `Command::new("tmux")` to return success but simulate "Enter eaten" by leaving payload visible in capture-pane output. Assert retry kicks in.
- Integration: launch a real Codex pane in an E2E test, inject a multi-line payload, assert the agent's model actually processed it (verifiable via `notify_parent` echo or similar).

## Done criteria

- `inject_input` either confirms Enter was consumed or retries until it is (or fails loudly after N attempts — silent failure is the worst outcome).
- Logs distinguish "Enter sent but not consumed" from "Enter send failed" from "Enter consumed successfully."
- Test coverage for Codex, Claude Code, and (when integrated) OpenCode panes.
- Harness-agnostic: the fix must work for every TUI we deliver to, not be Codex-specific.

## Related

- Per-runtime hook policy (#308) is a separate concern but same priority class — both are about runtime parity across agent harnesses.
- This delivery path is the fallback for Teams inbox / ACP / UDS routes. If those primary paths work, this bug is invisible; but for any agent that can't receive via the primary path (workers, Codex agents without Teams support), it's the only path.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: background orphan reconciler — periodic safety net for missed close paths
issues.description:
Even with #310 (bash chainlink CLI block) in place, there will always be paths that bypass the WASM dispatch: future tooling, operator manual edits to chainlink sqlite, third-party integrations, agents using a runtime we haven't sandboxed yet. This issue adds the runtime safety net: a background reconciler that periodically detects orphan worktrees and fires `IssueClosed` events for any chainlink issue whose live agent is still around.

## Behavior

A new tokio task in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/` running on a configurable interval (default: 60s).

Each tick:

1. Enumerate live agents from `.exo/worktrees/{slug}/` and the agent registry.
2. For each agent, resolve its assigned chainlink issue id (from `EXOMONAD_ISSUE_ID` env, agent registry, or chainlink session-work record).
3. Query chainlink for the status of each assigned issue: `chainlink_issue_show {id}`.
4. For any agent whose assigned issue is `closed`: fire the `IssueClosed` event into the event router. This is exactly the same event #302 already wires; the reconciler is just an alternative trigger source. Existing handlers do the rest (`DevDismissed` transition + `dispose_agent_resources`).
5. Log every reconciliation action with the original close-path attribution if knowable ("issue closed by bash CLI", "issue closed by operator at sqlite layer", "unknown").

## Symmetric reviewer reconciliation

Same tick should also sweep reviewer worktrees against PR state — peer of #311's post-merge sweep but as a periodic safety net instead of a single-shot at merge time. Enumerate `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-{N}-*`, look up PR #N in `.exo/prs.json`, and if `state=merged|closed`, dispose. This catches reviewers whose verdict-write event delivery was missed.

## Files to touch

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/orphan_reconciler.rs` — new service.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/mod.rs` — register.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/lib.rs` (or `serve.rs`) — spawn the reconciler task at server startup.
- `.exo/config.toml` — add `orphan_reconciler_interval_secs = 60` (optional override).

## Tests

- Unit (Rust): simulate orphan state — create a worktree dir for an agent whose chainlink issue is `closed`. Run one reconciler tick. Assert IssueClosed event was emitted.
- Integration: spawn a dev-leaf, close its issue via bash (or simulate by directly closing in chainlink sqlite). Within `interval` seconds, the worktree, tmux window, and agent dir are all gone.
- Integration: reviewer worktree exists for a merged PR. Within `interval` seconds, reviewer is disposed.

## Relationship to other issues

- **#302** — same disposal path, alternative trigger. Reconciler IS the safety net for #302's primary trigger.
- **#310** — primary fix (block bash bypass). Reconciler covers everything else.
- **#311** — reconciler's reviewer sweep is the periodic version of #311's one-shot post-merge sweep.
- **#312** — ADR addendum references this issue.

## Done criteria

- Background reconciler runs at configurable interval.
- Orphan dev-leaves disposed within one tick of their issue closing via any path.
- Orphan reviewers disposed within one tick of their PR merging/closing.
- Logs attribute the close path when knowable.
- Doesn't fire IssueClosed for issues that haven't actually closed (no false positives).

issues.title: ADR addendum: close bash-CLI carve-out in agent-lifecycle-invariants.md
issues.description:
The agent-lifecycle invariants ADR at `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` carved out bash-CLI close paths as out of scope: *"bash closes are operator escape hatches and the operator carries the responsibility."* That framing was wrong once AI operators became the primary callers — observed in nemotron-port 2026-05-19 where the TL used bash `chainlink issue close 7` to work around the round-counting bug, bypassing the IssueClosed event and producing an orphan dev-leaf.

Issue #310 (bash chainlink CLI block) closes the loophole structurally. This issue is the paired docs update.

## Files to touch

`docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` — under "Out of scope":

**Remove** this bullet:

> Bash-CLI close paths. Closing issues from raw bash bypasses the WASM dispatch and the precondition. Leaves are never created from bash-CLI workflows, so this is acceptable: bash closes are operator escape hatches and the operator carries the responsibility.

**Replace with** a forward-reference:

> Bash-CLI close paths were initially carved out as operator escape hatches. Observed orphan storm 2026-05-19 (nemotron-port: TL closed issues via bash `chainlink issue close` to work around a separate bug, producing orphan leaves and reviewers because the IssueClosed event never fired) showed AI operators reach for whatever runs. The carve-out is closed by **#310** (block bash chainlink mutating verbs) and **{this issue}'s sibling polling-reconciler safety net**. The runtime now refuses bash mutating close paths and reconciles any that slip through.

Update the "Implementation tracking" table at the bottom to add #310, #311, and the polling-reconciler issue.

## Done criteria

- The "Bash-CLI close" carve-out bullet is gone from "Out of scope."
- A short paragraph in its place explains what changed and why, with chainlink cross-references.
- Implementation tracking table reflects #310, #311, polling-reconciler issue.
- No other invariant text needs to change — the three invariants themselves are still correct.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: reviewer ephemerality — terminate after verdict write, not idle indefinitely
issues.description:
Reviewers are currently spawned and **persist indefinitely** after writing their verdict. Observed 2026-05-19 in nemotron-port: reviewers for PR #1, #2, #3, #4 are all still alive at Codex idle prompts, holding worktrees and tmux windows, after their PRs merged hours ago.

Worktrees that should be gone:
- `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-1-codex/` (PR #1 merged)
- `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-2-codex/` (PR #2 merged)
- `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-3-codex/` (PR #3 merged)
- `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-4-codex/` (PR #4 merged)

Reviewer cleanup is not covered by #302 — that invariant binds dev-leaf lifecycle to chainlink issue state. The reviewer's natural binding is to **PR state**, not issue state, and the reviewer is structurally a one-shot review function, not a persistent agent waiting for events.

## Invariant

A reviewer agent terminates immediately after writing its verdict to `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json`. No idle prompt, no event loop, no awaiting follow-ups. If the dev pushes fixes, a fresh reviewer instance spawns for that round (same model as workers).

## Why ephemeral, not persistent

The reviewer's job is bounded: read the diff, run any verification, write a verdict, exit. State machine `ReviewerPhase` already supports this — the terminal state is reached as soon as `approve_pr` / `request_changes` writes to `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json`. The current bug is that the runtime doesn't tear the agent down when the verdict lands.

Persistent reviewers also create a stuck-loop risk: if a reviewer somehow misses an event delivery, it sits at the idle prompt forever (which is exactly what we're seeing now across PRs #1-4).

## Mechanism

Two complementary paths, mirroring #302/#303:

1. **Verdict-write triggers self-termination.** The `approve_pr` / `request_changes` / `post_review_comment` tool handlers in `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs` already `applyEvent` to transition the ReviewerPhase. Extend that path to also fire a `ReviewerVerdictRecorded` world event after the verdict write succeeds. The reviewer's own event handler matches the event and triggers `dispose_agent_resources(project_dir, "review-pr-{N}-codex")` via the shared helper from #302.

2. **PR state change as a safety net.** When `merge_pr_local` succeeds (or a PR is closed via any path), iterate over `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-{pr_number}-*` and call `dispose_agent_resources` on each. This catches the case where the reviewer's self-termination missed (event drop, agent crashed mid-write, etc.).

## Files to touch

- `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs` — extend `approve_pr`/`request_changes`/`post_review_comment` handlers to fire `ReviewerVerdictRecorded` after successful verdict write. Add the corresponding event handler that calls into `dispose_agent_resources`.
- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Events.hs` — add `ReviewerVerdictRecorded` event type.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/merge_pr_local.rs` — after successful merge, glob `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-{N}-*` and dispose. Non-fatal if missing (reviewer may have already self-terminated).
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/` — wire the new event through the WASM dispatch path (peer of `IssueClosed`).
- `.exo/lib/ReviewerPhase.hs` — confirm the state machine terminal already exists after verdict; add a `ReviewerDismissed` if a clean terminal-after-disposal isn't already present.

## Tests

- Unit (Haskell): reviewer event handler transitions to dismissed on `ReviewerVerdictRecorded`.
- Unit (Rust): `merge_pr_local` post-merge sweep removes reviewer worktrees matching the PR number.
- Integration: spawn reviewer → reviewer writes approve verdict → assert worktree, tmux window, and agent dir are removed within one event-router tick.
- Integration: simulate missed self-termination (skip the event) → assert the post-merge sweep catches it.

## Interaction with other in-flight work

- **#302 (IssueClosed event)** — same `dispose_agent_resources` helper, same shape. Different trigger (PR state vs issue state).
- **#298/#299/#300 (reviewer authorship invariants)** — reviewer ephemerality reinforces these: an ephemeral reviewer that lives only long enough to write a verdict file has minimal opportunity to mutate authorship even if the OS sandbox (#309) is bypassed.
- **#309 (agent-sandbox)** — reviewer profile can be more aggressive when the agent is short-lived. `:read-only` plus `target/` writes for cargo test runs is plenty for a one-shot review.
- **#310 (bash chainlink CLI block)** — reviewer doesn't use chainlink at all (no row in agent-system.md matrix for reviewer × chainlink_*), so #310 has no interaction here.

## Done criteria

- Reviewer terminates within one event-router tick of writing its verdict.
- Post-merge sweep in `merge_pr_local` is a safety net that catches missed self-terminations.
- Existing E2E suites pass with the new ephemerality (no regression in review-round flows that spawn fresh reviewers for follow-up rounds).
- The reviewer's persistent-idle state is no longer reachable in normal operation.

issues.title: Block bash chainlink CLI mutating verbs; force MCP-only actuation
issues.description:
The chainlink CLI is implicitly trusted today — agents can run `chainlink issue close N` from bash and the close silently bypasses every WASM-dispatched enforcement we have:

- No `IssueClosed` event fires → dev-leaf disposal (#302) doesn't trigger → orphan leaves hold worktrees forever.
- No dirty-tree precondition (#304) → issues close on dirty trees.
- No provenance trace in OTel/logs → we lose attribution.

Observed 2026-05-19 in nemotron-port: TL closed issue #7 via bash `chainlink issue close` (to work around the round-counting bug). Dev-leaf for issue #7 is now orphaned in `.exo/worktrees/issue-7-decoder-pred-joiner-codex/` with no tmux window — the merge happened but the leaf-disposal cascade never fired because the close path wasn't MCP.

Same shape as the existing `blockGhCommand` in `.exo/lib/HookPolicy.hs:19` — gh CLI is blocked because we have `file_pr`/`merge_pr` MCP equivalents. The same trust gap exists for chainlink and needs the same closure.

## Codified principle

> If an MCP tool exists for an operation, the CLI form of that operation is blocked at the hook layer for any role that has the MCP tool. Read-only CLI verbs (those with no side effects on the orchestration graph) remain allowed.

This generalizes the existing gh block. It should be invoked by name in any future CLI/MCP collision (git merge vs merge_pr, etc.).

## Deny set for chainlink

Block these mutating verbs across all roles (TL/root/dev/worker/reviewer):

- `chainlink issue close|create|update|block|relate|comment`
- `chainlink subissue close|create`
- `chainlink session work|end`
- `chainlink timer start|stop`
- `chainlink milestone create`

Allow (read-only):

- `chainlink issue show|list|search`
- `chainlink session status`
- `chainlink timer show|list`

## Files to touch

- `.exo/lib/HookPolicy.hs` — add `blockChainlinkCLICommand` mirroring `blockGhCommand`. Token-scan the bash command (reuse `shellTokenSeparator`). Extract the chainlink verb after `chainlink` (handling `chainlink issue close` two-token form).
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/{TLRole,DevRole,WorkerRole,ReviewerRole,RootRole}.hs` — extend the `preToolUse` chain to invoke the new block. Same way `preToolUseWithGhBlock` is composed.
- Per-runtime dispatch through #308's `implementerToolsFor` / `shellWritePatternsFor` infrastructure: the bash hook fires for Codex `shell` and Claude `Bash` identically; the verb extraction logic is runtime-agnostic.

## Deny message

> BLOCKED: chainlink CLI mutating verbs are not allowed from agents — they bypass the IssueClosed event, dirty-tree precondition, and provenance trace. Use the chainlink_* MCP tool equivalents instead. Read-only CLI (show/list/search/status) remains available for inspection.

## Tests

- HookPolicy unit tests covering each verb in the deny and allow sets.
- E2E: TL attempts bash `chainlink issue close 1` → denied. TL calls `chainlink_issue_close` MCP tool → succeeds and fires IssueClosed (existing #302 path).
- E2E: dev-leaf attempts bash `chainlink session end` → denied. Calls MCP equivalent → routes through worker stop hook (#304 precondition).

## Rollout dependency

This depends on chainlink MCP tools being **reliable across all runtimes**. The 2026-05-19 dev-leaf for #97 reported *"Issue #97 not found despite session work 97 succeeding"* via MCP and fell back to bash. If we deny bash before that bug is fixed, agents get stuck mid-session. File and verify a separate `chainlink-mcp-reliability` investigation issue before rolling this out as a hard deny. Soft rollout option: log warnings on bash chainlink mutating verbs for one test session, see what breaks, then flip to hard deny.

## Done criteria

- `blockChainlinkCLICommand` in HookPolicy.hs.
- Applied to all five roles via preToolUse composition.
- Per-runtime aware via #308's infrastructure (no Claude/Codex-specific code paths).
- Unit + E2E tests cover both deny and allow sets.
- ADR addendum to `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` removes the "bash-CLI close is out of scope" carve-out and points here.

issues.title: agent-sandbox: role-aware Codex permissions profiles with write-path investigation
issues.description:
Codex has native filesystem sandboxing via `default_permissions` in `.codex/config.toml`. We are currently not using it for any role — every spawned Codex agent gets the default profile (effectively unrestricted writes within its worktree). This is the primary structural cause of:

- TL/root agents editing source files despite the documented Edit deny (observed 2026-05-19 in nemotron-port: Codex TL edited `.exo/review-policy.toml` directly).
- Reviewers being able to author commits (reviewer-authorship invariant from #298 unenforceable against Codex).

OS-level filesystem sandboxing is strictly superior to tool-name hook denies because:
- The kernel refuses the write — no string matching needed.
- Closes the entire class of "shell-mediated writes" (`cat > foo`, base64-pipe, python -c, etc.) that any hook deny would have to enumerate.
- Composable with our existing MCP path — MCP tools execute in the Rust runtime process outside the agent's sandbox, so `file_pr`, `merge_pr`, chainlink writes continue to work even with the agent's filesystem locked down.

## Decision

Extend `rust/exomonad-core/src/codex_config.rs` to render role-aware `[permissions.<role>]` blocks and `default_permissions = "<role>"` into every spawned Codex agent's `.codex/config.toml`. Define one profile per role following the principle of least privilege.

## Investigation phase (do this first)

Roger flagged: we do not know a priori the full set of write paths each role needs. Best-practice isolation requires enumerating these before writing the profiles.

For each role + common workflow, catalog every write the agent needs to make outside its `.git/` and `.exo/` paths. Use `strace -fe trace=openat,creat,unlink,rename` (or `fs_usage` on macOS) against a real run.

Workflows to cover:
- **TL / root**: spawning agents, calling MCP tools (file_pr, merge_pr), chainlink session ops, reading source files for spec writing, `git fetch` / `git status` / `git log`.
- **Reviewer**: reading the PR diff, running build/test (`cargo check`, `cargo test`, `just build`, `nix develop` shells), writing reviews to `.exo/reviews/`, running `gh pr view` against local PR registry.
- **Dev-leaf**: full source-tree write, build, test, commit, push.
- **Worker**: same as dev-leaf for the parent worktree.

Output of the investigation: a markdown table at `docs/decisions/agent-sandbox-profiles.md` mapping each role to its minimal write set, with the strace evidence.

## Proposed profile shapes (starting points; verify in investigation)

```toml
# TL / root: read-everywhere, write only to .exo/ and .git/ (for git fetch index updates)
[permissions.tl]
filesystem.":project_roots" = "read"
filesystem.":project_roots".".exo" = "write"
filesystem.":project_roots".".git" = "write"

# Reviewer: read-everywhere, write only to build artifact paths and .exo/reviews/
[permissions.reviewer]
filesystem.":project_roots" = "read"
filesystem.":project_roots".".exo/reviews" = "write"
filesystem.":project_roots"."target" = "write"
filesystem.":project_roots"."dist" = "write"
filesystem.":project_roots".".cache" = "write"
filesystem.":project_roots".".pytest_cache" = "write"
filesystem.":project_roots".".git" = "write"   # for git fetch
# Cargo registry/cache lives in $HOME/.cargo, outside :project_roots — works by default

# Dev-leaf and worker: full workspace write (current behavior)
[permissions.dev]
filesystem.":project_roots" = "write"

[permissions.worker]
filesystem.":project_roots" = "write"
```

## Reviewer tradeoff Roger flagged

Pure `:read-only` blocks `cargo check`/`cargo test`, which the reviewer often needs to verify a PR. The starting profile above grants writes only to build-artifact directories. Investigation must confirm:
- Does cargo write to anything outside `target/` and `$HOME/.cargo/`?
- Do test runs need `/tmp` writes? (Likely yes — should be allowed.)
- Does `nix develop` need writes outside the project? (Likely yes — `/nix/var/nix/profiles/per-user/<user>/` and similar.)

Where the standard build tooling needs writes outside the project, those go in the profile too. If reviewer-side `cargo` proves impractical to sandbox cleanly, document that explicitly and pick: (a) accept slightly broader writes for the reviewer, (b) move reviewer test runs into an MCP tool the Rust runtime executes outside the sandbox.

## Files to touch

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/codex_config.rs` — render the `[permissions.<role>]` block + `default_permissions = "<role>"` based on the agent's role.
- `docs/decisions/agent-sandbox-profiles.md` — new ADR documenting the investigation findings, the chosen profiles, the role/write-path matrix, and the tradeoff rationale for each role.
- `docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md` — cross-reference the new sandbox ADR; note that the worker self-commit invariant (#304) interacts with the worker's `write` permission (must keep `:project_roots` writable for that to function).

## Tests

- Unit (Rust): `codex_config.rs` snapshot tests asserting each role renders the correct TOML block.
- Smoke (E2E): each E2E test (`just e2e-messaging`, `just e2e-tangled-ci`, etc.) re-run with the new profiles. Assert no false-positive denials in normal operation. This is the regression suite for the investigation phase.
- Negative test: confirm that a TL Codex agent attempting `apply_patch` against a source file fails at the OS layer with the sandbox error, not silently succeeds.

## Done criteria

- Investigation ADR at `docs/decisions/agent-sandbox-profiles.md` with strace evidence and the role-to-write-paths matrix.
- `codex_config.rs` renders role-aware permissions blocks.
- All four roles have a defined profile.
- Existing E2E tests pass under the new profiles (or are explicitly updated to reflect the intended behavior).
- Negative test demonstrates source-file writes are blocked for TL/root/reviewer.
- This issue's outcome supersedes the runtime-tool-name deny for Codex (the deny stays for Claude as defense-in-depth per #308).

## Relationship to other issues

- #298 (reviewer Edit deny) — sandbox makes this automatic for Codex reviewers. Keep #298 for the Claude path.
- #308 (per-runtime hook policy) — complementary defense-in-depth for Claude where no sandbox exists.
- #304 (worker self-commit + clean-tree precondition) — depends on workers retaining `:project_roots = "write"`. Confirmed in the profile sketch above.

issues.title: Per-runtime hook policy modules: replace Claude-only deny with runtime-aware dispatch
issues.description:
The TL/reviewer/root PreToolUse deny lists (`.exo/roles/devswarm/TLRole.hs:83`, future #298 reviewer equivalent) contain only Claude Code tool names: `Edit`, `Write`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit`. Codex agents in those roles slip past the deny because they emit different canonical tool names (`apply_patch`, `shell` for writes via `cat > / tee / python -c "open"`). OpenCode is next and brings its own tool name set. Today the deny is silently Claude-only.

Observed 2026-05-19 in nemotron-port session: TL (gpt-5.5 Codex) edited `.exo/review-policy.toml` directly to relax the merge gate, despite TL Edit/Write deny supposedly being in place. Pane caption shows the Codex runtime; the deny passed through because `apply_patch` ≠ any name in `tlImplementerTools`.

## Decision

Replace the single Claude-only deny list with **per-runtime policy modules** dispatched by the `--runtime` flag already passed to `exomonad hook` (per `docs/decisions/codex-hook-wire-format.md`).

This is **defense in depth** — the primary enforcement should be OS-level Codex sandboxing (separate chainlink issue under `agent-sandbox`). Hook policy stays useful for:
- Claude agents (which don't have an OS sandbox of their own; PreToolUse is the canonical mechanism).
- Friendlier deny messages (the redispatch nudge text) that the OS sandbox can't surface.
- OpenCode agents until their sandboxing story is understood.

## Files to touch

- `.exo/lib/HookPolicy.hs` — refactor `tlImplementerTools` and the future reviewer equivalent into per-runtime policy tables. Resolve the runtime from `HookInput` (the `--runtime` flag value should land in the hook payload).
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/TLRole.hs:83` — replace `tlImplementerTools` with a call into `HookPolicy.implementerToolsFor(runtime)`.
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs` (when #298 lands) — same pattern.
- Add per-runtime tables in HookPolicy.hs:

```haskell
implementerToolsFor :: Runtime -> [Text]
implementerToolsFor Claude   = ["Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"]
implementerToolsFor Codex    = ["apply_patch", "str_replace_editor", "edit_file"]
implementerToolsFor OpenCode = ["edit", "write", "patch"]  -- placeholder; verify against OpenCode docs
implementerToolsFor Gemini   = []  -- read-only by default in current spawn config
```

- Add a `shellWritePatternsFor :: Runtime -> [Pattern]` that catches `shell`-tool writes that the canonical tool list doesn't cover:
  - `cat > foo`, `tee foo`, `>> foo` redirections
  - `python -c "...open(...,'w'/'a'/'x')..."`
  - `printf ... > foo`, `echo ... > foo`
- Token-scan applied through `preToolUseWithGhBlock` (or a new `preToolUseWithWriteBlock`) when the tool is `shell` and the runtime allows shell-mediated writes.

## OpenCode placeholder

OpenCode tool names are TBD pending integration. The structure must make it trivial to add the OpenCode row without touching role configs. Roger flagged this is coming up — file a small follow-up issue to verify OpenCode tool names against its actual tool schema once the integration is live.

## Tests

- `HookPolicy` unit tests covering each runtime:
  - Claude: `Edit` denied, `apply_patch` allowed (correct — Claude doesn't emit `apply_patch`).
  - Codex: `apply_patch` denied, `Edit` allowed (correct — Codex doesn't emit `Edit`).
  - Codex `shell` with `cat > foo`: denied.
  - Codex `shell` with `cat foo`: allowed.
  - OpenCode: stubbed per the row above.

## Done criteria

- Per-runtime policy tables in HookPolicy.hs.
- TL/Reviewer/Root preToolUse hooks dispatch by runtime.
- Codex-style writes via `apply_patch` and `shell` redirections blocked for TL/Reviewer/Root.
- All four runtimes have a row in the table (OpenCode and Gemini can be empty arrays initially with TODOs).
- `cabal test all` passes including new HookPolicy cases.
- TL/Reviewer redispatch messages are runtime-aware (mention the right tool name in the deny text).

## Out of scope

- The OS-level sandbox approach (filed separately under `agent-sandbox`). That is the structural fix; this issue is the belt-and-braces for runtimes without a sandbox path.
- Verifying real OpenCode tool names — that's a follow-up after OpenCode hook integration is live.

issues.title: Fix install-all-dev compile error
Update documentation for leaf lifecycle hardening
E2E test: agent lifecycle invariants (deferred)
issues.description:
Once #302, #303, and #304 land, we should have an end-to-end test exercising the agent-lifecycle invariants from docs/decisions/agent-lifecycle-invariants.md. Explicitly deferred — Roger does not have time to flesh out another E2E in the near term. This issue is the placeholder so the gap is tracked. Same pattern as #301 (the deferred reviewer-hardening E2E).

## Scope when picked up

A new `tests/e2e/lifecycle/` test following the existing E2E pattern (see `tests/e2e/messaging/` as the reference structure).

## Phases to cover

1. **Orphan-leaf disposal (#302)** — Spawn a dev-leaf, have it commit a benign change so its worktree is clean, then close its assigned chainlink issue from outside the leaf's session. Assert: leaf transitions to `DevDismissed` within one event-router tick; worktree, tmux window, agent dir, and branch are all removed by `dispose_agent_resources`.

2. **`dispose_leaf` wrapper (#303)** — Spawn a leaf, leave its worktree clean. TL calls `dispose_leaf {name, reason}`. Assert: chainlink issue closes with the reason in the note; same cleanup as phase 1 fires via the IssueClosed event; tool refuses on unknown name and on PR-in-flight states.

3. **Worker self-commit (#304, invariant 2)** — Spawn a worker that modifies a file. Worker attempts `chainlink session end` → refused with the file list in the error. Worker commits → session end allowed. Inspect the commit: `git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'` must equal `exomonad-{worker-name} <{worker-name}@exomonad.local>` (invariant 3).

4. **Dirty-tree close refusal (#304, invariant 2)** — TL's worktree has uncommitted changes (worker abandoned them). TL calls `chainlink_issue_close` → refused with the file list. TL calls `discard_worker_output {reason}` → working tree clean, reason logged. TL retries the close → succeeds.

5. **Dispose with force (#304 + #303)** — Leaf worktree has uncommitted changes worth keeping nothing about. TL calls `dispose_leaf {name, reason, force: false}` → refused. TL calls with `force: true` → succeeds; the discarded file list is captured in the chainlink session note for traceability.

## Companion layout

- Test subject: a worker (with a unique git identity) and a dev-leaf in its own worktree.
- Testrunner: Claude haiku, observes via read-only bash (`git log`, `tmux list-windows`, `chainlink issue show`), reports via `notify_parent`.

## Done criteria

- `just e2e-lifecycle` runs all five phases in a temp repo and reports pass/fail.
- Worker commits carry worker identity, not TL identity.
- Orphan leaves clean themselves up on issue close.
- Dirty-tree close paths are uniformly refused with actionable error messages.
- Force paths log discarded files.

## Why low priority

The unit and integration tests added in #302/#303/#304 already cover each invariant individually. The E2E provides composite verification — useful but not on the critical path. Roger's time is better spent on feature work until an E2E investment makes sense.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: refuse issue close + worktree teardown on uncommitted state
issues.description:
Workers can today run in the TL's worktree, modify files, end their chainlink session, and walk away leaving uncommitted changes. The TL can then close the issue with the worker's modifications still dirty in `git status`. Work either gets accidentally swept into a future unrelated commit, lost to a `git restore`, or rots until someone notices. Same risk applies on dev-leaf dismissal from #302 — tearing down a worktree with uncommitted changes silently destroys work.

## Invariant

A chainlink issue may not be closed (and a worktree may not be removed) while any modifications exist in the relevant worktree. Workers commit their own output under their own identity before session end; dev-leaves either commit or explicitly discard before dismissal. Strict and simple — no per-file provenance tracking, no diffing against session start, just `git status --porcelain` of the calling agent's CWD.

## Why CWD-of-caller is the natural "relevant worktree"

- **Worker case**: worker runs in TL's worktree. TL calls `chainlink_issue_close N` from its own CWD. The TL's worktree has the worker's dirty state. Check fires.
- **Dev-leaf case**: leaf runs in its own `.exo/worktrees/{name}/`. By the time `merge_pr_local` reaches the close step, the leaf's branch is already merged into the TL's branch and the leaf's worktree is removed. Check happens in TL's CWD, which is clean post-merge. Passes trivially.
- **Dispose/dismissal case (#302)**: refusal happens at the close layer before the IssueClosed event fires, so the dismissal path inherits the precondition for free.

No provenance tracking needed. Whoever calls the close gets checked in their own CWD.

## Worker self-commit (Layer A: source of correctness)

Wire a stop hook into the worker role (`.exo/roles/devswarm/WorkerRole.hs`):

```haskell
workerStopCheck :: Eff Effects StopHookOutput
workerStopCheck = do
  status <- runGitStatus  -- new effect, or shell out via process effect
  if T.null status
    then pure allowStopResponse
    else pure $ blockStopResponse $
      "Worker has uncommitted changes:\n" <> status <>
      "\nCommit under your own identity (`git add . && git commit -m \"...\"`) " <>
      "or discard explicitly via `discard_worker_output` before ending the session."
```

So the worker cannot exit clean while the tree is dirty. To make commit authorship correct (mirror #298–#300): the agent spawn path (`spawn_worker` in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/`) sets `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME` and `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL` env vars from the worker's identity (`exomonad-{agent-name}` / `{agent-name}@exomonad.local`). Worker's `git commit` picks them up automatically without `--author` discipline.

## Close precondition (Layer B: safety net)

`chainlink_issue_close` MCP tool (or whichever wrapper invokes the close — see #302's note on emitting IssueClosed from this path):

```haskell
closeIssue args = do
  status <- runGitStatusInCwd
  if not (T.null status)
    then pure $ errorResult $
      "Cannot close issue #" <> showT (issueId args) <>
      ": uncommitted changes in this worktree:\n" <> status <>
      "\nCommit, discard, or use `discard_worker_output` first."
    else proceedWithClose args
```

## Escape hatch: `discard_worker_output`

New TL-only MCP tool for the case where worker output is genuinely throwaway and the TL wants to close the issue without keeping the changes:

```
discard_worker_output { reason: string }
```

Behavior: `git restore .` + `git clean -fd` in the TL's CWD (the only callable context). Logs the reason. Idempotent. Refuses if HEAD has uncommitted *staged* changes (i.e., don't destroy work that the TL deliberately staged). Roger flagged the triggering case is rare but real; this is the named escape hatch so people don't reach for raw `git restore` and lose track.

## Interaction with #302/#303

- `dispose_leaf` (#303) inherits the precondition because it routes through the close path. If the leaf's worktree is dirty, dispose refuses. Add a `force: bool` flag for the genuine-orphan case (leaf hung, no recoverable work), defaulting to false. Force-dismissal logs the discarded file list to chainlink as a session note.
- The IssueClosed event (#302) only fires *after* the close succeeds, so a refused close means no dismissal, no worktree teardown, no lost work.

## Tests

- Unit: worker stop hook with clean vs dirty `git status`.
- Unit: close-issue handler with clean vs dirty CWD; verify error message includes file list.
- Unit: `discard_worker_output` clears the right files, refuses on staged changes.
- Integration: worker modifies a file, attempts `chainlink session end` → refused; commits → allowed; TL then closes the issue successfully.
- Integration: dispose_leaf on dirty leaf worktree → refused without force; with `force: true` → succeeds and notes discarded files.

## Done criteria

- Worker stop hook refuses session end on dirty worktree.
- Worker spawn path injects GIT_AUTHOR_* env vars so worker commits carry worker identity.
- `chainlink_issue_close` (and any path that closes an issue) refuses on dirty CWD with the file list in the error.
- `discard_worker_output` MCP tool exists, TL-only, refuses on staged changes.
- `dispose_leaf` (#303) honors the precondition with a `force` flag.
- Tests cover both layers and the escape hatch.

## Out of scope

- Tracking per-issue file provenance. Strict-and-simple wins; if multi-worker TLs become common we cross that bridge then.
- Forcing the TL itself to commit before closing — the TL never has the "did the worker mean to commit this?" knowledge problem since the worker now self-commits. The TL only sees clean state.
- Stash-and-cherrypick workflows for parallel workers in one TL. Parallelization is dev-leaf turf; workers stay sequential and one-off.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: dispose_leaf MCP tool (belt-and-braces wrapper)
issues.description:
The IssueClosed event from #302 makes dev-leaf disposal automatic when an issue closes. This issue adds the explicit TL-facing wrapper: a `dispose_leaf` MCP tool that closes the chainlink issue and ends the leaf in one call, for the cases where the TL wants to end a leaf without thinking about issue state.

Depends on #302 (the event + state machine + cleanup helper must exist first).

## Files to touch

- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/DisposeLeaf.hs` — new tool definition.
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/TLRole.hs` — register `DisposeLeaf` in the TL tool set (alongside `TLMergePR`, `TLForkWave`, etc.).
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/RootRole.hs` — register in root role too if root needs the same authority.
- Effect side: a new `dispose_leaf.*` effect namespace handled in Rust, or compose existing effects (chainlink close + agent cleanup) inside the Haskell handler. Prefer composition if the existing handlers expose enough.

## Tool surface

```
dispose_leaf {
  name: string,       # the leaf's agent name (= last dot-segment of its branch)
  reason: string      # human-readable rationale, included in the inject message and chainlink close note
}
```

## Behavior

1. Resolve the leaf's assigned issue id from `TeamRegistry` / `AgentResolver` / chainlink session-work record.
2. If the leaf has an active chainlink issue: close it with a note like `"Disposed by TL: {reason}"`. This will trigger the IssueClosed event from #302, which in turn does the actual leaf teardown.
3. If the leaf has no active chainlink issue (rare — leaf never started a session): fall back to firing the IssueClosed event directly with a sentinel `issue_id = 0`, so the leaf still receives the dismissal and cleans up.
4. Return success with the closed issue id and the agent name.

The cleanup itself (worktree remove, tmux window kill, agent dir remove) stays in the shared `dispose_agent_resources` helper from #302. This tool only emits the trigger.

## Restrictions

- TL and root only (mirror the role-restriction pattern from `TLMergePR`).
- Refuses to dispose a leaf that has already filed a PR in `Approved`/`MergeReady`/`Merged` state — those should be merged, not disposed. The check happens in the tool handler before any side effects.
- Refuses if `name` does not match a live leaf in the agent registry — return a clear error rather than silently succeeding.

## TL prompt update

Add a brief mention of `dispose_leaf` to `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md` under the worker correction loop / re-decomposition section: "If you want to end a leaf and reuse its slot, call `dispose_leaf`. If you want to keep the leaf alive and unblock it, use `send_message`."

Do NOT add language that makes `dispose_leaf` mandatory — the invariant from #302 covers the case where the TL forgets. This tool is a convenience, not the source of correctness.

## Tests

- Unit (Haskell): tool handler with various states — leaf with active issue, leaf with no issue, leaf in `DevReadyToMerge` (refused), unknown name (refused).
- Integration: end-to-end call `dispose_leaf` → verify chainlink issue closed → verify IssueClosed event fires → verify leaf transitions to `DevDismissed` and worktree/window/agent-dir removed.

## Done criteria

- `dispose_leaf` MCP tool exists, role-gated to TL/root.
- Closing path goes through the IssueClosed event from #302 — no parallel cleanup path.
- Tool refuses on PR-in-flight and unknown-name cases.
- TL prompt mentions the tool without making it mandatory.

issues.title: leaf-lifecycle: IssueClosed event → dev-leaf auto-disposal
issues.description:
A dev-leaf today has no way to learn that its assigned chainlink issue has been closed. When the TL decides to re-decompose (e.g., spawns a worker to handle prep work that supersedes the leaf), closes the issue, and moves on, the leaf is left parked at its agent's idle prompt holding a worktree, branch, and tmux window — waiting for a TL message that will never come.

Observed today: dev-leaf for issue #97 (textured-corridor-glb) hit a hard blocker (missing source .blend files), called `notify_parent` with failure, ended its chainlink session, and is now an orphan in window `🤖 issue-97-textured-corridor-glb-codex-`. TL closed #97 separately. Nothing connects the two.

## Invariant to establish

A dev-leaf's lifecycle ends when its assigned chainlink issue is closed by anyone other than itself via PR merge.

This binds leaf cleanup to issue state, not TL discipline. The TL keeps the leaf alive by keeping the issue open; the TL ends the leaf by closing the issue. No "remember to dispose" rule.

## Files to touch

- `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Events.hs` — add `IssueClosed` event type and `onIssueClosed` to `EventHandlerConfig`.
- `proto/effects/event.proto` (or wherever event payloads live) — add `IssueClosedEvent { issue_id: u64, closed_by: string }`.
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/` — wire `IssueClosed` into the WASM event dispatch path (same shape as `PRReview` / `SiblingMerged`).
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/merge_pr_local.rs:294-296` — the existing `close_chainlink_issue` call emits the event after success.
- A new `chainlink_issue_close` MCP tool wrapper (or whatever wraps the existing close path) emits the event after the close succeeds. Bash-CLI closes are out of scope for this issue — leaves should not be created from bash-CLI workflows.
- `.exo/lib/DevPhase.hs` — add `DevDismissed` terminal phase and the `IssueClosedEv` event transition.
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/DevRole.hs` — add `onIssueClosed` event handler that:
  1. Reads the leaf's assigned issue id (from `EXOMONAD_ISSUE_ID` env or chainlink session-work record).
  2. If the closed issue matches: `applyEvent` IssueClosedEv → `DevDismissed`, return `InjectMessage "[ISSUE CLOSED: #N closed by <actor>. Exiting; your worktree will be cleaned up.]"`.
  3. If it doesn't match: `NoAction`.
- Cleanup path: reuse `cleanup_worker_agents_for_parent` + `git_wt.remove_workspace` + `.exo/agents/{name}` removal from `merge_pr_local.rs:303-331`. Extract into a shared `dispose_agent_resources(project_dir, agent_slug)` helper in `services/` so both merge cleanup and dismissal cleanup share one code path.

## Why an event, not polling

Polling on BeforeModel would only fire on the next model turn. A blocked leaf could sit idle for hours before a turn happens. The event fires the moment the issue closes — leaf knows immediately.

## Edge cases

- Issue closed before leaf finishes its first chainlink `session work`: leaf may not have registered its assignment yet. Race is benign — if the leaf isn't in the registry, the dismissal event is a no-op and the leaf's normal startup will see the closed issue on its first chainlink call and self-exit through the existing failure path.
- Multiple leaves on the same issue (shouldn't happen but if): all receive the event. Each cleans up its own worktree. Idempotent.
- Leaf already on `DevReadyToMerge` when issue closes via merge_pr: the existing merge cleanup runs; the IssueClosed handler sees state is already terminal and no-ops.

## Tests

- Unit (Haskell): DevRole event handler with matching/non-matching issue id, asserting correct EventAction.
- Unit (Rust): merge_pr_local emits IssueClosed event after close_chainlink_issue succeeds.
- Integration: a dispose_agent_resources helper test that exercises tmux window kill + worktree remove + agent dir remove.

## Done criteria

- `IssueClosed` event type defined in proto + Haskell + Rust dispatch.
- merge_pr_local and the MCP close path both emit it.
- Dev-leaf handler transitions to terminal and triggers cleanup.
- Orphan leaf scenario (issue closed by TL while leaf is idle): leaf cleans itself up within one event-router tick.
- No regression in existing merge cleanup.

issues.title: E2E test: reviewer hardening + authorship preservation (deferred)
issues.description:
Once issues #298, #299, and #300 land, we should have an end-to-end test that exercises the full provenance-preservation path. Explicitly deferred — Roger does not have time to flesh out another E2E in the near term. This issue is a placeholder so the gap is tracked and the test gets written when bandwidth opens up.

## Companion layout

- Testrunner: Claude haiku, observes via read-only bash, reports via `notify_parent`.

issues.title: merge_pr: preserve worker authorship on merge commit
issues.description:
When the TL runs `merge_pr`, the merge commit's author is whoever's git identity is configured in the TL's worktree — not the worker that built the branch. Concrete evidence: backrooms-workspace commit 224a0e6 (`Merge PR #1 GLTF world startup`) is authored by `exomonad-review-pr-1-codex` rather than the original `exomonad-issue-80-gltf-world-codex`. Provenance from worktree conception is lost at merge time.

## Goal

The merge commit (and squash commit) created by `merge_pr` must be attributed to the worker that owns the head branch, regardless of which agent runs the merge tool.

## Files to edit

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/merge_pr_local.rs` — around lines 263-273 (the merge dispatch block).
- Add tests in `rust/exomonad-core/tests/` (new file or extend existing `merge_pr_local`-adjacent test if one exists).

## Implementation

Before the merge step:

```rust
let author_line = run_git_capture(
    project_dir,
    &["log", "-1", "--format=%an <%ae>", &head_branch],
).await
    .context("failed to read head-branch author for merge attribution")?;
let author_flag = format!("--author={}", author_line.trim());
```

Pass `&author_flag` to:
- `git merge --squash` path: the subsequent `git commit -m`.
- `git merge` / rebase path: the `git merge -m` invocation (yes, `git merge -m` accepts `--author`).

If `run_git_capture` doesn't exist yet, add it next to `run_git` — it should run git, capture stdout, and error on non-zero exit.

## Edge cases

- Head branch with multiple authors across commits: use the most recent commit's author (the head's `-1`). Acceptable trade-off — the merged-into-main commit attributes to whoever produced the final pushed state.
- Empty/missing author: fail the merge with a clear error; do not silently fall back to the runner's identity.

## Tests

- Unit test: set up a temp repo with a head branch whose last commit has a distinct `user.name`/`user.email`, run `merge_pr_local`, assert `git log -1 base_branch --format='%an <%ae>'` matches the head's author. Both `Merge` and `Squash` strategies.
- Test the failure path: if `git log` on the head branch produces empty output, merge should error rather than fall through.

## Verify

- `just build` (compiles)
- `cargo test -p exomonad-core` (new tests pass)
- `just install-all-dev`

## Done criteria

- Merge commit on the base branch is authored by the worker, not the TL.
- Squash commit on the base branch is authored by the worker.
- Tests cover both strategies and the empty-author failure case.
- No regression in existing `merge_pr_local` tests.

issues.title: Reviewer bash: deny commit-mutating git verbs, allow read-only
issues.description:
The reviewer's PreToolUse Edit deny (issue #298) closes the Edit-tool path, but the reviewer can still mutate authorship via bash git commands: `git commit`, `git commit --amend`, `git rebase`, `git cherry-pick`, `git merge` (non-ff), `git filter-branch`, `git revert`. We need a Bash-level guard that blocks every commit-mutating git verb on the reviewer while leaving read-only inspection commands fully usable — the reviewer must be able to determine where a detached HEAD is pointing.

## Scope

Add a new hook helper in `.exo/lib/HookPolicy.hs` and wire it into the reviewer's `preToolUse` only. Do not change TL/dev/worker policy.

## Files to edit

- `.exo/lib/HookPolicy.hs` — add `blockGitAuthorMutation` and `preToolUseWithGitAuthorBlock` (or extend `preToolUseWithGhBlock` to take an additional verb-set argument; pick whichever keeps the call sites cleanest).
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs` — apply the new guard before the existing gh block.

## Denied git verbs

`commit`, `commit --amend`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `merge` (any form), `filter-branch`, `replace`, `revert`, `reset --hard`, `reset --soft`, `am`, `apply --index`, `push --force`, `push --force-with-lease`, `update-ref`, `notes add/edit/remove`. (Allow `apply` without `--index` since it doesn't commit.)

## Allowed (read-only) verbs — explicit allowlist

`status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `fetch`, `rev-parse`, `symbolic-ref`, `branch -v`, `branch --show-current`, `ls-files`, `ls-tree`, `cat-file`, `blame`, `describe`, `for-each-ref`, `worktree list`, `config --get`, `remote -v`, `remote show`, `reflog show`, `stash list`, `stash show`. The reviewer must still be able to answer "where is HEAD pointing?" via `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git symbolic-ref HEAD`, `git status`.

## Implementation sketch

Token-scan the bash command (reuse `shellTokenSeparator` from existing code). After the leading `git`, take the first non-flag token as the verb; if it appears in the deny set, return `denyResponse` with:

> Reviewer cannot author or rewrite commits — provenance must remain with the worktree owner. Use `request_changes`/`post_review_comment` to send the fix back to the worker. Read-only git commands (status, diff, log, show, fetch, rev-parse, symbolic-ref) remain available for inspecting the PR's HEAD.

Be careful with command chains (`;`, `&&`, `|`) — split on those before scanning so a `git status && git commit` doesn't sneak through.

## Tests

- Extend `HookPolicy` tests with cases:
  - `git commit -m x` → denied
  - `git commit --amend --no-edit` → denied
  - `git rebase main` → denied
  - `git cherry-pick abc123` → denied
  - `git merge feature` → denied
  - `git status` → allowed
  - `git rev-parse HEAD` → allowed
  - `git log --oneline` → allowed
  - `git status && git commit -m sneak` → denied
  - `gitk` (similar prefix) → allowed (not a git invocation)

## Done criteria

- All denied verbs return the redispatch message via `denyResponse`.
- All allowed read-only verbs pass through.
- Reviewer can still run the read-only verbs listed above.
- TL/dev/worker bash unchanged.
- `cabal test all` passes including new HookPolicy cases.

issues.title: Reviewer PreToolUse: deny Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit
issues.description:
The reviewer role currently has no PreToolUse deny on Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit. Its preToolUse is just `preToolUseWithGhBlock` (.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs:317), which only blocks gh and chainlink sqlite. The reviewer can therefore edit files and commit changes under the reviewer git identity, breaking PR provenance (see backrooms-workspace commits c8f3890, 5a455e2 authored by exomonad-review-pr-N-codex on supposedly-worker branches).

## Scope
