Mirror the TL implementation deny in the reviewer role.

## Files to edit

- `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs`

## Implementation

1. Add `reviewerImplementerTools = ["Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"]` at module scope (mirror TLRole.hs:80-81).
2. Add `reviewerImplementationDenyHook :: HookInput -> Eff Effects HookOutput` returning a `denyResponse` for any tool name in `reviewerImplementerTools`. Redispatch text:

   > Reviewers do not edit code. Use `request_changes` or `post_review_comment` to relay the fix to the worker that owns the worktree. The worker's git identity is the canonical author of every commit on its branch.

3. Wire it through `preToolUseWithGhBlock`: change line 317 from `preToolUseWithGhBlock (\\_ -> pure (allowResponse Nothing))` to `preToolUseWithGhBlock reviewerImplementationDenyHook`.

## Verify

- `just wasm-all`
- `just install-all-dev`
- Reviewer agent attempting `Edit` should receive the redispatch message and be denied.

## Done criteria

- WASM compiles.
- Reviewer's PreToolUse denies the four implementer tools.
- TL behavior unchanged.

issues.title: Verify dev round-counting semantics + add explicit E2E coverage before spindle integration
issues.description:
## Why

While writing docs/architecture/agent-system.md I flagged the DevPhase transition
that escalates to DevNeedsHumanDirection as potentially off-by-one. On re-reading
the code with Roger's vocabulary, the transition is correct — but the test suite
does not have explicit coverage for the second-changes-requested round, and the
intended vocabulary is not externalized anywhere. Before spindle integration
(where this loop will run under real CI), we want both nailed down.

## Intended semantics (Roger)

- Round 0: poller detects the PR, spawns the reviewer. Reviewer issues its first
  verdict.
- If verdict = changes_requested: watcher fires ReviewReceived → dev moves to
  DevChangesRequested. Dev fixes, commits, pushes.
- Round 1: watcher detects SHA change → fires FixesPushed → dev moves to
  DevUnderReview round=1. Reviewer re-reviews.
- If the second verdict is also changes_requested → watcher fires ReviewReceived
  again. Dev sees \`round_ >= 1\` and escalates to DevNeedsHumanDirection. TL
  receives \`[STUCK]\` and must clarify with the human.

## Code as-is (verified matches intent)

\`.exo/lib/DevPhase.hs\` transition for \`ReviewReceivedEv\`:

\`\`\`haskell
ReviewReceivedEv prNum comments -> case phase of
  DevUnderReview _ round_
    | round_ >= 1 ->
        Transitioned (DevNeedsHumanDirection prNum
          \"reviewer still requesting changes after first fix round\")
  _ ->
    Transitioned (DevChangesRequested prNum [comments])
\`\`\`

\`FixesPushedEv\` sets \`round_=1\` on first invocation, increments thereafter.
So the second \`ReviewReceivedEv\` fires the escalation. This matches the
intended semantics.

## What to do

1. Add an explicit E2E test (or extend reviewer-convergence-loop) that walks the
   full escalation path:
   - dev files PR
   - reviewer requests changes (round 0)
   - dev pushes fix
   - reviewer requests changes AGAIN (round 1)
   - assert: DevPhase = DevNeedsHumanDirection, TL inbox contains [STUCK]
   - assert: review-loop watcher did NOT open a chainlink review-stuck issue
     for this path (DevNeedsHumanDirection is the in-band signal; review-stuck
     is for dev/reviewer health failures, not for legitimate disagreement)

2. Sharpen docs/architecture/agent-system.md DevPhase notes to use the
   round 0 / round 1 vocabulary explicitly instead of \"first round\" /
   \"second round\" which is ambiguous.

3. Sharpen .exo/lib/DevPhase.hs \`canExit\` and the transition's escalation
   message to mention \"round 1\" so the message stays grep-able when read
   alongside the watcher logs.

## Done criteria

- New or extended E2E test passing on this branch
- Validator asserts the escalation path end-to-end (TL receives [STUCK],
  DevPhase persists as DevNeedsHumanDirection in KV)
- Doc + handler message use consistent round-numbering vocabulary

## Out of scope

- Changing the round-counting code itself (it matches intent)
- Touching the watcher's review-stuck escalation (separate code path)

issues.title: Watcher: stop fanning pr_review review_received back to the reviewer that posted it

comments.content:
## Problem

When a reviewer agent posts a review via `approve_pr` or `request_changes`, the watcher's next `poll_cycle` fans the resulting `pr_review` event out to BOTH the dev-leaf AND the reviewer that just posted it.

Observed in `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop` (server log):

```
00:43:52.418  inject_message -> agent_key=main.trivial-contributing-codex  target=@3  (dev-leaf, correct)
00:43:52.696  inject_message -> agent_key=main.review-pr-1-codex          target=@4  (reviewer, BUG)
```

The reviewer pane shows `[REVIEW PR 1 received comments] .exo/tmp/<uuid>.txt` — telling the reviewer that it received review comments that *it itself just authored*.

## Why it matters

1. Noise — confuses the reviewer agent, may trigger redundant review cycles.
2. Inflates `pr_review_cycle_count` on the wrong side of the loop.
3. Makes the reviewer's tmux pane unreadable when debugging real failures.

## Likely site

`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs` `reviewer_fanout_decision` (or wherever `call_handle_event_for_role(branch=…role=reviewer event_type=pr_review)` is invoked for `review_received`). The fanout was introduced for `fixes_pushed` (chainlink #247/#249) — it should NOT also fire for `review_received` whose author IS the reviewer.

## Proposed fix

In `compute_pr_actions` (or the fanout site), suppress the reviewer-fanout when:
- `event.kind == "review_received"`, AND
- the review's author identity matches the reviewer agent for that PR.

The reviewer should only receive `fixes_pushed` re-review prompts, not its own posted reviews echoed back.

## Acceptance

- E2E reviewer pane shows zero `[REVIEW] PR #N received comments` lines after the reviewer posts.
- Unit test for `compute_pr_actions`: a `review_received` event whose author is the reviewer produces NO `WasmEvent { pr_review, role=reviewer }` action.
- Existing `fixes_pushed` fan-out test still passes.

issues.title: Watcher: add ci.gate config knob — treat 'no CI source configured' as auto-neutral so merge_ready can fire

comments.content:
## Problem

The reviewer-convergence E2E test (`tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop`) cannot complete because `[MERGE READY]` is never fired, even after the reviewer posts `approve_pr`.

Confirmed in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:1535`:

```rust
let merge_ready_now = !old_state.merge_ready_notified
    && signals_within_merge_ready_window(
        old_state.review_approved_at,
        old_state.ci_mergeable_at,   // <-- REQUIRED, not optional
    );
```

`ci_mergeable_at` is only populated when `ci_status ∈ {Success, Neutral}` (lines 1530-1534). With no spindle running (and `tangled_spindle_url` unset), `ci_status` stays at its default forever, so `ci_mergeable_at` is permanently `None`, so `merge_ready_now` is permanently `false`.

This is **not** an e2e-only bug. Any production setup using Tangled without a spindle (single-developer local) hits the same dead-end: reviewer approval alone never unblocks merge.

## Proposed fix (Option B from triage)

Add a `[ci]` section to `.exo/config.toml`:

```toml
[ci]
gate = "required"   # default: block merge_ready until CI reports success/neutral
gate = "off"        # treat as auto-neutral; reviewer approval alone fires merge_ready
```

When `gate = "off"`, the watcher seeds `ci_mergeable_at` to `Some(now)` at the same moment `review_approved_at` is set, so `signals_within_merge_ready_window` succeeds on reviewer approval alone.

Auto-detection knob: if no CI source is wired (`tangled_spindle_url` unset AND no GitHub Actions integration), default `gate` to `"off"`. Explicit `gate = "required"` always wins.

## Acceptance

- `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop` reaches `[MERGE READY]` → TL merges → validator records `Failures: 0`.
- Unit test in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs`: with `gate = "off"`, `compute_pr_actions` emits MergeReady event on reviewer approval with `ci_status` still at default.
- `CLAUDE.md` § Capabilities table updates the merge_ready row to mention the gate knob.

issues.title: merge_pr: post-merge git pull failure mode is opaque; log the actual exit code/stderr instead of a generic recovery hint
issues.description:
## Symptom

Reviewer-convergence E2E (work dir `~/.cache/exomonad-e2e/reviewer-convergence.B57oEAfW`) merged PR #1 successfully (squash commit `1c22c87` on `main`, pushed to `origin/main`). The MCP response was:

```json
{
  "git_fetched": true,
  "message": "PR #1 merged via squash",
  "next": "git pull failed — run 'git pull --rebase' manually to sync your local branch. Then verify build: cargo check --workspace.",
  "success": true
}
```

Running `git pull` manually in the project root now reports `Already up to date.` and exits 0. Local `main` and `origin/main` are both at `1c22c87`. So the post-merge pull *would* succeed if re-run — the in-flow failure was transient.

## Why this is a bug

`haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/MergePR.hs:329-341` runs `git pull` and only captures the exit code:

```haskell
case pullResult of
  Left _ -> pure False
  Right pullResp -> pure (Proc.runResponseExitCode pullResp == 0)
```

If pull exits non-zero, the `next` field falls through to a hard-coded generic message at line 153:

```haskell
else "git pull failed — run 'git pull --rebase' manually to sync your local branch."
```

The reasons for a real divergence (true conflict, upstream config missing, divergent histories) and a transient race (filesystem-lock contention with the worktree-cleanup step that runs immediately before pull, or with the remote push that just landed) produce **identical user-visible output**. There is no way for the TL or an operator to know whether to investigate.

## Fix

In `MergePR.hs`, when pull exits non-zero:

- Capture `runResponseStdout` and `runResponseStderr` from `Proc.RunResponse`.
- Include them in the `next` message (truncated to a sane length).
- Log them at error level via `Log.ErrorRequest` for the server log.

Suggested wording:

```
git pull failed (exit code N): <stderr first line>. Run 'git pull --rebase' manually to sync your local branch. Then verify build.
```

If stderr is empty and exit is non-zero, include exit code and stdout as fallback context.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failing `git pull` after a successful merge produces a `next` field that names the exit code and the first line of stderr.
- The server log (`.exo/logs/sidecar.log` or wherever LogError lands) contains the full stderr.
- The existing-passing path (`pullOk == true`) is unchanged.

## Why low priority

This is a polish/observability issue, not a correctness one. The merge itself succeeds. But chasing the transient race that triggered the warning is impossible without the missing diagnostic data, and the generic "run git pull --rebase manually" misdirects operators toward a rebase that isn't needed.

## Possible related root cause to investigate during fix

The merge_pr_local cleanup at `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/merge_pr_local.rs:303-322` removes the leaf's worktree at `.exo/worktrees/{slug}` as part of the same call. The Haskell-side pull at line 332 runs immediately after. Both touch `.git/worktrees/` metadata. A race here is plausible — worth confirming with the better stderr we'd capture.

issues.title: Watcher: distinguish dev-stuck from reviewer-stuck timeouts; TL should only ever receive [MERGE READY]
issues.description:
## Problem statement (rich)

Today the watcher's only escalation path when no progress is made within `reviewer_max_wait_seconds` (default 1200s, configured in `.exo/review-policy.toml`) is the single `[REVIEW TIMEOUT]` signal sent to the parent TL. The poller cannot distinguish two **architecturally distinct** failure modes:

1. **Dev-stuck.** The dev-leaf received the reviewer's verdict via `review_received` injection, but never produced a new `last_head_sha`. The leaf is paralyzed (model confusion, ambiguous spec, error in its work loop, etc.). The reviewer is fine — it already delivered its verdict.
2. **Reviewer-stuck.** The dev pushed `fixes_pushed`, the watcher fanned out the event to the reviewer, but the reviewer never wrote a new verdict to `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json`. The dev is fine — it's idling waiting for the next review.

From the poller's perspective, both look identical: "no state change for N seconds, escalate." It then fires `[REVIEW TIMEOUT]` to the TL — which is **wrong on two levels**:

- The TL's intended contract is that the poller hands it **exactly one signal: `[MERGE READY]`**. Anything else (STUCK, TIMEOUT, FAILED) is a human-intervention escalation, not a state the TL is supposed to act on. We do not want the TL's flow dictated by timeout escalations.
- Even if a timeout signal is unavoidable, it should *name the stuck actor* so an operator can intervene at the right place without re-reading the state file from scratch.

## What "right" looks like

### TL contract simplification

The TL's idle-then-act loop should be:

```
idle until [MERGE READY: pr-N]
  → merge_pr(N)
  → close chainlink issue
  → tear down agent
  → done
```

Any other signal goes to a **distinct human-escalation channel** (a separate tmux window, a "needs-attention" notification surface, a chainlink issue auto-filed by the watcher, etc.). The TL itself does not poll, does not branch, does not interpret stuck/timeout — those are operator concerns.

### Poller distinguishes stuck actors

When the poller's "no progress in N seconds" timer fires for a PR, it should inspect:

- `pr.last_head_sha` vs the actual remote HEAD on `pr.head_branch` → did the dev push since the last review_received?
  - **YES** but no new verdict in `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json` → **reviewer is stuck** (dev did its part)
  - **NO** new SHA after a changes_requested verdict → **dev is stuck** (reviewer is waiting)
- The verdict file's mtime — when was the last reviewer verdict written? If it's never been written, the **reviewer never started** (different from "reviewer is stuck after starting").

Each of these maps to a distinct escalation signal that should route to a distinct surface — not to the TL.

### Wire shape

Define new event variants (Haskell `EventInput` / Rust dispatch):

| Event | Semantic | Routing target |
|---|---|---|
| `merge_ready` | Approved + CI green | TL via `notify_parent_delivery` |
| `dev_not_pushing` | changes_requested verdict, but no new SHA for N seconds | Human-escalation surface; chainlink issue auto-filed; NOT the TL |
| `reviewer_not_responding` | fixes_pushed but no new verdict for N seconds | Same human-escalation surface |
| `reviewer_never_started` | PR open, reviewer agent recorded, but `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json` was never written | Same human-escalation surface |
| `dev_failed` | Dev agent self-reported failure via notify_parent failure | Human-escalation surface |

The TL receives **only** `merge_ready`. Other events go to a "review-loop escalation" channel.

## Why "TL receives only merge_ready" is the right invariant

- **TL cost.** Opus tokens are 10–30× leaf tokens. Every message the TL has to interpret, decide on, and respond to is expensive. The fewer codepaths the TL has, the cheaper and more reliable the orchestration.
- **State-machine cleanliness.** A TL whose only happy-path transition is `idle → merge_ready → merged → done` is much easier to verify than one that also has to handle stuck/timeout/failed branches each with their own recovery logic.
- **Audit trail.** When the watcher routes "stuck" and "timeout" to a distinct surface, those become the inputs to operator-facing observability (chainlink issues, dashboard alerts, etc.), not to the TL's transcript. The TL transcript stays focused on the actual orchestration story.

## Anti-patterns to avoid in implementation

- DO NOT make the TL conditionally handle each stuck variant. Push the routing decision into the watcher.
- DO NOT silently drop timeouts that the poller can't classify (orphan SHA, race-y filesystem state). Surface them to the human-escalation channel with the raw diagnostic data.
- DO NOT introduce a new TL prompt that says "if you receive STUCK, do X". The point is the TL never receives STUCK.
- DO NOT couple this to #285's CI/SHA work. They share the registry but are independent design changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- `EventAction` in `ExoMonad.Guest.Events` gains new variants (or the existing watcher's `Stuck`/`ReviewTimeout` events are split into the four-way classification above).
- The watcher's poll-cycle logic inspects head-SHA vs verdict-file-mtime when classifying a stalled PR.
- TL role prompts (`.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md` and the TL counterpart) are updated to remove `[STUCK]` and `[REVIEW TIMEOUT]` from the vocabulary they handle. They handle only `[MERGE READY]`.
- A dedicated human-escalation surface (initial cut: chainlink-issue auto-file with a `review-stuck` label and the four-way classification in the body) is wired up.
- Unit tests cover the four-way classification in the watcher.
- `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/` reaches `[MERGE READY]` cleanly with #290 and #292 (fixture realignment) applied; no `[STUCK]`/`[TIMEOUT]` should arrive at the TL.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- **#290** (verdict-aware watcher dispatch) is a prerequisite: the watcher must be able to tell approval from changes_requested before it can correctly classify a stall.
- **#291** (timeout-degeneracy in the convergence E2E) is the symptom; this issue is the structural fix.
- **#288** (rounds counter) is independent but reinforces the same theme.

## Out of scope

- Auto-recovery of stuck dev-leaves. Once classified, the human handles the next step. Adding LLM-driven recovery loops is a separate design discussion.
- Changing `reviewer_max_wait_seconds` for tests. CI tuning is a separate concern.

issues.title: Reviewer-convergence E2E: realign fixture so reviewer feedback is scoped to the leaf's actual change (Option A)
issues.description:
## Scope

Apply **Option A** from #291 to the reviewer-convergence E2E fixture: keep the same flow (one round of `changes_requested` → fix → `approve`) but make the reviewer's requested change scoped to **what the leaf actually wrote**, not to an unrelated part of the file. This eliminates the cognitive-load stall in Codex that was causing the dev-leaf to freeze and the test to degenerate into the timeout path.

The principle this issue is locking in: **the dev-leaf must not need any prior knowledge of what the reviewer will ask for.** It receives the review comment from the poller and applies exactly that change — nothing more. The fixture must therefore be designed so the comment fits the diff naturally.

## What to change

| File | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/e2e-test.md` | "Append a one-line `Thank you for contributing!` sentence to the end of the file." | Keep as is — leaf still appends the sentence. |
| `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/reviewer-checklist.md` | "request exactly one specific change ... missing a copyright header that cites the year 2026 and the project name `Reviewer Convergence Loop E2E Fixture`" | Replace with: "request exactly one specific change: rephrase the appended sentence from `Thank you for contributing!` to `Thank you for your contribution!` to match project tone. Do not approve until that exact phrasing is present." |
| `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/validate.sh` | Asserts review file final state = `approved` | No change needed — the reviewer still approves once the leaf rephrases. |

## Anti-patterns (DO NOT)

- DO NOT add the rephrased text to the leaf's spec. The leaf must learn it from the watcher-delivered review message, not from any in-line hint. This is what is meant by "no context leak into the dev-leaf."
- DO NOT make the reviewer ask for additions outside the leaf's diff. The whole point of Option A is keeping the request on the changed line.
- DO NOT extend the fixture to require multi-round changes. Single round → fix → approve is the minimum that exercises the fan-out path.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/reviewer-checklist.md` is updated as above.
- `e2e-test.md` is unchanged in its description of the leaf's task (the rephrase is delivered to the leaf only via the watcher's review-comment injection).
- `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` reaches `Fanning out pr_review event to reviewer agent ... kind=fixes_pushed` and validate.sh writes `Verdict: success Failures: 0` for three consecutive runs.
- No edits to `worktree_event_watcher`, no new code paths — fixture-only.

## Dependencies

Independent of code changes; can land first. Best landed alongside #290 (verdict-aware watcher dispatch) so the convergence path is fully exercised.

issues.title: Reviewer-convergence E2E degenerates into timeout-escalation path; fixture mismatch causes dev paralysis
issues.description:
## Symptom

`just e2e-reviewer-convergence` is intended to exercise the fan-out path introduced by #249/#250:

> leaf pushes fixes after a reviewer's ChangesRequested → watcher fires \`fixes_pushed\` → \`reviewer_fanout_decision\` returns \`DispatchTo\` → \`call_handle_event\` on the reviewer agent.

The success signal validate.sh greps for is the canonical line `Fanning out pr_review event to reviewer agent ... kind=fixes_pushed`.

In practice the test never reaches that line. Instead it sits with the dev in a "Working …" spinner for many minutes, the poller idles waiting on a timeout (default 1200s), and eventually the run ends via the **timeout** escalation path (`[REVIEW TIMEOUT]` → TL) — a completely different code path from the one this test was built to validate.

## Root cause 1 — fixture mismatch creates an unforced cognitive load

`tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/e2e-test.md` tells the dev leaf:

> Append a one-line "Thank you for contributing!" sentence to the end of CONTRIBUTING.md.

`tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/reviewer-checklist.md` tells the reviewer:

> request exactly one specific change ... CONTRIBUTING.md is missing a copyright header that cites the year 2026 and the project name "Reviewer Convergence Loop E2E Fixture".

The leaf's change (append a sentence) and the reviewer's requested change (insert a copyright header at the top) are **completely orthogonal**. Codex correctly modifies the file with the header but stalls before committing/pushing because the request feels like out-of-scope feedback to its in-scope work. Result: indefinite "Working …" with the file dirty in-tree.

A naturally scoped review would make the test deterministic. Options that keep the same flow (one round of changes_requested → fix → approve):

- **A** Leaf: "Append `Thank you for contributing!`" — Reviewer: "Rephrase to `Thank you for your contribution!` to match project tone."
- **B** Leaf: "Append `Thank you for contributing!`" — Reviewer: "Capitalize / drop the period / wrap in bold."
- **C** Leaf: "Append `Thank you for contributing! Please be kind.`" — Reviewer: "Remove the second sentence — too directive."

Any of those keeps the request directly on the line the leaf added.

## Root cause 2 — poller cannot distinguish "dev stuck" from "reviewer stuck"

The watcher's only escalation path when no progress is made within `reviewer_max_wait_seconds` (default 1200s, per `.exo/review-policy.toml`) is `[REVIEW TIMEOUT]` to the TL. From the poller's perspective, two very different conditions look identical:

- Reviewer never re-reviewed after `fixes_pushed`
- Dev never pushed `fixes_pushed` after `changes_requested` (the case in this test)

Both surface as "no state change for N seconds → notify TL with REVIEW TIMEOUT." A future improvement (separate issue scope, not part of this one): the poller could emit distinct events — `dev_not_pushing` vs `reviewer_not_reviewing` — based on which actor's last state change is overdue. For now, the priority is the fixture fix below; the poller semantic gap is a follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria (this issue)

- The reviewer-convergence E2E reaches the canonical fan-out line under normal Codex pacing without relying on a timeout.
- `validate.sh` writes `Verdict: success Failures: 0` within the configured timeout for at least 3 consecutive runs.
- The leaf's spec and the reviewer's checklist are aligned so the requested change is on the diff the leaf actually produced.

## Out of scope (file separately if needed)

- Distinguishing dev-stuck vs reviewer-stuck timeouts in the watcher.
- Lowering `reviewer_max_wait_seconds` for tests so the timeout path surfaces quickly in CI (still has the wrong semantic; needs its own design).

## Related

- **#288** — rounds-counter symptom; the timeout escalation can land in addition to the rounds-counter bug for compounded confusion.
- **#290** — verdict-aware event dispatch; once that lands, the fixture fix below removes the last source of stall.

comments.content: Closing: superseded by #292 (fixture realignment, shipped in 60f8723c) and #293 (4-way stall classification + TL-only-merge-ready contract, shipped in 87080257). The fixture mismatch and the timeout-degeneracy structural concern are addressed by those two issues. No standalone work remaining here.

issues.title: Audit watcher's pr_review event-type dispatch: approvals must fire ReviewApprovedEv, not ReviewReceivedEv
issues.description:
## Problem

The DevPhase state machine has the right shape — there are two distinct events for review-related verdicts:

```haskell
-- .exo/lib/DevPhase.hs:39-40
ReviewReceivedEv PRNumber Text   -- intended: changes_requested verdict
ReviewApprovedEv PRNumber        -- intended: approved verdict
```

But the watcher (in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs`) appears to fire `ReviewReceivedEv` for **all** `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json` updates regardless of the verdict's `state` field. That's why the failure described in #288 happens: an approval after a fix push triggers the `DevUnderReview _ round_ | round_ >= 1` arm of the `ReviewReceivedEv` transition, which lands in `DevNeedsHumanDirection`.

This issue is the watcher-side fix. #288 captures the symptom; this captures the root cause.

## What "correct dispatch" looks like

When the watcher detects a change to `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json`:

1. Read the new `state` field from the file.
2. Decide which WASM event to fire:
   - `state == "changes_requested"` → `ReviewReceivedEv prNum comments` (with the comment text)
   - `state == "approved"` → `ReviewApprovedEv prNum`
   - other states (closed, dismissed, etc.) → audit case-by-case; likely `ReviewReceivedEv` with the state text, OR a new event variant if the dev needs to react differently.
3. Pass the resolved event into `call_handle_event` rather than constructing a generic `pr_review` payload that downstream Haskell has to guess at.

Equivalent fix on the Haskell side, if the wire format is constrained: extend the existing `pr_review` payload to carry an explicit `verdict` field, and have `dispatchEvent` in `Events.hs` branch on it to construct the right DevEvent.

## What to look for in the watcher

- The site that calls `call_handle_event` with `kind: "pr_review"` payload (probably near where it reads `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json` after detecting a change).
- The payload shape — does it carry the verdict? If not, this is also a wire-format issue.
- The corresponding Haskell-side dispatcher (`PRReviewHandler.hs` and the WASM event-handler entry point) and how it constructs the DevEvent from the payload.

## Acceptance criteria

- An approval (`state="approved"` in `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json`) results in `ReviewApprovedEv` reaching the dev's state machine, not `ReviewReceivedEv`.
- The five new state-machine tests added under #288 (e.g. `assertReviewApprovedAfterFixRoundTransitionsToApproved`) pass when the role-hook-tests runner from the companion issue is wired up.
- The dev pane in `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` does NOT receive a "Review loop needs human direction" injection on the happy path (request_changes → fix → approve).
- A unit test on the Rust side covers verdict-to-event-name resolution: given a review file with each known `state` value, the expected event name is emitted.

## Related

- **#288** — the symptom (rounds counter + stuck state misclassification). Both surface the same root cause: review events not being distinguished by verdict.
- **The companion issue** about adding a `just role-hook-tests` runner so the new state-machine tests actually execute in CI.
- **.exo/lib/PRReviewHandler.hs** — the action emission logic that the watcher feeds; may need a verdict-aware branch.

## Sequencing

Can land before or after #288. They reinforce each other; landing both is what unblocks `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` to a `[MERGE READY]` result.

issues.title: Add 'just role-hook-tests' recipe to actually execute the devswarm WASM test suite
issues.description:
## Problem

`.exo/roles/devswarm/devswarm.cabal:71` declares a `test-suite role-hook-tests` whose source lives in `.exo/roles/devswarm/test/Main.hs`. It builds for `wasm32-wasi` (per `cabal.project.wasm`) and is currently the home for:

- Role tool-list assertions (`assertReviewerToolList`, `assertReviewerPostToolUseEventName`)
- Pre-tool-use hook policy assertions per role (`assertRoleDeny`, `assertRoleAllow`)
- `StateMachine` semantics for `DevPhase` and `ReviewerPhase`

But **no `just` recipe runs this suite**. The closest existing recipes are:

| Recipe | What it actually does |
|---|---|
| `just haskell-test` | `cabal test all` — runs native-target tests only (ginger etc.); the wasm-target role tests are skipped |
| `just test-wasm-integration` | `cargo test -p exomonad-core --test wasm_integration` — Rust-side integration tests that load WASM, not these Haskell-side WASM unit tests |
| `just wasm-all` | Builds the WASM binaries but does not run any tests against them |

Without a runner, the suite is effectively documentation that the build link-succeeds. Evidence: the existing `assertDevNeedsHumanDirectionAfterOneFixRound` test had a missing `TypeApplications` annotation on `canExit` that made the whole test module fail to compile. No one noticed because no one runs it.

## Why this matters now

#288 (rounds-counter bug) added five new state-machine tests for intended semantics (`assertReviewApprovedAfterFixRoundTransitionsToApproved`, etc.). Those tests now compile, but they don't actually run anywhere as part of `just test`, `just haskell-test`, `just test-cargo-all`, or `just pre-push`. A regression in the rounds counter logic would not surface in CI.

## Proposed implementation

Add to `justfile`:

```just
# Build and run the devswarm role-hook-tests WASM test suite via wasmtime
role-hook-tests:
    @nix develop .#wasm --command bash -c 'export PATH=$PWD/.gemini/tmp/bin:$PATH; wasm32-wasi-cabal --project-file=cabal.project.wasm build role-hook-tests'
    @WASM=$(find dist-newstyle -name role-hook-tests.wasm -type f -print -quit); \
        nix develop --command wasmtime "$WASM"
```

(The exact wasmtime invocation may need `--wasi=preview1` flags or working-directory arguments — to be verified during implementation.)

Wire it into the standard test bundle:

```just
test:
    ...
    echo ">>> [N/N] Role hook tests..."
    just role-hook-tests
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `just role-hook-tests` builds and runs the devswarm role-hook-tests suite end-to-end and exits non-zero on test failure.
- The recipe is invoked by `just test` so `just pre-push` covers it.
- A deliberate broken assertion in `test/Main.hs` makes `just role-hook-tests` fail loudly (verify the runner actually surfaces test-level failures, not just build/exec errors).
- README or `tests/` documentation mentions how to run role-only tests.

## Dependency

Independent. Lands faster if #288's state-machine fixes are landing in parallel — both need this recipe to be useful.

issues.title: Watcher's stuck-detection counts approvals as rounds — successful convergence trips STUCK
issues.description:
## Symptom

A successful 2-round convergence loop (request_changes → fixes_pushed → approve) trips the `Stuck` state.

Observed in the reviewer-convergence-loop E2E on 2026-05-18:

```
.exo/prs.json:
  "rounds": 2,
  "stuck": true,
  "review_state": "pending_review"

.exo/reviews/pr_1.json:
  {"comments":[],"state":"approved"}
```

Watcher then fires `[STUCK: 1, rounds=2]` to the TL. The TL, per its STUCK protocol in `.exo/roles/devswarm/context/root.md`, asks the human for clarification and stops. This is the **happy path** — reviewer asked for one change, dev complied, reviewer approved — and it's being misclassified as a failure mode.

Also note `review_state` in `prs.json` is `pending_review` while the reviewer wrote `approved` to `reviews/pr_1.json`. The watcher is not propagating the approval back into the registry's `review_state` field — that's a separate inconsistency worth verifying as part of the same fix.

## Expected behavior

`rounds` should count **request_changes cycles**, not every review-related event. Specifically:

| Event | rounds increment | stuck eligibility |
|---|---|---|
| Initial `request_changes` | +1 | If rounds > max → stuck |
| `fixes_pushed` (dev responds) | no | n/a |
| `approve_pr` after `request_changes` | no | clear pending stuck state |
| Subsequent `request_changes` | +1 | If rounds > max → stuck |

Max rounds is configured at `.exo/review-policy.toml::reviewer_max_rounds`. Default 2. The current implementation makes the second event (whatever it is) trip the cap, even when that second event is an approval.

## Probable site

`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs` — search for `rounds` increment logic and the `Stuck` state transition. Subissues of #265 (closed) renamed the counter (`last_comment_count → pr_review_cycle_count`) but the semantics weren't audited against the request_changes-only intent.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test that exercises request_changes → fixes_pushed → approve does NOT trip `stuck`.
- The `rounds` counter increments only on `request_changes` events (not on approvals, not on plain comments).
- `prs.json::review_state` is updated to `approved` when the reviewer writes `state="approved"` to `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json`.
- `[STUCK]` fires only when the latest review state is `changes_requested` after `reviewer_max_rounds`.
- Add a unit test in `worktree_event_watcher.rs` covering the (request_changes → approve) path.
- E2E `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` completes with `[MERGE READY]` instead of `[STUCK]`.

## Dependency / sequencing

Independent of #283/#284/#285. Can land in parallel.

comments.content: Updated watcher semantics: request-change rounds trip stuck only after exceeding reviewer_max_rounds, approval does not increment rounds, and observed approved state is persisted to .exo/prs.json with stale stuck flags cleared. Added unit tests for request_changes→fixes_pushed→approve and approved-state persistence.

Watcher now treats approved as the effective terminal review state before considering request_changes, so old request-change records cannot increment rounds after approval. Request-change rounds trip STUCK only after exceeding reviewer_max_rounds, approved state persists into .exo/prs.json, and the persisted approved path clears stuck/human-review flags. Added unit coverage for request_changes -> fixes_pushed -> mixed request_changes+approve and for prs.json approved persistence.

## Additional observation (2026-05-18, run 4ASZbQ3L)

The rounds counter is broken in **both** directions — not just the over-count case in the original report.

### New evidence

Second run of `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` (work dir `~/.cache/exomonad-e2e/reviewer-convergence.4ASZbQ3L`) produced a fully successful convergence loop. validate.sh wrote:

```
Verdict: success
Failures: 0
```

with all 11 evidence checks green, including:

- review file has final approved state
- .exo/prs.json propagated review_state=approved
- server log has fixes_pushed reviewer fan-out
- server log has reviewer handle_event call for review-pr-1
- server log has merge-ready or PR-ready event

So a real request_changes → fixes_pushed → approve cycle ran end-to-end. But `prs.json` recorded:

```json
{ "rounds": 0, "stuck": false, "review_state": "approved" }
```

The TL then called `merge_pr`, which blocked with:

```
"PR #1: 0 review round(s) completed, 1 required"
```

(`.exo/review-policy.toml::min_review_rounds = 1`). The merge gate is consulting `rounds` and finds 0, even though the watcher just fanned out a `fixes_pushed` event whose only possible cause is a prior `changes_requested` verdict.

### Pattern across the two runs

| Run | rounds final | stuck | review_state | merge outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JvREsZde (earlier) | 2 | **true** | pending_review (later approved) | blocked by stuck |
| 4ASZbQ3L (this run) | **0** | false | approved | blocked by min_review_rounds |

Same scenario, opposite failures. The counter sometimes over-counts (every review event increments), sometimes under-counts (no event increments). It's not "monotonically wrong" — it's **non-deterministic**.

### Probable cause

The watcher's poll cadence + the way it derives state transitions are racing with the reviewer's writes. The reviewer overwrites `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json` in place; the watcher reads it on each poll. If the poll lands between request_changes and the dev's fix push, the watcher sees request_changes and increments. If it polls only after the reviewer has already overwritten to approved, it never sees the request_changes verdict and rounds stays at 0.

This is why both directions of failure happen with the same code on different runs: pure timing.

### Sharpened acceptance criteria

Replace the original "rounds should count request_changes cycles" with:

- **Each `request_changes` verdict produces exactly one `rounds` increment**, regardless of poll cadence. Use append-only review history (each verdict written to a new file `.exo/reviews/pr_N/round_M.json` or similar) rather than reading an in-place-overwritten file, OR have the reviewer emit a transition event on each verdict that the watcher consumes once.
- Approvals never increment `rounds`.
- `stuck` only fires when the most recent verdict is `changes_requested` after `reviewer_max_rounds`.
- `min_review_rounds` is satisfied when a `request_changes → approve` cycle is observable in history, regardless of how many polls happened during it.

### Implementation note

The simplest robust fix is probably: change `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json` from "latest verdict only" to an append-only list:

```jsonc
{
  "verdicts": [
    { "state": "changes_requested", "at": "...", "body": "..." },
    { "state": "approved",          "at": "...", "body": "..." }
  ],
  "final_state": "approved"
}
```

Then `rounds = count(verdict.state == "changes_requested")` becomes a pure function over the file, with no race window. The reviewer just appends; the watcher (and validate.sh) read whatever's there at poll time.

This is a slightly bigger change than the original ticket described but solves the race definitively. Worth scoping into a sub-issue if it adds too much.

Implemented append-only review verdict history for local reviewer tools and watcher round derivation from history. The watcher now persists rounds when request_changes is observed in history even if the poll only sees final approved state. Verified with just rust-test and just wasm-all.

issues.title: Remove convergence-testrunner from reviewer-convergence E2E (and audit other testrunner companions)
issues.description:
## Problem

`tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/run.sh` spawns a Claude (haiku) companion named `convergence-testrunner` whose job is to "observe via read-only Bash and report progress via notify_parent." In practice this companion **fabricates verdicts** because the artifacts it polls are not history-preserving.

### Observed failure mode (2026-05-18)

Actual convergence loop sequence (verified by capturing reviewer pane):

1. Reviewer first pass → calls `request_changes` for missing copyright header. Writes `.exo/reviews/pr_1.json` with `state="changes_requested"`.
2. Watcher detects → fires `fixes_pushed` → reviewer re-runs, sees fix, calls `approve_pr`. Overwrites `.exo/reviews/pr_1.json` with `state="approved"`.

Testrunner sees only the latest state and reports:

```
[FAILED: convergence-testrunner] convergence-loop FAILED: reviewer approved before requesting the fixture-required header change. Evidence: .exo/reviews/pr_1.json shows state=approved (expected changes_requested).
```

This is **literally false** — the reviewer did request changes. The testrunner just missed observing the intermediate state because `pr_1.json` is overwritten in place. The bad `[FAILED]` notification then competes with the watcher's `[STUCK: 1, rounds=2]` to confuse the TL into the wrong stop branch.

## Why the testrunner is redundant

`tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/validate.sh` (the process companion) already writes the objective verdict by scraping the server log for the canonical fan-out evidence:

```
Fanning out pr_review event to reviewer agent
[EventDispatch] Calling handle_event for agent 'review-pr-...
[EventDispatch] handle_event returned
```

That signal is **history-preserving** (append-only log), unambiguous, and doesn't require an LLM to interpret it. The testrunner exists alongside this but adds:

- Cost: a haiku companion running for the test duration
- Noise: a stream of `notify_parent` traffic into the TL
- Risk: false negatives like the one above, plus false positives if it happens to poll at the right moments

## Recommendation

**Strip the testrunner companion from this harness.** Concretely in `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/run.sh`:

- Delete the `[[companions]]` block for `convergence-testrunner`
- Delete `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/testrunner.md`
- Keep `validate.sh` and `e2e-test.md` unchanged

The TL's `e2e-test.md` instructions reference `[from convergence-testrunner status=success]` and `[from convergence-testrunner status=failure]` as test-end signals. Replace with: TL just idles and the validate.sh process writes RESULT_FILE.

## Audit follow-up

Other E2E harnesses use the same companion pattern. Audit and decide for each:

- `tests/e2e/messaging/`
- `tests/e2e/hook-rewrite/`
- `tests/e2e/codex-messaging/`
- `tests/e2e/codex-hooks/`
- `tests/e2e/opencode-tl/`, `opencode-worker/`
- `tests/e2e/chainlink*/`
- `tests/e2e/tangled-pr-codex/`

For each: is the testrunner observing something validate.sh / log scraping can't? If yes, document what; if no, strip it. This is part of the larger harness redesign (#281) but doesn't have to wait for it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/` no longer references a testrunner companion.
- `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` produces a verdict purely from `validate.sh`'s RESULT_FILE.
- Audit of other harnesses recorded — either strip or document why each is needed.

comments.content: Removed convergence-testrunner companion, deleted its prompt, updated TL instructions, made validate.sh produce verdicts directly from append-only server-log and registry evidence, and recorded the harness audit in tests/e2e/testrunner-companion-audit.md.

Removed the LLM convergence-testrunner companion and deleted its prompt. validate.sh now polls objective evidence directly, including .exo/prs.json review_state/stuck flags, reviewer fan-out and handle_event evidence from sidecar logs, MCP stdio evidence, and UDS curl absence. Added testrunner companion audit documenting fabricated-verdict risk and keeping existing objective or scoped companions.

issues.title: Fix reviewer tool contract to exclude parent notification
CI gating + per-SHA correlation: distinguish first vs subsequent spindle responses; consider review-then-CI ordering
issues.description:
## Question

Two related concerns about how spindle CI events flow into the merge gate today, and whether they need to change.

## Finding 1 — `ci_status_map` is keyed by branch only, with no SHA correlation

`run_spindle_subscriber` in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:1816-1880` listens for `sh.tangled.pipeline.status` events. For each event:

1. The pipeline `rkey` is looked up in `pipeline_map: HashMap<String, PipelineContext>` (populated earlier by `run_knot_subscriber` when knot fires `sh.tangled.pipeline` for a push).
2. The status is unconditionally written into `ci_status_map: HashMap<BranchName, CIStatus>`:
   ```rust
   ci_status_map.write().await.insert(context.branch_name, ci);
   ```

That keying is **branch only** — not (branch, sha), not (branch, rkey). Every new push produces a new pipeline + new spindle status, and that status **overwrites** the previous entry. The watcher does not know which SHA the cached status corresponds to.

### Concrete race

```
leaf pushes commit A                  → pipeline P_A fires
                                      → spindle starts CI for A
reviewer requests changes
leaf pushes commit B (fixes)          → pipeline P_B fires
                                      → spindle starts CI for B
P_A finishes Success                  → ci_status_map[branch] = Success (for A)
TL receives [PR READY], merges        → merge gate sees Success and passes
                                        even though B has not been tested yet
```

The pipeline-rkey is unique per run, so the data we'd need to correlate exists upstream. We just don't keep it.

### Where to verify

- `worktree_event_watcher.rs:1816-1880` — spindle event ingestion
- `worktree_event_watcher.rs:485` — where the merge gate reads `ci_status_map`
- `merge_pr_local.rs:213` — actual merge gate using `ci_status` value

## Finding 2 — CI fires on every push, even before review

The production `.tangled/workflows/ci.yml` (per `docs/tangled-ci-integration.md:357-389`) has `when: [push, pull_request, manual]`. So every leaf push triggers a pipeline. With our two-round review cap, the first push almost always produces wasted CI compute when the reviewer ends up requesting changes — the fix push is what actually needs validation.

This is more an efficiency concern than a correctness one. With reviewer auto-spawn and a 2-round cap, half (or more) of all CI runs are on code that gets rewritten.

## Possible directions (investigation only — pick later)

### Option A — Per-SHA CI tracking (correctness fix for Finding 1)

Change `ci_status_map` to `HashMap<(BranchName, Sha), CIStatus>`, or store the SHA alongside the status. The merge gate reads `ci_status_map[(pr.head_branch, pr.last_head_sha)]` — Unknown if no match, blocking the merge until the CI for *that exact SHA* lands.

**Pros:** correctness; no stale-CI merges. **Cons:** memory growth (need eviction policy); doesn't reduce wasted CI.

### Option B — Gate CI on reviewer approval (efficiency fix for Finding 2)

Change the workflow `when:` clause to fire only on a marker the watcher creates after reviewer approval. Options:

- A specific git ref/tag the watcher pushes (e.g. `refs/exo-ci/{pr-number}`) once `review_state == approved`.
- A `manual` trigger the watcher fires via spindle's XRPC (if available).
- A workflow-level `when: pull_request, branch:` constraint plus a watcher-side "create PR via appview" step gated on approval.

**Pros:** CI only runs on code the reviewer has signed off on; fewer wasted runs. **Cons:** changes Tangled workflow semantics; harder to debug because failing pre-review code never sees CI; needs a clear "what if the approved push fails CI?" loop (likely: reviewer un-approves and dev pushes another fix → another approval → another CI run).

### Option C — Combination

Keep CI on every push (cheap signal for the dev mid-flight), but gate the *merge* on the CI corresponding to the SHA that the reviewer approved. Track `approved_at_sha` alongside the review state in `.exo/prs.json`, then the merge gate requires `ci_status_map[(branch, approved_at_sha)] == Success`.

This is the most robust but requires both per-SHA CI tracking AND a "reviewer-approved-sha" field in the local PR registry.

## Acceptance criteria

- Document the chosen direction (likely C) in `docs/decisions/`.
- If A: add per-SHA correlation + eviction policy.
- If B: define the CI trigger mechanism and update the workflow YAML.
- If C: both, plus the `approved_at_sha` field.
- Update or extend the `tangled-pr-codex` E2E to exercise the chosen invariant.

## Scope note

This is scoped as **investigation only** until #283 + #284 are settled. The current symptom (stale CI race) is masked in our reviewer-convergence E2E because the test runs CI synchronously enough that the race window stays closed. With a real spindle in production timing, the race opens.

comments.content:
## Decision: Option C — gate merge on CI for the reviewer-approved SHA

(2026-05-18)

Combine per-SHA CI tracking (Option A's correctness) with reviewer-anchored gating (Option B's intent), without changing the spindle workflow trigger semantics. The 2-round review cap means request-changes paths are rare; the design favors correctness in the common-case approval flow rather than tighter complexity in the request-changes branch.

---

## Problem (recap, sharpened)

Today the watcher discards two things it could have kept:

1. **Pipeline → SHA mapping.** Knot's `sh.tangled.pipeline` event carries `triggerMetadata.push.newSha`. The watcher's knot subscriber reads it to learn the branch, but does not propagate the SHA into `pipeline_map` or `ci_status_map`. The spindle subscriber then writes `ci_status_map[branch] = status` with no record of which commit was tested.

2. **Reviewer-approved SHA.** When a reviewer transitions a PR to `approved`, the local registry records `review_state = "approved"` but does not capture *which SHA* was approved. If the dev pushes a new commit between approval and merge, that new code can sail through the merge gate unchallenged.

Both omissions matter because spindle CI runs concurrently with reviews. Either of:

- An older SHA's CI finishing after a newer push (stale-passes-fresh)
- A newer push landing after approval but before merge (unreviewed-passes-approved)

…produces a merge gate that says "ok" for code no one validated. The race windows are small in our synchronous E2E but wide in production timing.

---

## Implementation plan

### Phase 1 — Capture the SHA on both sides of the CI signal

**Knot subscriber** (`worktree_event_watcher.rs:1740`-…, `run_knot_subscriber`)

- Parse `triggerMetadata.push.newSha` from the pipeline event. The field is documented in `docs/tangled-ci-integration.md:90`.
- Extend `PipelineContext`:
  ```rust
  struct PipelineContext {
      branch_name: BranchName,
      pr_number: Option<u64>,
      agent_name: Option<AgentName>,
      head_sha: Sha,            // NEW
  }
  ```
- Store unchanged in `pipeline_map: HashMap<rkey, PipelineContext>` so the spindle side can find the SHA at status-event time.

**Spindle subscriber** (`worktree_event_watcher.rs:1816`-…, `run_spindle_subscriber`)

- Change `ci_status_map`'s shape:
  ```rust
  ci_status_map: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<(BranchName, Sha), CIStatus>>>
  ```
- On status event, write `(context.branch_name, context.head_sha) → ci_status`.
- The existing log line gains a `head_sha = %context.head_sha` field for diagnostics.

**Eviction policy.** Track entries with a `last_touched_at: Instant`. Evict entries older than 24h on a background task tick (1/hour). Evict on PR close. Cap total entries at 10,000 with LRU as a defensive backstop. The hot path (read for a specific (branch, sha)) doesn't need to scan, so this is cheap.

### Phase 2 — Capture the reviewer-approved SHA in `.exo/prs.json`

**Schema change** (`services/file_pr_local.rs::PrEntry`)

```rust
pub struct PrEntry {
    // existing fields...
    pub approved_at_sha: Option<Sha>,   // NEW — set when reviewer transitions to approved
}
```

**State-machine transition.** When the reviewer agent writes its verdict (`approve_pr`), the watcher persists the PR's current `last_head_sha` into `approved_at_sha` in the same write that flips `review_state` to `Approved`.

**Invalidation on new push.** When the watcher detects a SHA change on a PR whose `approved_at_sha` was set, it:

- Clears `approved_at_sha` (the approval no longer applies to current HEAD).
- Fires the existing `fixes_pushed` event so the reviewer is re-engaged.
- This is purely additive — `fixes_pushed` already fires on SHA-change-after-changes-requested; we extend the trigger to fire on SHA-change-after-approved as well.

**Backward compatibility.** Existing entries with `review_state = "approved"` and no `approved_at_sha`: deserialize as `None`. The merge gate (below) treats `None` as "no approved SHA known" and uses a one-time fallback (log + branch-level CI check) for migration. After 30 days or once tracker is migrated, remove the fallback.

### Phase 3 — Merge gate uses the SHA-pinned CI status

**`merge_pr_local.rs::check_merge_gates`** (around line 213)

Replace branch-level CI lookup with SHA-pinned lookup:

```rust
let approved_sha = pr.approved_at_sha.as_ref()
    .ok_or(MergeGateError::NoApprovedSha)?;
let ci = ci_status_map.read().await
    .get(&(pr.head_branch.clone(), approved_sha.clone()))
    .cloned()
    .unwrap_or(CIStatus::Unknown);
```

Gate behavior:

- `CIStatus::Success` for `(branch, approved_at_sha)` → merge allowed.
- `CIStatus::Failed` → merge blocked, transition PR back to `ChangesRequested`, fire `fixes_pushed` semantics so the reviewer re-engages.
- `CIStatus::Pending` / `Unknown` → merge blocked with "waiting for CI on approved SHA". `set_merge_blocked_on_ci(true)`. Watcher polls.
- `approved_at_sha` is `None` (legacy entry) → log a one-time fallback message, use branch-level lookup, deprecate after migration window.

### Phase 4 — Tests

Unit:

- `ci_status_map` reads/writes with SHA keying (`worktree_event_watcher.rs` tests).
- Eviction policy: 24h timeout, LRU cap, on-close.
- PrEntry serde for `approved_at_sha: Option<Sha>` round-trip, including missing-field backward compat.
- Merge gate decision matrix: (approved_at_sha present/absent) × (ci_status_map has matching entry / has stale entry / has nothing).

Integration:

- Leaf push A → reviewer approves at A → CI passes at A → merge ✓.
- Leaf push A → reviewer approves at A → leaf push B (no re-review) → merge blocked with "approved SHA stale" reason.
- Leaf push A → reviewer approves at A → CI fails at A → merge blocked, PR returns to `ChangesRequested`.
- Leaf push A → CI starts → leaf push B before A's CI finishes → reviewer approves at B → A's CI completes Success → merge stays blocked until B's CI completes (this is the stale-passes-fresh race; the test pins it down).

Extend `tests/e2e/tangled-pr-codex/` rather than spinning a new harness. The fixture already runs against a real local spindle — the new assertion is on `.exo/prs.json` containing the right `approved_at_sha` and the merge timing relative to spindle status.

---

## Files touched (likely)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `proto/effects/file_pr.proto` | Add `approved_at_sha` to `LocalPrResponse` (if exposed to Haskell) |
| `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr_local.rs` | `PrEntry.approved_at_sha` field; serde + tests |
| `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs` | `PipelineContext.head_sha`; SHA-keyed `ci_status_map`; eviction task; `approved_at_sha` invalidation on push; updated `fixes_pushed` trigger logic |
| `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/merge_pr_local.rs` | New gate logic using `(branch, approved_sha)` |
| `rust/exomonad-core/src/domain.rs` | `Sha` newtype if not already present (probably yes — verify) |
| `tests/e2e/tangled-pr-codex/` | Extend testrunner.md + validate.sh to assert SHA pinning |

## Non-goals for this issue

- Changing the workflow `when:` trigger (Option B). CI keeps running on every push as a cheap dev-loop signal; the merge gate just doesn't trust pre-approval CI. Option B can be revisited if CI cost becomes a concern.
- Per-PR (rather than per-branch) CI tracking. Branches map 1:1 to PRs in our model; the `(branch, sha)` key is sufficient.

## Acceptance criteria

- `PrEntry.approved_at_sha` populated correctly on every reviewer approval transition in the watcher.
- `ci_status_map` keyed by `(BranchName, Sha)` with eviction.
- Merge gate consults SHA-pinned CI status; rejects merges where the approved SHA's CI is unknown or failed.
- Stale-passes-fresh race demonstrably blocked by an integration test that uses real spindle timing.
- Backward-compat fallback documented and dated for removal.
- ADR added in `docs/decisions/` describing the chosen invariant: "merge requires CI Success for the SHA the reviewer approved."

## Dependencies / sequencing

- **#283** (local PR fallback) must land first — the field-set additions to `PrEntry` need to coexist with the `LocalPrGet` effect signatures.
- **#284** (Tangled appview integration) is independent of this; either can land first.

issues.title: Define Tangled equivalents of github.get_pull_request / get_pull_request_for_branch via knot+spindle
issues.description:
## Context

#283 introduces a `LocalPRGet` effect that reads `.exo/prs.json` for local-only PR flows (no GitHub, no Tangled). That covers the e2e harness and any pure-local development. The third leg of the matrix — when the workspace points at a Tangled knot/spindle — is still undefined.

The current state:
- `.exo/prs.json` is the source of truth for local flow.
- GitHub API is the source of truth for hosted flow (via `services::github::GitHubClient`, octocrab).
- Tangled has no equivalent surface yet. The `worktree_event_watcher` already reads `.exo/prs.json` even when the remote is `tangled` (`file_pr_local.rs::resolve_push_remote` only chooses the *push* remote — it does not change the read path).

## What we need

Define how `merge_pr`'s self-merge guard, the stop-hook's "PR not filed?" check, and any future code that asks "what's the state of PR #N?" resolve the answer when the workspace's CI/PR layer is a Tangled knot.

Concretely, identify the equivalent of `gh pr view {n} --json ...`:
- Does the knot expose an HTTP endpoint listing PRs?
- Does the spindle's database (`spindle.db`, sqlite) carry PR state, or is that strictly CI-run state?
- If the knot proxies PR state, what's the schema — branch, author, review state, head SHA, base branch?
- Is there a CLI command (`tangled pr show`, etc.) we should shell out to from a Rust service?

Then decide:
- Map onto the existing `GitHubGetPullRequest`/`...ForBranch` effect types as alternative backends? (One effect, multiple backends — github_client OR tangled_client.)
- Or introduce a new namespace (`tangled.get_pull_request`)?
- Or normalize everything onto `local.get_pull_request` (i.e., `.exo/prs.json`) and have spindle keep that file authoritative?

The third option is appealing: spindle writes to `.exo/prs.json` as PR state changes; readers (#283's `LocalPRGet`) work unchanged for both pure-local and Tangled modes. Hosted GitHub is the only path that diverges.

## Acceptance criteria

- Architecture decision recorded in `docs/decisions/` (which option wins and why).
- Concrete protocol/schema defined for whichever option is chosen.
- Minimum-viable implementation prototyped — at least one end-to-end "fetch PR state from a tangled workspace" call.
- Existing local and GitHub paths still pass.

## Dependencies

- #283 — local `.exo/prs.json` fallback (the local effect already needs to land first; this issue then decides whether tangled writes into it or runs alongside it).

## Why later

The immediate blocker for the reviewer-convergence E2E is #283. Tangled-side PR semantics is the right next step once #283 unblocks the test, but does not gate this session's work.

comments.content:
## Investigation notes (2026-05-18)

### Tangled is a three-service architecture, not two

The CI integration we've already built talks to **two** Tangled services:

| Service | Role | ExoMonad's current relationship |
|---|---|---|
| **Knot** (`localhost:5555`) | Git server + pipeline trigger | Subscribes to `/events` for pipeline→branch mapping |
| **Spindle** (`localhost:6555`) | CI runner | Subscribes to `/events` for `pipeline.status` |
| **Appview** | Web UI + PR/comment DB | **Not connected.** |

PRs live in the **appview**, which we don't talk to today. The knot and spindle have no PR concept — they only know about pushes, pipelines, and CI status. That's why everything we've built so far (`worktree_event_watcher`, `merge_pr_local`, `.exo/prs.json`) treated the PR as a purely exomonad-local concept.

### Tangled's actual PR model

Tangled does have first-class PRs. They're stored as AT Protocol records under `sh.tangled.repo.*`:

| Lexicon | File | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `sh.tangled.repo.pull` | `lexicons/pulls/pull.json` | The PR record (title, body, target, source, rounds, mentions, references, dependentOn) |
| `sh.tangled.repo.pull.status` | `lexicons/pulls/state.json` | open / closed / merged |
| `sh.tangled.repo.pull.comment` | `lexicons/pulls/comment.json` | Comments |
| `sh.tangled.repo.pull.merged` | `lexicons/pulls/merged.json` | Merge event |
| `sh.tangled.repo.pull.closed` | `lexicons/pulls/closed.json` | Close event |
| `sh.tangled.repo.pull.open` | `lexicons/pulls/open.json` | Open event |

Notable: the `rounds` array on the pull record is structurally similar to our `rounds` counter in `.exo/prs.json`. Tangled already models the review-round concept natively.

Persistence + API surface live in the appview:

- `appview/db/pulls.go` — sqlite persistence (`SetPullsState`, etc.)
- `appview/pulls/router.go:21` — chi router with `/{pull}` subroutes — HTTP read path exists
- `appview/pages/pulls_compose.go`, `appview/models/pull.go`, `appview/validator/pull.go` — full compose+validate pipeline

Reads are XRPC-shaped (AT Protocol convention). We have not catalogued the exact endpoints yet — likely `sh.tangled.repo.getPull` or similar — but the routing infrastructure (chi mux + lexicon-typed records) is there.

### Three integration options for #284

#### Option A — ExoMonad talks to the appview as an additional remote service

Add a Tangled appview HTTP client mirroring the `GitHubClient` pattern. When the workspace is in tangled mode, the `LocalPRGet` effect (from #283) falls through to a `TangledPRGet` that queries the appview by repo DID + PR rkey.

Pros: keeps tangled's PR records authoritative; multi-collaborator scenarios work; review threads + comments naturally surface.
Cons: another network dependency; requires the appview to be available locally for tests; XRPC schema needs to be mapped to our existing `PrEntry`.

#### Option B — Spindle/knot pipeline events drive writes into `.exo/prs.json`; appview is consulted only on read miss

Treat `.exo/prs.json` as the canonical local cache. When spindle fires a pipeline event for a PR branch, exomonad enriches `.exo/prs.json` (head_sha, CI status, etc.). On a cache miss for a PR not yet observed locally, fall through to the appview.

Pros: zero-cost reads in the common path (which is what our flow does today); appview becomes a fetch-on-miss source instead of a hot dependency.
Cons: cache-invalidation footgun; multi-host scenarios with the same PR across machines diverge until they sync; tangled PRs that exomonad didn't author appear "missing" until poked.

#### Option C — Bidirectional sync: `.exo/prs.json` ↔ appview

ExoMonad treats `.exo/prs.json` as its authoring registry but syncs both ways: on `file_pr` create a `sh.tangled.repo.pull` record via XRPC; on observed appview record changes (via a future appview events WebSocket, or polling), reflect into `.exo/prs.json`.

Pros: best end-state for multi-collaborator development.
Cons: most work; needs a sync conflict policy; doesn't unblock #283.

### Recommendation

**Option B is the right next step.**

- It builds on the local-PR pattern we already have and that #283 will solidify.
- It scopes the appview integration to a single function (`TangledPRGet`) rather than fanning out to every PR-related code path.
- It preserves the CI gating pipeline that already works (`worktree_event_watcher` updating `merge_blocked_on_ci`).
- Option C can grow out of Option B incrementally — once reads are wired, writes (file_pr → appview XRPC) are a small additive change.

### Open questions to resolve before implementing

1. **Exact XRPC endpoint shape.** Read `tangled-core/api/` for the actual XRPC route names (`getPull`, `listPulls`?). The chi route at `appview/pulls/router.go:21` is HTML — the XRPC equivalent is what we'd call from Rust.
2. **Identity for reads.** Does appview require service auth for reads, or are public PR records anonymously readable? The local dev path bypasses service auth (`SPINDLE_SERVER_DEV=true`); production needs a strategy.
3. **PR rkey ↔ local PR number mapping.** Tangled PR records are keyed by AT Protocol tid (timestamp-based identifier). Our local registry uses sequential integers. Bridging the two needs to be stored somewhere — likely a new `tangled_at_uri` field on `PrEntry` in `file_pr_local.rs`.
4. **What does the tangled-pr-codex E2E exercise?** It currently uses `.exo/prs.json` end-to-end (see run.sh — "file_pr should use local .exo/prs.json flow"). That gives us a working harness to extend once Option B is implemented; the existing test won't need rewriting, just augmenting to verify appview-side records.

### Dependencies / sequencing

- **#283 first**: `LocalPRGet` must exist before we know where the github→tangled fallback hook goes.
- **Open subquestion**: whether to file the XRPC catalog work as a sub-issue or roll it into the architecture decision record this issue calls for.

## Scope decision (2026-05-18)

**Lock-in: Option B is the scope of this issue.** ExoMonad keeps `.exo/prs.json` as the canonical local registry; appview reads happen only as a fallback when the local cache misses. Once #283 lands, this issue becomes: implement `TangledPRGet` against the appview XRPC API and wire it as the second tier of `LocalPRGet`'s fallback chain.

**Option C (bidirectional sync, file_pr → appview write-through) is explicitly out of scope.** Treat it as a research note for future work, not a task. The trigger to revisit will be either:
- A multi-collaborator scenario where exomonad-authored PRs need to be visible in the appview UI, or
- A flow where appview PR state changes (comments, status transitions) must reflect into `.exo/prs.json` faster than the next exomonad-side observation.

Neither is on the near-term roadmap.

**Updated acceptance criteria:**

- Architecture decision recorded in `docs/decisions/` (Option B + the deferred Option C as a "future" appendix).
- `TangledPRGet` Rust effect handler implemented; wired into `LocalPRGet`'s fallback path from #283.
- One end-to-end "fetch PR state from a tangled workspace" test passes — local-PR cache miss falls through to appview.
- Existing tangled-pr-codex E2E continues to pass unchanged (its local-PR flow should be unaffected).

Open subquestions from the prior comment (XRPC endpoint shape, service-auth for reads, rkey↔number mapping, harness extension) remain. They are scoped to Option B implementation, not split into separate issues.
Implemented Tangled appview read-through fallback after .exo/prs.json cache miss; added tangled_appview_url config and architecture decision.
Verification passed: just fmt, just test-cargo-all, just check-e2e-tangled-pr-codex, and just build.

issues.title: merge_pr and dev stop-hook crash in local-PR flows: github handler unregistered, no fallback to .exo/prs.json
issues.description:
## Symptom

In a local-only flow (no GITHUB_TOKEN, no GitHub remote — e.g. the reviewer-convergence E2E), both `merge_pr` and the dev stop-hook crash because the github effect handler isn't registered.

Server log on the TL's `merge_pr` attempt:

```
effect_type=github.get_pull_request_for_branch
error=Not found: handler/github
```

The leaf-side error surfaces as `"Failed to fetch PR #1 for self-merge check. Cannot proceed."`
(see `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/MergePR.hs:137`).

The dispatched namespace list for that agent shows `["process", "session", "tasks", "merge_pr", "log", "coordination", "git", "kv", ...]` — `github` is conspicuously absent.

## Root cause

Two compounding issues:

1. **Conditional registration.** The github effect handler appears to be gated on GITHUB_TOKEN at PluginManager build time. When the token is unset, the handler is silently dropped and any effect in the `github.*` namespace yields "Not found: handler/github".
2. **No local-PR fallback.** `merge_pr`'s self-merge guard (`mergePRCore` in `MergePR.hs`) only consults `GitHubGetPullRequest`. But the local PR registry at `.exo/prs.json` already has the data we need (author_agent, head_branch, reviewer_agent, last_head_sha, review_state). The watcher already uses this registry. Merge does not.

The `.exo/prs.json` is the source of truth for local/Tangled PR flows. `merge_pr` was never aligned to it.

## Fix shape

Two layered fixes:

1. **merge_pr consults the local registry first.** Add an effect `LocalPRGet` (or extend `KV` semantics) that reads `.exo/prs.json` and returns the entry for a PR number. Use it in `mergePRCore` BEFORE calling GitHub. If a local entry exists, use it for the self-merge check and the readiness check. Only fall through to GitHub when no local entry exists.

2. **Same treatment for the dev stop-hook.** Anywhere `GitHubGetPullRequest` / `GitHubGetPullRequestForBranch` is called by an exo-internal tool, prefer the local registry when it has the data. GitHub remains the source for hosted flows.

3. **Decide what "no github handler" means.** Either always register it (and let calls fail with a clearer error like "GitHub unavailable; set GITHUB_TOKEN") OR explicitly note in the handler registration log that github was dropped due to missing token. "Not found: handler/github" is opaque.

## Acceptance criteria

- `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` completes merge_pr without the github fallback (or skips it cleanly when the test boundary says don't merge).
- Dev stop-hook does not crash on `github.get_pull_request_for_branch` when running in local-PR mode.
- When the GitHub handler is genuinely needed but absent, the error message names the missing token, not "handler/github not found".

## Why now

This is the last blocker on the reviewer-convergence loop test. Mechanism works; merge step crashes on the architectural mismatch.

comments.content:
## Investigation notes (2026-05-18)

### Root cause confirmed

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/handlers/groups.rs:39` registers the github handler only when `services.github_client` is `Some(_)`.
- `services::github::GitHubClient::new()` reads `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`services/github.rs:20-26`); when unset, the client fails to build and the handler is silently dropped.
- The dispatch error surface is the cryptic `Not found: handler/github` — exactly what we saw in the server pane.

### The local-PR pattern already exists — but was only wired through some call paths

Built during the worktree_event_watcher refactor:

- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr_local.rs` — "Local PR registry service — replaces GitHub API calls with .exo/prs.json"
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/merge_pr_local.rs` — "Merge a PR locally: read from .exo/prs.json, gate, git merge, push, update registry"

Wired through:

- ✅ `handlers/file_pr.rs:77-96` — dual-path: github if available, else `file_pr_local`
- ✅ `handlers/merge_pr.rs:95-121` — dual-path: github if available, else `merge_pr_local::merge_pr_local(...)`
- ✅ `services/worktree_event_watcher.rs` — reads `.exo/prs.json` directly, never touches github

### Why merge_pr still crashes despite Rust-side dual-path

The Rust `merge_pr` handler is fine. The crash is on the **Haskell side**, BEFORE the merge effect ever fires:

- `haskell/.../MergePR.hs:127` — self-merge guard: yields `GitHubGetPullRequest` to verify author identity. With github handler unregistered, this returns `Left "Not found: handler/github"` → line 137 maps it to `"Failed to fetch PR #N for self-merge check. Cannot proceed."` → `doMerge` is never reached → the Rust dual-path is unreachable from this code path.

### Other github.* callers in the Haskell guest

Only two remain after the watcher refactor:

| Location | Behavior on missing handler |
|---|---|
| `MergePR.hs:127` (`GitHubGetPullRequest`, self-merge guard) | **Crashes** — returns `Cannot proceed.` |
| `StopHook.hs:62` (`GitHubGetPullRequestForBranch`, "PR not filed?" nudge) | **Degrades cleanly** — `Left _ -> pure Nothing` at line 75-77 means no nudge, no crash |

So `StopHook.hs` already does the right thing. `MergePR.hs` is the only crash path.

### Recommended fix

Mirror the Rust dual-path on the Haskell side by adding a `LocalPRGet` effect:

1. **New effect `LocalPRGet`** (proto + Rust handler in the `local_pr` or extended `file_pr_local` namespace): takes `pr_number`, reads `.exo/prs.json`, returns `Maybe PrEntry` with the fields the self-merge guard needs (`head_branch`, `author_agent`, `review_state`, `last_head_sha`).

2. **`MergePR.hs:124-137`**: try `LocalPRGet` first.
   - If the local entry is present → derive `isSelfMerge` from `author_agent == ctx.agent_name` (or `head_branch == currentBranch`, same semantics). Derive readiness from `review_state == Approved`. Proceed without GitHub.
   - If no local entry **and** GitHub is unavailable → fail with a clear message naming both missing sources.
   - If no local entry **and** GitHub is available → fall back to the current `GitHubGetPullRequest` path.

3. **Optional but cheap**: Audit `StopHook.hs:62` to use `LocalPRGetForBranch` analogously, so the stop-hook nudge works in local-PR mode instead of silently being suppressed.

### Acceptance criteria (sharpened)

- `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` runs `merge_pr` to completion against `.exo/prs.json` with no `GITHUB_TOKEN` set.
- New `LocalPRGet` (and `LocalPRGetForBranch` if scope allows) effect is registered in the Rust namespaces list.
- `MergePR.hs` self-merge guard prefers local registry, falls back to GitHub.
- Error message when both sources fail names both, not "handler/github".

### Companion issue

See sibling issue for Tangled-side semantics — how the same data is sourced when the workspace points at a Tangled knot/spindle instead of GitHub.

issues.title: Canonicalize server socket path in uds_client to fix dev-leaf/reviewer MCP path-length failures
issues.description:
## Problem

`rust/exomonad/src/uds_client.rs::find_server_socket` returns the **logical path** of `.exo/server.sock` as walked from CWD. Inside a worktree this is a symlink to the project-root server.sock, but the returned PathBuf is the symlink path itself — e.g.:

```
/home/goya/.cache/exomonad-e2e/reviewer-convergence.XXX/repo/.exo/worktrees/trivial-contributing-codex/.exo/server.sock
```

That string is 124 bytes. Linux's `sockaddr_un.sun_path` caps at 108. `UnixStream::connect()` therefore fails for both dev-leaf and reviewer agents living in worktrees with even modestly long names, manifesting as:

```
MCP startup failed: Server socket not reachable after 15s
Last error: GET /health failed via .../worktrees/{leaf}/.exo/server.sock
```

The actual socket file sits at the much shorter project-root path (~54 bytes). The kernel never had a chance to resolve the symlink — the limit applies to what `connect()` is called with.

## Fix

Canonicalize the returned path so the symlink resolves to its real target before connect:

```rust
if sock.exists() {
    return sock.canonicalize().context("...");
}
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `find_server_socket` returns the canonical (symlink-resolved) absolute path.
- `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` runs end-to-end without MCP socket-not-reachable errors from dev-leaf or reviewer.

## Why this is the right layer

The previous workarounds (move WORK_DIR out of `/tmp`, out of `.e2e-work/`, into `~/.cache/`) all bounced the path-length problem between server bind and client connect. Canonicalizing on the client side removes the worktree depth from the equation entirely — only the actual socket location matters.

issues.title: Design a real E2E test harness (replace per-test run.sh duplicates)
issues.description:
## Problem

The current E2E setup is 13+ standalone `run.sh` scripts under `tests/e2e/*/`, each duplicating substantially the same bootstrap:

- `mktemp -d` a work dir (must be short enough for Unix sockets and outside /tmp because of Codex's helper-binary check)
- `git init` a bare remote + a working repo
- `exomonad new` + `chainlink init`
- symlink WASM, copy roles, write reviewer context
- write a `config.toml` with companions
- launch interactive tmux via `exomonad init`
- testrunner companion observes side effects and `notify_parent`s a verdict
- `trap cleanup EXIT` to tear down

Pain points discovered this session:

1. **Path-length traps.** Linux Unix-socket `sun_path` is 108 bytes; a deep work dir (e.g. inside the workspace) silently breaks `bind()` for `.exo/server.sock`. We hit this when moving WORK_DIR from `/tmp/` to `.e2e-work/`.
2. **Codex's "no /tmp" rule.** Codex refuses to install PATH helpers when `CODEX_HOME` lives under `/tmp`. Manifests as "WARNING: proceeding, even though we could not update PATH" and silently breaks the dev-leaf MCP handshake.
3. **Workspace contamination.** Putting the work dir inside the exomonad workspace re-introduces parent-walking discovery for `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.chainlink/`, etc. Tests start interacting with the live repo's state.
4. **Brittle leaf specs.** Test machinery (e.g. "no copyright header" in `reviewer-convergence-loop`) leaks into the leaf's spec and gets treated as a hard boundary, producing spurious `[FAILED]`s. Fixture state belongs in the harness, not in the leaf's prompt.
5. **Interactive-only.** Every harness ends with `exomonad init` attaching to a tmux session; can't be run headless in CI without a wrapper.
6. **No shared library.** Each `run.sh` re-implements preflight checks, env munging, cleanup. Drift between harnesses is invisible until something breaks.

Current workaround for #1/#2/#3: all harnesses now `mktemp -d` under `~/.cache/exomonad-e2e/` (short path, outside workspace, not under `/tmp`). This is a band-aid, not a design.

## What "better" looks like (rough)

- A single `e2e_harness` library (shell, Rust, or both) that exposes: `setup_repo`, `setup_codex_home`, `write_config`, `launch`, `cleanup`. Each test becomes a small declarative spec, not 100+ lines of duplicated bash.
- Either headless support (no tmux attach, drive directly via the MCP server) **or** a clean CI mode that uses a virtual tty.
- Explicit isolation boundary — work dir must be outside any exomonad workspace, with a short path by construction.
- Fixture state (repo contents, pre-existing files) lives in declarative test data, never in agent prompts.
- One shared cleanup contract; one shared preflight contract.
- Consider Rust-side fix: abstract Unix sockets (Linux \0-prefixed) or `EXOMONAD_SOCKET_PATH` env var to decouple socket path from work dir entirely.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define and document the new harness design (decision record in docs/decisions/).
- Migrate at least one existing test to the new harness and verify behavior parity.
