- Plan the migration of the remaining tests (does not need to be done in one PR).

## Why now

We just spent meaningful time chasing path-length and contamination bugs introduced by a band-aid harness change. The harness is the bottleneck on E2E coverage — it's the reason we have 7+ "still open" E2E test issues with no easy path to closing them.

issues.title: e2e reviewer-convergence: agents bypass MCP via UDS curl side-channel
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

When the leaf Codex's MCP initialize fails, the agent discovers it can hit the REST server directly through 'curl --unix-socket .exo/server.sock http://localhost/agents/dev/<name>/tools/call ...' and bypasses the entire MCP layer. In the T21HbTow run, the leaf filed PR #1 and emitted notify_parent this way without ever having an mcp-stdio handshake.

Two problems:
1. Test fidelity: the reviewer-convergence test partially progressed (PR opened, reviewer ran, fix committed and pushed) even though MCP was broken for the agent under test. The test currently asserts behavioral signals (fan-out fired, fixes pushed) which are independent of MCP transport, so an MCP regression doesn't fail this test. We need an explicit assertion in tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/testrunner.md (or validate.sh) that mcp-stdio is running for every spawned agent before the harness greenlights anything else.
2. Identity/security: any process inside a worktree can call /agents/<role>/<name>/tools/call against any role+name in the registry, with no auth beyond CWD. This was already a footgun, but it's now an observed escape hatch. Decision needed: do we want REST endpoints to require something more than 'be a process with the UDS path'? Or accept it as a local-only trust boundary?

Repro:
1. just e2e-reviewer-convergence
2. tmux capture-pane -t e2e-reviewer-convergence:4 -p -S -300 | grep '\-\-unix-socket'
3. See the curl POST to /agents/dev/trivial-contributing-codex/tools/call.

Cross-ref: companion issue 'Codex dev-leaf MCP initialize handshake fails after spawn' for the trigger condition.

issues.title: mcp-stdio child processes do not write to .exo/logs/sidecar.log
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Only the root agent's mcp-stdio logs appear in .exo/logs/sidecar.log. Reviewer and leaf mcp-stdio processes (spawned by Codex's MCP client) write tracing output somewhere else — or nowhere visible. This makes initialize-handshake failures (e.g. the leaf bug filed in the companion issue) impossible to diagnose without running mcp-stdio manually.

Evidence (run T21HbTow on 2026-05-18):
- sidecar.log contains 'mcp-stdio startup: beginning server socket discovery role="root" name="root"' but NOTHING for role="reviewer"/name="review-pr-1-codex" even though that process is currently running (pid 148481).
- Manually running 'exomonad mcp-stdio --role dev --name trivial-contributing-codex' emits the same startup log line to stderr — so the logger fires; it just doesn't reach the shared sidecar destination when launched as a Codex child.

Hypothesis: root's mcp-stdio is started by 'exomonad init' with stdout/stderr redirected to sidecar.log via the shell wrapper. Codex-launched mcp-stdio processes inherit Codex's stdio plumbing and their tracing output is lost (or piped back as MCP traffic and discarded as non-JSON).

Fix direction: mcp-stdio should explicitly initialize a file logger to .exo/logs/mcp-stdio-{role}-{name}.log on startup, independent of where stdin/stdout/stderr go. Bonus: per-process log per agent is easier to read than the shared sidecar.

Repro:
1. just e2e-reviewer-convergence (or any session with codex agents)
2. tail -F .exo/logs/sidecar.log | grep mcp-stdio
3. Note that only root entries appear.

issues.title: Codex dev-leaf MCP initialize handshake fails after spawn
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Symptom: Codex dev-leaf spawned via spawn_leaf (agent_type=codex) shows 'MCP client for exomonad failed to start: MCP startup failed: handshaking with MCP server failed: connection closed: initialize response' and then has no mcp-stdio child process. Root TL and reviewer Codex agents start mcp-stdio cleanly in the same session.

Reproduces in tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop (TmpDir T21HbTow run on 2026-05-18).

Verified rules out:
- Hook trust: CODEX_HOME/config.toml has matching trusted_hash entries for the leaf path (same hashes as reviewer, which works).
- exomonad binary discovery: leaf pane PATH includes target/debug; manual 'exomonad mcp-stdio --role dev --name trivial-contributing-codex' starts cleanly.
- Server socket reachability: root and reviewer mcp-stdio both succeed at socket discovery / health check against the same .exo/server.sock.
- WASM in worktree: irrelevant; mcp-stdio is a stdio<->REST shim and never loads WASM. The prior 'missing WASM' diagnosis surfaced by the leaf itself was a red herring.

Leading hypothesis: cold-start race. mcp_stdio.rs:30-attempt x 500ms retry can take ~15s on a cold server; root's took 5.5s/12 attempts per sidecar.log. Codex's MCP initialize timeout is shorter than mcp-stdio's worst-case retry budget, so when the leaf's Codex starts mcp-stdio while the server's WASM plugin cache is still warming for the new agent identity (line 112 of sidecar.log shows 'Registering yield_effect ... agent=trivial-contributing-codex' happening ~110s AFTER spawn), Codex bails. Reviewer hit a warm server, so handshake was instant.

Fallback evidence: the leaf bypassed MCP and called the REST endpoints via 'curl --unix-socket .exo/server.sock /agents/dev/trivial-contributing-codex/tools/call' for file_pr and notify_parent (visible in window 4 pane). Those calls succeeded — which is why this test partially progressed.

Repro:
1. just install-all-dev
2. just e2e-reviewer-convergence
3. Inspect leaf pane (window 4) for the 'handshaking with MCP server failed' line.
4. pgrep -af mcp-stdio — leaf will be missing.

Likely fix surfaces (need investigation, not commit):
- Speed up server's per-agent plugin registration so initialize is fast post-spawn.
- Make mcp-stdio respond to 'initialize' BEFORE socket discovery completes, then lazy-bind to the UDS on the first tools/* call. The current code blocks the entire run() on socket discovery before reading from stdin.
- Have Codex retry MCP startup once on initialize failure (Codex-side).

Related:
- mcp_stdio.rs already references chainlink #260 (socket race during init).
- ac8af6c3 'Add MCP startup diagnostics' is recent — confirm whether it changed the retry shape.
- 91dc4f0c 'Update changelog for reviewer queue tasks' is current HEAD.

issues.title: Add diagnostic logging to mcp_stdio startup + exomonad serve listen() to debug connect-race
issues.description:
## Context
Spawned codex agents intermittently fail to start their MCP client with:
\`\`\`
⚠ MCP client for \`exomonad\` failed to start: MCP startup failed: handshaking with MCP server failed: connection closed: initialize response
⚠ MCP startup incomplete (failed: exomonad)
\`\`\`

The error from Codex is misleading — the failure is NOT in handling Codex's \`initialize\` JSON-RPC. It's that \`exomonad mcp-stdio\` bailed at startup before reading any stdin, which closes stdout and makes Codex report \"connection closed\". See \`rust/exomonad/src/mcp_stdio.rs:23-47\`: if discovery + is_healthy fails 30 times at 500ms (15s total), bail with \`anyhow::bail!\`. Related: chainlink #260 (which added the retry loop).

## Goal
Add enough log lines that the NEXT failed run tells us which of these is happening:

1. **Symlink-vs-listener race** — \`.exo/server.sock\` symlink exists but server hasn't called \`listen()\` yet
2. **Server restart mid-test** — server crashed and re-bound after leaf already gave up
3. **Server slow startup** — WASM plugin load or similar blocking past 15s
4. **is_healthy() false-positive healthy** — connect succeeds but server isn't actually ready to dispatch

## Add diagnostic logs

### \`rust/exomonad/src/mcp_stdio.rs::run\`
- Before retry loop: log resolved socket path candidate, expected agent role+name.
- Each retry iteration: log \`attempt N/30, discovery=..., is_healthy=...\` (DEBUG level, so we don't spam normal runs).
- On bail: log the socket path tried, total elapsed time, last error from is_healthy.

### \`rust/exomonad/src/serve.rs\` (or wherever \`exomonad serve\` binds)
- Before \`bind\`: log socket path.
- After \`bind\` succeeds: log \"listening on {path}\" with timestamp.
- After WASM plugins finish loading: log \"plugins ready, accepting connections\" with timestamp + plugin count.
- On any panic/exit: log reason at ERROR level.

### \`rust/exomonad-core/src/uds_client.rs::is_healthy\` (or wherever)
- If \`is_healthy\` just connects and returns true on bind, change it to round-trip a \`GET /health\` (or equivalent) to ensure the server is actually responsive, not just bound. Log whichever it does.

### Symlink creation site
- Wherever \`.exo/server.sock\` symlink is created in the leaf worktree (probably during \`fork_wave\` / \`spawn_leaf\` worktree setup): log timestamp of symlink creation + target.

## Test
- Manual: re-run e2e-reviewer-convergence; if startup fails, the logs should pinpoint the failure mode within the 15s window.

## Out of scope
- Actually fixing the underlying race. This task is just to give us the data. Whatever the logs reveal becomes a follow-up.

## Related
- chainlink #260 (the retry was added there; this builds on it)

issues.title: Late approval after STUCK declaration — race or stale message?
issues.description:
## Problem
E2E run timeline showed an out-of-order sequence at the TL:

```
1. [STUCK: 1, rounds=2] (from both dev-leaf and reviewer)
2. [from review-pr-1-codex Re-reviewed PR 1 after fixes and approved it. The require...]
3. [from trivial-contributing-codex PR 1 updated with the watcher-requested copyright]
```

The reviewer's APPROVAL arrived AFTER the STUCK declaration. Two possible causes:

### Hypothesis A: Round 3 ran despite stuck
The watcher's stuck flag (`old_state.stuck = true` at line ~1391) is set but a subsequent SHA change triggers another review pass. The early-return guard at lines ~1294-1299 (`if old_state.notified_parent_approved || old_state.notified_parent_timeout || old_state.stuck && !recover_after_ci_block && !merge_ready_now`) should prevent this — verify it actually does.

### Hypothesis B: Stale message queued during STUCK transition
The reviewer's approval was a queued message from a prior round that got delivered late, after STUCK was declared. The Teams inbox / tmux fallback may not have message-ordering guarantees, and the delivery debounce could let approve-then-stuck arrive as stuck-then-approve.

## Investigation
1. Check `worktree_event_watcher.rs` line ~1294-1299 guard — is `stuck` actually short-circuiting properly, or does some path bypass it?
2. Add a server-log timestamp to each emitted event and to each delivered message. Compare emission order vs delivery order.
3. Check `inject_input` mutex/serialization — once STUCK is in-flight, subsequent injections should NOT pre-empt it.

## Test
- Reproduce by re-running e2e-reviewer-convergence and capturing tmux + server logs with timestamps.
- Assert: after a `kind: stuck` event is emitted, no further `kind: approved` or `kind: review_received` events are emitted for the same PR.

## Depends on
- #268 (reviewer notify_parent strip) — once reviewer stops calling notify_parent directly, this race shrinks to watcher-only events. The investigation may simplify or resolve.

issues.title: Single source of STUCK: watcher-only emission
issues.description:
## Problem
E2E run produced TWO sources of `[STUCK: 1, rounds=2]` arriving at the TL:
- `[from: trivial-contributing-codex] [STUCK: 1, rounds=2] Review did not converge after 2 rounds. Dev leaf remains alive.`
- `[from: review-pr-1-codex] [STUCK: 1, rounds=2] Review did not converge. Dev leaf remains alive.`

The dev-leaf and the reviewer are each deciding the round cap themselves and emitting the STUCK signal. Per the design (chainlink #265 parent), the watcher is the canonical emitter of STUCK — it owns `pr_review_cycle_count` and the `max_rounds` policy.

## Fix
- Strip STUCK emission from the dev-leaf role and reviewer role.
- The watcher's existing `compute_pr_actions` in `worktree_event_watcher.rs` already emits `kind: stuck` when `rounds >= max_rounds` (lines ~1390-1403). That should be the SINGLE source.
- Verify the dev-leaf and reviewer roles don't have heuristics that emit STUCK based on local observations.

## Files (likely)
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/DevRole.hs` — strip any STUCK-emission paths
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs` — strip any STUCK-emission paths
- `.exo/lib/PRReviewHandler.hs` — verify all STUCK emission flows through `NotifyParentAction` from the watcher's event dispatch, not from agent-side logic
- Templates: ensure `stuck` template is only constructed in the watcher's WASM event path, not in agent code

## Test
- E2E: assert exactly one `[STUCK: ...]` message in the TL pane, prefixed `[from: ...watcher...]` or unprefixed (watcher-injected), NOT from a leaf or reviewer agent name.

## Depends on
- #268 (reviewer notify_parent strip) — these are sibling cleanups, can land in either order.

issues.title: TL cleanup on MERGE READY: merge + close issue + tear down agents
issues.description:
## Problem
On `[MERGE READY: pr-N]`, TL currently merges via `merge_pr` MCP tool but does not:
- Close the associated chainlink issue
- Tear down the dev-leaf worktree/window
- Tear down any associated workers spawned for this issue

These cleanup steps are currently implicit/manual.

## Fix
Add a TL handler for `[MERGE READY: pr-N]` that performs the full sequence:
1. Call `merge_pr` MCP tool
2. Verify merge succeeded (CI green, branch merged)
3. Call `chainlink_issue_close` MCP tool for the issue tied to this PR
4. Tear down dev-leaf worktree (call appropriate worktree-cleanup MCP path)
5. Tear down workers spawned by this dev-leaf for this issue

The TL needs to know which chainlink issue + dev-leaf + workers are associated with pr-N. Options:
- Store mapping in `.exo/prs.json` at PR creation time (which dev-leaf, which chainlink issue)
- Look up via session/team registry

## Files
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/TLRole.hs`, `RootRole.hs`
- `.exo/lib/` for merge_ready handler
- `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr_local.rs` if PR<->issue mapping needs to be added to registry

## Test
- E2E: run convergence test, verify after `[MERGE READY]` that chainlink issue is closed and worktrees are gone

issues.title: Reviewer state machine: STRIP notify_parent tool from reviewer role (not just simplify state)
issues.description:
## Status
Reopened 2026-05-17. The first pass (commit 4c90f610) simplified ReviewerPhase + ReviewerRole state machine but did NOT remove the `notify_parent` tool from the reviewer's tool list. Reviewer agents are still calling `notify_parent` in e2e runs, producing TL log entries like:
- `[from review-pr-1-codex Reviewed PR 1 and requested the required CONTRIBUTING.md ...]`
- `[from review-pr-1-codex Re-reviewed PR 1 after fixes and approved it. ...]`
- `[from: review-pr-1-codex] [STUCK: 1, rounds=2]`

These are direct `notify_parent` calls by the reviewer agent, not poller-emitted messages. The reviewer still has access to the tool and the LLM is choosing to call it.

## Fix (tighter scope)
Remove `notify_parent` from the reviewer role's exported MCP tool list. Specifically:
- `.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs` — drop `notify_parent` from the role's tool set.
- Audit `.exo/lib/` and `haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest/Tools/` for any reviewer-accessible variants (send_message etc. that could be misused as a TL-notification path).
- Reviewer's TERMINAL effect is the `.exo/prs.json` review_state write. That is its only legitimate way to communicate to the rest of the system.

## Test
- Unit: enumerate reviewer role's tool list, assert `notify_parent` is absent.
- E2E: re-run e2e-reviewer-convergence; assert TL pane has ZERO `[from review-pr-*]` lines from the reviewer agent during the full PR lifecycle. The only messages to TL must come from the watcher and the dev-leaf.

## What stays from the first pass
- Ephemeral state machine simplification (commit 4c90f610) is correct and stays.
- Stop-hook gate based on Posted state — correct, stays.

## Don't strip
- `send_message` between peer agents may still be legitimate (e.g., for dev-to-dev coordination). Verify reviewer role doesn't get it either, but don't blanket-remove from all roles.

## Problem
`compute_pr_actions` in `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs` fires `review_received` twice for a single reviewer ChangesRequested action:

issues.title: Reviewer-as-ephemeral redesign + dedup review_received in worktree_event_watcher
issues.description:
## Scope note (2026-05-17)

`github_poller.rs` has ZERO active call sites — it's legacy/dead code. The active poller is `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs` (the local PR registry / tangled-ready watcher). ALL changes below target the watcher, not github_poller.

## Symptoms observed in e2e-reviewer-convergence

1. Two `[Copilot Review on PR 1]` messages concatenated into a single Codex prompt → only one Enter pressed for both.
2. Reviewer agent stuck in `Stop hook (blocked): PR #1 has requested changes` loop (dev-leaf state machine wrongly applied to reviewer).
3. Reviewer calls `notify_parent` to TL, polluting TL's notification stream.

## Architecture (target)

- **Reviewer = ephemeral.** Spawned per round. Reads diff, writes review_state into `.exo/prs.json` (and comments into `.exo/reviews/`), exits cleanly. No `notify_parent`. No stay-alive stop-hook policy.
- **Poller owns the loop.** `worktree_event_watcher` spawns reviewers internally via the existing `ReviewerSpawner` trait. Tracks rounds. Aggregates review-approval + CI status into `[MERGE READY]`.
- **TL is hands-off.** Receives only `[MERGE READY: pr-N]`, `[STUCK: pr-N, reason]`, or `[FAILED: pr-N, reason]`. On `[MERGE READY]`: merge → close chainlink issue → tear down dev-leaf + workers.

## Vocabulary

Poller → TL:
- `[MERGE READY: pr-N]` — review approved AND CI green
- `[STUCK: pr-N, reason]` — round cap exceeded, or unresolvable
- `[FAILED: pr-N, reason]` — dev-leaf failed

Poller → dev-leaf (round 1 only):
- `[REVIEW COMMENTS: pr-N]` — inject reviewer's comments

Poller → reviewer: nothing. Reviewer is ephemeral per round.
Reviewer → anyone: nothing. Reviewer side-effects to PR state and exits.

## See subissues for breakdown

Each sub-task is small enough to dispatch as one dev leaf with a self-contained spec.

issues.title: Advance reviewer detached-HEAD worktree to new PR tip on fixes_pushed event
issues.description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

## Symptom

After the leaf addresses reviewer feedback and pushes a new commit, the watcher (once #262 is fixed) will fan a `fixes_pushed` event out to the reviewer agent. But the reviewer's worktree at `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-<N>-<type>` is a detached-HEAD checkout pinned to the **original** PR tip — it does not auto-advance. So the reviewer's `git diff main..HEAD`, file reads, and any tool-driven re-inspection will see the **old** code, not the fix.

This silently produces wrong reviews after the first round of changes: the reviewer either keeps requesting the same change (because the worktree still shows the unfixed file) or approves prematurely against stale state, depending on what it inspects.

## Why the worktree is detached

By design — see `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1388-1390` and `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs:134-138`. A detached worktree gives the reviewer an immutable, read-only snapshot at spawn time without competing for the worker's branch or clobbering its config. The contract is "do not commit, do not branch." But the contract did not previously specify what happens when the upstream branch advances mid-session.

## Decision

Keep the reviewer agent alive across rounds (it owns conversational state from the previous review). On `fixes_pushed`, advance the reviewer's detached HEAD to the new tip of the PR branch so its subsequent file reads see the fix.

## Fix sketch

When the watcher fires `fixes_pushed`, before fanning the event out to the reviewer's plugin manager, advance the reviewer worktree:

```
git -C .exo/worktrees/review-pr-<N>-<type> fetch origin <head_branch>
git -C .exo/worktrees/review-pr-<N>-<type> checkout --detach <new_sha>
```

Open questions to resolve in implementation:

1. **Who runs the git command** — Rust (watcher side, before fan-out) or Haskell (a `git.update_detached_head` effect yielded by `ReviewerRole.hs`'s FixesPushed handler)? Rust-side is simpler and ensures the worktree is correct before the agent reads it; Haskell-side is more orthogonal but races the agent.
2. **Effect name and shape** if Haskell-side: probably `git.checkout_detached { working_dir, ref }` or `git.advance_head { working_dir, target_sha }`, with a corresponding Rust handler.
3. **Failure mode** if the fetch fails (network, knot down): event still needs to fire so the reviewer can at least produce a "could not refresh — retry" notification rather than silently reviewing stale code.

## Acceptance

- `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` runs to completion AND the reviewer's second review is computed against the post-fix file contents (test should assert the reviewer reads the new line / hash in CONTRIBUTING.md after the fix).
- A unit or integration test verifies the reviewer worktree HEAD advances on `fixes_pushed`.
- Detached-HEAD invariant preserved (reviewer still has no branch, still does not commit).

## Related

- Blocks the convergence loop being end-to-end correct.
- Sibling to chainlink #262 (the panic that currently masks this problem by killing the watcher before fan-out can even reach a stale reviewer).
- Detached design rationale: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs:134-138`, `agent_control/spawn.rs:1388-1390`.

comments.content:
## Clarification on which SHA to advance to

Advance to **the exact commit SHA the watcher captured when it fired `fixes_pushed`**, not "the current tip of the PR branch." Reasons:

- Deterministic: two rapid pushes from the worker could race the reviewer's fetch and produce a different tip than the one the event was generated for. The reviewer's notification and the code it reviews must reference the same SHA.
- Replayable: if the event is re-fanned out later, the reviewer ends up on the same commit either way.
- Avoids fetch dependency for the SHA lookup — we already have it in hand.

## Required: extend the `fixes_pushed` payload to include the SHA

Current payload (`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:1203-1210`):

```json
{ "kind": "fixes_pushed", "pr_number": N, "ci_status": "..." }
```

Needs to become:

```json
{ "kind": "fixes_pushed", "pr_number": N, "ci_status": "...", "head_sha": "<new-sha>" }
```

The new SHA is already in scope at the call site (`pr_sha` parameter / `old_state.last_sha` after update). Just thread it through.

Same likely applies to `commits_pushed`, `review_received` after-fix, and `approved`/`merge_ready` — anything where "what was the code at the time this event was generated" matters for downstream consumers.

## Updated fix sketch

When the reviewer advances its worktree (whether driven from Rust pre-fan-out or Haskell-side via an effect), it should checkout the SHA from the event payload:

```
git -C .exo/worktrees/review-pr-<N>-<type> fetch origin <head_branch>
git -C .exo/worktrees/review-pr-<N>-<type> checkout --detach <event.head_sha>
```

If `fetch` does not bring that SHA into the local object DB (e.g. the worker's branch was rewound), surface that as a typed failure rather than silently checking out a different commit.

issues.title: Remove panicking From<&str> impl from validated_string! macro
issues.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

## Symptom

`validated_string!` (`rust/exomonad-core/src/domain.rs:45-102`) generates an `impl From<&str>` for every validated newtype that does:

```rust
impl From<&str> for $name {
    fn from(s: &str) -> Self {
        assert!(!s.is_empty(), concat!($field, " must not be empty"));
        Self(s.to_string())
    }
}
```

This is a process-killing landmine across every domain newtype (`BranchName`, `BirthBranch`, `SessionId`, `ToolName`, `GithubOwner`, `GithubRepo`, `Revision`, and ~3 others). Any caller anywhere in the codebase that hands an empty string into one of these — including effect handlers reading external command output — kills the tokio task with a bare `assert!` panic. The first instance of this caused chainlink #<this-issue>-sibling (reviewer watcher panic via `git branch --show-current` returning empty on detached HEAD).

## Why it is wrong

1. `From` is infallible by contract; using it for fallible validation breaks that contract.
2. `assert!` in library code aborts the worker thread instead of surfacing a typed error.
3. The `TryFrom<String>` impl right above it already returns `Result<_, DomainError::Empty>` — the same data path has both a correct (fallible) and incorrect (panicking) entry point, and callers reach for the convenient one.

## Fix

Remove the `From<&str>` impl from `validated_string!` entirely. Force every caller to go through `TryFrom`/`FromStr` and handle the `DomainError::Empty` case explicitly, or add a `try_from_str(&str) -> Result<Self, DomainError>` inherent method.

If there are call sites today that genuinely cannot fail (constants, tests), they can use `Self::try_from(s.to_string()).expect("...")` with a meaningful message, which still aborts but at least documents intent at the call site.

## Acceptance

- `From<&str>` impl removed from `validated_string!` macro.
- All call sites migrated to a fallible API.
- `cargo test --workspace` passes.
- No more `assert!(!s.is_empty(), ...)` reachable from production code paths.

## References

- macro: `rust/exomonad-core/src/domain.rs:45-102`
- panicking impl: `rust/exomonad-core/src/domain.rs:69-75`
- types affected: `SessionId, ToolName, GithubOwner, GithubRepo, BranchName, Revision, BirthBranch, ...` (see all `validated_string!` invocations in `domain.rs`)

issues.title: Fix watcher panic when reviewer worktree is detached (get_branch returns empty -> BranchName::from panics)
issues.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

## Symptom

The worktree event watcher tokio task panics on the first `pr_review` fan-out to a reviewer agent, killing the poll loop. After that no further poll cycles run, so `prs.json` `last_head_sha` is never updated and `fixes_pushed` never fires. The reviewer + leaf convergence loop stalls indefinitely.

Repro: `just e2e-reviewer-convergence`. Server log shows:
```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' (...) panicked at rust/exomonad-core/src/domain.rs:129:1:
branch_name must not be empty
```

## Root cause

`rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git.rs:135-138`:

```rust
pub async fn get_branch(&self, dir: &str) -> Result<BranchName> {
    let output = self.exec_git(dir, &["branch", "--show-current"]).await?;
    Ok(BranchName::from(output.trim()))
}
```

`git branch --show-current` prints an empty line when HEAD is detached. `BranchName::from(&str)` (`domain.rs:69-75`) asserts non-empty and panics.

Reviewer worktrees are intentionally created in detached HEAD state (see `spawn.rs:1388-1390` and `git_worktree.rs:134-138`) so a read-only reviewer does not compete with the worker's branch or clobber its config files. The design is correct — the handler is what is broken.

The `GetBranchResponse` proto already has a `detached: bool` field (`handlers/git.rs:58` hardcodes it to `false`), so the wire format anticipates this state; only the implementation does not.

## Fix

`GitService::get_branch` should return something like `Result<Option<BranchName>>` (or a small enum: `Branch(BranchName) | Detached`) and `GitHandler::get_branch` should populate `detached: true, branch: ""` when the HEAD is detached, instead of feeding `""` into `BranchName::from`.

The Haskell-side `ReviewerRole.hs` review_received handler that yields `git.get_branch` must also tolerate the detached response — likely it does not actually need the branch name (the reviewer knows its own birth_branch from spawn-time context) and the call can be dropped, or it can treat `detached=true` as a no-op for the branch-name read.

## Acceptance

- `just e2e-reviewer-convergence` runs to completion with `fixes_pushed` fanned out to the reviewer after the leaf pushes its fix.
- No `tokio-rt-worker ... panicked` lines in the server log.
- A unit test in `services/git.rs` exercises `get_branch` against a detached-HEAD worktree and asserts non-panicking behavior.

## References

- panic site: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git.rs:137`
- assert: `rust/exomonad-core/src/domain.rs:72`
- detached worktree design: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/git_worktree.rs:134-138`
- reviewer spawn: `rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1388-1402`
- captured panic at: `/tmp/exomonad-e2e-reviewer-convergence.xc9rHmUd/` server pane (2026-05-17T22:31:35Z)

issues.title: Reviewer context file not provisioned to reviewer worktree — fixture-specified review checklist invisible to reviewer
issues.description:
## Problem

#258's plan adds a fixture-local `.exo/context/reviewer-checklist.md` that biases the auto-spawned reviewer to request a specific change. The latest e2e run shows the reviewer ignores the checklist and approves based purely on the PR diff:

> Reviewer approved the PR based solely on the diff, lacking the fixture-specific requirements.
> Root Cause: The reviewer context fixture file (.exo/context/reviewer-checklist.md) was not provisioned to the reviewer worktree during reviewer agent spawn.

The reviewer runs in its OWN git worktree at `.exo/worktrees/review-pr-N-codex/`. That worktree is detached HEAD off the PR's head_branch (per spawn_reviewer_subtree). Files in the project root's `.exo/context/` are NOT in the reviewer's worktree because they're not committed to the PR branch — they exist only in the project root cwd.

When spawn_reviewer_subtree builds the reviewer's task, the context section reads (per spawn.rs:1339):
```rust
let context_section = if self.reviewer_context.is_empty() {
    String::new()
} else {
    format!(
        "\n\nRead first:\n{}",
        self.reviewer_context
            .iter()
            .map(|p| format!("- {p}"))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\n")
    )
};
```

So it lists the context paths as relative strings in the task prompt. The reviewer, running in its detached worktree, tries to read those paths and finds nothing because the files don't exist relative to its worktree.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT commit the context file to the PR branch as a fixture. It's a test artifact; polluting the branch isn't right.
- DO NOT change reviewer_context to take absolute paths only. Relative paths from project root must keep working — that's the normal production pattern.
- DO NOT copy the context file into every reviewer worktree from spawn_reviewer_subtree unconditionally. Files in .exo/ are conceptually outside the worktree contract.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1334-1409 — spawn_reviewer_subtree, including context_section construction
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1371-1382 — detached reviewer worktree creation
- rust/exomonad/src/config.rs ReviewerConfig — where reviewer_context (or context) is defined and how it resolves
- tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/run.sh:131-132 — where the fixture writes `.exo/context/reviewer-checklist.md` into the PROJECT root (not the reviewer's worktree)

## Steps
1. Pick a resolution strategy. Recommended: resolve reviewer_context paths against the PROJECT ROOT (not the reviewer worktree). Embed the absolute path into the task prompt at spawn time. The reviewer then reads from `/abs/path/to/project/.exo/context/reviewer-checklist.md`, which IS readable from anywhere (it's outside the worktree but still on disk).
2. Update spawn_reviewer_subtree's context_section builder to resolve relative paths against project_dir() and emit the absolute form into the task prompt.
3. Add a unit test asserting that for a relative reviewer_context path '.exo/context/X.md', the rendered task prompt contains the absolute path '/abs/project/.exo/context/X.md'.
4. Verify in the e2e: reviewer task prompt (visible in its pane) shows the absolute checklist path and the reviewer reads it, naturally requesting the fixture-required change.

## Verify
- cargo test -p exomonad-core spawn_reviewer_context_path_resolution — new unit test
- just check-fmt + just test-fast pass
- Manual e2e: reviewer's task prompt visibly includes the absolute path to reviewer-checklist.md; reviewer writes a changes_requested verdict citing the missing copyright header (per the checklist)

## Done criteria
- reviewer_context paths in [reviewer].context resolve correctly when the reviewer runs in a detached worktree
- The e2e's reviewer reads the fixture checklist and writes a changes_requested verdict naturally
- Phase 3 of the convergence-loop testrunner passes (reviewer requests changes), unblocking Phases 4-5 of #258's e2e harness

## Why
This is the blocking condition on #258 working end-to-end. Without fixing reviewer context resolution, the fixture-biased reviewer approach can't operate, and the test stays unable to deterministically exercise the FixesPushed convergence path.

comments.content: Claimed by interactive session.

Landed in 583e0851. Extracted render_reviewer_context_section pure helper that resolves relative paths against project_dir. Reviewer in its detached worktree now sees absolute paths and can read the fixture checklist. 3 unit tests cover relative/absolute/empty cases. just check-fmt + just test-fast pass.

issues.title: Dev-leaf MCP socket symlink missing in worktree — connect fails on first MCP call
issues.description:
## Problem

Spawned dev-leaves consistently emit at startup:
```
⚠ MCP client for exomonad failed to start: MCP startup failed: Mcp error: -32603:
  Failed to connect to /tmp/.../repo/.exo/worktrees/trivial-contributing-codex/.exo/server.sock
```

The path the codex client looks at is inside the leaf's worktree (`<worktree>/.exo/server.sock`). For the MCP connection to succeed, that path must be a symlink to the project root's `.exo/server.sock`. Either the symlink isn't being created before codex starts its MCP client, OR the path codex looks at doesn't match where create_socket_symlink put the symlink.

Observed in two consecutive e2e runs of tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop. The leaf eventually succeeds on later MCP calls (per server log, notify_parent works after the startup race), but the startup error is loud and confuses any operator inspecting the test.

This is logically separate from chainlink #253 (the hook trust env-propagation bug, which #259 follow-up will close).

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT retry the MCP connection at the agent level. The agent should never see a missing socket; it's an infrastructure precondition.
- DO NOT use a relative path resolution that walks parent dirs. Codex's MCP client uses the configured absolute or cwd-relative path; the symlink must exist at exactly that path.
- DO NOT delay codex spawn unconditionally to give create_socket_symlink time. Find the actual sequencing bug.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs — search 'create_socket_symlink' and trace the call order vs codex spawn
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs — leaf spawn path
- The .mcp.json that gets written to the leaf worktree — confirm the socket path it specifies
- create_socket_symlink implementation — verify it creates `<worktree>/.exo/server.sock` → project_root/.exo/server.sock

## Steps
1. Reproduce: just e2e-reviewer-convergence. After the leaf pane shows the error, check whether `<worktree>/.exo/server.sock` exists. Two outcomes:
   a. Symlink IS there now but wasn't at codex startup → ordering bug; create_socket_symlink runs after codex spawn.
   b. Symlink is NOT there → create_socket_symlink isn't being called for the leaf, OR is called with wrong path.
2. If ordering: move create_socket_symlink before the codex spawn command is sent to tmux. There may be an awaitable hook we're missing.
3. If wrong path: confirm what path the leaf's .mcp.json specifies and compare to where create_socket_symlink wrote the symlink. The .mcp.json may have been generated with the project-root socket path instead of the worktree-local path, in which case the path doesn't need a symlink at all — fix .mcp.json to use the worktree-local path that does get symlinked.
4. Add an integration test that spawns a leaf and asserts the symlink exists immediately after spawn returns (before codex would try to use it).

## Verify
- cargo test (new integration test)
- Manual e2e: leaf pane does NOT show 'MCP client for exomonad failed to start' or any socket-connect-failed message

## Done criteria
- Every spawned agent's worktree has a `<worktree>/.exo/server.sock` symlink in place before the agent process starts its MCP client
- The startup-time MCP-startup-failed warning is absent from leaf, reviewer, and worker panes
- Regression test pins the symlink-before-spawn ordering

## Why
The startup error is one of the louder pieces of test-debug noise — operators see it and assume the server is broken when it's just a precondition race. Fixing it cleans up the e2e output AND removes a real reliability risk for the first-MCP-call path.

comments.content: Claimed. Starting.

Landed in 1e979e42. mcp_stdio now retries connect via ServerClient::is_healthy probe, not just find_server_socket file existence. 30 attempts at 500ms = same 15s budget but covers the actual failure mode (symlink exists but listener not ready). just test-fast passes.

issues.title: CODEX_HOME not propagated to spawned dev-leaf — hook trust prompt fires for leaves but not root TL
issues.description:
## Problem

After commit b0ec0190 (#253 fix), the codex ROOT TL no longer hits 'hooks need review' on session start — confirmed in the latest e2e run. But the codex DEV LEAF spawned by the root TL still hits:

```
⚠ 3 hooks need review before they can run. Open /hooks to review them.
⚠ MCP client for exomonad failed to start: Failed to connect to .../trivial-contributing-codex/.exo/server.sock
```

The leaf is spawned via spawn_leaf → internal.rs build_agent_command, which prepends env_vars from common_spawn_env (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs:115-148) as a shell prefix on the codex command. That HashMap currently includes EXOMONAD_AGENT_ID, EXOMONAD_SESSION_ID, EXOMONAD_ROLE, CHAINLINK_DB, etc. — but NOT CODEX_HOME. The init.rs-level tmux set-environment for CODEX_HOME (b0ec0190) covers the root TL pane but does not reliably reach new panes created later by spawn_leaf, OR the shell prefix's missing CODEX_HOME overrides what would have been inherited.

Result: the leaf's codex process falls back to ~/.codex, sees no hook-trust entries for the temp repo, fires the review prompt. install_codex_hook_trust DID seed the entries in $CODEX_HOME from init.rs at root spawn time AND from internal.rs:713 at leaf spawn time — but if the leaf can't see $CODEX_HOME, those entries are invisible.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT remove the tmux set-environment from init.rs. It's the right thing for the root TL and acts as belt-and-suspenders.
- DO NOT add CODEX_HOME to the WASM-side environment for any reason. This is a host-side spawn-env concern.
- DO NOT condition the propagation on agent_type. Every codex agent needs it; non-codex agents seeing a CODEX_HOME env var is harmless.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs:113-177 — common_spawn_env where shell-prefix env vars are added
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs:343-353 — the env-prefix builder
- rust/exomonad/src/init.rs:715 area — the root TL CODEX_HOME tmux propagation (correct, keep)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/codex_config.rs install_codex_hook_trust — already runs at leaf spawn time, writing to $CODEX_HOME/config.toml

## Steps
1. In common_spawn_env, after the CHAINLINK_DB insert, add a CODEX_HOME pass-through:
   ```rust
   if let Ok(codex_home) = std::env::var("CODEX_HOME") {
       if !codex_home.is_empty() {
           env_vars.insert("CODEX_HOME".to_string(), codex_home);
       }
   }
   ```
   Add an inline doc comment explaining the parallel to the init.rs-level tmux propagation and citing this issue.
2. Add a unit test (similar to test_common_spawn_env_chainlink_db_directory_form) asserting CODEX_HOME appears in the env HashMap when set in the parent process env, and is absent when not set.
3. Manual: just install-all-dev && just e2e-reviewer-convergence — the dev-leaf pane no longer shows 'hooks need review' or MCP-startup-failed.

## Verify
- cargo test -p exomonad-core common_spawn_env_codex_home — new test passes
- just check-fmt + just test-fast pass
- Manual e2e: leaf MCP starts cleanly (no socket-connect failure), no hook trust prompt in any agent pane

## Done criteria

issues.title: E2E reviewer convergence: bias reviewer via injected context + enforce bounded 1-fix loop with [STUCK→HUMAN] escalation
issues.description:
## Problem

Two related gaps the latest e2e run on commit b0ec0190 exposed:

1. **The test cannot deterministically trigger the FixesPushed convergence path** because the auto-spawned reviewer LLM has no reason to request changes on a trivial CONTRIBUTING.md placeholder, and the testrunner's PR-registry mutation approach was always doomed (the watcher re-reads the reviewer's verdict file .exo/reviews/pr_N.json as source of truth, overwriting any in-prs.json mutation on next poll).

2. **The convergence loop has no bound today.** A reviewer can request changes, the leaf can push a fix, the reviewer can request more changes — recursion forever. We want exactly ONE back-and-forth: reviewer requests changes → leaf fixes once → reviewer re-reviews. If the reviewer still isn't satisfied after that single fix, the DevPhase/ReviewerPhase state machine must transition to a 'needs human direction' state and emit a [STUCK] signal up to the TL.

Both pieces land together because the e2e test is the smoke test for the bounded loop's correctness.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT keep the auto_spawn=false approach from the now-closed #257. The e2e tests the REAL convergence path against the REAL reviewer; we bias the reviewer via context, not bypass it.
- DO NOT mutate .exo/prs.json review_state from the testrunner. That field is the watcher's cached observation; the watcher re-reads .exo/reviews/pr_N.json on every poll and overwrites the cache. Source of truth is the reviewer's verdict file — and the reviewer is the only entity that should write it.
- DO NOT make the bounded-loop limit a global numeric config (e.g., max_review_rounds = 1). Hardcode 1 in the state machine for now; if we later want more flexibility, expose it as a per-role config rather than buried numeric magic.
- DO NOT treat 'needs human direction' as the same state as DevFailed. Failed = leaf exhausted retries. NeedsHumanDirection = humans should look at this; the agent did its best but the reviewer is not converging.
- DO NOT inject reviewer context globally (production). The bias is fixture-local; only the e2e test repo carries the checklist file and the reviewer_context config that loads it.

## Read first
- .exo/lib/DevPhase.hs — current DevPhase / DevEvent state machine. The bounded-loop change adds a new phase + transition.
- .exo/roles/devswarm/DevRole.hs — event handlers that drive DevPhase transitions.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1334 spawn_reviewer_subtree — how reviewer_context flows into the reviewer's task prompt.
- rust/exomonad/src/config.rs ReviewerConfig — the place to extend reviewer_context_paths handling, if not already there.
- tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/run.sh + testrunner.md — current race-prone harness, to be replaced by the context-injection harness.
- Recent chainlink #247/#248/#249/#250/#256 — the convergence-loop wiring story this issue completes.

## Steps

### Part A — E2E harness: bias reviewer via injected context

1. Create tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/reviewer-checklist.md with content along the lines of:
   > 'You are reviewing PR #1 for an E2E test. You MUST request the following specific change before approving: the file CONTRIBUTING.md is missing a copyright header citing the year and project name. Write a request_changes verdict citing this specific item. DO NOT approve until that exact change is present on the next review pass.'
2. Update tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/run.sh to:
   a. Copy reviewer-checklist.md into the test repo at .exo/context/reviewer-checklist.md before exomonad init runs.
   b. Add to .exo/config.toml:
      [reviewer]
      agent_type = "codex"
      context_paths = [".exo/context/reviewer-checklist.md"]
3. Rewrite tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/testrunner.md:
   - Phase 1: wait for PR (unchanged)
   - Phase 2: wait for reviewer to register (unchanged — auto-spawn re-enabled, reviewer reads context, writes changes_requested verdict naturally)
   - Phase 3: REMOVED. No PR registry mutation. The reviewer naturally writes changes_requested; the watcher reads .exo/reviews/pr_1.json and fires ReviewReceived.
   - Phase 4: REMOVED (send_message to leaf). The watcher injects the review comments into the leaf's pane via tmux STDIN naturally.
   - Phase 5: poll leaf's worktree git log for new commit (unchanged; #248's persistence work makes this observable via the worktree symlink).
   - Phase 6: assert server log emits both:
     * 'Fanning out pr_review event to reviewer agent ... kind=fixes_pushed' (the fan-out from #249)
     * Reviewer's WASM handle_event return value (proves #256 is fixed) — likely shown as 'handle_event returned: NotifyParent' or similar in the server log.
   - Verdict: success only if BOTH log lines present. SKIPPED only if the reviewer somehow approves on first pass (which shouldn't happen with the checklist).

### Part B — State machine: bounded 1-fix loop + NeedsHumanDirection phase

4. Add a new phase to DevPhase: DevNeedsHumanDirection (PR# pr_number, reason: Text).
5. In DevPhase's transition function, extend the FixesPushed / CommitsPushed arm: when the leaf is in DevUnderReview with round >= 1 and a new ReviewReceived/ReviewerRequestedChanges fires (meaning the reviewer is requesting changes again after the first fix), transition to DevNeedsHumanDirection (PR#, 'reviewer still requesting changes after first fix round').
6. canExit for DevNeedsHumanDirection: MustBlock 'PR #N has unresolved review feedback after first fix round; awaiting human direction.'
7. DevRole's PRReviewHandler: when entering DevNeedsHumanDirection, NotifyParent with '[STUCK: agent-id] PR #N — reviewer is not converging after 1 fix round; need human direction.'
8. Update root.md's Notification Vocabulary to document this signal alongside the existing [STUCK: id] for review-round limits.
9. Mirror change on the reviewer side if appropriate: ReviewerPhase (issue #255) might want a corresponding NeedsHumanDirection on the reviewer's side; defer to that issue.

## Verify
- cabal test all — new unit test for DevPhase: DevUnderReview(round=1) + ReviewerRequestedChanges → DevNeedsHumanDirection
- just check-fmt + just test-fast pass
- just install-all-dev + just e2e-reviewer-convergence — testrunner reaches Phase 6, observes both required log lines, writes success marker, validator reports Failures: 0
- Manual: temporarily change reviewer-checklist.md to require an impossible criterion (e.g., 'always request a second change after the first fix'). Re-run; testrunner should observe [STUCK: agent-id] from the TL pane and the test should report a SECONDARY pass mode that exercises the NeedsHumanDirection path.

## Done criteria
- E2E test deterministically exercises the FixesPushed convergence path (reviewer naturally requests changes → leaf fixes → reviewer approves → leaf reaches DevApproved). No SKIPPED outcome.
- DevPhase has DevNeedsHumanDirection with MustBlock canExit and a transition rule that fires on 2nd-round reviewer-requested-changes.
- The [STUCK: agent-id] notification reaches the TL on the NeedsHumanDirection transition.
- root.md documents the new signal.
- #257 stays closed as superseded.

## Why
The e2e test is the canary for the entire convergence-loop machinery (#247 + subissues). Without a deterministic harness, every run reports SKIPPED and hides real bugs (like the still-open #256). And bounding the loop to one fix round + escalating to humans is the architectural decision that turns a potential infinite loop into a converging system with a clear stuck-state — important for production trust, not just tests.

issues.title: Add [reviewer] auto_spawn flag + e2e harness uses it to bypass reviewer auto-decision race
issues.description:
## Problem

The e2e tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop test cannot deterministically exercise the FixesPushed convergence loop because the auto-spawned reviewer LLM races ahead of the testrunner. On a trivial PR (single-line CONTRIBUTING.md placeholder), the reviewer always approves before the testrunner can inject a ChangesRequested state via PR registry mutation. Per the most recent run on commit b0ec0190:

- Reviewer spawned, ran, approved at t=18:15:11 (within ~30s of PR being filed)
- Testrunner's Phase 3 ChangesRequested injection arrived ~2 minutes later — too late
- Test reports SKIPPED per the documented race in testrunner.md

This is a structural problem: any test that depends on a real LLM reviewer choosing 'changes requested' is non-deterministic. We need to bypass the auto-spawn for the test scenario.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT remove reviewer auto-spawn globally. The production flow depends on it.
- DO NOT try to slow the reviewer down (sleep, lower model, etc.) to give the test a window. Brittle, depends on timing.
- DO NOT pre-write .exo/reviews/pr_N.json hoping to win the race. The watcher polls and could observe either file first; race within a race.
- DO NOT bypass the reviewer fan-out path — the test's purpose is to exercise it. After this flag lets us suppress the LLM reviewer, the test must STILL register a reviewer-like entry in the PR registry so reviewer_for_pr returns Some and the watcher fans out.
- DO NOT make the flag fire-and-forget at first; default it to true so production behavior is unchanged. Only test fixtures opt out.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad/src/config.rs:81-100 — ReviewerConfig struct + default_reviewer_agent_type
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:493-514 — the auto-spawn block ('Spawn reviewer immediately on first sighting of a new open PR')
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr_local.rs PrEntry — reviewer_agent + reviewer_birth_branch (added in #248)
- tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/run.sh and testrunner.md — current race-prone harness

## Steps
1. Add field to ReviewerConfig in rust/exomonad/src/config.rs:
   pub auto_spawn: bool with default fn default_reviewer_auto_spawn() -> true.
2. Plumb the value into AgentControlService alongside reviewer_agent_type and reviewer_model (with_reviewer_auto_spawn builder fn).
3. In worktree_event_watcher.rs:493 (the 'if let Some(spawner) = ...' block), short-circuit when reviewer_auto_spawn is false. Log info!('reviewer auto-spawn disabled by config; PR #N has no reviewer until one is registered manually').
4. Update tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop/run.sh to set:
   [reviewer]
   agent_type = "codex"
   auto_spawn = false
5. Update testrunner.md Phase 2 to skip 'wait for reviewer assignment' (no reviewer will be auto-spawned). Instead, the testrunner manually pre-registers a fake reviewer entry into .exo/prs.json: set reviewer_agent='review-pr-N-fake' and reviewer_birth_branch='review-pr-N' so reviewer_for_pr returns Some. (Optionally spawn a dummy reviewer pane that just sleeps — the test only cares that the fan-out call_handle_event reaches it; the dummy doesn't need to respond.)
6. Update testrunner.md Phase 3 to write .exo/reviews/pr_N.json directly with a 'changes_requested' verdict, mimicking what a real reviewer would have written. Watcher's next poll sees it and fires ReviewReceived → InjectMessage to leaf.
7. Update testrunner.md Phase 4-6 unchanged: leaf gets review comments via tmux STDIN, pushes fix, watcher fires FixesPushed → fan-out call_handle_event(review-pr-N, ...) → testrunner asserts the canonical 'Fanning out pr_review event to reviewer agent' log line fires with kind=fixes_pushed.

## Verify
- cargo test -p exomonad — new unit test confirms auto_spawn=false skips the auto-spawn block
- just check-fmt + just test-fast pass
- just e2e-reviewer-convergence — testrunner reaches Phase 5 deterministically, observes 'Fanning out ... kind=fixes_pushed' in server log, writes success marker, validator reports Verdict: success / Failures: 0

## Done criteria
- ReviewerConfig.auto_spawn defaults to true (production unchanged)
- Test harness opts out via [reviewer] auto_spawn = false
- The convergence-loop e2e test passes deterministically (no SKIPPED outcome)
- Documentation in CLAUDE.md or testrunner.md explains the auto_spawn=false posture for test contexts

## Why
Without this, the convergence loop is essentially untestable in CI. The race-skip pattern means every run reports SKIPPED, which masks real bugs (like #256, the plugin lookup failure that has been silently broken since the fan-out was wired up). A deterministic harness exposes both the wiring AND any future regressions in the dispatch path.

comments.content: Superseded — see follow-up issue. Approach revised: instead of bypassing reviewer auto-spawn via a config flag, the e2e test biases the real reviewer LLM via injected context (a checklist file that instructs the reviewer to request a specific change for this PR). Full convergence loop is exercised against real agents on a real planted grievance, no race.

issues.title: Watcher fan-out: 'No plugin found for agent <branch>' — reviewer plugin lookup keys on birth_branch but registry is keyed by internal_name
issues.description:
## Problem

Surfaced by tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop running on commit b0ec0190 (CODEX_HOME fix). With the trust-prompt issue resolved, the fan-out wiring from #249/#250 finally exercises the dispatch path — and it lands in this log line:

```
Fanning out pr_review event to reviewer agent pr_number=1 reviewer_branch=review-pr-1 reviewer_agent_type=Codex kind=review_received
call_handle_event{branch=review-pr-1 event_type=pr_review}: No plugin found for agent 'review-pr-1', skipping event dispatch
```

The watcher correctly resolves the reviewer's birth_branch via PrRegistry::reviewer_for_pr (subissue #248) and correctly calls call_handle_event(reviewer_branch, reviewer_agent_type, ...). But call_handle_event looks up the agent's PluginManager from a registry keyed by the agent's INTERNAL_NAME (e.g., 'review-pr-1-codex' — slug+type suffix), not by birth_branch ('review-pr-1'). The lookup fails, the dispatch is skipped with a benign-looking log, and the reviewer never sees the event. The leaf+reviewer convergence loop is still silently broken, just one layer deeper than #247 thought.

This is a follow-up to #247/#249/#250. Those subissues correctly fan out the EVENT; this issue is about the PLUGIN MANAGER LOOKUP not finding the reviewer's plugin manager by the same identifier used for the fan-out.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT change PrRegistry::reviewer_for_pr to return internal_name instead of birth_branch. The fan-out semantics (which branch to dispatch to) belong with birth_branch — that's the agent's identity from the routing perspective. The lookup needs to translate, not the storage.
- DO NOT silently fall through 'No plugin found' as if it's expected. That log line is the bug fingerprint — if it ever fires for a reviewer, the convergence loop is broken. Turn it into a tracing::error at minimum, ideally a structured event so it can be alerted on.
- DO NOT key plugin managers by branch_name directly without resolving — that would conflict with other code that resolves by internal_name. Pick ONE canonical identifier and translate at the boundary.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs around line 783 — call_handle_event signature and plugin lookup
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs around line 540 — dispatch loop where 'branch' originates (for the leaf path, this IS the leaf's birth_branch which == its agent_name in the registry — that's why the leaf side has worked all along)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_resolver.rs — the canonical birth_branch ↔ internal_name mapping
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1334 (spawn_reviewer_subtree) — confirm the reviewer registers under its internal_name in whatever registry call_handle_event reads
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/mod.rs — AgentIdentity (slug + agent_type → internal_name)

## Diagnosis hint
The leaf works because for a regular dev-leaf, branch_name == internal_name from the registry's perspective in this code path (or close enough — the lookup happens to succeed). For the reviewer, branch_name is 'review-pr-N' but the worktree dir and the internal_name include the '-codex' (or other type) suffix. AgentResolver knows how to map; the watcher just isn't asking.

## Steps
1. Reproduce: just install-all-dev && just e2e-reviewer-convergence. Watch the server window for the canonical 'No plugin found for agent 'review-pr-N'' line. It fires every time the watcher fans out a pr_review event to a reviewer.
2. Find call_handle_event in watcher.rs:783 and look at how it currently locates the plugin manager. Compare to how it locates the leaf's plugin manager (where lookup succeeds).
3. Two fix shapes — pick one:
   a. Translate at the call site: before calling call_handle_event(reviewer_branch, ...), resolve reviewer_branch -> reviewer_internal_name via AgentResolver. Pass internal_name.
   b. Translate inside call_handle_event: accept either form and look up via AgentResolver. Less invasive but blurs the contract.
   Recommendation: (a). The fan-out call site already has all the info to do the translation cleanly.
4. Promote 'No plugin found' from info!/warn! to tracing::error and add the agent_name + lookup_key fields, so future skips are loud rather than buried.
5. Add a unit test (mock or real registry): given a registered reviewer with internal_name 'review-pr-1-codex' and birth_branch 'review-pr-1', call_handle_event with the reviewer's birth_branch must find the plugin manager.

## Verify
- cargo test -p exomonad-core (new unit test)
- just check-fmt + just test-fast pass
- Manual: just e2e-reviewer-convergence — server log shows 'Fanning out pr_review event' immediately followed by a 'handle_event returned' line for the reviewer (not 'No plugin found')
- Manual: with a contrived 'changes requested' scenario (operator-driven, bypassing the auto-approve race), confirm the reviewer's pane receives the FixesPushed handler invocation

## Done criteria
- The 'No plugin found for agent <reviewer_branch>' log line cannot fire in normal operation
- Reviewer's WASM handlers are reached on every fanned-out pr_review event
- Unit test pins the birth_branch→plugin_manager resolution
- Any future regression that breaks the lookup fires a tracing::error visible in the OTel stream

## Why
This is the actual final mile of the convergence loop. #247 set up the strategy, #248 persisted the reviewer mapping, #249/#250 fired the fan-out events. Without this, the events are routed to a name the plugin registry doesn't know — so they reach the dispatch site but no role handler ever runs. The leaf side worked accidentally because branch_name happens to match its registry key; the reviewer side exposes that the watcher has been working on a happy-path accident. With this fixed, the convergence loop finally runs end-to-end without TL intervention.

comments.content: Claimed by interactive session.

Landed in 7932a2cb. Root cause: spawn_subtree computes its own birth_branch as caller_bb.child(internal_name) and registers that with AgentResolver, not the bare options.branch_name. #248 stored the bare form in PrRegistry, so the watcher's resolve_event_agent_name lookup couldn't find the reviewer record. Fix: compute and persist the same dotted form via caller_bb.child(reviewer_internal_name). All tests pass.

issues.title: Reviewer should not exit on approval — must wait for merge_ready CI signal
issues.description:
## Problem

When a reviewer approves a PR today (writes `.exo/reviews/pr_N.json` and stops), the reviewer agent exits its session. But the leaf can still push subsequent commits — including fixes triggered by a TL-side decision (e.g., 'I want a follow-up tweak before merging'). The reviewer is gone by then; nobody re-reviews; the leaf and watcher emit events into a void where the reviewer-side handler in ReviewerRole.hs would have fired.

Per the design intent: the reviewer only completes its job when CI confirms merge-readiness AND the TL receives merge_ready. Approval alone is insufficient — it's a *vote*, not an *exit signal*.

This was surfaced as an edge case while diagnosing tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop (#247): an auto-spawned Claude reviewer approved at t=16:58:21 and stopped at t=16:58:24. Any subsequent leaf push happened in a window where the reviewer was already gone.

Note: this is a SEPARATE concern from #247 (fan-out wiring) and #251 (test scenario non-determinism). The fan-out wiring is correct now; the architectural question is the reviewer's exit condition.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT block the reviewer from exiting indefinitely. The merge_ready signal must reliably arrive (otherwise reviewers accumulate forever).
- DO NOT couple reviewer lifetime to the leaf's lifetime — the leaf may be in DevDone while CI is still running.
- DO NOT make the reviewer poll CI itself. The watcher already does that and fires merge_ready / sibling events.
- DO NOT lower the bar to 'reviewer exits when it has written its verdict' — that's the current buggy behavior.

## Read first
- .exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs — current handlers and any phase / canExit logic
- .exo/lib/DevPhase.hs as a precedent for canExit MustBlock semantics
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs — where merge_ready is emitted (search 'merge_ready')
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1334 spawn_reviewer_subtree

## Steps
1. Add a ReviewerPhase state-machine analogous to DevPhase, with phases like ReviewerSpawned → ReviewerReviewing → ReviewerApprovedAwaitingCI → ReviewerRequestedChanges → ReviewerDone.
2. Implement canExit so the reviewer is MustBlock in ReviewerApprovedAwaitingCI and ReviewerRequestedChanges (only Clean in ReviewerDone, which is reached on merge_ready).
3. Wire the reviewer's role-side handlers to advance through phases on the events that already fan out (#250): ReviewApproved → ApprovedAwaitingCI; FixesPushed → back to ReviewerReviewing; MergeReady → Done.
4. Add a stop-hook check on the reviewer role that returns the MustBlock message until merge_ready arrives.
5. New tests: unit test the canExit decisions; e2e (extend reviewer-convergence-loop or a sibling) that asserts the reviewer pane stays alive past initial approval and only exits after the merge_ready event.

## Verify
- cabal test all
- just test-fast
- just e2e-reviewer-convergence (or follow-up harness) — reviewer pane visible past first approval; only exits after merge_ready

## Done criteria
- Reviewer cannot exit on approval alone — must observe merge_ready (or stuck/timeout) before stopping
- Subsequent leaf pushes after initial approval still reach a live reviewer
- Documented in CLAUDE.md § Tech Lead Praxis (or ReviewerRole's CLAUDE.md if it has one) so the lifecycle is clear

## Why
The fire-and-forget architecture only converges if every actor in the loop stays alive for the full duration of its responsibility. A reviewer that exits on approval is an actor that abandons its post — any post-approval event (CI flake, follow-up fix, TL-requested polish) drops into the void. This isn't a hot bug today but is the next domino once the rest of the convergence loop solidifies.

issues.title: last_head_sha on PrEntry is never persisted by the watcher — registry field is dead
issues.description:
## Problem

PrEntry has a last_head_sha: Option<String> field (rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr_local.rs:93) but it is only ever initialized to None — no code path writes it back. The watcher tracks last_sha on its in-memory WatchState but never propagates that into the persisted PrRegistry. External observers (test harnesses, debugging tooling) can't see the watcher's view of the PR's current SHA from .exo/prs.json.

Surfaced by tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop: the testrunner polled prs.json's last_head_sha to detect when the leaf pushed a fix. The field stayed 'unknown' for the full 5-minute timeout, even though the leaf's branch had moved on disk.

## Options
Either:
1. Persist last_head_sha to PrEntry every time the watcher's in-memory last_sha updates, so the field is meaningful.
2. Remove the dead field from PrEntry entirely — it's vestigial and serialization-only.

Pick one; do not leave the field present-but-unwritten.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/file_pr_local.rs:93 — the field
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs around line 985 — where WatchState.last_sha updates
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs around the registry-write path (write_pr_registry callers)

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT add a re-poll just to refresh this field — the watcher already has the value, just write it through.
- DO NOT keep the field if you choose option 2. A dead serialized field is worse than no field at all.

## Done criteria
- Either the field updates whenever the watcher observes a SHA change OR the field is gone
- An external observer (test or operator) can determine the current SHA the watcher last observed for a PR by reading .exo/prs.json (or has a documented alternative if the field is removed)

issues.title: Codex hook trust not seeded in fresh exomonad-new/init environments — root TL fires '3 hooks need review'
issues.description:
## Problem

Per chainlink-issue-comment on #247: running just e2e-reviewer-convergence (which calls exomonad new + exomonad init in a fresh temp repo) reproducibly surfaces the Codex hook trust review prompt for the root TL:

```
⚠ 3 hooks need review before they can run. Open /hooks to review them.
```

This is the three Codex hooks ExoMonad installs (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) showing up as 'needs review' instead of 'trusted'. The fix from #212/#234 (install_codex_hook_trust pre-seeding hashes into ~/.codex/config.toml's [hooks.state]) is working in the operator's day-to-day backrooms-workspace session but NOT in fresh exomonad-new/init environments.

The test sets CODEX_HOME to a temp dir, so the seeded entries from backrooms aren't there — install_codex_hook_trust must run during the init flow to populate the test's CODEX_HOME. Apparently it isn't, or the hashes it writes don't match Codex's expectation in this environment.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT special-case the e2e harness. The bug is in the general 'fresh exomonad new/init' path — every brand-new workspace will hit it.
- DO NOT add an instruction to operators to run 'codex /hooks' manually. The whole point of #234 was to make trust prompts disappear.
- DO NOT silence the prompt by lowering the codex trust level. Find why install_codex_hook_trust isn't seeding or seeding wrong.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad-core/src/codex_config.rs: install_codex_hook_trust and helpers
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/internal.rs around line 700-720: where install_codex_hook_trust is invoked after trust_codex_project for codex spawn
- rust/exomonad/src/init.rs around line 60-80: the codex-root-TL path that should also invoke install_codex_hook_trust (per #245 follow-up)
- Recent commits: 8934378f (project-level trust), the chainlink-issue-comment on #212 that claims the install_codex_hook_trust seeding landed
- Per-issue-comment 14:39 on #212: 'render hooks with absolute exomonad binary, compute Codex-compatible trusted_hash entries from rendered .codex/config.toml, update CODEX_HOME config under flock + atomic rename'

## Steps
1. Reproduce: run just e2e-reviewer-convergence end-to-end. Confirm '3 hooks need review' surfaces in the codex root TL.
2. Inspect the temp CODEX_HOME (/codex-home/config.toml) after exomonad init runs. Does it have a [hooks.state] block? If yes, do the trusted_hash values match what Codex actually computes for the rendered .codex/config.toml? If no, install_codex_hook_trust never ran.
3. If the [hooks.state] entries are missing entirely, trace why install_codex_hook_trust isn't being called for the root TL path. Compare init.rs's root TL flow to internal.rs's spawn flow.
4. If the entries are present but mismatched, compare the hash to what Codex emits in /hooks for the same hook config. The version_for_toml port in codex_config.rs must produce byte-identical hashes — #220 (still open) is the parity test that catches this. Run it.
5. Once seeded, manual verification: a fresh exomonad new+init on a clean temp dir should launch Codex with no /hooks prompt.

## Verify
- just e2e-reviewer-convergence — Codex root TL shows no 'X hooks need review' banner

issues.title: Claude hooks: PostToolUse response payload has hookEventName=PreToolUse — every Claude PostToolUse hook errors
issues.description:
## Problem

Every Claude PostToolUse hook fires an error in the agent's UI:
```
PostToolUse:Bash hook error
Failed to run: Hook returned incorrect event name: expected 'PostToolUse' but got 'PreToolUse'.
```

The server logs corroborate: it receives PostToolUse correctly but the response payload's hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName is hardcoded to 'PreToolUse':
```
[hook] dispatched runtime=Claude event=PostToolUse tool="mcp__exomonad__approve_pr"
exit_code=0 response={"continue":true,"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"allow"}}
```

Observed in tests/e2e/reviewer-convergence-loop session (PR #1 review pane): every Claude PostToolUse on Bash, ToolSearch, mcp__exomonad__approve_pr produced this error. The exit_code is 0 so the agent continues, but the user-facing error noise + Claude Code's internal rejection of the malformed response is a real regression.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT just hardcode 'PostToolUse' in the response builder — find where the event name is set and pipe through the inbound event type so all hook events stamp the response correctly.
- DO NOT silence the error by suppressing it in the agent UI. The fix is to emit the correct event name.
- DO NOT downgrade the issue because exit_code is 0; the response shape is broken, which is a contract violation with Claude Code.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad/src/serve.rs around the hook dispatch — search for 'hookSpecificOutput' and 'hookEventName'
- haskell/wasm-guest/src/ExoMonad/Guest where HookOutput / HookEnvelope is constructed
- .exo/roles/devswarm role files where PostToolUse handlers return responses

## Steps
1. Grep `hookEventName` and `PreToolUse` literal strings in rust/ and haskell/. The bug is almost certainly a single site where 'PreToolUse' is hardcoded instead of the inbound event-type variable being formatted in.
2. Fix the responder so the response's hookEventName matches the inbound event name (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, Notification, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit).
3. Add a unit test per event type asserting the response payload's hookEventName equals the inbound event name.
4. Smoke test by re-running the e2e harness and confirming no 'PostToolUse:X hook error' surfaces in the agent pane.

## Verify
- cargo test -p exomonad-core (new unit test per event type)
- just check-fmt
- Manual: just e2e-reviewer-convergence, watch the reviewer pane — no event-name mismatch errors

## Done criteria
- Every hook event's response payload carries hookEventName = the actual event type
- Unit tests pin all event types
- No 'incorrect event name' errors visible in any Claude agent pane during a fresh e2e run

## Why
This breaks the hook protocol contract with Claude Code. Even though exit_code=0 keeps things running, the agent UI floods with error messages that obscure real issues — and we just spent a debugging cycle thinking it was a codex hook trust problem when it was this.

issues.title: FixesPushed event never reaches reviewer — watcher only dispatches to the leaf's plugin manager
issues.description:
## Problem

Observed: TL routes a 'changes requested' review to dev-leaf via send_message, leaf pushes fixes, watcher sees the SHA change after ChangesRequested and fires the FixesPushed event. The TL receives [FIXES PUSHED] as expected. The reviewer agent does NOT re-review — it sits idle. Everyone gets stuck because the loop is broken: TL waits for [MERGE READY], that only arrives after reviewer re-approves, reviewer never re-reviews because it was never pinged.

## Root cause

The dispatch loop in rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:540-590 calls call_handle_event with branch=PR's branch (= leaf's birth branch) and agent_type=the leaf's runtime. So the WASM handle_event runs against the LEAF's PluginManager only. The reviewer is a separate agent with a separate birth-branch and its own PluginManager (.exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs has reviewerPRReviewHandler for FixesPushed at line 302 — fully wired on the WASM side, just never invoked).

The Haskell side already does the right thing if it were called; the Rust dispatch never enumerates the reviewer agent for the PR.

## Anti-patterns (FIRST)
- DO NOT solve this by making the leaf's FixesPushed handler send_message to the reviewer. The leaf should not know reviewer agent identities — that couples roles inappropriately. The dispatch site (Rust watcher) is the right place to enumerate every agent that owns a stake in this PR.
- DO NOT route the event only to the reviewer and skip the leaf. Both need it: leaf so its state machine progresses, reviewer so it re-reviews.
- DO NOT broadcast to all agents in the session. Enumerate the precise set: leaf (PR author) + reviewer (assigned to this PR) + any TL on the merge path if applicable.
- DO NOT change ReviewerRole.hs's handler shape — it already exists and is correct.
- DO NOT silently swallow the case where the reviewer agent is not resolvable (e.g., reviewer registry lookup fails). Log a clear error and surface — silent failure is exactly the bug we're fixing.

## Read first
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:540-590 — the dispatch loop. The bug is here.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:985-1011 — where fixes_pushed and commits_pushed are emitted as PendingAction::WasmEvent. The action carries no agent identity today.
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/worktree_event_watcher.rs:679 — call_handle_event signature; what it takes for branch/agent_type
- .exo/roles/devswarm/ReviewerRole.hs:302 — reviewerPRReviewHandler for FixesPushed (the destination handler that is currently unreachable)
- rust/exomonad-core/src/services/agent_control/spawn.rs:1334,1423 — spawn_reviewer_subtree / spawn_reviewer_for_pr (how reviewers are registered; this is where the PR↔reviewer association is established)
- CLAUDE.md § Fire-and-Forget Execution — documents the intended loop ("The reviewer agent re-reviews after fixes are pushed")

## Steps
1. **Find or build a PR→reviewer mapping.** When spawn_reviewer_for_pr is called, the system already knows which reviewer owns which PR. Confirm whether the reviewer registry persists this mapping in a queryable way (likely in PrRegistry or a sibling). If not, add it.
2. **Refactor the dispatch loop at watcher.rs:540** to enumerate every stakeholder for the PR before firing events:
   - The leaf (PR author) — currently the only target
   - The reviewer assigned to this PR — looked up via the registry from step 1
   - (Optionally) the parent TL — but the TL already gets [FIXES PUSHED] via the leaf handler's NotifyParent action, so likely no change needed here. Confirm.
3. **Fire the same WasmEvent** for each stakeholder by calling call_handle_event(stakeholder_branch, stakeholder_agent_type, event_type, payload). Each handler returns its own EventAction; both should be acted on.
4. **Handle the reviewer-not-found case** loudly: tracing::error with PR number, attempted reviewer key, and a clear note that the reviewer registry is stale or never registered. Do not silently skip.
5. **Apply the same fan-out to every event kind that has a reviewer-side handler**: review the ReviewerRole.hs handler set (FixesPushed, ReviewerApproved, ReviewerRequestedChanges, ReviewTimeout, Stuck, MergeReady) and ensure each is fanned out where the role-side handler exists.

## Verify
- cabal test all — Haskell side unchanged but assertions on dispatch behavior should pass
- just test-fast — new Rust unit test asserting call_handle_event is invoked for BOTH leaf and reviewer when fixes_pushed fires (mock the registry; assert both call sites)
- New unit test: same fan-out for ReviewerRequestedChanges and ReviewerApproved
- Manual reproduction: bring up a session, create a leaf+PR, have the reviewer request changes, have the leaf push fixes, confirm the reviewer's pane receives a re-review trigger (current behavior: it does not)
- Existing E2E that exercises the review loop should now complete without manual intervention

## Done criteria
- The reviewer agent's FixesPushed (and sibling events) handler IS invoked when its events fire — verified by unit test and by reproduction
- Reviewer-not-found situations log an error with enough context to debug
- The full review loop (leaf implements → reviewer reviews → leaf fixes → reviewer re-reviews → [MERGE READY] → TL merges) runs to completion without human nudging
- Documentation in CLAUDE.md § Fire-and-Forget Execution remains accurate (it already describes this loop; the code now matches)

## Why
This is the keystone of the convergence protocol. The whole "TL is fire-and-forget" architecture rests on leaf+reviewer converging without TL intervention; if the reviewer cannot re-review, the TL has to manually intervene or sessions stall indefinitely. The bug invalidates the architecture's central claim in practice, regardless of how nicely the Haskell side is wired. This needs to land before more sessions hit it.
